struct.domain: Structures, thermal, power and large space infrastructure

bottlenecks.name: Qualification evidence, margins and model credibility
bottlenecks.description: Proving primary structure will not fail. Practice stacks deterministic factors of safety (ultimate ~1.25 uncrewed, ~1.4 crewed, general), empirical buckling knockdown factors from 1960s lower-bound curves (NASA SP-8007; a universal 0.65 for composites that NASA itself calls possibly unconservative), building-block test pyramids from coupons to full-scale static tests, and model-credibility processes (NASA-STD-7009). Each dedicated qualification article costs months to years.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~25% of structures/thermal engineering effort on a new vehicle or large spacecraft (analyst estimate, general)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High for the math, capped for the payoff. Worst-case imperfection theory and model-form error are genuinely open; reliability-based margins, rare-event estimation and certified error bounds are solved in principle but expert-scarce, which is exactly what on-demand AI supplies. Standards bodies and agencies gate the benefit, so downstream nodes are capped at Medium.

bottlenecks.name: Launch loads and dynamics
bottlenecks.description: Coupled loads analysis (CLA) cycles with the launch provider using Craig-Bampton component models, repeated as designs mature; random vibration, acoustic and shock environments enveloped from flight data plus fixed margins; the mid-frequency band where neither finite elements nor statistical energy analysis is reliable. NASA NESC built Norton-Thevenin Receptance Coupling (2023-2024) precisely because full CLA is slow and costly.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium-High. CLA setup and model reduction are expert-scarce routine work that AI agents can run on demand (fast, P1); the mid-frequency problem is open applied math (slower, P6). Forcing-function uncertainty (liftoff acoustics, buffet) and mandatory qualification-by-test remain.

bottlenecks.name: Damage tolerance, fatigue and inspection for reuse
bottlenecks.description: Crack growth and composite damage under the low-cycle, high-amplitude, cryogenic and thermal-cycling spectra of reusable stages; COPV liner cracks; non-destructive inspection turnaround between flights; qualifying structural health monitoring (SHM) with a probability of detection. First stages are ~70% of launch-vehicle cost (ONERA, 2026), so reuse economics hinge on inspection cost.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~15% and rising with reuse (analyst estimate, general)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium. Inverse-problem stability, optimal sensor placement and model-assisted POD are solved in principle but expert-scarce (AI helps quickly). Damage physics is data-limited: theory needs coupon-to-subcomponent test campaigns. Catalog families 372, 365, 366 touch this only through confidence (P5) and one ceiling (P3).

bottlenecks.name: Thermal design and heat rejection
bottlenecks.description: Radiator sizing under the Stefan-Boltzmann T^4 law with view factors to Earth, Sun and the spacecraft itself; heat transport (pumped liquid and two-phase loops, heat pipes) whose microgravity behavior is still correlation-based; thermal-model correlation after thermal-vacuum tests; the chip-temperature versus chip-life trade. For compute satellites thermal is now a primary mass term: ~25% of SpaceX AI1's reconstructed 2.1 t (33FG, Jun 2026).
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~20%, much higher on orbital compute programs (analyst estimate, general)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium. Radiator and loop design optimization and model correlation are expert-scarce and well-posed (AI helps fast). The physics is fixed (T^4, junction-temperature limits) and the binding gates are manufacturing at Starlink volume and flight data for two-phase models. Family 369 (hot spots) is a nil link.

bottlenecks.name: Large deployables and in-space assembly
bottlenecks.description: Deployment reliability of booms, membranes and panels; the impossibility of representative 1 g ground tests for 100 m to km structures; nonsmooth contact and friction dynamics, membrane wrinkling, thermally induced vibration; robotic assembly. ACS3 (2024) flew an ~80 m2 sail on 7 m booms; follow-on booms target 2,000 m2.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium-Low. Better models and scaling laws help, but qualification needs flight data, and formation flying (Google Suncatcher's 81-satellite 1 km cluster; SpaceX Starmind's ~10-satellite clusters) is displacing monolithic km-scale structures.

bottlenecks.name: Power-system integration (fission and very large solar)
bottlenecks.description: For Fission Surface Power: reactor, shield, closed Brayton converter, 500-600 K radiators and lander integration within ~6 t (reactor) on a heavy lander, with radiation transport for shielding (outside the release) and nuclear launch approval. For orbital compute: solar array areal density, which 33FG identifies as AI1's primary mass constraint (ROSA-class 1.8-2 kg/m2 needed).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low-Medium. Multiphysics trades accelerate, but fuel, licensing, nuclear ground testing, heavy-lander availability and solar-cell/array manufacturing dominate. First-of-a-kind designs freeze before AI design capability matures.

struct.scenario_contrast: S1 (plateau): research-grade applied math reaches outside teams around 2030, so the cognitive tiers (1-4) land 2028 to beyond 2031 and only 7 of 16 are Medium or better by 2031. The early wins are AI agents running routine analysis (2028) and expert confirmation of the elasticity and hot-spots manuscripts; tiers 5-7 are mostly Low or Speculative (4 of 13 Medium or better, two of them hardware anchors that happen without AI math). S2 (exponential, base case): the cognitive clock compresses by about 2 years on average (median tier 1-4 year 2029; all 16 Medium or High by 2031). Worst-case imperfection theory, certified uncertainty margins, SHM detection limits and radiator optimization arrive in 2028; the physics nodes (composite damage, microgravity two-phase flow, deployment dynamics) arrive in 2030 because data, not cognition, binds. The physical tiers move only about 1 year on average (median 2030) because standards revisions, build-and-qualify cycles, sensor qualification, manufacturing ramps and launch cadence bind. By 2031 under S2: lighter buckling rules (Medium), a first flight structure sized with AI-certified margins (Medium, 2030), SHM inspection credit (Medium), 100 kW/t compute satellites (Medium, 2030) and 1 GW of orbital compute (Medium, 2031, with AI math a second-order contributor), while a km-scale monolith stays Speculative and the lunar 100 kWe reactor stays Low in every scenario. S3 (recursive): moves half the cognitive nodes another year (mainly physics nodes through autonomous labs, and verified numerics) but only 4 of 13 physical nodes, by one year each (reusable-stage life management, a 1,000 m2 sail, 1 GW orbital compute, the structural-mass step). It cannot compress orbital exposure, fleet flight hours, heavy-lander schedules, nuclear licensing or standards cycles. Net: in this domain the S1-to-S2 gap is large in analysis labor and design rules, small in flown hardware by 2031; most of the S2 payoff lands in second-generation hardware after 2031.
key_insights: The catalog barely reaches this domain; the capability does. Only five families touch it (372, 365, 366, 368 elasticity and fracture; 369 hot spots), all as confidence (P5) except one possible ceiling: 365's conductivity nonuniqueness (T3) may bound resistance-based damage sensing in carbon-fiber structures. The hot-spots result (369) changes no thermal design.

The largest near-term effect is labor, not theorems: AI agents running and checking stress, loads and thermal analyses (prototypes exist in 2026) compress design cycles severalfold by ~2028 under S2. This is 'solved in principle but expert-scarce' work, and it is the only node that is High by 2031 in every scenario.

The clearest 'lighter primary structure' chain runs through an open applied-math problem, not a famous conjecture: worst-case imperfections in thin shells. Raising a knockdown factor from 0.65 to 0.80 cuts buckling-critical wall mass ~10% (t scales as KDF^-1/2); optimized shells save 14-31% (Wagner et al. 2025). Standards revision and validation tests cap it at Medium, and the vehicle-level payoff is ~1-3% payload.

Uniqueness is not stability. For structural health monitoring, AI-produced problem-specific stability estimates and probability-of-detection curves matter far more than 372-style uniqueness theorems, because inspection credit depends on what damage size N sensors can see at 90/95 confidence.

For orbital data centers, heat rejection is an engineering and manufacturing problem, not a math or physics blocker. Thermal mass per GW falls from ~19,400 t (Starlink-like, 310 K, one-sided) to ~3,400-3,500 t (AI1 or StarThink V2, ~370 K, two-sided) through temperature and architecture choices already made; AI-optimized design adds perhaps a further 10-25% of thermal mass (~350-900 t, or 3-9 Starship flights per GW), i.e. a few percent of launched mass.

First-of-a-kind timing trap: Fission Surface Power (launch-ready target Q1 FY2030) and AI1 (spec published Jun 2026) freeze their designs before S2's AI design-optimization capability (~2029) matures, so AI-math gains land in second-generation units after 2030.

Formation flying is displacing km-scale structures: Google Suncatcher (81 satellites within 1 km) and SpaceX Starmind (~10-satellite tight clusters, Oct 2026) solve the aperture and bandwidth problem with GNC and optical links. A km-scale monolith stays Speculative by 2031 even under S2.

Data, not cognition, gates the physics nodes (composite damage, microgravity two-phase flow, deployment dynamics, mid-frequency vibration). Compute-satellite fleets streaming thermal telemetry from ~2027-28 become the most valuable two-phase dataset in history; whoever owns the fleet will own the models.

Certification by analysis is the biggest prize (each avoided qualification article saves tens of millions of dollars and a year) but sits behind the slowest gate. Verified finite-element numerics (P2) help less here than in flight software because discretization error is rarely the dominant structural uncertainty.

S3 versus S2 barely matters at tiers 5-7 in this domain: S3 moves 4 of 13 physical nodes forward by one year (reusable-stage life management, a 1,000 m2 sail, 1 GW orbital compute, the structural-mass step), mostly because autonomous labs speed damage-model testing, while qualification tests, flight data, manufacturing ramps, nuclear licensing and launch cadence hold the rest. S1 to S2 moves the cognitive tiers about 2 years but the physical tiers only about 1.
nil_effects: Stefan-Boltzmann is not negotiable: radiator area per watt at a given temperature is fixed, and chip junction limits (~85-105 C) cap radiator temperature unless heat pumps spend power to lift it. No theorem changes the ~0.7 km2 of panel per GW at ~1,400 W/m2.
Launch cadence, heavy-lander availability, capital and chip supply set the dates for GW-scale orbital compute and lunar fission power under all three scenarios.
Space nuclear power gates (fuel supply, nuclear launch approval, ground testing, budget) are untouched; radiation transport for shield design is outside the release entirely.
Material strength, stiffness and density limits do not move with mathematics; any gains come from using existing materials closer to their limits (materials domain covers new materials).
Qualification testing of first-of-kind primary structure, thermal-vacuum and vibration tests remains mandatory through 2031; analysis can reduce tests on derivatives, not eliminate them.
Galactic speedups (107 matrix multiplication, 130 FFT) give no speedup to finite-element, vibroacoustic or thermal codes.
Well-posedness theorems (372, 366, 368) change no simulation code; they raise confidence that what the codes approximate exists and is unique.
Family 369 (hot spots) has no effect on radiator or panel thermal design: real hardware is 3D with radiative boundaries and is designed numerically.
Micrometeoroid and debris flux is a property of the environment; mathematics changes only the design response (segmentation, armoring), not the threat to km2-scale radiators.

verif.domain: Flight software, autonomy assurance and certification

bottlenecks.name: Verification and test labor
bottlenecks.description: Requirements-based unit and integration testing, structural coverage (MC/DC at the highest criticality), code reviews and regression re-verification after every change. In DO-178C Level A practice this is the dominant cost: verification can reach 80% of a Level A software budget, effective productivity is under 10 lines per person-day, and cost runs about $25-100 per line. NASA IV&V adds a further 10-15% of development cost.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~40-50% of safety-critical flight-software effort (up to 80% of a DO-178C Level A budget when all verification is counted)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mostly 'solved in principle but expensive and expert-scarce'. DO-333 already lets formal proof replace most executable-object-code testing except hardware/software integration tests (Airbus replaced unit tests with proofs on A380 software in 2002). Agents that write contracts and proofs, checked by an already-qualified prover, attack this cost directly. This is the largest cost lever in the domain.

bottlenecks.name: Requirements, specifications and environmental assumptions
bottlenecks.description: Writing correct, complete requirements and interface control documents, and stating what the software may assume about sensors, terrain, timing, units and hardware behavior. Most software-caused mission losses trace here: Ariane 501's reused range assumption, Mars Climate Orbiter's units, Schiaparelli's IMU-saturation duration, Hakuto-R M1's terrain, Starliner OFT's timer source.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~15-20% of effort, but the root of all 9 software-related losses in our failure table
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Split. Drafting formal specs from English, unit-typing interfaces, and checking consistency and realizability is expert-scarce work AI does well (cheap unlock). Validating that a spec matches mission intent and physical reality is partly open and data-bound: it needs sensor characterization, terrain data and human sign-off. Once proofs are cheap, this becomes the binding bottleneck (analyst position h).

bottlenecks.name: GNC and numerical algorithm assurance
bottlenecks.description: Showing that guidance, navigation and control code, estimators and onboard optimizers behave as designed: stability margins under saturation and delay, measurement-rejection gates, floating-point round-off and overflow, solver convergence within a timing budget.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~5-10% of effort (concentrated in a few scarce specialists)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mostly expert-scarce rather than open: round-off proofs (NASA DAIDALUS with PVS, PRECiSA and Frama-C), runtime-error analysis (Astree), Lyapunov and barrier certificates, reachability. Nonlinear hybrid verification at full-vehicle scale and certified onboard optimization are partly open research. Lean coverage of floating point (FloatLib, Sep 2026) and of ODEs and numerics is the formalization gate.

bottlenecks.name: Integration, fault management, configuration and timing
bottlenecks.description: Hardware-in-the-loop and end-to-end testing, fault-combination testing of fault detection, isolation and recovery (FDIR), reboot and timing behavior, parameter tables, command sequences and in-flight patches. Starliner OFT, Beresheet, Hitomi and IM-1 failures sit in this class.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~15-20% of effort; HIL rig time often sets schedule
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Model checking of FDIR and mode logic and verification of configuration data are mature in principle; the cost is building faithful models, which agents can extract from code and ICDs. Physical HIL and hardware characterization (for example, whether restarting one IMU blocks the other's data) stay on the physical clock.

bottlenecks.name: Certification evidence, tool qualification and independent review
bottlenecks.description: Producing and defending evidence for DO-178C/DO-333/DO-330, NASA NPR 7150.2D and NASA-STD-8739.8B, NPR 8705.2C human rating, ECSS-E-ST-40C Rev.1 and ECSS-Q-ST-80C Rev.2, and FAA Part 450 section 450.141; qualifying or accrediting tools; independent verification and validation.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~10-15% of effort; sets the pace of credit, not of engineering
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Little cognitive help needed; the gate is regulatory. The key unlock is architectural: keep the AI outside the trusted base and route proofs through an already-qualified checker, so only the checker needs qualification. Qualifying Lean itself as a TQL-4/5 tool is the slower path (shared node infra-tool-qualification).

bottlenecks.name: Assurance of learned and autonomous components
bottlenecks.description: Neural perception for terrain-relative navigation and hazard detection, learned guidance, and onboard decision-making for landers, rendezvous and constellations. Aviation guidance (SAE ARP6983 / EUROCAE ED-324, EASA NPA 2025-07) relies on data and process assurance, not proof.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Genuinely open for direct verification: exact neural-network verification is NP-hard and 'correct perception' is defined by data, so VNN-COMP-scale tools remain far from flight vision networks. Strong help for the workaround: proving a small runtime-assurance monitor, recoverable set and backup controller (Simplex architecture).

verif.scenario_contrast: S1 (plateau): research-grade math reaches outside teams around 2028. Agents prove ordinary code well, but Lean coverage of numerics and dynamics stays thin to about 2030, so the cheap wins are runtime-error freedom, FDIR and configuration model checking, and AI-drafted specs. First certification credit for AI-generated proofs (through already-qualified checkers) arrives around 2029, with crewed-lander use after 2031. Full Level-A program software costs fall only 20-30%. S2 (exponential, base case): the cognitive clock collapses by 2027-28. Code proofs, specs, round-off bounds, barrier certificates and model building all become compute jobs, and the cost of a fully verified line falls 30-100x. Every remaining gate is physical or institutional: human review of specs, hardware-behavior and terrain data, HIL time, software freezes 12-18 months before flight, a few lander and rendezvous flights a year, and regulator plan acceptance. So uncrewed commercial landers and constellations, which have no certifying regulator for mission software, adopt first (2028-29), while crewed HLS autonomy and Part 450 credit arrive around 2029-30 and stay capped at Medium. S3 (recursive): cognitive work is near-free from 2028 and autonomous labs speed sensor characterization and HIL test automation, pulling environment models and RPO assurance forward by about a year. Launch cadence, lunar truth data, human-rating authority and the open problem of specifying correct perception do not move, so S3 differs from S2 by about a year on the physical nodes, not by a new class of outcome. In every scenario the binding constraint ends up being 'is the spec right?', not 'can we prove it?'.
key_insights: In this domain the catalog barely matters. The relevant evidence is the pipeline: agent-written Lean for the main results of 162 papers in under four weeks (openai/math, T3, unchecked), on top of a public trend from 82% Dafny vericoding (Sep 2025) to 27 of 43 repository-scale verified builds (Vero, Aug 2026). Only family 104 (game solving for synthesis) and, as theory only, family 143 touch verification at all, and neither changes workflows.

Keep the AI outside the trusted base. Under DO-330, a tool whose output is independently checked needs no qualification. If AI writes proofs and an already-qualified checker (SPARK, Frama-C, Astree) verifies them, DO-333 credit for replacing unit tests can flow without qualifying the AI. The regulatory gate becomes a plan-acceptance step (around 2028 in S2), not a new standard. Lean-native pipelines, where AI labs are strongest, must take the slower route of qualifying Lean itself (around 2030 in S2).

Specifications, not proofs, are the bottleneck. Of 12 notable losses and near-losses (Ariane 501 to Athena), 9 were primarily or partly software, logic or configuration errors. In all 9 the missing piece was a wrong or missing assumption, interface spec or process step (Ariane 4 ranges, units, IMU saturation duration, a crater rim, IMU restart bus behavior, the timer source), not proof capacity. Cheap proofs pay off only alongside AI spec drafting and assumption falsification, and those are bound by data and human review.

Uncrewed commercial space adopts fastest because nobody certifies its mission software. Lunar landers and constellations need only internal or customer acceptance, so they lead (S2: 2028-29). Aviation-style DO-178C credit, NASA human rating (NPR 8705.2C) and FAA Part 450 credit all need a regulator, so they are capped at Medium and arrive later.

Cost model: a fully verified line gets 30-100x cheaper (from about $300-600 to about $5-20 under S2), but a certified Level-A program's software gets only about 2.4x cheaper. Hardware/software integration and system testing stay physical, and DO-333 itself keeps integration tests. The bigger change is the assurance level per dollar and re-verification turnaround (weeks to days).

Timing: Artemis IV's 2028 crewed landing software is largely frozen before public research-grade verification arrives, so proofs reach crewed lunar autonomy in 2029-31 block upgrades. Constellations, with more than 355,000 autonomous-dominated avoidance maneuvers a year at Starlink and weekly updates, are where verified autonomy pays first.

Neural-network verification remains genuinely open even in S3, because 'correct perception' is defined by data. The practical route is proven runtime-assurance wrappers (Simplex), which agents make cheap.

Even if it all works, it will be hard to see by 2031. There will be too few landings to show a statistically lower software-caused loss rate, and recent lander losses (Peregrine, Resilience, Athena) were mostly hardware and sensor physics that software proofs do not touch.
nil_effects: Hardware and sensor-physics failures: Peregrine's helium valve (2024), Resilience's degraded rangefinder (2025) and Athena's altimeter interference and low-sun lighting (2025) are untouched by software proofs. That is roughly half of recent lunar-landing losses.

Hardware/software integration testing, HIL time and environmental qualification (thermal vacuum, vibration, radiation) stay on the physical clock. DO-333 explicitly retains hardware/software integration tests.
Multicore timing interference, worst-case execution time on new processors and radiation-induced upsets are measured, not proven. Isolation and timing proofs assume correct hardware.
The number of rendezvous, docking and propellant-transfer flight demonstrations needed for HLS (reportedly around 15-17 Starship flights per landing) does not shrink because software is proven.
Direct verification of flight-scale neural perception stays out of reach through 2031 in every scenario; assurance routes around it with runtime monitors.

Standards revision cycles stay slow: DO-178B (1992) to DO-178C (2011), NPR 7150.2C (2014) to NPR 7150.2D (2022) (general). No DO-178D or regulator-endorsed AI-proof standard is likely before the 2030s, so credit comes through existing alternative-means clauses.
FAA Part 450 license timelines, driven by environmental review, mishap investigations and public-safety analysis, do not shorten because of formal evidence (general).

Catalog results with no verification effect: Unique Games (102), random-SAT thresholds (235), Subset Sum (138) and L=RL=BPL (103) do not change SAT/SMT solver practice on structured verification problems. The galactic speedups for matrix multiplication (107) and the FFT (130) give no onboard or toolchain gain. Learning-theory results (139, 140, 222) do not provide neural-network verification methods.
Command-link cryptography: nothing in the release weakens deployed authentication or encryption. A frontier model pointed at cryptanalysis is a watch item (analyst position f), not a present effect.

signposts.event: The first independent Comparator runs and statement audits of the openai/math Lean files (via Hexagon or Buzzard's group), including the rate of statement gaps.
signposts.what_it_changes: It calibrates how far agent-written formal artifacts can be trusted without human proof review. A low statement-gap rate supports the checker-not-generator path; a high one shifts weight onto spec review and slows verif-checker-not-generator.

signposts.event: Public release of a research-grade math and verification model (OpenAI or a rival) with agentic Lean, Dafny, SPARK or Frama-C workflows.
signposts.what_it_changes: It turns on P1 and P2 for outside space teams and dates the S1-versus-S2 fork for verif-code-proof-agents, verif-closed-loop-guarantees and every node downstream.

signposts.event: A vendor or agency case study of AI-generated proofs over more than 10 KLOC of production embedded code (AdaCore, AbsInt, TrustInSoft, Galois, NASA, ESA), or Vero-class repository benchmarks above 90%.
signposts.what_it_changes: It confirms verif-code-proof-agents and the cost-collapse chain; failure to appear by end-2027 pushes S2 dates back about a year.

signposts.event: An FAA or EASA certification review item, certification-authority paper or software certification plan accepting AI-generated proof artifacts checked by a qualified tool under DO-333.
signposts.what_it_changes: It opens the certified path (verif-checker-not-generator) and makes verif-afss-part450 and verif-hls-autonomy-certification reachable within the horizon.

signposts.event: Publication of SAE ARP6983 / EUROCAE ED-324 and EASA's second NPA under RMT.0742 (2026), and whether they credit runtime assurance or formal robustness proofs.
signposts.what_it_changes: Credit for runtime assurance moves verif-runtime-assurance toward High; silence on formal methods confirms that learned components are assured by process rather than proof.

signposts.event: The root cause of the next commercial lander or rendezvous failure (IM-3, Blue Ghost 2, ispace M3, Griffin, Blue Moon MK1, Starship transfer demos).
signposts.what_it_changes: A spec or assumption root cause supports the thesis that specifications bind; a logic error that a cheap proof would have caught shows adoption lagging capability; a hardware cause supports the nil effects.

signposts.event: NASA guidance on AI-generated code and verification evidence (a revision of NPR 7150.2, the software-engineering handbook, or IV&V practice), or a lander team declaring formally verified descent GNC and fault management at a readiness review.
signposts.what_it_changes: It confirms the uncrewed-first adoption path (verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight) and signals whether NASA's technical authority will accept proofs for human rating.

signposts.event: Maturity of Lean numerics: FloatLib or FloatSpec stable releases, verified ODE and linear-algebra libraries, and a qualification kit for the Lean kernel or Comparator.
signposts.what_it_changes: It sets the dates for infra-verified-numerics, verif-verified-gnc-numerics and the Lean route to infra-tool-qualification.

signposts.event: Starship ship-to-ship propellant transfer demonstration (reported for Q4 2026) and the Artemis III LEO docking test (late 2027).
signposts.what_it_changes: These set the physical clock for verif-rpo-assured-autonomy and verif-hls-autonomy-certification regardless of verification capability.

signposts.event: A mission loss or near-miss traced to an AI-written specification or proof, as opposed to AI-written code.
signposts.what_it_changes: This negative signpost would trigger regulator caution, pull certification-dependent nodes down a band, and strengthen the case for human spec review as the binding gate.

astro-formal-astrodynamics-library.title: Formal astrodynamics library
astro-formal-astrodynamics-library.description: Machine-checked definitions and core theorems for orbital mechanics (Kepler's equation, Lambert's problem, the circular restricted three-body problem and its Jacobi integral, Clohessy-Wiltshire relative motion, quaternion attitude kinematics, standard probability-of-collision definitions) in Lean or Isabelle, so GNC and traffic properties can be written as formal specifications.
astro-formal-astrodynamics-library.status_oct2026: Essentially absent from Mathlib (general). Building blocks appeared in 2026: a Lean 4 Lyapunov-stability library for autonomous ODEs, Lean integral curves and flows on Banach manifolds (arXiv 2602.13247), and an agent pipeline that brought 84 of 175 statements of a numerical-ODE textbook to proof-complete Lean (arXiv 2606.14000, Jun 2026). No catalog family applies.
astro-formal-astrodynamics-library.why: Every verified-GNC and verified-traffic chain below needs agreed formal definitions to state specifications against; today a team that wants to prove a guidance property must first formalize orbital mechanics itself. The openai/math pipeline produced agent-written Lean for 127 families in under four weeks; a core astrodynamics library is perhaps 10-30k lines (assumption), i.e. weeks of agent time under S2 rather than person-years. Parts touching numerical-integration error wait on infra-mathlib-applied.
astro-formal-astrodynamics-library.strongest_case_small: Libraries are cheap; agreement is not. Definitions must match what flight-dynamics codes compute (reference frames, time systems, ephemerides, units), and the June 2026 audit found kernel-accepted agent formalizations with weakened hypotheses and parameter restrictions, so a library can compile and still misstate the physics.
astro-formal-astrodynamics-library.signpost: A public Lean or Isabelle orbital-mechanics library covering Lambert, CR3BP and Clohessy-Wiltshire, adopted or cited by a NASA, ESA or university GNC group, by end-2027.

astro-catalog-dynamics-results.title: Catalog chaos results (weak link)
astro-catalog-dynamics-results.description: The openai/math families closest to orbital dynamics: positive metric entropy for the Chirikov standard map (146), counterexamples to strong forms of Arnold's fixed-point conjecture (347), sharp symplectic ball-packing criteria (343), and uniform limit-cycle bounds for planar polynomial vector fields (143). They concern model maps and planar fields, not the n-body problem.
astro-catalog-dynamics-results.status_oct2026: 146 is T1 (manuscript only); 347 is T3 (agent-written Lean, unchecked by outsiders); 343 is T1; 143 is T3. The release contains nothing on n-body dynamics, KAM theory for the three-body problem, or Arnold-diffusion rates.
astro-catalog-dynamics-results.why: Band refers to the results becoming established (T4 for the Lean families, outside endorsement for the manuscripts); their astro implication is separately judged nil-to-Low. The standard map is the textbook model of resonance overlap (Chirikov criterion), used heuristically to judge where near-resonant orbits turn chaotic; if 146 holds (conditional, T1), chaos there is measure-theoretically real, not a numerical artefact. 347 limits what periodic-orbit existence theorems can promise for Hamiltonian maps; 343 bounds symplectic phase-space packing. None yields a stability region, timescale or station-keeping number for a real orbit, so the downstream astro effect is confidence only (P5), conditional for 146 and 343.
astro-catalog-dynamics-results.strongest_case_small: No mission designer assumed the standard map was integrable; numerical chaos indicators (FLI, MEGNO, Lyapunov exponents) already guide practice, and these results change zero design decisions. Planar polynomial limit cycles (143) do not describe orbital dynamics at all.
astro-catalog-dynamics-results.signpost: Celestial-mechanics groups citing 146 or 347 in a three-body or resonance paper by 2028; if none do, treat the link as nil.

astro-nbody-transport-proofs.title: Rigorous n-body transport bounds
astro-nbody-transport-proofs.description: Computer-assisted proofs, with explicit constants, of transport, diffusion and escape-time bounds in realistic restricted and full three- and four-body models (Earth-Moon CR3BP, bicircular, ephemeris-forced), for example how long trajectories starting near a DRO or lunar frozen orbit provably stay bounded.
astro-nbody-transport-proofs.status_oct2026: Open frontier; not in the catalog. Capinski and Gidea gave a computer-assisted proof of Arnold diffusion in the planar full three-body problem for a Neptune-Triton-asteroid system (arXiv 2504.09273, Apr 2025): existence with explicit parameter ranges, not operational timescales. Practice relies on Monte Carlo propagation.
astro-nbody-transport-proofs.why: This is the bespoke, hard-but-not-famous problem class that analyst position (a) says the capability absorbs first. A single computer-assisted diffusion proof took a leading group years; at roughly 3 hours of compute per research result, a library of system-specific theorems (one per orbit family of operational interest) becomes cheap once outside teams have access. Value: replaces 'we ran 10^4 propagations' with 'no trajectory starting in set A leaves before time T', the form a disposal-orbit or parking-orbit safety case wants.
astro-nbody-transport-proofs.strongest_case_small: Proven bounds in chaotic regimes are usually orders of magnitude looser than observed behaviour (Nekhoroshev-type times are exponentially pessimistic), and solar gravity, radiation pressure and ephemeris perturbations break the clean models proofs need; operators will keep using Monte Carlo and active station-keeping.
astro-nbody-transport-proofs.signpost: An AI-assisted paper by 2028 proving explicit-time confinement or escape bounds for a real DRO, NRHO or lunar frozen-orbit family in a model that includes solar gravity.

astro-stability-atlas.title: Certified cislunar stability atlas
astro-stability-atlas.description: Validated (interval or Taylor-model) maps of where lunar frozen orbits, DROs, halo/NRHO families and resonant orbits stay bounded for 10-100 years, plus certified station-keeping delta-v budgets for stated navigation and maneuver-execution errors.
astro-stability-atlas.status_oct2026: Practice is numerical (Monte Carlo, chaos indicators). Verified propagation exists but reaches days to weeks in LEO (verified regularized Dromo interval propagation, TU Delft), not decades in chaotic regimes. ESA's Lunar Pathfinder targets a lunar frozen orbit; Moonlight navigation services are planned for end-2028 to 2030.
astro-stability-atlas.why: Long-lived lunar relay and navigation constellations (Moonlight: four navigation and one communication satellite), surface-base support orbits and disposal orbits need decade-scale budgets. A certified atlas turns propellant margins from 'Monte Carlo 99th percentile plus engineering margin' into a proven envelope; illustratively, halving a 20-30% station-keeping margin buys small relays years of life. It needs new theory plus verified numerics, so it lands a year after the pure proofs.
astro-stability-atlas.strongest_case_small: Chaos sets a hard horizon: NRHOs are unstable with prediction horizons of days to weeks, so no proof yields ballistic predictions beyond that; certified budgets then depend on controller and navigation-error models that are engineering assumptions. Frozen orbits and DROs are already known numerically to be stable enough for practice.
astro-stability-atlas.signpost: A lunar relay or navigation operator (ESA Moonlight, a CLPS relay provider) citing certified stability or station-keeping bounds in orbit selection or disposal planning.

astro-scp-guarantees.title: Guarantees for convex landing guidance
astro-scp-guarantees.description: Proofs of convergence, iteration bounds, recursive feasibility and robustness margins for the real-time guidance algorithms used in powered descent and proximity operations: lossless convexification beyond the 3-DoF case, 6-DoF successive convexification with state-triggered constraints, and robust or chance-constrained variants.
astro-scp-guarantees.status_oct2026: Lossless convexification gives global optimality with deterministic convergence for 3-DoF powered descent (general; the Acikmese-Blackmore line of work behind G-FOLD and reusable-booster landing guidance). Successive convexification has convergence-to-stationarity guarantees via the prox-linear framework, extended to continuous-time, passively safe 6-DoF powered descent (Elango, Vinod, Di Cairano, Weiss, MERL TR2025-008, AIAA SciTech Jan 2025). Global optimality and worst-case iteration bounds for 6-DoF nonconvex problems remain open. No catalog family.
astro-scp-guarantees.why: These are 'solved in principle, expert-scarce' problems: perhaps a few dozen groups worldwide write such proofs (general). On-demand research math turns each new constraint type (plume impingement, glideslope, sensor pointing, passive abort safety) into a same-week theorem instead of a dissertation chapter. Proven iteration bounds are what onboard schedulers need to guarantee a solution inside a fixed guidance cycle (roughly 1-10 Hz replanning for landing, general).
astro-scp-guarantees.strongest_case_small: Reusable boosters already land routinely with convex/SCP-style guidance without global guarantees, relying on Monte Carlo campaigns and fallback logic; a proof changes paperwork, not landing accuracy, unless it lets designers cut propellant or divert margins.
astro-scp-guarantees.signpost: AI-assisted proofs of recursive feasibility or iteration bounds for 6-DoF successive convexification published by a leading GNC group by end-2027.

astro-verified-onboard-solver.title: Verified onboard optimization solvers
astro-verified-onboard-solver.description: Embedded SOCP/QP solver code with machine-checked proofs that, in the flight processor's floating-point arithmetic, it terminates within N iterations and returns an epsilon-feasible, epsilon-optimal solution or a certified infeasibility flag.
astro-verified-onboard-solver.status_oct2026: Pieces exist (verified floating-point analysis tools, formalized convex-optimization theory in Coq and Isabelle), but no verified SOCP solver has flown (general). Agent formalization of numerical analysis is immature: a June 2026 audit found that compilation-based metrics substantially overstate formalization quality (arXiv 2606.14000).
astro-verified-onboard-solver.why: The flight risk in convex guidance sits less in the convex problem than in the implementation: conditioning, iteration caps, timeouts and floating-point rounding. A solver is roughly 5-20k lines (assumption), the size agent-written proofs can cover in weeks once S2's Mathlib numerics catch-up (2027-29) supplies the analysis library. Output: one reusable certified component for every lander, docking system and collision-avoidance planner.
astro-verified-onboard-solver.strongest_case_small: Embedded solvers are small and tested by millions of Monte Carlo runs; numerical failures in flight are rare; DO-178C-style assurance can be met with testing and coverage without proofs, so programs may not pay to switch.
astro-verified-onboard-solver.signpost: An open-source verified SOCP or interior-point solver with floating-point error bounds released by a lab or formal-methods group (NASA Formal Methods 2027/2028 or CAV).

astro-global-optimality-certificates.title: Global optimality certificates
astro-global-optimality-certificates.description: Methods that prove a low-thrust, multi-body or rendezvous trajectory is globally optimal, or within a stated percentage of the best possible, using moment/sum-of-squares relaxations, tight convex relaxations or rigorous branch-and-bound.
astro-global-optimality-certificates.status_oct2026: Active and accelerating: differential-algebra Taylor expansions plus moment-SOS optimization with guaranteed convergence to the global optimum, demonstrated on low-thrust station-keeping in the Earth-Moon CR3BP (Evans, Fossa, Armellin, Henrion, Zanetti, arXiv 2607.15801, Jul 2026); sparse Lasserre hierarchy with GPU ADMM (STROM, arXiv 2406.05846). Scaling to many-revolution low-thrust transfers is open.
astro-global-optimality-certificates.why: Flown low-thrust and multi-body designs are locally optimal from a designer's initial guess; nobody knows the gap to the global optimum. A certificate turns 'best we found' into 'within 0.5% of the best possible' and stops the global search. The open work is cognitive: exploiting sparsity and problem structure to keep the semidefinite programs tractable and proving when relaxations are exact.
astro-global-optimality-certificates.strongest_case_small: SDP size grows combinatorially with relaxation degree and variable count, so certificates may stay limited to short-horizon or low-dimensional problems; the gaps found are typically a few percent of delta-v, which rarely changes what a mission can do.
astro-global-optimality-certificates.signpost: A certified-global (or certified within 1%) solution to a GTOC-class or many-revolution low-thrust problem published by 2028.

astro-nongaussian-uq-certified.title: Certified collision-probability math
astro-nongaussian-uq-certified.description: Fast methods that propagate orbit uncertainty that has become non-Gaussian (curved, skewed, multimodal) and compute probability of collision (Pc) with rigorous error bounds, replacing the 2D Gaussian Pc shortcut where it fails.
astro-nongaussian-uq-certified.status_oct2026: NASA CARA uses 2D Pc as the main risk input and brute-force Monte Carlo where 2D Pc is unreliable, and notes that Gaussian assumptions suppress the true non-Gaussian structure of position uncertainty. Differential-algebra, Gaussian-mixture and equinoctial-sampling methods exist without certified error bounds at catalog scale. Catalog 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, T3) is a weak link: orbit-state posteriors are generally not log-concave.
astro-nongaussian-uq-certified.premise_tier: n/a (139 is T3 and not load-bearing)
astro-nongaussian-uq-certified.why: Starlink executed 148,696 avoidance maneuvers Jun-Nov 2025 and 207,152 Dec 2025-May 2026 (over 40 per satellite per year) at a Pc threshold of 3e-7, 100x stricter than the 1e-4 norm. Part of that conservatism is uncertainty about the uncertainty. Certified Pc bounds let operators replace margin-on-margin with a provable bound. Illustrative, not sourced: if conjunction Pc values spread roughly evenly across decades, a defensible move from 3e-7 to 1e-5 would remove on the order of 2-5x of maneuvers.
astro-nongaussian-uq-certified.strongest_case_small: Pc error is dominated by input covariance realism (drag, unannounced maneuvers, sensor biases), not by the propagation method; a perfectly computed Pc from a wrong covariance is still wrong. Operators may keep strict thresholds for reputational and regulatory reasons regardless.
astro-nongaussian-uq-certified.signpost: CARA, ESA CREAM or a commercial SSA provider adopting a bounded-error non-Gaussian Pc method in operational software by 2028.

astro-coordination-protocols.title: Provably safe maneuver-coordination rules
astro-coordination-protocols.description: Coordination protocols for independently operated autonomous fleets (right-of-way rules, maneuver-intent exchange, behaviour under communication loss) with machine-checked proofs that compliant fleets never maneuver into each other, plus game-theoretic analysis of non-cooperating operators.
astro-coordination-protocols.status_oct2026: No standard exists. Starlink is autonomous within its own fleet; on Dec 9, 2025 a payload from a Chinese Kinetica-1 launch passed about 200 m from Starlink-6079 with no coordination or ephemeris sharing. TraCSS screens (52 pilot users plus UK and Australia accounts, about 11,125 satellites, Jun 2026) but does not arbitrate. Catalog 104 (quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games, T3) is a weak, theory-level link to synthesizing strategies for game models of such protocols.
astro-coordination-protocols.premise_tier: n/a (104 is T3 and not load-bearing)
astro-coordination-protocols.why: This is aviation's TCAS problem in orbit, and TCAS logic took years of formal analysis to trust. Multi-agent protocols with timing, message loss and asymmetric information are a natural target for agent-written proofs, which removes the expert-cost barrier. With about 13-14k active satellites today and filings for roughly 200k (China, Dec 2025) and up to 1 million (SpaceX orbital data centers, Jan 2026), pairwise human coordination cannot scale.
astro-coordination-protocols.strongest_case_small: The binding problem is political and commercial (US-China data sharing, ITU, liability), not proof; a proven protocol nobody adopts is worthless, and bilateral API coordination between Western operators already works without proofs.
astro-coordination-protocols.signpost: A CCSDS, ISO or CONFERS draft standard for machine-readable maneuver intent that includes a formal-verification annex, by 2028.

astro-cislunar-od-uq.title: Cislunar tracking in chaotic dynamics
astro-cislunar-od-uq.description: Orbit determination, initial orbit determination, sensor tasking and uncertainty propagation for non-Keplerian cislunar orbits (NRHO, DRO, L1/L2 halos, transfers) from sparse optical data, with proven consistency and custody guarantees.
astro-cislunar-od-uq.status_oct2026: Earth-centric surveillance networks are not designed for cislunar space, and three-body dynamics make uncertainty dominate performance; more than 30 lunar missions are planned 2024-2030. AFRL's Oracle-Prime spacecraft passed a major milestone (Apr 2026), with delivery in 2026 and launch sought for 2027. NASA cancelled the Gateway station on Mar 24, 2026, removing the main planned NRHO traffic node.
astro-cislunar-od-uq.why: Method development is cognitive and the expert community is small, so P1 is a large multiplier; but cislunar objects are faint and few sensors see them, so performance is capped by data. The math advance mainly lets a sparse sensor set keep custody with fewer observations.
astro-cislunar-od-uq.strongest_case_small: Cislunar object counts stay in the tens through 2031, so manual analyst attention suffices; with Gateway cancelled, NRHO congestion is no longer a near-term driver.
astro-cislunar-od-uq.signpost: Oracle-Prime launch (2027) and published custody performance; a Space Force or commercial cislunar object catalog.

astro-nav-filter-guarantees.title: Navigation filters with proven error bounds
astro-nav-filter-guarantees.description: Estimators for autonomous navigation (optical and terrain-relative, X-ray pulsar, GNSS at lunar distance, crosslink ranging) with machine-checked consistency and integrity bounds (protection levels), including non-Gaussian and sensor-fault cases.
astro-nav-filter-guarantees.status_oct2026: EKF/UKF variants dominate, tuned by experts; integrity frameworks are mature for aviation GNSS but not for lunar PNT. LuGRE tracked GPS and Galileo and obtained a navigation fix on the lunar surface (Mar 3, 2025); NASA's SEXTANT demonstrated real-time X-ray pulsar navigation (general). Catalog 140 (memory-sample lower bounds for noiseless Gaussian regression, T3) is a ceiling result (P3) for streaming estimation on memory-limited processors; 139 (T3) helps only where posteriors are log-concave.
astro-nav-filter-guarantees.premise_tier: T3 for the catalog pieces (140, 139); n/a for the main chain
astro-nav-filter-guarantees.why: Lunar PNT (Moonlight initial services end-2028, LunaNet interoperability tests 2029) needs integrity guarantees like aviation GNSS has. Proving filter consistency and fault detection under weak-signal geometry is bespoke applied math that on-demand capability makes routine.
astro-nav-filter-guarantees.strongest_case_small: Navigation accuracy is set by sensors and clocks (weak GNSS signals at lunar distance, pulsar photon counts giving kilometre-class XNAV fixes), not by filter proofs; proofs add assurance, not accuracy.
astro-nav-filter-guarantees.signpost: LunaNet or Moonlight integrity requirements specifying formally verified protection-level algorithms.

astro-hybrid-rpo-verification.title: Verified docking and capture logic
astro-hybrid-rpo-verification.description: Reachability and barrier-certificate proofs for rendezvous, proximity operations, docking and debris capture that cover mode switches, contact, sensor dropouts and learned (neural) controllers under runtime assurance.
astro-hybrid-rpo-verification.status_oct2026: Neural-network-controlled spacecraft docking under Clohessy-Wiltshire dynamics is a standard verification benchmark (ARCH-COMP); scalable branch-and-bound verification of nonlinear neural feedback systems appeared in Sep 2026 (arXiv 2609.16298); AFRL flew neural-network attitude control of a satellite bus with watchdog and guardrail runtime assurance in shadow mode (Jul 28, 2026). NASA's revised Artemis III (2027) is a low-Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test of Orion with the lander.
astro-hybrid-rpo-verification.why: Hybrid verification is limited by state explosion and by the scarcity of people who can construct barrier certificates and decompositions; AI-generated certificates checked by a kernel are a near-ideal fit. It is also the route by which learned controllers, already flying under runtime assurance, gain static guarantees.
astro-hybrid-rpo-verification.strongest_case_small: Contact dynamics (friction, compliance, plume impingement, capture-mechanism behaviour) is the uncertain part; a proof over an unvalidated contact model gives false confidence, and air-bearing and robotic hardware-in-the-loop tests remain the qualifying evidence.
astro-hybrid-rpo-verification.signpost: A servicing or debris-removal operator (Astroscale, ClearSpace, Starfish) citing formal reachability proofs in a mission safety review.

astro-thermosphere-drag-uq.title: Storm-proof drag forecasts
astro-thermosphere-drag-uq.description: Physics-plus-data models of upper-atmosphere density and its uncertainty that keep LEO orbit predictions and covariances realistic through geomagnetic storms.
astro-thermosphere-drag-uq.status_oct2026: Drag is the largest LEO prediction uncertainty. In the May 2024 Gannon storm LEO objects sank about 180 m per day, thousands of satellites maneuvered at once and collision prediction was degraded for days (Parker and Linares, arXiv 2406.08617). Consider-parameter methods fail to represent stochastic drag (UC3M work). Starlink is lowering its ~550 km shells to ~480 km during 2026, raising drag sensitivity.
astro-thermosphere-drag-uq.why: AI can build better reduced-order density models and calibrated uncertainty (data assimilation with guarantees), the input that certified Pc needs. But density is sparsely measured and storm drivers (coronal-mass-ejection arrival time and magnetic orientation) are forecast at most a day or two ahead, so model gains saturate on observations. S3 gains a year through autonomous analysis of existing data, not through new physics.
astro-thermosphere-drag-uq.strongest_case_small: The binding constraints are solar-wind forecasting and in-situ density data; neither moves with math. More satellites flying lower increases exposure faster than models improve.
astro-thermosphere-drag-uq.signpost: The next G4-G5 storm: whether conjunction screening again degrades for days as in May 2024.

astro-debris-evolution-models.title: Kessler-threshold models with error bars
astro-debris-evolution-models.description: Long-term debris-environment models (source-sink and Monte Carlo) with proven stability thresholds (when runaway collisional growth starts) and honest uncertainty from fragmentation physics and compliance assumptions.
astro-debris-evolution-models.status_oct2026: MIT MOCAT (source-sink plus Monte Carlo, open-source pySSEM 2025) uses equilibrium stability as a capacity measure. ESA's 2026 report: more than 40,000 catalogued objects, about 54,000 larger than 10 cm and 1.2 million between 1 and 10 cm; LEO collision risk up 20% since 2024. The CRASH Clock (time to a likely collision if all maneuvering stopped) moved from 2.8 days in its Dec 2025 preprint to 5.5 days (vs 164 days in 2018) in the Jan 2026 revision, showing how assumption-sensitive headline metrics are.
astro-debris-evolution-models.why: Regulators face a SpaceX application for up to 1 million satellites (filed Jan 30, 2026) and roughly 200k Chinese ITU filings (Dec 2025); capacity questions need defensible math. Stability thresholds of source-sink ODE systems and their sensitivity are tractable applied math (P1); results reach practice as confidence about where the cliff is (P5). Band refers to the models existing with proofs and quantified uncertainty; the uncertainty band itself stays wide.
astro-debris-evolution-models.strongest_case_small: Outputs are dominated by inputs no theorem fixes: future launch rates, disposal compliance and fragment distributions drawn from a handful of hypervelocity tests. Estimates will span an order of magnitude regardless; Mach33's Oct 2025 analysis put a risk-based carrying capacity near 2.9 million objects, far above today's population.
astro-debris-evolution-models.signpost: An IADC-, FCC- or ESA-cited capacity study with proven thresholds and published sensitivity bands by 2028.

astro-certified-gnc-toolchain.title: Proof-carrying GNC software toolchain
astro-certified-gnc-toolchain.description: An engineering pipeline in which engineers write formal requirements and AI agents produce guidance, navigation, attitude-control and collision-avoidance code together with machine-checked proofs of stability, constraint satisfaction, timing and floating-point error bounds.
astro-certified-gnc-toolchain.status_oct2026: NASA's FRET-to-Copilot chain turns structured requirements into runtime monitors; DO-333 gives aviation certification credit for formal methods; DARPA PROVERS (Collins) applies formal methods to autonomous air vehicles. Lean and agent workflows are not qualified tools, and no AI-produced proof is part of any flight-software safety case (general).
astro-certified-gnc-toolchain.why: Verification and validation commonly consume around half of flight-software cost (general). Formal methods were limited by expert cost, not tools (analyst position b); the openai/math pipeline formalized the main results of 162 papers in weeks. Applied to GNC modules, proof cost per function falls from expert-weeks to agent-hours, putting verified GNC within reach of smallsat and startup teams, not only NASA.
astro-certified-gnc-toolchain.strongest_case_small: Specifications become the bottleneck: a proof of the wrong property is worthless, and the June 2026 audit showed kernel-accepted formalizations with weakened hypotheses; the same failure in specifications would give false assurance at scale.
astro-certified-gnc-toolchain.signpost: A NASA center, ESA or a major prime publishing a GNC module delivered with agent-written machine-checked proofs (NASA Formal Methods 2027 or 2028).

astro-trajectory-design-on-demand.title: Trajectory design on demand
astro-trajectory-design-on-demand.description: AI agents that take a mission description in plain language and return verified low-thrust, multi-body or low-energy trajectories (ballistic lunar transfers, manifold transfers, gravity-assist tours), with optimality certificates where available, in hours instead of the weeks to months of expert time typical today.
astro-trajectory-design-on-demand.status_oct2026: Emerging before the release: HELIOS (arXiv 2607.24051, Jul 27, 2026) has an LLM derive Pontryagin conditions, check them symbolically, generate C++ shooting code and solve, compiling 11 of 11 scenarios from 8 to 48 variables. A GTOC 12 study (arXiv 2602.03630, Feb 2026) found strategic scores nearly doubled in two years (9.3 to 17.2 of 26) but agents failed on units, boundary conditions and debugging loops.
astro-trajectory-design-on-demand.why: Trajectory design is solved in principle but expert-scarce (analyst position a): perhaps a few hundred specialists worldwide design multi-body low-thrust transfers (general). The GTOC 12 failure modes are exactly what stronger reasoning plus verification removes. Low-energy designs matter for small lunar missions: published work finds ballistic-transfer entries saving about 59 m/s over the best previously known transfers. Certificates (astro-global-optimality-certificates) strengthen but do not gate this node.
astro-trajectory-design-on-demand.strongest_case_small: Trajectory design is perhaps 1-3% of mission cost (general); heritage tools (GMAT, MONTE, Copernicus, EMTG) already automate much of it; gains are speed and access for small teams, and delta-v gains of a few percent rarely change what a mission can do.
astro-trajectory-design-on-demand.signpost: An AI agent placing top-3 in a GTOC with minimal human input, 2027-28; NASA or ESA flight-dynamics groups publishing agent-in-the-loop design workflows.

astro-catalog-scale-screening.title: Certified screening for a million objects
astro-catalog-scale-screening.description: Conjunction screening and risk software whose filters are proven never to discard a conjunction above threshold (under stated covariance assumptions), whose code is formally verified, and which scales to 100k to 1 million objects plus operator ephemerides.
astro-catalog-scale-screening.status_oct2026: Screening runs on Space Force and commercial catalogs of roughly 35,000-40,000 tracked objects; TraCSS added on-demand bulk ephemeris screening for constellations (May 2025) and is onboarding operators, but the FY2027 request cuts the Office of Space Commerce from $52.5M to $11M.
astro-catalog-scale-screening.why: Filter soundness (apogee-perigee, orbit-path and time filters) is a classic formal-methods target, and false negatives are a known risk class. The catalog will grow severalfold as sensors improve and constellations deploy (Starlink above 10,900; Amazon Leo in the hundreds; Guowang and Qianfan each planned above 10,000; orbital-compute fleets filed). Compute is not binding; trust in completeness is.
astro-catalog-scale-screening.strongest_case_small: Screening already works at 40,000 objects; missed conjunctions come from untracked objects and poor covariances, not filter bugs, so verified screening mostly certifies what already works.
astro-catalog-scale-screening.signpost: TraCSS, ESA or a commercial SSA firm publishing formal soundness proofs for its screening filters; the FY2027 Office of Space Commerce appropriation outcome.

astro-landing-guidance-proven-flight.title: Proven landing guidance flies
astro-landing-guidance-proven-flight.description: A powered-descent or docking guidance system whose convergence, feasibility and solver numerics are machine-checked, not only Monte Carlo-tested, flies on a lunar lander, a vertical-landing test vehicle or an RPO demonstrator.
astro-landing-guidance-proven-flight.status_oct2026: Convex and SCP guidance fly operationally without full proofs. NASA reshaped Artemis in Mar 2026: Artemis III in 2027 becomes a low-Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test with the lander, with crewed landings targeted for 2028. CLPS landers fly several times a year.
astro-landing-guidance-proven-flight.why: Once a verified solver and toolchain exist (S2 2028), flight requires integration, software freeze and 12-24 months of test campaigns (general) plus a vehicle on the manifest. Cheapest first demos: terrestrial vertical-landing testbeds and smallsat RPO. Illustrative value: proven feasibility could let designers trim divert-propellant reserves, typically a few percent of descent propellant.
astro-landing-guidance-proven-flight.strongest_case_small: Flight teams trust Monte Carlo; adding proofs adds schedule risk; the first crewed landings use software frozen in 2026-27, so proven guidance reaches crewed landers no earlier than the 2030s.
astro-landing-guidance-proven-flight.signpost: A CLPS provider, university hopper or RPO demonstrator announcing guidance flight software with machine-checked convergence and numerics proofs.

astro-autonomous-nav-demo.title: Earth-independent nav with certified integrity
astro-autonomous-nav-demo.description: Flight demonstration of autonomous cislunar or deep-space navigation (optical, pulsar, lunar GNSS or LunaNet signals) whose filter carries machine-checked integrity bounds.
astro-autonomous-nav-demo.status_oct2026: ESA Moonlight: Lunar Pathfinder relay in a lunar frozen orbit from 2026, initial navigation services end-2028, interoperability tests 2029, full operations 2030. LuGRE proved GNSS fixes at the Moon (2025).
astro-autonomous-nav-demo.why: Navigation demos fly on their own schedule; the AI-math contribution is certified integrity in the filter, cheap in S2 by 2028. The first natural opportunity is the 2029 Moonlight/LunaNet interoperability campaign. S3 cannot beat the launch manifest, so S2 and S3 share a year.
astro-autonomous-nav-demo.strongest_case_small: Navigation programs may not prioritize formal integrity proofs; demos succeed or fail on sensor and clock hardware.
astro-autonomous-nav-demo.signpost: Moonlight or NASA lunar PNT program documents calling for formally verified integrity algorithms.

astro-verified-rpo-servicing.title: Servicing with a proven safety envelope
astro-verified-rpo-servicing.description: An autonomous servicing, inspection or debris-capture mission whose safety case includes formally verified keep-out zones, abort reachability and capture logic.
astro-verified-rpo-servicing.status_oct2026: Commercial servicing and debris-removal demonstrations are under way (general); ESA's CREAM programme is preparing in-orbit autonomous collision-avoidance demos; none uses formal proofs as primary safety evidence (general).
astro-verified-rpo-servicing.why: Proximity operations are where autonomy risk is highest and where verified hybrid logic is most valuable. Missions take 2-4 years from contract to launch (general), so proofs ready in 2028 meet a 2030 flight.
astro-verified-rpo-servicing.strongest_case_small: Mission safety reviews already accept test-based evidence; contact-model uncertainty limits what proofs certify.
astro-verified-rpo-servicing.signpost: A servicing mission (Astroscale, ClearSpace, Starfish or a government demonstrator) publishing a safety case built on formal verification.

astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.title: Missions fly AI-designed trajectories
astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.description: A lunar, cislunar or deep-space mission whose baseline trajectory and contingency set were produced primarily by an AI design agent and verified by the flight-dynamics team.
astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.why: Designs freeze 6-18 months before launch (general), and there are many small lunar and cislunar missions (more than 30 planned 2024-2030); if agents are trusted by 2027 (S2), a 2028 launch can fly one. S3 cannot compress the manifest, so it matches S2.
astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.strongest_case_small: Attribution: flight-dynamics teams re-optimize in heritage tools, so the 'AI-designed' label may be cosmetic and the delta-v or time benefit marginal.
astro-ai-designed-trajectory-flown.signpost: A mission press kit or AAS/AIAA paper crediting an AI agent for the baseline trajectory.

astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.title: Proof-backed GNC in operational spacecraft
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.description: Operational uncrewed spacecraft (constellation satellites, landers, servicers) run GNC or collision-avoidance software whose safety case relies materially on AI-produced machine-checked proofs.
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.status_oct2026: None known. Formal methods in space flight software remain niche (NASA research programs, some ESA work). Commercial operators update fleet software frequently without regulator review of the code (general).
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.why: Uncrewed commercial systems need no tool qualification, so adoption is a cost decision: if proofs cut V&V cost and shorten update cycles, software-defined fleets adopt first. This precedes crewed certification by years.
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.strongest_case_small: Testing culture is entrenched and works; one high-profile incident with a 'proven' but mis-specified module could stall adoption.
astro-proof-backed-flight-software-ops.signpost: An operator or prime stating publicly that flight GNC or collision-avoidance code ships with machine-checked proofs.

astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.title: Autonomous cross-operator collision avoidance
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.description: Satellites of different operators (Starlink, Amazon Leo, OneWeb, Guowang, Qianfan, orbital-compute fleets) detect, negotiate and execute avoidance maneuvers autonomously under a shared protocol with formal safety guarantees, at 50,000-100,000-plus active satellites.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.status_oct2026: Starlink is autonomous within its own fleet; ESA CREAM's AutoCA and AutoSTM components are in pilot use with in-orbit demos being prepared; cross-operator coordination is manual or bilateral; there is no US-China ephemeris sharing (Kinetica-1 near-miss, Dec 2025). Five moderate-to-high-risk Starlink conjunctions clustered on Aug 9-13, 2026, one reported at 24% Pc.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.why: The verification math is ready around 2028 in S2. Standards (CCSDS or ISO, typically 3-5 years, general), license conditions (FCC) and software rollout set the date; among US and European operators 2030 is plausible. Inclusion of Chinese constellations is a geopolitical gate the math cannot move. Capped at Medium because it needs regulator and standards acceptance.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.strongest_case_small: Bilateral automation between Western operators will arrive without formal guarantees and will handle most of the risk; proofs add assurance, not capability.
astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.signpost: A public automated maneuver-coordination agreement between two megaconstellation operators; an FCC license condition requiring machine-readable maneuver intent.

astro-cislunar-traffic-management.title: Cislunar traffic management service
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.description: An operational catalog, conjunction-screening and coordination service for cislunar space (low lunar orbit, NRHO, DRO, transfers, Earth-Moon L1/L2), comparable to TraCSS for LEO.
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.status_oct2026: None operational. Gateway cancelled (Mar 24, 2026) in favour of a roughly $20B lunar surface base over seven years; Moonlight relay and navigation services 2028-2030; Oracle-Prime demonstration launch sought for 2027.
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.why: Algorithms are ready by 2028-29 in S2; space-based cislunar sensors and a funded operator are the gates, and US civil SSA funding is under pressure (Office of Space Commerce FY2027 request down about 80%). A basic military or commercial service is plausible by 2031.
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.strongest_case_small: Cislunar traffic remains tens of objects; demand for a formal service may lag the capability; Gateway's cancellation removes the most congested planned orbit.
astro-cislunar-traffic-management.signpost: A Space Force, NASA or commercial announcement of a cislunar catalog or screening service; extension of TraCSS-like screening beyond GEO.

astro-human-rated-proof-credit.title: AI proofs accepted for crewed GNC
astro-human-rated-proof-credit.description: NASA human-rating, FAA commercial human-spaceflight rules or ECSS accept AI-produced machine-checked proofs as certification evidence for crew-critical GNC (landing, docking, abort).
astro-human-rated-proof-credit.status_oct2026: Aviation's DO-333 gives formal-methods credit, but Lean and agent workflows are unqualified tools; there is no precedent for AI-generated certification evidence in human spaceflight (general). The first crewed Artemis landings (targeted 2028) will use software frozen before such evidence exists.
astro-human-rated-proof-credit.why: Certification regimes move on their own clock: formal-methods credit in aviation took years after DO-333 (2011) to become routine (general). Even in S3, human-rating requires flight heritage of the uncrewed version and qualified tooling, so the physical and institutional clock binds.
astro-human-rated-proof-credit.strongest_case_small: Crewed GNC is a small share of flight software and already has a strong safety record; the gain is cheaper assurance, not safer missions.
astro-human-rated-proof-credit.signpost: NASA or FAA guidance (a technical-standard update or advisory-circular draft) addressing AI-generated formal evidence.

astro-leo-safety-at-scale.title: LEO stays safe at 100k satellites
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.description: Collision risk and avoidance-maneuver burden per satellite stop rising, and begin to fall, while the active LEO population grows 3-10x toward 50,000-100,000-plus.
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.status_oct2026: Maneuvers per Starlink satellite rose to more than 40 per year (Jun 2025-May 2026), with yearly totals more than 3x 2024; ESA puts LEO collision risk up 20% since 2024; close approaches under 1 km occur every 22 minutes in the 550 km Starlink shell (Thiele et al.).
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.why: AI math contributes three levers: certified Pc (fewer false alarms), verified coordination (no maneuver-into-each-other events) and better capacity models. But the dominant residual risk is about 1.2 million untracked 1-10 cm fragments that no math can see, plus drag-forecast limits and non-cooperating operators. The physical gate (sensors that track smaller objects, and their deployment) binds, so even S2 does not deliver this by 2031.
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.strongest_case_small: Most per-satellite risk reduction will come from non-math moves already under way: lower altitudes (Starlink 550 to 480 km, cutting ballistic decay time by over 80% at solar minimum), five-year disposal rules and better sensors.
astro-leo-safety-at-scale.signpost: Starlink semiannual reports showing maneuvers per satellite flat or falling while the fleet grows; ESA's 2027-28 environment reports showing LEO risk growth slowing.

astro-capacity-licensing.title: Capacity-based orbital licensing
astro-capacity-licensing.description: Regulators (FCC, national agencies, eventually ITU) license megaconstellations against an aggregate, model-based orbital capacity or risk budget, using verifiable debris-evolution and conjunction models.
astro-capacity-licensing.status_oct2026: The FCC has a five-year post-mission disposal rule (2022) but no aggregate capacity regime; the FCC Space Bureau accepted SpaceX's up-to-1-million-satellite orbital data center application for filing in Feb 2026; China filed for roughly 200k satellites at the ITU (Dec 2025).
astro-capacity-licensing.why: Filings at the million-satellite scale force a capacity framework this decade regardless of AI. AI math changes whether the framework rests on defensible, auditable models (proven thresholds, verified screening) or on rules of thumb. Rulemaking (notice, comment, order) takes 2-4 years (general). Capped at Medium.
astro-capacity-licensing.strongest_case_small: Policy will be set by politics and spectrum economics; regulators can adopt simple per-operator rules without sophisticated models.
astro-capacity-licensing.signpost: An FCC notice of proposed rulemaking or license condition using an aggregate collision-risk or capacity metric, triggered by the 1-million-satellite application.

astro-gnc-assurance-cost.title: Verified autonomy becomes cheap
astro-gnc-assurance-cost.description: At early adopters, the cost and calendar time of verifying GNC and autonomy software fall by half or more, making formally assured autonomy standard for smallsats and commercial landers rather than a NASA-only luxury.
astro-gnc-assurance-cost.status_oct2026: Formal methods are confined to a few high-value programs (general).
astro-gnc-assurance-cost.why: If V&V is roughly half of flight-software cost (general) and agent-written proofs replace a substantial share of test-based evidence for GNC modules, early adopters could halve assurance cost. Commercial uncrewed fleets realize it first; regulated crewed programs last.
astro-gnc-assurance-cost.strongest_case_small: Proofs add new costs (specification writing and review, independent checking); hardware test campaigns remain; net savings could be modest.
astro-gnc-assurance-cost.signpost: Published cost data from an operator or NASA program comparing proof-based versus test-based assurance for a GNC module.

auton-mass-action-permanence.title: Reaction networks that never lose a species
auton-mass-action-permanence.description: Family 149 claims the permanence (boundedness plus persistence) conjecture for every finite weakly reversible mass-action reaction network: all concentrations stay between epsilon and 1/epsilon forever, whatever the positive rate constants. Once independently confirmed it becomes a theorem-level guarantee for idealized closed chemical and microbial loop models.
auton-mass-action-permanence.status_oct2026: Family 149, T1 per the release overview and the analyst catalog (no entry in lean/formalization.yaml). Newer detail found in the repo: lean/docs/149.md describes a Lean formalization of global boundedness and persistence with a Comparator statement (ComparatorChallenges/MassAction.lean). If that holds up it would be T3 for the formal part. No outside Comparator run reported as of 2026-10-07; repo has a single commit (Oct 6).
auton-mass-action-permanence.why: Persistence and permanence of weakly reversible networks sit at the core of chemical reaction network theory (the global attractor conjecture family, open for decades, general). 'Achieved' here means independently checked (Comparator run plus statement audit) or reconstructed by CRN theorists. Because a formal statement already exists, verification is a checking task, not a research task; under S2/S3 checking bandwidth is abundant. Under S1 the field is niche and may not be prioritized by volunteer checkers, hence Medium.
auton-mass-action-permanence.strongest_case_small: Real life-support loops are not closed weakly reversible mass-action systems: they include harvesting, control inputs, light-limited and saturating kinetics (Monod, Michaelis-Menten), growth and death, contamination and small-population noise. The epsilon in the theorem depends on network, rates and initial state and may be numerically useless. The result raises confidence in a modeling idealization, not in any habitat.
auton-mass-action-permanence.signpost: An independent Comparator run on MassAction.lean posted to Hexagon or by a recognized checker (Buzzard, Tao, Mathlib maintainers), plus reuse by CRN theorists within 12 months.

auton-contact-wellposedness.title: Rigorous theory of frictional contact
auton-contact-wellposedness.description: Existence, uniqueness or explicit selection rules for rigid and near-rigid bodies with many frictional contacts and impacts (the Painleve paradox regime), plus convergence proofs and rates for the time-stepping schemes that robot simulators actually use. This is the mathematics under every grasp, docking latch, connector mate, wheel-soil contact and assembly simulation.
auton-contact-wellposedness.status_oct2026: Open (general). Rigid-body Coulomb friction can admit no solution or many; measure-differential-inclusion time-stepping schemes (Stewart-Trinkle, Anitescu-Potra) converge only in weak senses and without practical rates. No catalog family addresses it. The pattern is the same as family 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness): an equation that does not by itself pin down the physics, so a selection principle is needed.
auton-contact-wellposedness.why: Outside teams can pose this only once research-grade math is purchasable (S2: 2027). It is a hard but well-specified applied-analysis problem of the kind the release shows the capability can now reach (cf. the forced Navier-Stokes blowup claim of Sep 2026 and the PDE families). Under S2's 6-9 month doubling of solvable depth, a convergence theorem for at least one widely used regularization with computable rates is plausible by 2028. A negative result (nonuniqueness in configurations robots actually hit) would be equally useful: it tells simulator developers where results are artifacts of the chosen regularization.
auton-contact-wellposedness.strongest_case_small: Practitioners already get usable results from compliant contact tuned to test data; the residual sim-to-real gap in grasping and assembly is dominated by unknown parameters (friction coefficients, dust adhesion, cable stiffness), which a theorem about idealized Coulomb friction does not touch.
auton-contact-wellposedness.signpost: An AI-produced paper resolving a named contact-mechanics question (convergence with rates for a mainstream time-stepping scheme, or classification of Painleve non-uniqueness) accepted in an applied-math or mechanics venue, or formalized in Lean, by end-2028.

auton-granular-wellposedness.title: Well-posed equations for flowing regolith
auton-granular-wellposedness.description: Prove well-posedness (or pinpoint ill-posedness and its minimal regularization) for continuum models of dense granular flow such as mu(I) rheology and nonlocal granular-fluidity models, so excavation, conveying, berm-building and plume-cratering codes converge under mesh refinement for physical reasons rather than tuned numerics.
auton-granular-wellposedness.status_oct2026: Open (general). mu(I) rheology is known to be ill-posed at low and high inertial numbers (Barker et al., J. Fluid Mech. 2015, general); nonlocal models exist without a global well-posedness theory. No catalog family addresses granular media.
auton-granular-wellposedness.why: Regolith handling is simulated today with DEM (10^6-10^8 particles, days to weeks per design point, general) or with continuum/MPM codes built on rheologies that are not well-posed. A proven-convergent continuum model would make design sweeps 100-1,000x cheaper than DEM (general estimate) and trustworthy under refinement, feeding excavation and sintering design. Under S2 this is an AI-applied-math problem of 2028-29 difficulty; S3 a year earlier.
auton-granular-wellposedness.strongest_case_small: Engineers already regularize empirically and DEM is adequate for bucket-scale design. The 52x spread in excavation energy across plausible polar ice forms dwarfs any modeling error a theorem removes.
auton-granular-wellposedness.signpost: An AI-produced well-posedness or ill-posedness theorem for a named granular rheology, then adoption of the selected model in an open-source MPM or continuum granular code.

auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.title: Correct-by-construction mission planners
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.description: Planners, schedulers and fault responses generated automatically from temporal-logic specifications (reactive synthesis, energy/mean-payoff games, probabilistic model checking) at the scale of real surface operations, each shipped with a proof that the plan meets the spec under the modeled environment.
