auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.status_oct2026: Theory mature, flight use rare: synthesis works for small specs, but abstractions (terrain, energy, comm windows) and specs are built by scarce experts (general). Family 104 (T3, Lean in repo, unchecked) gives quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff and turn-based stochastic games; the formalized part is a randomized quasipolynomial algorithm for mean-payoff games. Mean-payoff ('energy') objectives match battery-constrained rovers.
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.why: The cost of synthesis is building a sound abstraction and a correct spec, which is exactly bespoke expert math. An agent that proposes the abstraction, proves it sound, writes the spec, synthesizes the controller and emits Lean or model-checker certificates turns months of formal-methods work into days. 'Achieved' = a synthesized planner for a realistic multi-day surface scenario (energy, thermal, comm windows, faults) with machine-checked certificate, produced with under 10% specialist effort. Family 104 changes the theoretical ceiling for stochastic and mean-payoff games, but practical solvers (Zielonka, strategy iteration) already handle realistic sizes, so its own contribution is P3, small.
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.strongest_case_small: Mission operations culture values human-readable, human-reviewed plans; even the AI-planned Perseverance drives were validated by simulation, not proof. Specs, not proofs, are the hard part, and a proof of the wrong property adds little (analyst position h).
auton-temporal-logic-synthesis.signpost: A CLPS, LTV or NASA surface payload announces spec-to-plan synthesized autonomy in flight software, or ESA/NASA solicitations require correct-by-construction planners.

auton-ops-planning-ceilings.title: Known limits for robot fleet scheduling
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.description: Hardness and optimality results tell surface-ops planners which multi-robot task-allocation, scheduling, partitioning and depot-siting problems can be solved near-optimally and which cannot, so effort moves to problem structure, exact solvers on small instances and heuristics.
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.status_oct2026: 102 Unique Games Conjecture (T3) fixes optimal approximation ratios for many labeling and partitioning problems; 125 metric k-median threshold 1+2/e (T3) bounds depot, charging-pad and relay siting; 124 polynomial-time unit-job scheduling on three identical machines with precedence (T1 per release overview; repo lean/docs/124.md lists a Comparator statement, so possibly T3); 110 optimal randomized k-server (T1) and 111 one-sample matroid prophet inequalities (T1; competitive ratio 2^-310, no polynomial-time implementation asserted) for online dispatch.
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.premise_tier: T3 (102, 125); T1 (124, 110, 111): conditional for those parts
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.why: A lunar base with dozens of robots and crew visits every six months is an online scheduling and allocation problem with precedence constraints. Ceilings act in months: they stop teams chasing general-purpose 'optimal' fleet planners and let them judge vendor claims. 124 is a cute fit for a three-robot team with precedence-constrained unit tasks. The parts resting on 124, 110 and 111 are conditional (T1).
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.strongest_case_small: Real instances are small and structured and are solved well by MILP/CP solvers; worst-case hardness and galactic constants (111's 2^-310) say little about them. Most of these results were already believed; the change is from belief to theorem.
auton-ops-planning-ceilings.signpost: Planning papers or vendor documentation for lunar and Mars operations cite these ceilings when scoping fleet planners; otherwise no measurable change expected.

auton-certified-contact-sim.title: Contact simulators with error bars
auton-certified-contact-sim.description: Physics engines for grasping, latching, digging and assembly that carry proven convergence and computable error bounds for stated friction and compliance parameters, so a simulation run can count as verification evidence instead of a physical test.
auton-certified-contact-sim.status_oct2026: Not available (general): mainstream engines (MuJoCo, Drake, PhysX/Isaac) use different contact regularizations with no certified error bounds. Not addressed by the catalog.
auton-certified-contact-sim.why: Space robotics qualification leans on physical testing in low-fidelity analogs (air-bearing tables, parabolic flights, dirty thermal-vacuum chambers). A certified simulator, validated against a modest set of vacuum and dust experiments, could replace a large share of those tests with analysis. The math is cognitive-clock work under S2; the binding gate is the validation experiments for dusty, cold, vacuum contact.
auton-certified-contact-sim.strongest_case_small: Error bounds will be conditional on parameters measured in the lab; for lunar dust (electrostatic adhesion, cold welding, abrasion) parameter uncertainty dominates and certified numerics only shrink the smaller error term.
auton-certified-contact-sim.signpost: A contact solver released with a formal convergence proof (e.g. inside Drake or MuJoCo), and a NASA ISAM or Moon Base program accepting its results as verification evidence.

auton-ecls-reliability-uq.title: Honest reliability numbers for life support
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.description: System-of-systems reliability, sparing and crew-maintenance models for regenerative life support with Bayesian uncertainty from ISS failure history: the analysis that decides how many tonnes of spares a Mars crew carries and how much crew time maintenance eats.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.status_oct2026: Methods exist (Langley's EMAT, semi-Markov sparing, Bayesian estimation) but scale poorly to system-of-systems; last public ECLSS reliability data release was 2004 (ICES 2025). A 2025 Bayesian study estimates 907 crew-hours of ECLSS maintenance (~45 min/day) and availability 0.9687 for a 1,200-day mission. 'Solved in principle, expert-scarce and data-limited'.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.why: In the 2025 study the 5th-percentile spares mass matches a 10x MTBF improvement, i.e. the uncertainty band spans an order of magnitude in MTBF. A model that uses every ISS failure record, component physics and shelf-life data, with uncertainty propagated end to end, narrows that band; if it halves MTBF uncertainty, spares mass at fixed risk could fall ~20-40% (general estimate). Under S2 this is routine AI applied statistics by 2027, gated by NASA releasing the data.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.strongest_case_small: Thin data cannot be cured by better math; failure data accrue only with operating hours, and ISS, the only large source, retires around 2030-2032 (extension to 2032 proposed). Better UQ may simply confirm the wide band.
auton-ecls-reliability-uq.signpost: NASA publishes an updated ISS ECLSS failure and replacement dataset; Mars architecture studies cite AI-built sparing models.

auton-isru-rom-control.title: Fast, trustworthy models of oxygen reactors
auton-isru-rom-control.description: Reduced-order multiphysics models (electrochemistry, melt flow and heat transfer, gas evolution, composition drift) of molten-regolith electrolysis, carbothermal and solid-oxide reactors, with error bounds, used for model-predictive control, optimal test design and scale-up decisions.
auton-isru-rom-control.status_oct2026: Bespoke per team. LR-1 MRE: 0.07 kg O2/h for 9 h on 25 kg simulant in vacuum (ICES 2026); CaRD solar-carbothermal integrated test completed Feb 2026 (no public rate); MOXIE peak 12 g/h; OxEon MOMS designing for 1-3 kg/h O2 with >65% CO2-to-CH4 conversion and 5,000+ h stack tests. Melt composition, liquidus and viscosity drift during electrolysis (Acta Astronautica 2025).
auton-isru-rom-control.why: Going from 0.07 kg/h to a 10 t/yr plant (~1.1 kg/h continuous at under 30 kW, 2025 systems study) is a ~16x step for MRE; MOXIE to MOMS is ~80-250x. Each build-test cycle costs months; good ROMs plus Bayesian experiment design cut the number of cycles, and MPC handles regolith composition drift. Under S2 this is routine AI applied math by 2028.
auton-isru-rom-control.strongest_case_small: The uncertainty sits in property data at 1,600 C (melt viscosity and conductivity vs composition, anode corrosion), not in model reduction; teams already run COMSOL-class models. Plant performance is capped by hardware life and power, which models do not change.
auton-isru-rom-control.signpost: An ISRU payload flies with model-predictive control built on a published reduced-order model; ICES or Acta Astronautica papers report AI-generated reactor ROMs validated against test data.

auton-granular-regolith-model.title: Validated models of digging icy regolith
auton-granular-regolith-model.description: Calibrated, well-posed continuum-plus-DEM models of excavation, conveying and trafficability for polar regolith, including ice-cemented and vapor-deposited ice forms, predictive enough to size excavators and water-extraction feeders.
auton-granular-regolith-model.status_oct2026: Lab-only. Ice-cemented simulant: excavation energy 2.74 to 143 J/g as ice rises 1 to 12 wt% (52x); pressure-sintered: 0.35 to 0.11 J/g (Space and Planetary Resources, Sep 2026). DEM calibration with realistic particle shapes and agglutinates ongoing (2024-2026). The ice form at the poles is unknown.
auton-granular-regolith-model.why: Without knowing the ice form, excavator power and wear sizing is uncertain by more than 10x. A well-posed model calibrated on lab simulants and then tested blind against the first in-situ polar data (2028) becomes a design basis. S3 cannot beat S2 here because the gate is the ground-truth mission, not cognition.
auton-granular-regolith-model.strongest_case_small: One or two landing sites may not represent the variability across permanently shadowed regions; designers will overbuild regardless, and early ice mining may target easier deposits.
auton-granular-regolith-model.signpost: VIPER or another polar lander returns geotechnical data, and a published model predicts it blind within a factor of two.

auton-mre-anode-materials.title: Anodes that survive molten regolith
auton-mre-anode-materials.description: Discovery and life prediction of inert anode and crucible materials for oxygen-evolving electrolysis of molten regolith at ~1,600 C, the component that limits molten-regolith-electrolysis plant life.
auton-mre-anode-materials.status_oct2026: Active research: iridium anodes (costly), zirconia-based hollow anodes (Acta Astronautica, Jun 2025). Longest reported integrated large-scale run: hours (LR-1, 9 h). Plants need thousands of hours.
auton-mre-anode-materials.why: A 10 t/yr plant with anodes lasting 1,000 h needs ~8 anode swaps a year, each a robotic maintenance operation in a 1,600 C cell; at 10,000 h it needs fewer than one. AI-guided and autonomous-lab materials search (S2/S3) can shortlist compositions quickly, but each candidate still needs a multi-thousand-hour endurance test.
auton-mre-anode-materials.strongest_case_small: Endurance testing is inherently slow (10,000 h is about 14 months per test) and AI cannot compress it; and the carbothermal route avoids the inert-anode problem entirely, so the whole node may be bypassed.
auton-mre-anode-materials.signpost: A continuous MRE run longer than 1,000 h reported; an AI-discovered anode composition published with endurance data.

auton-blss-stability-theory.title: Bioregenerative loops with stability guarantees
auton-blss-stability-theory.description: Multi-compartment models of bioregenerative life support (bacteria, algae, higher plants, crew) with certified stability and recovery margins, and controllers designed against those margins.
auton-blss-stability-theory.status_oct2026: MELiSSA pilot plant has integrated liquid streams of three compartments and prepared gas closure across four (ICES 2025); a 2025 npj Microgravity review flags critical US capability gaps in bioregenerative systems. Family 149 (T1; possible T3 per repo docs) proves permanence for closed weakly reversible mass-action networks, an idealized building block.
auton-blss-stability-theory.premise_tier: T1 (149 part is conditional); main channel is capability
auton-blss-stability-theory.why: Instability (microbial washout, crop failure, CO2/O2 imbalance) is the main operational risk of bioregenerative systems and the reason they carry large physico-chemical backups. Certified stability margins define safe operating envelopes and shrink buffer stocks. 149 contributes only the idealized guarantee that a closed mass-action core cannot lose a species; the real value is AI building validated reduced models and Lyapunov or permanence-type certificates for the controlled loop. The 149-dependent part is conditional (T1).
auton-blss-stability-theory.strongest_case_small: Biology is not mass-action and real failures come from contamination, disease and equipment; validation needs months-to-years closed tests, so the model may only re-describe what operators already manage empirically.
auton-blss-stability-theory.signpost: MELiSSA or a Chinese Lunar Palace successor publishes model-based loop control with stability certificates validated over a multi-month closed run.

auton-radiation-risk-uq.title: Narrower uncertainty on crew radiation risk
auton-radiation-risk-uq.description: Mechanistic radiobiology models (high-LET track structure, non-targeted effects, dose-rate) that shrink the uncertainty on cancer and cardiovascular risk per unit dose for Moon and Mars crews.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.status_oct2026: NASA limit: 600 mSv career effective dose, independent of age and sex. Space Weather (Mar 2026): staying under 600 mSv on a Mars mission requires flying near solar maximum or faster transfers. Tomography review (Jul 2026): recent NASA Space Cancer Risk model revisions and non-targeted-effect scenarios suggest risks may be higher than earlier estimates; uncertainty remains substantial for high-LET radiobiology. Transport models predict dose well (blind Artemis I validation, 2025).
auton-radiation-risk-uq.why: Risk-per-dose uncertainty drives shielding mass and allowed mission duration. Halving it could relax design margins, but that requires new biological data: animal cohorts (years to cancer endpoints), organoid and beam studies at NSRL (limited beam time). S3's autonomous labs could scale in-vitro work, but in-vivo latency is a fixed physical clock.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.strongest_case_small: The 600 mSv limit is a policy choice, not a model output, and is unlikely to move within five years whatever models say; dose physics (not math) sets the mass needed to shield.
auton-radiation-risk-uq.signpost: NASA revises its Space Cancer Risk model with mechanistic components, or changes the 600 mSv standard.

auton-verified-surface-autonomy.title: Proof-carrying autonomy for lunar robots
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.description: Rover, excavator and LTV flight software whose planner, fault responses and safety monitors ship with machine-checked proofs: a synthesized planner plus a runtime-assurance wrapper around learned perception, produced by AI agents at a cost a commercial lunar company can afford.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.status_oct2026: Not flown. CADRE (late 2026, IM-3) demonstrates multi-robot autonomy (leader election, task re-allocation, cooperative mapping) without proofs; Perseverance's AI-planned drives (Dec 2025) used digital-twin checking. LTV awards (May 2026: Astrolab $219M, Lunar Outpost $220M; Pegasus offers manual, autonomous and remote modes).
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.why: Moon Base Phase 1 (up to 30 CLPS landings from 2027) puts many robots on the surface with small operations teams; verification cost per autonomous behavior becomes the binding cost of autonomy. Agents that synthesize and prove planners and wrap learned components in proven monitors collapse that cost. Uncrewed commercial robots need no regulator, so no Medium cap applies; NASA software assurance acceptance is the qualification gate.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.strongest_case_small: Most lunar robot losses so far are hardware and environment (landers tipping, thermal, dust, comms), not logic errors; proofs cover the model, not the Moon.
auton-verified-surface-autonomy.signpost: A CLPS, LTV or NASA payload provider advertises formally verified autonomy with published proof artifacts; NASA's Fly Foundational Robotics mission or CADRE follow-ons adopt them.

auton-earth-independent-fdir.title: Crew-side fault diagnosis without Mission Control
auton-earth-independent-fdir.description: Onboard diagnosis and repair guidance for habitats, life support and crew medicine that a crew 4-24 light-minutes from Earth can trust: model-based reasoning and AI assistants whose conclusions are cross-checked against verified system models.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.status_oct2026: Research prototypes: DARIA/STAMPS anomaly-response architecture (AIAA SciTech, Jan 2026); NASA's progressively Earth-independent medical operations (EIMO) framework names clinical AI as a high-value target (2025); AI-assisted medical diagnostics tests on ISS reported in Mar 2026 (press headline only). ISS relies on ground engineering teams.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.why: Mars crews face light-time delays and blackouts; ECLSS maintenance alone is estimated at ~45 min/day. Faster, trustworthy diagnosis cuts downtime, spares and risk. As an advisory tool (crew decides) it needs adoption, not certification; Gateway's pause (Mar 2026) moves the uncrewed-habitat testbed role to ISS and the Moon base.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.strongest_case_small: Advisory AI is already available; trust, training and procedures, not mathematics, limit adoption, and for the Moon (1.3 s delay) NASA will keep the ground in the loop.
auton-earth-independent-fdir.signpost: NASA flies an onboard diagnostic assistant with a formal cross-check component on ISS or an Artemis landing mission.

auton-excavation-design.title: Design excavators from models, not guesses
auton-excavation-design.description: Model-based sizing and design optimization of excavators, conveyors and ice-processing feeders for polar regolith, replacing much of today's build-and-dig-in-simulant iteration.
auton-excavation-design.status_oct2026: NASA's IPEx is designed to excavate on the order of 20 t of regolith per mission; designs are iterated in simulant test bins. 2026 work on bucket design uses vision-based fill analysis (arXiv 2609.25724).
auton-excavation-design.why: With a validated regolith model, AI multiphysics design optimization can trade bucket geometry, power and wear against the in-situ ice form, avoiding a 10x over- or under-sized machine. The gate is the ground-truth data and model validation, not the optimizer.
auton-excavation-design.strongest_case_small: Excavator mass is a small share of a lunar base; conservative over-design costs little compared with landing slots, so precision design may not change what flies.
auton-excavation-design.signpost: An ISRU excavator or ice-mining payload selected for a 2029-2031 flight with a model-based design report validated against in-situ data.

auton-sinter-process-control.title: Reliable recipes for sintering regolith
auton-sinter-process-control.description: Process windows and closed-loop control for microwave, solar or laser sintering and melting of regolith into landing pads, roads and blast berms, avoiding thermal-stress cracking in lunar thermal extremes.
auton-sinter-process-control.status_oct2026: Multiphysics modeling (Coatings, Feb 2026) finds microwave-sintered bodies crack when cooled faster than ~16 C/min (safe below 15 C/min). Startups pursuing lunar construction: Lunar Forge (Jul 2026), Astroport with Vermeer on autonomous construction machinery (Apr 2026). Plume-surface interaction models that set pad requirements are immature (see prop-psi-models).
auton-sinter-process-control.why: Coupled electromagnetic-thermal-stress models are expert-scarce but well-posed; AI can map process windows across regolith compositions and design controllers that hold cooling rates, cutting the test matrix. Pads matter because landing plumes eject regolith at high speed, a hazard that grows with Starship-class landers.
auton-sinter-process-control.strongest_case_small: Regolith composition and grain size vary by site; vacuum-thermal test facilities are scarce; and on the Moon the binding constraint is kW-to-100s-of-kW power for sintering, not recipes.
auton-sinter-process-control.signpost: A relevant-environment test produces sintered pads that survive a rocket-plume test; a CLPS manifest includes a construction demo.

auton-certified-assembly-skills.title: Robot assembly skills with proven safety envelopes
auton-certified-assembly-skills.description: Learned or optimized manipulation skills (connector mating, truss and solar-array assembly, cable routing, refueling interfaces) wrapped in certified contact simulation and runtime assurance, so qualification can lean on analysis rather than exhaustive physical testing.
auton-certified-assembly-skills.status_oct2026: Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle launched Jul 22, 2026 with two NRL robotic arms and three Mission Extension Pods; NASA's Fly Foundational Robotics mission (Motiv arm, PickNik MoveIt Pro on Space ROS, Feb 2026) targets autonomous and ground-supervised manipulation. Industry calls assembly the ISAM capability 'furthest from reality' (Payload, Apr 2026).
auton-certified-assembly-skills.why: Contact-rich assembly is where learned policies outperform hand-coded ones, but they are hard to qualify. Certified contact simulation provides envelope evidence; runtime assurance keeps the learned policy inside it. The binding gate is validating the envelope in vacuum and microgravity analogs.
auton-certified-assembly-skills.strongest_case_small: Customers buy servicing (inspection, life extension, refueling) with scripted, teleoperated arms; large-scale assembly lacks a paying customer before Starship-era structures, so the technique may wait for demand rather than math.
auton-certified-assembly-skills.signpost: MRV or FFR on-orbit results reporting autonomous contact tasks under a runtime-assurance monitor; a program accepting simulation evidence for a contact task.

auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.title: First measurements of how hard polar ice is to dig
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.description: In-situ geotechnical and volatile data from lunar south-pole regolith (VIPER, CLPS drills, Chang'e-7, LUPEX, Moon Base Phase 1 rovers): the physical data gate for every excavation and water-extraction model.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.status_oct2026: PRIME-1 drill on IM-2 (Mar 2025) returned limited data after the lander tipped over (general). VIPER delivery tasked to Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mk1 (Dec 2025 task order), but the May 28, 2026 New Glenn static-fire explosion destroyed LC-36 ground systems (best-case pad restoration ~15 months per reporting), and NASA is evaluating Falcon Heavy. Moon Base Phase 1 targets up to 30 CLPS landings from 2027.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.why: This node exists to show a gate AI cannot move: the excavation models above cannot be validated until a polar lander digs. Multiple independent attempts (US, China, India/Japan) make data by 2031 likely in every scenario; S2/S3 do not change the date.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.strongest_case_small: Data from one or two sites may not generalize across permanently shadowed regions, leaving models under-constrained even after first contact.
auton-icy-regolith-ground-truth.signpost: Blue Moon Mk1 with VIPER launch date after the LC-36 rebuild; Chang'e-7 or LUPEX polar operations.

auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.title: First oxygen made on the Moon
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.description: A flight demonstration that extracts measurable oxygen (grams to kilograms) from lunar regolith on the surface, by carbothermal reduction, molten-regolith electrolysis or another route.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.status_oct2026: Ground prototypes only: CaRD integrated solar-carbothermal test (Feb 2026), LR-1 MRE (0.07 kg/h, late 2024), Blue Origin Air Pioneer MRE (Jun 2026). NASA's lunar ISRU strategy is a leader/follower sequence of flight demos leading to a pilot plant (NTRS 2025).
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.why: AI-built reactor models and test design can pull flight-unit readiness forward by about a year in S2/S3, but the date is set by CLPS manifests and lander success. Recent CLPS-era landing outcomes have been mixed (several tip-overs and failures, general), so even with many 2027-2031 flights the demo stays Medium.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: The demo would happen on roughly this schedule without AI math; oxygen chemistry from regolith was shown on the ground decades ago, and the bottleneck is a landing slot, power and dust-tolerant hardware.
auton-lunar-o2-flight-demo.signpost: An ISRU oxygen payload manifested on a named 2027-2029 CLPS mission.

auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.title: A lunar robot flies proof-carrying autonomy
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.description: A rover, excavator or LTV operates on the Moon using autonomy software whose planner and safety monitors carry machine-checked proofs.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.status_oct2026: None. CADRE (late 2026) will be the first autonomous multi-robot team on the Moon, without proofs.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.why: Once proof-carrying autonomy is cheap (S2 2028), adoption needs only one willing payload provider and one successful landing; with up to 30 CLPS landings planned from 2027 and LTVs arriving with Artemis IV, several opportunities exist before 2031. In S3 cheap proofs arrive earlier and become a default supplier practice.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.strongest_case_small: Providers may see no customer pull for proofs on uncrewed robots, and landing failures may consume the opportunities.
auton-verified-autonomy-lunar-flight.signpost: A lunar mission press kit or NASA payload description lists formally verified autonomy as a feature.

auton-blss-closed-test.title: Long closed life-support test run by certified control
auton-blss-closed-test.description: A ground test of 180+ days in which a bioregenerative or hybrid life-support loop runs under model-based control with stability certificates, at higher closure (food, O2, water) than prior tests.
auton-blss-closed-test.status_oct2026: Precedent: China's Lunar Palace 1 ran a 370-day crewed closed test in 2017-18 (general); MELiSSA pilot plant progressing toward full loop closure with rat crew mock-up (2025).
auton-blss-closed-test.why: Crop cycles (60-120 days, general) and the need to observe disturbances and recoveries make the test inherently months long; S3 autonomous labs can run more parallel small-scale loops, but a crew-scale test still takes calendar time.
auton-blss-closed-test.strongest_case_small: Funding, not modeling, has limited US bioregenerative work (npj Microgravity 2025); a better controller does not create a test facility.
auton-blss-closed-test.signpost: Announcement of a new long-duration closed-loop campaign (MELiSSA full loop, Lunar Palace successor, or a NASA/commercial analog) citing model-based stability control.

auton-assembly-flight-demo.title: Robotic assembly in space with certified skills
auton-assembly-flight-demo.description: An on-orbit or lunar-surface demonstration of multi-step robotic assembly (structure, array or connector mating) using learned or optimized skills qualified mainly by certified simulation plus runtime assurance.
auton-assembly-flight-demo.status_oct2026: MRV (launched Jul 2026) begins servicing operations; FFR in development; OSAM-1 was cancelled in 2024 (general).
auton-assembly-flight-demo.why: Needs the certified-skills toolchain (S2 2030) and a flight slot; servicing vehicles already on orbit could host a software-upgraded demo, which is why S3 reaches Medium.
auton-assembly-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: No paying assembly customer before Starship-era structures; demonstrations remain government-funded one-offs.
auton-assembly-flight-demo.signpost: MRV or a successor performing an autonomous multi-step contact task beyond grapple-and-dock.

auton-mars-isru-demo.title: Kilogram-per-hour propellant production on Mars
auton-mars-isru-demo.description: A MOMS-class solid-oxide unit (1-3 kg O2/h plus methane) operating on Mars, 80-250x MOXIE's peak rate.
auton-mars-isru-demo.status_oct2026: OxEon MOMS hardware in design (ICES 2026). SpaceX reached orbit with Starship on Flight 14 (Sep 28, 2026); ship-to-ship propellant transfer is expected in early 2027; Musk called a 2026 Mars attempt a 'distraction' (Jan 2026 headline). Remaining Mars departure windows in the horizon: late 2028/early 2029 and early 2031.
auton-mars-isru-demo.why: Only two windows fit in the horizon. Operation by 2031 essentially requires a successful Starship (or other) Mars landing from the 2028-29 window carrying an ISRU unit. AI math cannot add windows, shorten transits or raise landing reliability; S3 equals S2.
auton-mars-isru-demo.strongest_case_small: Everything here is launch, landing and power; the math contribution is a slightly better-tuned reactor.
auton-mars-isru-demo.signpost: SpaceX or NASA announces a 2028 Mars cargo manifest that includes ISRU hardware.

auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.title: AI plans rover operations, machines check the plans
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.description: Routine use of AI agents to plan multi-sol rover traverses and multi-robot surface activities, with automated simulation and formal checks replacing most human plan review.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.status_oct2026: Demonstrated once at Mars: Perseverance's first AI-planned drives on Dec 8 and 10, 2025 (210 m and 246 m; Claude vision-language models used orbital imagery and slope data to lay waypoints), checked via JPL's digital twin across more than 500,000 telemetry variables (JPL, Jan 30, 2026). JPL describes a goal of kilometer-scale drives with minimal operator workload.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.why: This is the capability channel in its purest form: no catalog theorem is involved. Ground operations dominate extended-mission cost, and the Moon Base plan multiplies the number of robots per operator. Formal plan checking (model checking of command sequences against flight rules) makes AI plans acceptable without line-by-line human review.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.strongest_case_small: Already happening without any new mathematics; rover productivity is capped by power, comm passes, hazards and science-team decision time, not planning.
auton-ai-planned-ops-routine.signpost: JPL reports a majority of a rover's drives in a quarter as AI-planned, or a kilometer-scale AI-planned drive; Moon Base robot operators adopt the same workflow.

auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.title: Lunar base runs itself between crew visits
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.description: Robots, LTVs and base systems operate, maintain and resupply lunar base elements autonomously for months between crewed landings, with Earth supervising rather than commanding.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.status_oct2026: NASA's Moon Base plan (Mar 24, 2026): phased build-up, crewed landings initially every six months, Gateway paused in its current form; budget reported at ~$30B with bulk launch buys near (Bloomberg via 33FG, Oct 6, 2026). Artemis III is a 2027 Earth-orbit test; first landing 2028. Lunar Reactor-1 fission system to land in 2030.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.premise_tier: n/a (102 T3, 124 T1 for planning ceilings only)
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.why: Between six-month crew visits a base has months of idle infrastructure that must be maintained (dust, thermal cycling, power management). Cognitive enablers are ready by 2028 in S2; the binding gate is that there must be enough base to operate: power (2030 reactor), habitats and logistics delivered by 2029-2031. Gateway's pause removes the planned uncrewed-habitat autonomy testbed, so the surface base inherits that role.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.strongest_case_small: With a 1.3 s light-time, the Moon can be run by teleoperation and ground scheduling; autonomy is a cost saver, not an enabler, and little base infrastructure will exist by 2031.
auton-crew-optional-lunar-ops.signpost: NASA Moon Base Phase 2 contracts specifying autonomous operations between crewed missions; LTVs operating uncrewed for months after Artemis IV.

auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.title: Tonne-per-year lunar oxygen plant
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.description: An operational lunar oxygen plant producing at least ~1 t/yr toward a 10 t/yr pilot scale, feeding life support and lander propellant.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.status_oct2026: No flight unit. A 2025 systems study sketches 10 t/yr by molten regolith electrolysis at under 30 kW with vertical solar arrays and an excavator.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.why: Needs the flight demo (2028-2030), then a funded pilot plant, tens of kW of continuous power, regolith handling and maintenance robots; the leader/follower demo sequence plus landing cadence puts operations after 2031 except under S3 with everything going right.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.strongest_case_small: Every gate is physical (power, landed mass, funding, hardware life); AI math shaves design time on a path dominated by launch cadence.
auton-lunar-oxygen-ops.signpost: NASA funds an ISRU pilot plant as part of Moon Base Phase 2 with a named delivery date.

auton-closed-loop-habitat.title: Mars-class closed-loop life support, demonstrated
auton-closed-loop-habitat.description: Regenerative ECLSS with at least 98% water recovery, 75%+ oxygen recovery and demonstrated reliability good enough for a ~1,000-day Mars mission, flown on ISS, a commercial station or a lunar habitat.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.status_oct2026: ISS: 98% water recovery (2023); Exploration ECLSS testbed integration on ISS in progress (ICES Jul 2026); ISS extension to 2032 proposed. Oxygen recovery from CO2 on ISS is roughly half (general).
auton-closed-loop-habitat.why: Reliability is demonstrated with operating hours: a zero-failure demonstration of MTBF M at 95% confidence needs about 3M unit-hours (general). For an assembly with a 20,000 h MTBF target that is ~60,000 unit-hours, about 7 unit-years, so parallel units and years of operation are required. AI can design better hardware and tests, but not compress hours; S3's autonomous labs could run many parallel ground units, hence Medium.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.strongest_case_small: The gap is hardware maturity and test time, which math does not touch; ISS retirement may end the only long-duration flight testbed before demonstration completes.
auton-closed-loop-habitat.signpost: Exploration ECLSS units accumulate multi-year ISS run time with published failure data; a commercial station adopts closed-loop O2 recovery.

auton-mars-propellant-plant.title: Starship-scale propellant plant on Mars
auton-mars-propellant-plant.description: Mars ISRU producing on the order of 1,000 t of methane and oxygen per return flight: about 65 kg O2/h over ~500 days, roughly 5,000x MOXIE's peak rate, plus water-ice mining and order-1-MW continuous power (general estimates).
auton-mars-propellant-plant.status_oct2026: No hardware at this scale; MOXIE demonstrated 12 g/h; MOMS targets 1-3 kg/h.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.why: Requires landed megawatt-class power, ice mining and a sub-scale demo first, across 26-month windows. Even a perfect design in 2027 could not be landed, assembled and run at scale before 2031.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.strongest_case_small: This is the case: the effect of AI mathematics on this node inside the horizon is nil.
auton-mars-propellant-plant.signpost: SpaceX discloses a Mars power and ISRU architecture with flight hardware in test.

auton-surface-productivity.title: Ten times more robot work per operator
auton-surface-productivity.description: Useful surface work (km driven, kg excavated, tasks completed) per ground-operator hour rises about tenfold versus 2025 practice, through AI planning, multi-robot coordination and verified autonomy.
auton-surface-productivity.status_oct2026: Baseline: large ground teams plan rover activities daily (general); first AI-planned Mars drives Dec 2025; CADRE multi-robot demo late 2026.
auton-surface-productivity.why: Moon Base Phase 1 cannot be staffed like MER/MSL-era teams per robot; planning automation plus cheap verification removes the operator bottleneck. This is the domain's largest five-year outcome and rests on the capability, not the catalog.
auton-surface-productivity.strongest_case_small: Productivity is bounded by power (two-week nights), comm windows, dust and hardware failures; operator hours may not be the binding constraint for most robots.
auton-surface-productivity.signpost: NASA or a CLPS provider reports operator-hours per km or per tonne excavated falling severalfold across successive missions.

auton-mars-architecture-close.title: Mars outpost logistics cut by a third
auton-mars-architecture-close.description: Validated ISRU, closed-loop life support and robot-first precursors reduce Earth-supplied mass for a first Mars outpost by roughly 30-40%.
auton-mars-architecture-close.status_oct2026: Industry model (33FG, May 2025): a 10-person Mars outpost needs ~152 t of cargo; ISRU is ~40% of cargo cost, life support ~20% of mass, power ~25% of mass; a robot-only precursor cuts ~29% of cost and ~36% of mass but cannot delete ISRU, power and construction.
auton-mars-architecture-close.why: Needs Mars ISRU validated on Mars, Mars-class ECLSS validated in flight and crew-optional operations proven on the Moon, each gated by physical clocks extending to or past 2031.
auton-mars-architecture-close.strongest_case_small: Even under S3, the validation chain runs through Mars windows and reliability hours; design studies can claim the savings earlier, but validated savings arrive after 2031.
auton-mars-architecture-close.signpost: A Mars architecture study from NASA or SpaceX that books ISRU and closure savings against flight-validated data.

cap-research-math-internal.title: Research-grade math inside the labs
cap-research-math-internal.description: Frontier labs' internal models resolve research-level open problems on request, across all of mathematics, at about three hours of compute per result, with agent-written Lean for a large minority of results.
cap-research-math-internal.status_oct2026: Exists. openai/math (Oct 6, 2026): 722 manuscripts, 372 families from ~4,000 posed problems in under four weeks; 127 families carry unchecked agent-written Lean (T3), e.g. 102 Unique Games and 362 relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell. The model was trained from Aug 28, 2026 for about a month. Anthropic (67.2% of zeta zeros on the critical line; full FLT in Lean, Comparator-checked by Buzzard Sep 4) and Google DeepMind (AlphaProof Nexus, 9 Erdos problems, May 2026) are at or near the same level; the gap between labs is months.
cap-research-math-internal.why: About 9% of posed problems survived into result families; cost is roughly three hours of Pro-tier thinking compute per result, and OpenAI put its ten August results at ~$2,000 of tokens (~$200 each). The difficulty ladder moved from IMO gold (Jul 2025) to Erdos-type open problems (spring 2026) to famous conjectures (UGC, forced Navier-Stokes blowup, Sep-Oct 2026) in about 15 months. Every downstream node in the space tree starts here.
cap-research-math-internal.strongest_case_small: Nothing in the release is above T3; the only audit of an earlier OpenAI release covered ten results. The 4,000 problems were chosen by the lab and skew discrete and finitary; PDE (3 of 16 families formalized), dynamics (2 of 12) and topology (1 of 18) are thin, which is where space physics lives. Calegari scored the release at roughly 5 of 100 points on his own list of hard number-theory problems.
cap-research-math-internal.signpost: An independent Comparator run plus statement audit on a headline family (102 or 362) moving it to T4; a published error rate from a random sample of 30 or more families.

cap-research-math-public.title: Research-grade math for outside teams
cap-research-math-public.description: An outside engineering team can buy, on demand, mathematics at roughly the October-2026 internal level (journal-grade open problems, proofs with Lean output) through a public or trusted-access product, for under ~$1,000 per result.
cap-research-math-public.status_oct2026: Partly. Public GPT-6 Astra (paid users from Sep 4, 2026) solved 106 ErdosBench open problems (43 completely) and became the first model to solve any FrontierMath Erdos problem (2 of 68; Epoch, Sep 3, 2026) - research math at the easy end. AlphaEvolve has been generally available to Google Cloud customers since Jul 9, 2026. The model behind openai/math is unreleased; GPT-6.1 Astra was withheld on Sep 29, 2026; Anthropic's Mythos tier is restricted. OpenAI's ChatGPT for Academic Researchers gives 10,000 researchers free access now and 100,000 by 2027 (Jul 29, 2026). OpenAI's chief scientist says the lab does not prioritize math in public models (Sep 10, 2026).
cap-research-math-public.why: The reveal-to-release lag for Astra was about five weeks (Aug 1 reveal, Sep 4 public), but the most capable versions get held back for safety (GPT-6.1 Astra) or restricted (Mythos), and US pre-release review adds 12-30 days. Under S2 a public model matches the Oct-2026 internal level 6-12 months out (mid-to-late 2027); under S1, 12-18 months (2028). At least four labs compete (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, SpaceXAI with 35-58-day Grok cadence) and open-weight followers trail by about a year, which forces release. The binding gate is release governance (lab safety holds plus government review), coded here as regulatory.
cap-research-math-public.strongest_case_small: Labs may keep their best math models internal: OpenAI says its urgency is recursive self-improvement and alignment, the Advisory Group asks labs not to test open problems on proprietary models, and dual-use cyber capability (not math) drives the holds. Public models are jagged - strong on discrete Erdos-style problems, weaker on PDE analysis - so an engineering team may get less than the catalog suggests.
cap-research-math-public.signpost: Any public model scoring 20% or more on FrontierMath Erdos (GPT-6 Astra: 3% in Sep 2026) by end-2027 (S2 on track) versus under 10% (S1); a lab launching a research-math API tier with Lean output.

cap-autoformalization.title: Agentic Lean formalization at scale
cap-autoformalization.description: Agents turn informal proofs into Lean and complete them, at the scale of hundreds of papers or a multi-million-line project in weeks.
cap-autoformalization.status_oct2026: Exists for discrete and algebraic math. openai/math formalized the main results of 162 papers by agent (unchecked, T3). Anthropic's FLT formalization (13.4M lines) passed Buzzard's Comparator run (Sep 4, 2026). Meta reportedly autoformalized textbooks into a large Lean library using 183B tokens (May 2026, secondary report). Weak where Mathlib is thin: PDE 3 of 16 families, dynamics 2 of 12, topology 1 of 18.
cap-autoformalization.why: Lean is hard to fool once the statement is right, and proof labor is no longer scarce: the same pipeline that formalized 162 papers can prove properties of flight algorithms and code (P2). 362 shows agents can build missing PDE infrastructure for a single result. What remains scarce is formal semantics for real code and correct statements.
cap-autoformalization.strongest_case_small: Coverage is uneven exactly where space needs it (PDE, numerics, stochastic processes). Agent-written Lean can be enormous and slow to check: two of three openai/math targets exceeded a 7 GiB memory cap in an outside run. A proof of the wrong statement is worthless.
cap-autoformalization.signpost: An agent formalizes a PDE or numerical-analysis paper end to end, including missing library infrastructure, with an outside Comparator pass.

cap-applied-math.title: AI does research-grade applied math
cap-applied-math.description: Engineers routinely get, from AI, well-posedness and stability analyses of their own models, numerical schemes with certified error bounds, uncertainty quantification with guarantees, and optimal-control results with proofs.
cap-applied-math.status_oct2026: Not yet a routine service. The catalog shows applied-adjacent depth: 362 Vlasov-Maxwell [L, T3]; 363 and 364 Boltzmann (T1); 372 elasticity inverse problem (T1); 365 boundary recovery [L, T3]; plus the separate forced Navier-Stokes blowup claim (Sep 8). These were lab-posed problems, PDE formalization is thin, and nothing in the release touches UQ, stiff numerics or radiation transport.
cap-applied-math.why: Most engineering math is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems (position a); what it adds is messy context: empirical coefficients, real boundary conditions, and a need for explicit constants and rates. A stability proof for a specific control law or a convergence bound for a specific solver is a week-to-month task for a specialist (general), which fits inside the S2 task horizon by 2027-28. Under S1, diffusion waits on public access (2028) plus domain workflows. This is mostly 'solved in principle but expert-scarce' work, so on-demand expertise is the unlock.
cap-applied-math.strongest_case_small: Engineers already get adequate answers from simulation and test without proofs; certified bounds for realistic 3D multiphysics are often too loose to use; the gain is confidence, not performance (position d). Several catalog premises are T1, so implications resting on 363, 364 and 372 are conditional.
cap-applied-math.signpost: A NASA, ESA or major-prime technical report, or an AIAA paper, in which an AI-produced stability proof, convergence proof or certified error bound decides a design question.

cap-physics-theory.title: AI builds validated physics theory
cap-physics-theory.description: AI derives closures, reduced-order models with proofs, and plasma, materials or combustion theory that beat the human state of the art on held-out experimental data.
cap-physics-theory.status_oct2026: Not yet. The catalog touches foundations (364 Boltzmann from Newtonian gases, T1; 278 Kohn-Sham ensemble representability fails, T1; 263 ionization bounds [L, T3]), but no AI-built closure has displaced an engineering model. The data-driven precedent is weather: ECMWF's AI forecast system went operational on Feb 25, 2025, beating physics models on many measures (up to 20% on cyclone tracks) at ~1,000x less energy per forecast - an emulator, not new theory.
cap-physics-theory.why: Theory-building needs month-to-year research horizons (S2: 2028-29) and validation data. Where databases exist (turbulence DNS, DFT databases, plasma experiments) validation is a cognitive task and S2 delivers by 2029; where it needs new experiments, the physical clock binds. Under S3 closed-loop labs supply validation data from ~2028. These are genuinely open problems, unlike most nodes in this tree.
cap-physics-theory.strongest_case_small: Turbulence and anomalous-transport closures have resisted 60+ years because the missing information is not in the equations; learned closures have historically failed out of distribution. The catalog premises here are T1, so the chain is conditional.
cap-physics-theory.signpost: An AI-derived closure or reduced model adopted in a production code (NASA FUN3D, US3D, or a major plasma code) after blind validation on data it never saw.

cap-design-optimization.title: AI multiphysics design with guarantees
cap-design-optimization.description: AI runs end-to-end multiphysics design optimization (aero-thermal-structural-propulsion) with constraint satisfaction and error bounds, producing designs that pass existing engineering review gates.
cap-design-optimization.status_oct2026: Early. Generative structural design and AI-generated engine geometry exist (general); AlphaEvolve is generally available for problems with checkable objectives (Jul 9, 2026). Chip design is the leading indicator: Cadence reported a fully autonomous design agent (Jun 2026), Synopsys and AMD launched agents (Oct 2, 2026), and OpenAI-Synopsys announced an EDA-operating model (Oct 6, 2026) - all secondary press reports.
cap-design-optimization.why: EDA shows the pattern: when the simulator is trusted and the objective is checkable, agents already do weeks of design work. Space multiphysics simulators are less trusted (turbulence, ablation, combustion), so guarantees hold only inside validated envelopes. Under S2, applied math (2027) plus trusted emulators (2028) give design loops by 2028; under S1, 2030.
cap-design-optimization.strongest_case_small: Design quality is bounded by model fidelity, and optimizers exploit model error. Launch-vehicle performance is set mostly by the rocket equation and propellant chemistry, leaving single-digit percent gains; the hardware still has to be built and tested.
cap-design-optimization.signpost: A prime or NewSpace firm publicly attributes a flown or hot-fired hardware design (engine, structure, heat shield) to an AI design loop whose model-based margins its review board accepted.

cap-autonomous-labs.title: AI-run closed-loop labs at scale
cap-autonomous-labs.description: AI plans, runs and interprets experiments on robotic lab hardware, closing design-build-test loops for materials, chemistry and components at 10x or more the throughput of human-run labs.
cap-autonomous-labs.status_oct2026: Early. Periodic Labs launched with a $300M seed (Sep 30, 2025); Radical AI and others run self-driving materials labs; DOE's Genesis Mission (~$5B starter allocation, first awards Jul 22, 2026) funds autonomous laboratories at national labs. No space-qualified material has come out of a closed loop yet.
cap-autonomous-labs.why: Cognition is not the lab bottleneck; robots, synthesis throughput and characterization are. Under S2 and S3 the planning agent is effectively free, so capital (roughly $10-100M per lab, general) and the physics of synthesis bind. Solution chemistry and thin films speed up most; bulk aerospace materials least.
cap-autonomous-labs.strongest_case_small: Superalloys, UHTCs and ablators need furnaces, bulk processing and days per sample; creep, oxidation and radiation tests run in real time (years of creep data cannot be compressed). Qualification, not discovery, sets the insertion timeline for space materials.
cap-autonomous-labs.signpost: An autonomous lab reports a new material entering a space-qualification program; Genesis Mission autonomous-lab throughput milestones.

infra-mathlib-applied.title: Lean libraries for analysis, PDE and numerics
infra-mathlib-applied.description: Mathlib or companion libraries cover Sobolev spaces, weak solutions, standard PDE energy estimates, ODE and numerical-analysis theory, and stochastic processes well enough that applied results formalize routinely.
infra-mathlib-applied.status_oct2026: Thin. Mathlib has ~138,000 definitions, ~290,000 theorems and 772 contributors (stats page, accessed Oct 7, 2026). openai/math formalized 3 of 16 PDE families and 2 of 12 dynamics families versus 5 of 6 logic families. 362 [L, T3] shows agents can build what one result needs.
infra-mathlib-applied.why: Agents now write library code at FLT scale, so proof labor is not the gate; good abstractions and community review are. Under S2, agent-built applied libraries mature in 2027 and are integrated into Mathlib by 2028; under S1, review bandwidth stretches this to 2030. Every P2 chain that touches continuous physics (GNC stability, plasma, CFD error bounds) waits on this node.
infra-mathlib-applied.strongest_case_small: Mathlib's maintainers and review process are the bottleneck and may resist agent-written code; parallel libraries could fragment the ecosystem; formal PDE theory still won't cover the empirical closures engineers actually use.
infra-mathlib-applied.signpost: Mathlib or a Lean FRO-backed library merges Sobolev embeddings, Lax-Milgram and standard energy estimates; an applied PDE family from the catalog (363, 364 or 372) receives a Comparator-checked formalization.

infra-verified-numerics.title: Verified floating-point and numerics toolchain
infra-verified-numerics.description: A toolchain that proves floating-point programs and numerical methods (ODE integrators, linear solvers, convex optimizers, filters) meet stated error bounds, from the mathematics down to compiled code.
infra-verified-numerics.status_oct2026: Pieces exist outside Lean - Coq's Flocq and CompCert, Gappa, FPTaylor, Frama-C (general) - but there is no integrated stack and Lean lacks a mature IEEE-754 plus numerical-analysis library. The catalog contains no numerics results, and the release does not touch numerical analysis of stiff systems.
infra-verified-numerics.why: Verified numerics is solved in principle but expert-scarce: a round-off and truncation analysis of a GNC loop takes a specialist weeks to months (general). Agents that already write millions of lines of Lean remove the labor; integration with existing Coq tools or a Lean port is a 1-2 year engineering job under S2.
infra-verified-numerics.strongest_case_small: Proofs on real flight code stall on compiler semantics, nonstandard FPUs on rad-hard processors and environment models, not on the numerics; many GNC teams already use fixed-point or conservative margins that make the proof unnecessary.
infra-verified-numerics.signpost: An agent-generated, machine-checked round-off bound for a flight Kalman filter or guidance law reported by NASA, ESA, AdaCore, Galois or a prime.

infra-tool-qualification.title: Regulators accept AI-produced proofs
infra-tool-qualification.description: Certification authorities (FAA via DO-178C, DO-333 and DO-330; NASA software assurance; ECSS; Space Force) grant credit for formal proofs produced by AI agents, with a qualified proof checker as the trusted base.
infra-tool-qualification.status_oct2026: No credit yet for AI-generated proofs. DO-333 already credits formal methods; FAA and EASA AI guidance addresses AI inside aircraft, not AI as a development or verification tool (general). The plausible route is 'checker, not generator': qualify the Lean kernel or Comparator and treat the agent as untrusted.
infra-tool-qualification.why: Aviation software standards turn over on 5-10+ year cycles (DO-178B 1992, DO-178C 2011), but the checker route needs no new standard: DO-330 already qualifies tools, and a small proof kernel is a better qualification target than any test tool. Under S2, first project-level credit lands in 2029-30. Capped at Medium because it needs regulator acceptance.
infra-tool-qualification.strongest_case_small: Regulators move slowly and specifications become the bottleneck. Uncrewed commercial space needs no software certification at all, so this gate matters mainly for crewed vehicles, aviation-adjacent systems and NASA human-rating.
infra-tool-qualification.signpost: An FAA issue paper, NASA project or ESA mission accepting Lean-checked proofs as verification evidence; a DO-330 qualification kit for a Lean checker.

verif-independent-check.title: Independent checks of AI math
verif-independent-check.description: Outside groups run Comparator on the labs' Lean challenges and audit formal statements against the manuscripts, moving key results from T3 to T4.
verif-independent-check.status_oct2026: Not yet for any openai/math family. Kingy AI (Oct 6, 2026) ran Comparator on three challenge targets on an 8 GiB VM: one passed twice, two hit a 7 GiB memory cap; same operator, no statement audit, so no tier change. Hexagon launched Oct 6 (beta; Buzzard on its advisory board) but does not require formalization and holds no OpenAI deposits yet. Precedent: Buzzard's Comparator run on Anthropic's FLT (Sep 4, 2026).
verif-independent-check.why: A Comparator run needs hours and a large-memory machine; the statement audit needs a domain expert for days per family. Headline Lean families (102, 362) should reach T4 within one to three months; the long tail of 127 formalized families and the 245 unformalized ones takes years. Under S2, AI-assisted statement audits speed the tail.
verif-independent-check.strongest_case_small: Human bandwidth is the limit: a few dozen qualified readers per field and 722 manuscripts at once. Independent machine checks confirm only formal statements, and statement gaps already exist (the quasi-RH challenge targets zeta only).
verif-independent-check.signpost: Hexagon, Buzzard's group or another expert team publishes a Comparator pass plus statement audit for 102 or 362.

capability-horizon-compounding.title: Month-long autonomous research tasks
capability-horizon-compounding.description: AI agents complete, at 50% reliability or better, technical research tasks that take a human expert a full work-month (~170 hours), up from about a work-week in late 2026.
capability-horizon-compounding.status_oct2026: METR measured frontier 50% time horizons of ~16-20 hours in Feb-Mar 2026 and says its suite cannot reliably measure above ~16 hours (Frontier Risk Report, May 19, 2026); GPT-5.6 Sol was ~11.3 hours (95% CI 5-40, flagged unreliable; Jun 26, 2026). Long-run doubling ~7 months since 2019, ~4 months in 2024-25 (METR, Jul 14, 2025). In mathematics the internal model returns, in ~3 hours of compute, results that take experts weeks to months.
capability-horizon-compounding.why: Parametrization: start at ~40 h (one work-week) in Oct 2026, one 7-month doubling past the measured 16-20 h. S1 doubles every 12-18 months: ~76 h end-2027, ~230 h end-2029, ~700 h end-2031 (~4 work-months). S2 doubles every 6-9 months: ~150 h end-2027 (range 120-200), ~1,300 h end-2029, ~12,000 h end-2031 (2-26 work-years across the 6-9 month range). S3 follows S2 to end-2027 then doubles every ~3 months, so the metric stops being meaningful around 2029. The month threshold is the point where a whole applied-math project (model, analysis, proof, code) fits in one autonomous run.
capability-horizon-compounding.strongest_case_small: METR suites saturate and measure well-specified software tasks; research is open-ended and judgment-heavy; 80%-reliability horizons are several times shorter than 50% horizons, and engineering needs high reliability. Capability is jagged across domains.
capability-horizon-compounding.signpost: A successor horizon suite (METR or Epoch) reporting a frontier 50% horizon of 80 hours or more by end-2027 (S2 on track) or under 40 hours (S1).

capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.title: AI speeds up its own development 3x
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.description: AI systems accelerate frontier AI research and engineering, including chip design and software stacks, by 3x or more overall - the hinge between S2 and S3.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.status_oct2026: METR estimates ~1.5x acceleration during Claude Opus 5.5's development, a ~30% chance of 2x, and judges it unlikely to fully automate AI R&D (Sep 22, 2026). OpenAI's chief scientist names recursive self-improvement and automated alignment research as priorities (Sep 10, 2026). Agentic EDA (Cadence, Synopsys, OpenAI-Synopsys) applies the same loop to chips.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.why: Software-side acceleration is bounded by compute for experiments. Epoch: frontier training compute grows ~5x/yr, compute stock ~3.4x/yr, GW-scale sites take ~2.1 years at ~$38B per GW; Anthropic alone lists ~$518B of decade-long compute obligations. S3 assumes acceleration past 3x by 2028 converts into ~10x/yr effective efficiency gains, collapsing the cost of cognitive work; even then the recursion runs on fabs and power, which are a physical clock.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.strongest_case_small: Amdahl's law inside AI labs: experiments need GPUs, and CoWoS, HBM and power supply chains are physical. METR reports weak judgment and foresight. Safety holds (GPT-6.1 Astra) and government review slow deployment even when capability races ahead.
capability-ai-rnd-acceleration.signpost: Lab system cards or METR reporting 2x+ uplift with high confidence; frontier release cadence under 30 days across several labs; AI-designed accelerator tape-outs.

capability-cost-collapse.title: A research result costs less than an engineer-day
capability-cost-collapse.description: The public price of a research-grade math result (problem posed to checked proof or derivation) falls below ~$1,000 and then below ~$100, cheaper than one day of a specialist's time.
capability-cost-collapse.status_oct2026: Internally ~3 hours of Pro-tier compute per result; OpenAI put Astra's ten August results at ~$2,000 at API rates (~$200 each). GPT-6 Astra is public in ChatGPT and the API (Sep 2026), with a new $500/month Pro tier and a cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol reported as near-Astra at a fifth of the price (press). Epoch: price for a fixed capability level fell 9-900x per year in 2022-25; AI chip price-performance improves ~49%/yr.
capability-cost-collapse.why: At ~$200 per result, a space program posing 1,000 hard analysis problems a year spends ~$0.2M - less than one engineer. Illustratively, an Oct-2026-grade result falls to ~$20-70 by 2028 in S1 (3-10x/yr) and ~$1-10 in S2. Price stops being a gate for math in every scenario; access, trust and integration remain.
capability-cost-collapse.strongest_case_small: The cost of checking dominates the cost of producing: a $200 proof that needs a $20,000 expert audit is a $20,000 result. Frontier tasks get longer, so spend per frontier task may stay flat even as fixed-capability prices fall.
capability-cost-collapse.signpost: Lab price sheets for long-horizon reasoning tiers; enterprise contracts that bundle research math with Lean output; space-firm disclosures of AI analysis spend.

capability-controlled-data-access.title: Frontier math on ITAR and classified networks
capability-controlled-data-access.description: Research-grade models run inside ITAR/EAR-compliant, CUI and classified environments, so space primes, Space Force and NRO programs can pose problems with export-controlled engineering data.
capability-controlled-data-access.status_oct2026: GenAI.mil reached ~3M DoD personnel with a ChatGPT-based 'ChatGPT Mil', Grok and Gemini (Fortune, Sep 1, 2026; ~500,000 power users per DefenseScoop, Sep 23); OpenAI, Google, xAI and others were cleared for classified networks (May 2026). The DoD designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk, upheld by the DC Circuit on Sep 25, 2026, barring contractors from using Claude on DoD work - the lab behind the only Comparator-checked mega-formalization (FLT). Civil NASA is unaffected: JPL used Claude to plan two Perseverance drives (Dec 2025).
capability-controlled-data-access.why: Much space engineering data (propulsion, GNC, hypersonics, defense payloads) is ITAR-controlled, and P1 works best when teams pose problems with real data. Accredited government clouds have trailed commercial releases by months (general). No US export control restricts API access to closed models today; controls target chips (general), and policy can still remove a lab overnight.
capability-controlled-data-access.strongest_case_small: The math itself is not controlled: engineers can pose sanitized problems without technical data. Defense adoption is limited by security culture and model-weight custody more than availability. Policy volatility cuts both ways.
capability-controlled-data-access.signpost: A research-math-capable model accredited at IL6 or Top Secret; a change to the Anthropic designation; State Department or DDTC guidance on AI processing of ITAR technical data.

capability-open-weights-math.title: Open-weight model at research-math level
capability-open-weights-math.description: An open-weight model matches the October-2026 internal research-math level, removing lab release decisions and access controls as a gate for everyone, including adversaries.
capability-open-weights-math.status_oct2026: Not yet. Press frames Moonshot's Kimi K3 as Astra's competitor (Aug 2026); the US threatened to blacklist Moonshot over distillation (Jul 22, 2026). Open models have historically trailed the closed frontier by about a year (general).
capability-open-weights-math.why: With a ~12-month open-weight lag, the Oct-2026 internal level reaches open weights in late 2027 to 2028 under S2. For space this matters two ways: on-premises use with ITAR data without cloud accreditation, and competitors and adversaries getting the same on-demand math for trajectory design, constellation tasking and weapons-relevant analysis.
capability-open-weights-math.strongest_case_small: Open models may lag more at the frontier of math reasoning (RL compute is expensive), and distillation crackdowns could widen the gap; most engineering math does not need the frontier anyway.
capability-open-weights-math.signpost: An open-weight model solving FrontierMath Erdos problems or matching GPT-6 Astra's ErdosBench score.

capability-crypto-watch.title: AI cryptanalysis of space-link crypto (watch item)
capability-crypto-watch.description: An AI-produced result materially weakens a standardized primitive used in satellite command and data links (lattice schemes such as ML-KEM, elliptic curves, or AES modes), forcing re-keying or hardware upgrades on long-lived spacecraft.
capability-crypto-watch.status_oct2026: Nothing in openai/math breaks deployed cryptography: 279 (exact quantum factoring over a fixed gate set, T1) is theory only and does not cut qubit budgets; 272 and 266 refine quantum-key-distribution theory. One of Astra's ten August problems was in lattice cryptography, with no reported effect on deployed schemes. Models' demonstrated strength is implementation bugs and historical ciphers, not number-theoretic breaks.
capability-crypto-watch.why: Satellites fly 5-15 years with fixed cryptographic implementations and limited on-orbit agility (general). Even a non-practical weakening (say, tens of bits off a lattice parameter set) would trigger costly re-keying and upgrade programs. Research-grade AI math pointed at LWE, isogenies or discrete log is the channel; this node tracks it, it does not predict it.
capability-crypto-watch.strongest_case_small: Decades of human cryptanalysis; standardized parameter sets carry wide margins; AI's track record is bugs, not breaks. A software vulnerability is far likelier than a mathematical one and is a cybersecurity issue, not a math one.
capability-crypto-watch.signpost: Any AI-lab result on LWE, SIS, isogenies or discrete log; a NIST or NSA reassessment of post-quantum parameter margins.

capability-cheap-trust.title: Trust in hours: automated statement audits
capability-cheap-trust.description: AI-assisted pipelines check that a formal statement matches the engineering claim (definitions, hypotheses, units, scope), cross-check proofs with independent agents and produce human-readable audit trails, cutting the cost of trusting an AI result from expert-weeks to hours.
capability-cheap-trust.status_oct2026: Statement gaps are real: openai/math's quasi-RH challenge targets only zeta; the outside run of the Pi Exponent target found its formal statement omits a manuscript consequence. Human review does not scale to 722 manuscripts. AGMAI (Sep 29) and the Simons Institute report (Sep 28) call for disclosure and lineage norms.
capability-cheap-trust.why: In engineering, statement gaps become specification errors, the main residual risk in formally verified systems (general). An adversarial auditor model plus Lean plus a human sign-off turns P1 answers into evidence a design review can accept. This is the node that moves the bottleneck from proving to understanding (position h) back toward engineering.
capability-cheap-trust.strongest_case_small: Generator and auditor models can share blind spots; the final judgment of whether a property is the right one is irreducibly human and domain-specific.
capability-cheap-trust.signpost: Hexagon or a journal adopting AI-assisted statement audits as standard; a NASA or ESA review board accepting an AI audit trail.

capability-algorithm-discovery.title: AI-discovered algorithms in space codes
capability-algorithm-discovery.description: AlphaEvolve-style search (a model proposes code, an automatic evaluator scores it) improves practical heuristics and kernels used in space operations and engineering: constellation scheduling, conjunction screening, trajectory solvers, onboard compression, CFD kernels.
capability-algorithm-discovery.status_oct2026: AlphaEvolve's scheduling heuristic recovers ~0.7% of Google's fleet compute, a kernel sped up 23% (1% off Gemini training time) and FlashAttention up to 32.5% (May 14, 2025); generally available to Google Cloud customers since Jul 9, 2026. Unlike the catalog's galactic speedups (107, 130 - no practical gain), these have practical constants. Hardness results (102, 117, 125, all [L], T3) mark where general-purpose gains are capped.
capability-algorithm-discovery.why: It needs only an evaluator function, which space operations have (schedule value, screening runtime, compression ratio). For a 10,000-satellite constellation, a few percent of tasking or ground-contact efficiency is worth tens of millions of dollars a year (general). The hardness results (P3) tell teams to stop chasing general solvers and invest in instance structure, which is exactly what evolutionary search exploits.
capability-algorithm-discovery.strongest_case_small: Gains are incremental (single-digit percent); structured instances already solve well with commercial MIP solvers; worst-case ceilings say little about real instances.
capability-algorithm-discovery.signpost: A constellation operator or space agency publishing an AI-discovered heuristic in production with measured gains.

capability-learned-emulators.title: Trusted AI emulators of space physics codes
capability-learned-emulators.description: The weather-model playbook - train on decades of simulation or reanalysis data, run ~1,000x cheaper - applied to space codes (CFD and aerothermal, plasma, thermosphere, structures), with calibrated uncertainty or certified error bounds supplied by AI applied math.
capability-learned-emulators.status_oct2026: Weather: ECMWF's AIFS operational Feb 25, 2025, up to 20% better on some measures at ~1,000x less energy, though at 28 km versus 9 km grid spacing. Space: NASA and IBM released the open Surya heliophysics model (Aug 20, 2025; 16% better flare classification, nine years of SDO data) and SuryaBench (Mar 2026). CFD surrogates are common in design exploration but not trusted for margins (general).
capability-learned-emulators.why: Emulators remove the compute cost of design loops and ensembles. Weather moved from research models to operations in about 15 months on the back of 40+ years of reanalysis. Space domains split: where training data can be generated by simulation (CFD, structures, thermal) emulators are data-unconstrained and arrive first; where data come only from nature (one Sun, rare extreme storms, few hypersonic flights) they arrive late and extrapolate poorly.
capability-learned-emulators.strongest_case_small: Emulators are only as good as their training data, and extrapolation to new vehicles or extreme storms - exactly where margins matter - is where they fail. Coarser resolution (as with AIFS) can hide local extremes such as peak heating.
capability-learned-emulators.signpost: NOAA SWPC or ESA running an AI model in operations; a launch provider using a surrogate with stated error bounds in flight-readiness analysis.

capability-engineering-adoption.title: On-demand applied math in space engineering
capability-engineering-adoption.description: Space engineering organizations routinely pose their own hard analysis problems (stability, bounds, convergence, inverse problems, trade studies) to frontier models and use the checked answers in design reviews.
capability-engineering-adoption.status_oct2026: Early. JPL used Claude to plan two Perseverance drives with human review (Dec 2025); NASA and IBM ran a compressed model on the ISS (May 2026); IEEE Spectrum reports engineers' distrust of non-deterministic outputs (Sep 28, 2026). SpaceX owns a frontier lab (SpaceXAI; Grok releases every 35-58 days) and says its Grok bot will route tasks to the best model, including Claude Opus 5.5 (Oct 7, 2026).
capability-engineering-adoption.why: Most engineering math is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems: a specialist analysis that takes 2-8 weeks (general) becomes hours plus a check. Vertically integrated firms that own both models and hardware (SpaceX/SpaceXAI) adopt first; primes constrained by ITAR and DoD rules follow 6-12 months later; agencies last.
capability-engineering-adoption.strongest_case_small: Analysis is rarely on a space program's critical path; answers still need checking; legacy processes, roles and liability slow uptake; AI may expand analysis scope rather than speed programs.
capability-engineering-adoption.signpost: A major prime or NASA center publishing standard work for AI-derived analysis; AIAA papers where an AI-derived proof or bound is used in a flight design.

capability-ai-eda-space-processor.title: AI-designed radiation-tolerant space processor
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.description: Agentic EDA designs and formally verifies a radiation-tolerant processor or SoC for space (triple modular redundancy, error correction, upset-aware layout); it is taped out and radiation-tested.
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.status_oct2026: Agentic chip design is moving fast in commercial EDA (Cadence autonomous agent, Jun 2026; Synopsys and AMD agents, Oct 2, 2026; OpenAI-Synopsys, Oct 6, 2026; all secondary reports). Space processors lag commercial nodes by roughly a decade (general).
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.why: Design and verification (12-24 months for a rad-hard SoC, general) compress several-fold; fabrication (3-4 months per run), scarce heavy-ion beam time and QML-class qualification (1-2 years) do not. First tape-out in 2029-30 under S2; flight qualification after 2031.
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.strongest_case_small: Space is moving to COTS processors with system-level mitigation, the rad-hard market is small, and qualification rather than design sets the schedule.
capability-ai-eda-space-processor.signpost: A rad-hard SoC tape-out credited mainly to agentic EDA, with published heavy-ion test results.

capability-ai-native-spacecraft.title: Spacecraft engineered mostly by AI flies
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.description: An operational spacecraft whose design analyses, trade studies and flight-software verification artifacts were majority AI-generated (with human review) reaches orbit and operates.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.status_oct2026: Not yet. Ingredients exist piecemeal: AI-generated engine and structural geometry, agentic coding, JPL drive planning, agentic chip design.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.why: Chain: adoption (S2 2028) -> smallsat design and build in 12-18 months -> rideshare launch -> operations by 2029-30. A small company with no legacy process is the likely first mover; the binding gates are integration, test and a launch slot, not cognition. This is a process outcome, not a performance claim.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.strongest_case_small: It changes who does the engineering, not what flies: performance gains are small, 'majority AI-generated' is hard to verify, and the first claims will be marketing.
capability-ai-native-spacecraft.signpost: A company or agency announcing such a mission with published AI-generated verification evidence, followed by on-orbit success.

capability-program-cycle-compression.title: Development cycles shrink by a third, not 10x
capability-program-cycle-compression.description: Development time for new space systems (concept to launch) falls by roughly 30-40% under S2 (about 50% under S3, 10-20% under S1), bounded by Amdahl's law because fabrication, integration and test, qualification and launch dominate the critical path.
capability-program-cycle-compression.status_oct2026: Not yet. Major NASA projects routinely run late, mostly in hardware, integration and test (GAO reporting, general).
capability-program-cycle-compression.why: Illustrative critical-path shares (general): requirements and trades 10%, design and analysis 15%, software 10%, fabrication and procurement 25%, integration and test 25%, qualification and reviews 10%, launch campaign 5%. Speedups of 5-10x on cognitive work and 1.1-1.2x on physical work (S2) give a 1.6x overall speedup, a ~38% shorter schedule; S3 (20-50x cognitive, 1.3-1.5x physical) gives ~2x, ~51%; S1 (2x cognitive) gives ~18%. Fewer design escapes found in test cut rework, a second-order gain. Only programs started after adoption (2028+) show it, so evidence appears in 2030-31. Capped at Medium because flown evidence needs qualification.
capability-program-cycle-compression.strongest_case_small: Schedules are set by funding profiles, supply chains (rad-hard parts 12-24+ months), launch manifests and politics; teams may spend the gain on more analysis and scope (Jevons) instead of shorter schedules.
capability-program-cycle-compression.signpost: A GAO, ESA or company schedule analysis attributing cycle-time reduction to AI; smallsat build times falling below 9 months for new designs.

comms-ai-cryptanalysis.title: AI agents audit cryptography at research grade
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.description: Frontier models run closed-loop cryptanalysis: they propose attacks on published schemes, protocols and parameter sets, test them, and return exact witnesses for a human to judge. Achieved here means standards bodies and major vendors routinely run such audits on candidate schemes and parameters.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.status_oct2026: Partly exists. Olejnik and Naskręcki (arXiv 2608.21986, Aug 22 2026) report an autonomous agent workflow that found failures in eight published constructions, for example a Ring-LWR commitment that opens to any message and a lattice e-voting protocol that loses receipt-freeness. None is a NIST-standardized scheme. ML attacks on LWE recover only sparse or small secrets at reduced parameters (NoMod, arXiv 2510.02162). openai/math contains no attack on factoring, discrete log or lattices (tl-position-5).
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.why: The failures found so far sit one level above the hardness assumption: encodings, simulators, parameter certification, protocol composition. That is where space security is weakest. Bespoke key-management and command-authentication protocols on constrained links are written by small teams and rarely reviewed by cryptographers. Once research-grade models are public (cap-research-math-public), an audit that took a specialist weeks costs hours of compute, so every new satellite security protocol can be attacked before launch. Under S2 agent task horizons double every 6-9 months, so by 2028 agents audit whole protocol suites, not single constructions.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.strongest_case_small: The breaks so far are in obscure, non-standard constructions. Standardized primitives (AES-256, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) have decades of expert scrutiny. Most real-world failures come from implementation bugs and key handling, which human audits with existing tools already target.
comms-ai-cryptanalysis.signpost: An AI-found break or parameter downgrade in an IETF, CCSDS or NIST-standardized scheme; NIST or CCSDS stating that AI audits were used in a selection or review.
