comms-lattice-weakness.title: AI finds a structural weakness in post-quantum lattices
comms-lattice-weakness.description: Watch item, not a forecast: an AI-produced, independently verified result that cuts the concrete security of ML-KEM or ML-DSA parameter sets by 10 or more bits, or gives a subexponential algorithm for module-lattice problems. If it happens, satellites with lattice-only key exchange need an in-orbit algorithm swap.
comms-lattice-weakness.status_oct2026: Nothing in openai/math touches lattices, LWE, isogenies or discrete log (tl-position-5). Family 138 (Subset Sum in 2^0.49n worst case, T1) and 279 (exact quantum factoring, T1) are not attacks. Outside the release, a single-author, multi-part arXiv claim of a polynomial-time quantum attack on Module-LWE over 2-power cyclotomics (Luo, arXiv 2605.17412, May 2026) is unrefereed, and we found no expert endorsement. A similar 2024 quantum-lattice claim was withdrawn after a bug was found (general).
comms-lattice-weakness.why: Whether module lattices are hard is a fact about mathematics. AI capability cannot make them weak, only find a weakness that already exists. But the capability that produced the release's theoretical-CS results in weeks raises the chance that hidden structure, if it exists, is found inside the horizon; 2-power cyclotomic rings are the most-suspected surface. Chain: weakness found -> NIST revises or deprecates parameters -> satellites with lattice-only key exchange and no update path are exposed for the rest of a 15-year life. The hedge already exists: HQC (code-based, selected Mar 11 2025, final standard expected 2027) and hash-based signatures. Bands are judgments about discovery, not computed probabilities.
comms-lattice-weakness.strongest_case_small: Lattice problems have resisted about 30 years of cryptanalysis and come with worst-case to average-case reductions. ML-KEM-1024 has a large margin: even a 10-bit loss leaves it far outside attack range. The base rate of a practical break by 2031 is very low regardless of AI.
comms-lattice-weakness.signpost: Any lab release containing LWE, SIS or NTRU results; a Comparator-checked Lean proof of an improved lattice-reduction bound; a NIST statement re-examining ML-KEM parameters; the outcome of expert review of arXiv 2605.17412.

comms-hardness-ceilings-settled.title: Proven ceilings for scheduling and network partitioning
comms-hardness-ceilings-settled.description: Approximation limits that planners assumed become theorems. Beating the Goemans-Williamson Max-Cut ratio or a factor-2 vertex cover is NP-hard (UGC). Uniform sparsest cut has no constant-factor algorithm. Metric k-median siting is pinned at 1+2/e. Companion results: polynomial-time three-machine precedence scheduling and optimal-order randomized k-server.
comms-hardness-ceilings-settled.status_oct2026: 102 Unique Games [L], T3: Lean covers the UGC theorem and the vertex-cover factor below two. 117: the Lean main result is the semidefinite integrality gap (OAI.UniformSparsestCut.mainGap); the NP-hardness headline is T1 (statement gap). 125: Lean covers a companion recovery result (KMedianRecovery); the (1+2/e+ε) algorithm headline is T1 pending audit, and the matching hardness bound was already known (general). 124, 110 and 111 are T1. No outside Comparator run reported as of Oct 7 2026; the repo is a single-commit snapshot.
comms-hardness-ceilings-settled.why: Constellation operations are full of problems with these shapes. Splitting co-channel beams into two frequency groups to minimize conflicts is a Max-Cut variant. Picking a minimal set of links or beams that covers all conflicts is vertex-cover-like. Partitioning a laser mesh to isolate failures or traffic domains is a sparsest-cut problem. Picking gateway or ground-station sites from candidates is k-median. A proven ceiling tells a team to stop funding general-purpose 'optimal' solvers and invest in instance structure and exact methods for small cases (tl-position-3). It also lets buyers discount vendor claims of optimal scheduling at scale. In every scenario this lands within months of independent checking, because the only thing needed is that practitioners hear about it.
comms-hardness-ceilings-settled.strongest_case_small: These limits were already widely believed, so practice changes little (tl-position-3). Real instances are structured. A 96-satellite ground-station selection or a 10,000-request tasking day is solved well by MIP plus heuristics, and worst-case hardness says nothing about such instances.
comms-hardness-ceilings-settled.signpost: First independent Comparator run and statement audit on UniqueGamesTheorem.json; a survey or textbook treating UGC as a theorem; mission-planning vendors citing proven ceilings in benchmarks.

comms-optical-capacity-theory.title: Optical multi-user capacity limits become theorems (conditional)
comms-optical-capacity-theory.description: Family 273 claims a proof of the entropy photon-number inequality for beam-splitter mixing of bosonic inputs. This inequality was the missing step for the capacity region of the optical broadcast channel and for the secret-key capacity of optical wiretap channels with thermal noise (general). If the proof holds, the rate limits for one optical transmitter serving several receivers, and for links with an eavesdropper and background light, are proven rather than conjectured.
comms-optical-capacity-theory.status_oct2026: 273 is T1: manuscript only, and not in the repo's list of formalized main results. Single-user capacity of thermal-noise bosonic channels was already proven in 2014 (general). Lean infrastructure for quantum Shannon theory is forming: Lean-QIT formalizes the Holevo-Schumacher-Westmoreland classical-capacity theorem (arXiv 2607.09632, Jul 2026).
comms-optical-capacity-theory.why: Conditional. Engineers sizing optical relays (one GEO or LEO terminal serving several ground stations or users) and analyzing physical-layer secrecy of optical links already use the conjectured formulas; the proof removes the asterisk. The pathway is model confidence (tl-position-2): no link budget or hardware changes. The only difference between S1 and S2 is how fast a T1 quantum-information manuscript reaches T2-T4. In S2, Lean coverage of quantum entropy (building on Lean-QIT) lets an agent formalize it during 2027.
comms-optical-capacity-theory.strongest_case_small: Deployed and planned optical links use direct detection with PPM or on-off keying, well below the Holevo limit, so the gap to capacity is a receiver problem, not a theory problem. Operators use optical terminals point-to-point, not as multi-user broadcasters.
comms-optical-capacity-theory.signpost: A named quantum-optics information theorist endorsing the 273 argument, or a Lean formalization of it built on Lean-QIT.

comms-quantum-channel-limits.title: Settled limits for quantum links
comms-quantum-channel-limits.description: Three quantum-information results bound what space quantum links can do. 276 gives the exact classical capacity of every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel (loss with thermal noise). 266 shows there are exactly three mutually unbiased bases in dimension six. 272 builds an entangled state with zero distillable secret key and disproves the PPT-squared conjecture.
comms-quantum-channel-limits.status_oct2026: 276 [L], T3 (Lean OAI.GAD.main, Comparator challenge AmplitudeDamping.json; unchecked by outsiders). 266 T1: the exclusion of a fourth basis is a certified binary64 computation. 272 T1.
comms-quantum-channel-limits.why: For space quantum networks, 272 (conditional) says entanglement on a link is not enough to certify key: security must be shown through key-rate proofs, not entanglement witnesses. Because a PPT channel can have a non-entanglement-breaking square, a two-hop relay through such noisy links is not automatically useless. 266 (conditional) confirms that high-dimensional QKD should use prime-power dimensions, which is already practice. 276 gives an exact benchmark for thermal-noise qubit channels such as quantum memories and noisy downlinks. All three are ceilings or confidence results, so they take effect as soon as people read them.
comms-quantum-channel-limits.strongest_case_small: Every planned satellite QKD mission (Eagle-1, SpeQtre, QEYSSat, SPOQC, Jinan-1 successors) runs two-dimensional BB84 or BBM92 or continuous-variable QKD. None of these results changes a protocol, a key rate or a payload.
comms-quantum-channel-limits.signpost: An outside Comparator run on AmplitudeDamping.json; endorsement of 272 by a quantum Shannon theorist, since it disproves a named conjecture.

comms-expander-constructions.title: Explicit optimal expanders (conditional)
comms-expander-constructions.description: 178 builds nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs, the best possible spectral expanders, deterministically for every degree d≥3 and all large even sizes. 177 constructs bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension: the high-dimensional expansion behind locally testable codes and good quantum LDPC codes.
comms-expander-constructions.why: Conditional. A laser mesh in which each satellite has 3-4 terminals is a bounded-degree graph, and Ramanujan graphs give the largest spectral gap at that degree: short paths, high bisection bandwidth and graceful degradation when links fail. Explicit high-dimensional expanders feed code constructions (classical expander codes; qLDPC codes for quantum memories and repeaters). The pathway is new theory into tools (P6), so engineering use inside 2031 is a stretch; the band here is for the mathematics being established.
comms-expander-constructions.strongest_case_small: Random d-regular graphs are already within ε of Ramanujan with high probability, and bipartite Ramanujan graphs of every degree have been known to exist since 2013 (general). Real laser topologies are dictated by orbital geometry, link range, pointing and terminal slew time (+Grid, Motif, demand-aware designs), not by abstract graph choice.
comms-expander-constructions.signpost: A constellation-topology study that imposes Ramanujan-like structure under real geometric constraints and beats the best geometric heuristic by 10% or more in diameter or bisection bandwidth.

comms-certified-interference-bounds.title: Provable interference compliance for shared spectrum
comms-certified-interference-bounds.description: Interference showings for NGSO-GSO and NGSO-NGSO sharing delivered as certified bounds instead of Monte Carlo runs: interval or proof-backed bounds on time-weighted throughput degradation, unavailability and aggregate EPFD, with the model assumptions written as a checkable specification. Achieved means operators use such bounds in at least one filing or bilateral coordination agreement.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.status_oct2026: On Apr 30 2026 the FCC voted to replace its 26-year-old NGSO-GSO EPFD framework with performance-based rules. A Jan 9 2026 waiver (DA 26-36) had already raised co-frequency beams per location from 1 to 8, and GSO-arc avoidance tightened from 4 to 3 degrees (33FG). FCC NGSO-NGSO rules (FCC 24-117) cap time-weighted throughput degradation at 3% and added unavailability at 0.4% over an orbital simulation; the NGSO-GSO proposal used 3% and 0.1% (Roberts, arXiv 2609.36122). ITU Article 22 EPFD limits still govern internationally. Measured low-frequency EPFD from constellations exceeds radio-astronomy thresholds in 50-70% of samples (arXiv 2609.01995). No catalog family applies.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.why: The regulatory shift turned compliance from checking a power mask into a statistical claim about simulating tens of thousands of satellites. Disputes are now about simulation assumptions and tail events. Aggregates are where Monte Carlo is least trustworthy: keeping one interferer under threshold needs 8.1 degrees of separation, five need 15.5 and twenty need 27.0 (Roberts). A certified bound with a written specification can be re-checked by a rival operator or the FCC in hours. The math (geometry, order statistics, interval arithmetic) is expert-scarce rather than open. In S2, research-grade applied math is routine by 2027-28, so the first certified showings appear in 2028; in S1 they wait for public models and some years of diffusion.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.strongest_case_small: Spectrum disputes are commercial and political, not mathematical, and regulators accept Monte Carlo. Certified worst-case bounds are conservative and could cost capacity against statistical showings. The contested inputs (antenna patterns, traffic models, deployment plans) stay contested.
comms-certified-interference-bounds.signpost: An FCC or ITU-R WP4A filing citing machine-checked or interval-certified interference bounds; an operator publishing an open, verified EPFD or degradation calculator.

comms-certified-network-optimization.title: Near-optimal mesh routing with a proven gap
comms-certified-network-optimization.description: Per-snapshot joint optimization of laser-terminal pairing, routing, rate allocation and beam/frequency assignment at 10,000+ satellites, solved in seconds with a certified optimality gap (for example a Lagrangian dual bound), so operators know how much capacity the software leaves on the table.
comms-certified-network-optimization.status_oct2026: The per-snapshot joint problem is NP-hard. A Lagrangian decomposition into matching, shortest paths and an LP gains 35-145% throughput over non-joint baselines in simulation (arXiv 2601.21914), and a graph neural network that predicts the dual prices matches it orders of magnitude faster (arXiv 2601.21921). Topology designs tested on three months of Starlink data report up to 2.3x capacity and 45% lower delay than +Grid (arXiv 2602.07756). The baselines are naive and operator practice is proprietary. Family 120 (almost-linear exact matching and prescribed-degree factors, T1) solves the terminal-pairing subproblem asymptotically fast.
comms-certified-network-optimization.premise_tier: n/a (capability); T3 for the 102 ceiling, T1 for 117 hardness and 120
comms-certified-network-optimization.why: A certificate turns a capacity question into an investment decision. With a 3% dual gap, more capacity has to come from terminals, satellites or spectrum; with a 30% gap it can come from software. The math (decompositions, convergence and gap proofs, problem-specific relaxations) is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems (tl-position-4), so it becomes a P1 item as soon as research-grade models are public. The ceilings (UGC; 117, conditional) say that certified gaps must be instance-specific rather than worst-case.
comms-certified-network-optimization.strongest_case_small: Operators such as SpaceX already run strong in-house optimization. Realistic gain over their practice is probably 5-20% capacity (judgment), while V3 hardware is a 10x per-satellite step (33FG). Family 120 adds nothing practical at this scale: a 10,000-node, ~50,000-edge matching takes milliseconds with classical algorithms. Terminal count, acquisition time and gateway capacity bind first.
comms-certified-network-optimization.signpost: An operator, SDA or a vendor publishing optimality-gap metrics for live routing; an open solver with certified gaps at Starlink scale.

comms-verified-routing-software.title: Formally verified constellation control plane
comms-verified-routing-software.description: Machine-checked proofs that routing, handover and topology-reconfiguration code is loop-free and deadlock-free, converges under link churn and meets latency bounds. Agents produce the proofs and maintain them as the code changes.
comms-verified-routing-software.status_oct2026: An agent extended a 3,000-line SMT network verifier with OSPF areas, BGP route reflection and L3VPN by counterexample-guided learning against emulated routers (arXiv 2608.11340, Aug 2026). Satellite-specific work is small, for example model checking of a TDM inter-satellite-link algorithm (arXiv 2511.09485). The broader evidence is the openai/math pipeline: 127 families with agent-written Lean (T3), strongest in discrete mathematics, which is what protocols need.
comms-verified-routing-software.why: With handovers about every 15 s and a continuously changing topology, test coverage of control-plane states is poor; proofs cover all states. Commercial communications networks face no certification gate, so progress is limited by writing specifications of dynamic topologies, which agents began doing in 2026. Discrete properties formalize well: 20 of 40 theoretical-CS families in the release have Lean proofs.
comms-verified-routing-software.strongest_case_small: Mega-constellation operators ship software weekly and value iteration speed over proofs. Outages come more from hardware faults, space weather and the ground segment than from routing logic, and orbital dynamics and timing are hard to specify.
comms-verified-routing-software.signpost: An operator or SDA prime disclosing machine-checked proofs for routing or handover code; a satellite-network verifier released by a lab or vendor.

comms-pq-verified-implementations.title: Proven-correct post-quantum crypto for space processors
comms-pq-verified-implementations.description: Agents produce implementations of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, HQC and hash-based signatures for radiation-tolerant processors and FPGAs. Each comes with machine-checked functional correctness, constant-time and masking (side-channel) proofs, plus certified failure-probability bounds.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.status_oct2026: Exists for mainstream CPUs, not yet for space hardware. The Jasmin compiler is proven to preserve the IND-CCA security of an ML-KEM implementation used in Signal (Rocq, arXiv 2511.11292). Lean 4 proofs of arithmetic masking for NTT hardware found that one open accelerator masks only one round (arXiv 2604.20793). A certified ML-KEM-768 decryption-failure bound of 2^-164.81 holds in a stated abstraction (arXiv 2609.09983). NIST picked HQC as its backup KEM on Mar 11 2025; final standard expected 2027.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.why: Most real cryptographic failures are implementation bugs and side channels, not broken mathematics (general). Space adds unusual targets (LEON or radiation-hardened RISC-V cores, FPGAs) and tight memory, so verified libraries must be re-targeted and re-proven. That is proof labor, which agents now supply. Achieved here means a verified library for a space-grade target exists and a flight program uses it; certification credit is a separate node.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.strongest_case_small: FIPS 140-3 and NSA evaluations are test-based and slow. Many satellites use certified hardware crypto modules where code proofs add little, and programs freeze crypto choices years before launch.
comms-pq-verified-implementations.signpost: A verified ML-KEM, ML-DSA or LMS library released for a radiation-hardened processor; a flight program citing machine-checked crypto proofs.

comms-code-design-on-demand.title: Custom channel codes on request
comms-code-design-on-demand.description: AI designs codes and decoders for specific links, with machine-checked finite-blocklength performance claims. Targets: short packets for direct-to-device signaling, IoT and telecommand; photon-counting optical links; synchronization and deletion channels.
comms-code-design-on-demand.status_oct2026: LLM-guided search found seven record binary linear codes, improving 22 table entries, each verified exhaustively (arXiv 2609.37056, Sep 2026). A search for quantum LDPC bivariate-bicycle codes cost about $400 of inference (arXiv 2606.02418). AI-assisted, Lean-formalized information-theory results appeared in Sep 2026: a deletion-channel capacity upper bound (arXiv 2609.13351) and three binary-channel conjectures (arXiv 2609.27991). Short-block polar and LDPC designs sit fractions of a dB from finite-blocklength bounds (arXiv 2503.02782, 2512.17834).
comms-code-design-on-demand.why: Long-block codes are near capacity, so the remaining gains are in short blocks and unusual channels, where design is expert-scarce rather than open. 0.5 dB is about 12% power, and on a handset uplink at the edge of a beam that can decide whether a link closes. Adoption runs through 3GPP and CCSDS standards cycles of 2-4 years, which binds even in S3.
comms-code-design-on-demand.strongest_case_small: Coding gains are small next to antenna gain, power and spectrum. Standards bodies are conservative, decoder complexity, latency and patents decide adoption, and most space links already use standardized LDPC, turbo or polar codes.
comms-code-design-on-demand.signpost: A 3GPP NTN or CCSDS contribution containing an AI-designed code; AI-found record codes appearing in a product.

comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.title: Tight, machine-checked security proofs for satellite QKD
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.description: Composable finite-key security proofs for satellite QKD passes (decoy-state BB84, BBM92, continuous-variable QKD) that include real device imperfections and non-IID signals. Numerical parts are certified and the core argument is formalized.
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.status_oct2026: Human progress in 2026: an analytic finite-key proof with source and detector imperfections (arXiv 2606.29943); a numerical framework valid against coherent attacks with non-IID signals (arXiv 2605.12984); a GEO-QKD finite-key feasibility study (arXiv 2605.29706). Entanglement-based passes are finite-key limited (arXiv 2602.11833). Lean-QIT (arXiv 2607.09632) is the first reusable Lean layer for quantum Shannon theory. Catalog: 276 [L] T3; 272 T1.
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.premise_tier: T3 (276); T1 (272), conditional for that part
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.why: A LEO pass gives a few minutes of link; Jinan-1 shared up to 1.07 Mbit of secure key per pass (Nature, Mar 2025). At such block sizes finite-key penalties are large, and evaluators do not accept proofs that ignore device flaws. Tighter proofs that include imperfections raise certified key per pass (judgment: 10-40% at short passes). More important, they are what a security evaluation needs. The math is hard but within research-grade applied math. Formalization waits on quantum-information coverage in Lean, which S2 assumes catches up during 2027-29.
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.strongest_case_small: Key yield is set by loss, background light, weather and detectors, so proof tightness adds tens of percent at most. Satellite QKD as flown uses trusted nodes, so the satellite stays a point of trust whatever the proof says.
comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs.signpost: Eagle-1, SpeQtre or QEYSSat publishing security analyses with machine-checked components; an ETSI or ISO QKD evaluation citing formal proofs.

comms-optical-availability-models.title: Certified availability for optical ground networks
comms-optical-availability-models.description: Validated stochastic models of cloud, turbulence and pointing outage that predict the availability of a whole optical ground network with site diversity, with bounds good enough to sign service-level agreements against.
comms-optical-availability-models.status_oct2026: The bottleneck has moved from peak rate to repeatable service (Turyshev, arXiv 2606.23711, Jun 2026). NASA LCRD two-site combinations gave 83.8-88.5% availability; high reliability may need about 10 sites at least 500 km apart; fixed cost is of order $3-4k per TB at 0.5 h/day of contact. Peak demonstrations: 200 Gbps from LEO (TBIRD), 1.8 Gbps operational GEO relay (EDRS), 267 Mbps from about 19 million miles (DSOC, which ended Sep 2 2025 after returning 13.6 Tbit).
comms-optical-availability-models.why: Availability is a correlated-weather problem. Long cloud climatologies exist, so the modeling is cognitive work that compresses under S2. Validation needs multi-year availability records from operating optical networks, which only accumulate in real time; that data gate holds S3 to the S2 year.
comms-optical-availability-models.strongest_case_small: Availability is bounded by climatology, and site selection already uses standard cloud statistics, so better models move siting by a few percent. The number of telescopes, a capital decision, sets availability.
comms-optical-availability-models.signpost: ESA, NASA, KSAT or a commercial optical network publishing measured multi-site availability against predictions.

comms-quantum-receiver-theory.title: Receivers that beat photon counting
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.description: Theory and practical designs for joint-detection optical receivers that recover part of the gap between pulse-position modulation with photon counting and the Holevo limit, at deep-space photon flux and realistic background light.
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.status_oct2026: The Green Machine receiver showed superadditive capacity over any symbol-by-symbol receiver with BPSK in the photon-starved regime (Nature Communications, 2025). Photon-information-efficiency limits for PPM are reviewed in arXiv 2503.13161; a greedy receiver approaches the Helstrom bound for PPM (arXiv 2403.02634). DSOC used PPM with a 64-pixel superconducting-nanowire detector array (76% detection efficiency) at Palomar. Single-user Holevo capacity of the lossy channel is already known (general), so this node does not depend on family 273.
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.why: In the photon-starved regime, each extra bit per received photon is worth as much as a larger ground aperture, and aperture is the dominant cost of a deep-space optical ground terminal. Designing structured quantum measurements with provable gains is theory work that compresses under S2 (cap-physics-theory by 2028-29). Proving that the gain survives background light, loss and timing jitter needs laboratory experiments.
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.strongest_case_small: Joint-detection gains shrink quickly with background light and receiver optical loss, and daytime and near-Sun links are background limited. PPM with superconducting detectors is already within a few dB of practical limits (general), and no deep-space optical mission committed before 2031 is known to plan for such a receiver (general).
comms-quantum-receiver-theory.signpost: A lab demonstration of a receiver beating optimized PPM photon counting at deep-space-like flux with background; NASA or ESA funding a flight receiver study.

comms-constellation-design-optimizer.title: Constellation design with proven compliance
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.description: Design tools that co-optimize orbital shells, beam plans, spectrum use and laser topology, and output both a filing-ready design and certified interference and capacity bounds.
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.status_oct2026: More than 10,000 commercial communications satellites operate in LEO and 50,000+ more are planned; Amazon filed for a 5,105-satellite direct-to-cell constellation in Jul 2026 (Roberts). On Sep 30 2026 the FCC opened more than 1,000 MHz for satellite services in the 12.7-13.25 GHz and 42-42.5 GHz bands (33FG). Design tools are in-house and uncertified.
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.why: As filings multiply and sharing becomes performance-based, value moves to designs that are provably compliant and dense. That needs multiphysics design optimization with guarantees (cap-design-optimization, S2 2028-29) plus the two certified-bound nodes, so it trails them by about a year.
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.strongest_case_small: Constellation design is constrained by launch, manufacturing, spectrum rights and business plans. Filings are partly strategic placeholders, and incumbents' in-house tools are good.
comms-constellation-design-optimizer.signpost: A filing whose technical annex comes from a design optimizer with certified bounds; a tool vendor or new entrant shipping such a tool.

comms-hardness-aware-tasking.title: Tasking and ground planning built on proven limits
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.description: Tools for Earth-observation tasking, downlink scheduling, ground-station-as-a-service allocation and ground-station siting that combine exact solvers on structured instances, certified-gap heuristics and documented approximation ceilings, with AI formulating each mission's variant on request.
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.status_oct2026: EOS-Bench (arXiv 2604.25782) spans up to 1,000 satellites and 10,000 requests. Exact integer programming for ground-station selection stops scaling before Planet's 96-satellite fleet, while decomposition stays within 95% of optimum on small cases (arXiv 2510.03438). Ground-station-as-a-service revenue scheduling is NP-hard (arXiv 2608.22222). Catalog: 102 [L] T3; 124, 110, 111 and the 125 algorithm T1; 104 [L] T3 only for a randomized version (the deterministic headline and the stochastic and parity extensions are T1).
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.why: The ceiling effect is immediate, but most value comes from capability transfer. Each mission has its own constraints (agility, memory, energy, cloud forecasts, contact windows), and a model that formulates and proves a bespoke scheduler in hours replaces months of operations-research work. 124 (conditional) solves exactly the Garey-Johnson three-machine case: unit jobs with precedence constraints on three identical machines, such as three identical antennas or processors with dependency chains. 110 and 111 give worst-case guarantees for online request handling.
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.strongest_case_small: Tasking is limited by satellites, agility, cloud cover and downlink, which are physics and capital. The 1+2/e k-median algorithm needs candidate sites and does no better than MIP on siting problems with a few hundred candidates. 111 asserts no polynomial-time implementation, and 124 is a narrow special case.
comms-hardness-aware-tasking.signpost: Earth-observation operators or ground-station-as-a-service providers reporting AI-formulated schedulers with certified gaps; public benchmarks reporting optimality gaps alongside scores.

comms-crypto-agile-architecture.title: Crypto-agile satellites with proven update paths
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.description: Spacecraft security designs that can change algorithms in orbit: hybrid classical plus post-quantum key exchange, hash-based signatures for commands and software, and a code-based fallback such as HQC. Key-management, rekey and update protocols are proven secure by machine and sized for constrained links.
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.status_oct2026: NIST IR 8547 (draft, Nov 2024): RSA, ECDSA and ECDH at 112-bit security deprecated by 2030; all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms disallowed by 2035. NSA CNSA 2.0 sets national-security-system milestones running to 2035 (general). Post-quantum certificate-based authentication is costly on satellite links, which motivates pre-shared-key designs (arXiv 2607.23007) and quantum-safe IKE variants (arXiv 2605.28660). Gidney (arXiv 2505.15917, May 2025) cut the estimate for factoring RSA-2048 to under a million noisy qubits in under a week, from 20 million in 2019.
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.why: A GEO satellite launched in 2028 operates to about 2043: eight years past NIST's 2035 cutoff and possibly past the first code-breaking quantum computer. An in-orbit swap path is the only hedge, and it must work the first time. Proving the update and rekey protocols is proof labor that agents remove, and AI cryptanalysis (comms-ai-cryptanalysis) makes the threat model concrete. The band is capped at Medium because government programs need certification acceptance of the evidence.
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.strongest_case_small: Migration is mandated regardless of AI. Many satellites use pre-shared symmetric keys (AES-256) for telecommand, which are already quantum-safe, and certification bodies do not yet credit AI-produced proofs.
comms-crypto-agile-architecture.signpost: A CCSDS space-link-security profile with hybrid or post-quantum options; a GEO operator announcing in-orbit-updatable post-quantum crypto; NSA or NIAP accepting machine-checked protocol proofs as evidence.

comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.title: Flight demo of verified post-quantum command links
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.description: A satellite flies post-quantum or hybrid authenticated telecommand and key exchange using machine-checked implementations, and performs an in-orbit algorithm swap.
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.status_oct2026: We found no flight with machine-checked implementations. Several firms have announced post-quantum crypto demonstrations on small satellites since 2025 (general, unverified).
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.why: Once the architecture and verified code exist, a demo needs only a rideshare slot and a cooperative bus. Launch cadence does not bind for a cubesat-class demo, but integration lead times of 12-18 months do (general). The in-orbit swap is the new part: it shows the 15-year-asset problem can be managed.
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: This adds assurance, not capability. Post-quantum crypto can fly without proofs, and the first operators to need it (governments) will use their own certified modules.
comms-pq-ttc-flight-demo.signpost: An announced mission plan with an in-orbit post-quantum algorithm swap and published proofs.

comms-holevo-receiver-demo.title: Ground demo: optical receiver beats photon counting
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.description: A ground or lab demonstration in which a joint-detection receiver beats optimized PPM with photon counting by 25% or more in bits per received photon, at deep-space-like photon flux and background.
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.status_oct2026: Superadditivity has been shown in the lab with BPSK (Green Machine, 2025), but not under deep-space conditions with background light.
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.why: Even with designs in hand by 2029 (S2), building low-loss photonic circuits and testing them against realistic background takes a year or more. S3's autonomous labs shorten the iteration loop but not fabrication.
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.strongest_case_small: Gains shrink with background light and optical loss, the PPM-plus-SNSPD baseline keeps improving, and there is no flight slot to use such a receiver before 2031.
comms-holevo-receiver-demo.signpost: A peer-reviewed demonstration at photon flux and background matching a Mars-distance link.

comms-space-qkd-network-demo.title: Multi-node satellite QKD demonstrations
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.description: Satellite QKD missions deliver keys among three or more ground nodes in different countries in routine campaigns: Eagle-1 in-orbit validation, SpeQtre, QEYSSat, SPOQC and successors to China's Jinan-1.
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.status_oct2026: Jinan-1 (Nature, Mar 19 2025): 23 kg payload, ~100 kg portable ground station, up to 1.07 Mbit of secure key per pass, and a key between China and South Africa over 12,900 km (trusted-node satellite). ESA lists Eagle-1's launch for late 2026/early 2027, followed by three years of in-orbit validation. The SpeQtre ground campaign produced 7.56 kbps at 4.78% QBER over 1.8 km (arXiv 2605.19689). QEYSSat has a digital twin (arXiv 2608.21968), and the SPOQC continuous-variable QKD cubesat was planned for early 2026 (arXiv 2602.23510).
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.why: These missions are funded and largely built, so they run on the physical clock regardless of AI mathematics. They are the platform where AI-tightened proofs (comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs) would be applied.
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.strongest_case_small: This node is the physical anchor: no scenario moves it, and AI mathematics adds little to it.
comms-space-qkd-network-demo.signpost: Eagle-1 launch and its first published key-exchange campaign.

comms-certified-mesh-operations.title: Mega-constellation mesh run with certified optimality
comms-certified-mesh-operations.description: A large LEO operator runs laser-mesh routing and radio resource allocation in production with certified per-snapshot optimality gaps and verified control-plane software.
comms-certified-mesh-operations.status_oct2026: No operator has disclosed this. Starlink, Amazon Leo and SDA's transport layer (21 Tranche 1 satellites launched Sep 2025, per 33FG) run proprietary or government software stacks.
comms-certified-mesh-operations.why: Software rolls out at the speed of an operator's deployment pipeline, so this node tracks its cognitive prerequisites closely. Value: judgment of 5-20% more delivered capacity at fixed hardware, plus fewer control-plane outages. Mega-constellation revenues are tens of billions of dollars a year (general), so even 5% is a lot of money, which is why adoption is likely once the tools exist.
comms-certified-mesh-operations.strongest_case_small: Operators may already be near-optimal on their own instances. Hardware upgrades (V3: 10x per satellite) and the regulatory lift (EPFD reform, reported at up to 7x capacity) dwarf a software gain (33FG), and certificates are a nice-to-have.
comms-certified-mesh-operations.signpost: Operator engineering talks or filings citing optimality gaps or formal verification of routing; SDA contract language requiring them.

comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.title: Predictive coexistence scheduling for direct-to-device
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.description: Direct-to-device and broadband constellations schedule beams, power and emissions against certified interference budgets for adjacent bands, other operators and radio astronomy, instead of using blunt avoidance zones.
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.status_oct2026: SkyShare (arXiv 2609.00821) schedules spot beams within EPFD-budgeted regions and cuts unserved cells by up to 90.68% versus boresight avoidance at 25 radio-astronomy sites, using Starlink geometry. The 2620 MHz D2D downlink's second harmonic already causes at least 59% geodetic-VLBI data loss (arXiv 2608.11659). D2D spectrum is consolidating: in May 2026 the FCC approved EchoStar's spectrum sale to SpaceX with a $2.4B escrow, and Starlink's D2C service got a +10 dB power waiver in Mar 2025 (33FG).
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.why: Coexistence is moving from static masks to dynamic, budgeted scheduling, and doing it precisely gains operators served cells, so incentives line up. Certified budgets let science users and regulators trust a schedule without seeing proprietary traffic.
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.strongest_case_small: Harmonics and out-of-band emissions are fixed by filters in hardware, not by scheduling. D2D capacity is set by spectrum holdings, aperture size and power, and operators have weak incentives to protect science bands without regulation.
comms-d2d-coexistence-scheduling.signpost: An operator agreement with a radio observatory or NSF that uses predictive, budgeted scheduling; an FCC order referencing certified coexistence budgets.

comms-optical-ground-network-service.title: Weather-robust optical ground network service
comms-optical-ground-network-service.description: An optical ground network sells weather-inclusive availability of about 99% for LEO or GEO data return, using site diversity, availability models and autonomous scheduling.
comms-optical-ground-network-service.status_oct2026: Operational optical relay exists: EDRS at 1.8 Gbps, with 80,000+ links at 99.53% reliability (arXiv 2606.23711). Direct-to-ground optical service at high availability does not yet exist at scale.
comms-optical-ground-network-service.why: Better models and schedulers say where to put telescopes and how to use them. The telescopes, sites, fiber and staff are capital that no scenario makes free. S2 moves the date by removing the planning delay, not the build.
comms-optical-ground-network-service.strongest_case_small: RF ground networks already deliver, and demand for optical downlink may stay limited to a few high-rate customers. Capital cycles for ground networks are long.
comms-optical-ground-network-service.signpost: A commercial optical ground network announcing an availability service-level agreement; ESA or NASA contracting for optical ground service at a stated availability.

comms-space-qkd-backbone.title: Certified operational space QKD service
comms-space-qkd-backbone.description: A sovereign satellite QKD service routinely delivers keys to government users across 10 or more ground nodes, with a security evaluation that accepts its finite-key proof (for example EuroQCI's space segment).
comms-space-qkd-backbone.status_oct2026: Demonstrations only (see comms-space-qkd-network-demo). China is likely to field an operational quantum-communication constellation first, on its own timeline (general, unverified).
comms-space-qkd-backbone.why: The service needs satellites, ground terminals and a security evaluation; AI mathematics shortens only the evaluation. The band is capped at Medium because it needs certification acceptance. The physical clock (procurement, launch) sets the year, which is why S3 equals S2.
comms-space-qkd-backbone.strongest_case_small: Western security agencies have preferred post-quantum cryptography to QKD for national-security use (general). Trusted-node satellites limit the security gain, and budgets may go to PQC instead.
comms-space-qkd-backbone.signpost: A EuroQCI space-segment procurement award; an accredited security evaluation of a satellite QKD service.

comms-pq-fleet-migration.title: Satellite fleets crypto-agile before the 2035 cutoff
comms-pq-fleet-migration.description: From this year, most new government and major commercial satellites carry in-orbit-updatable post-quantum crypto with machine-checked update paths, and legacy fleets are protected by ground-side controls.
comms-pq-fleet-migration.status_oct2026: Government migration planning is under way (NIST IR 8547, CNSA 2.0); space-specific post-quantum profiles are still being written (general).
comms-pq-fleet-migration.why: Mandates drive the migration; AI mathematics makes the verified version affordable. Procurement cycles (contracts signed 2-4 years before launch) set the pace, which is why S3 does not beat S2.
comms-pq-fleet-migration.strongest_case_small: The migration happens with or without AI proofs. The AI contribution is assurance quality, which buyers may not pay for.
comms-pq-fleet-migration.signpost: Government satellite RFPs requiring crypto-agility and machine-checked evidence; the first GEO comsat contract with in-orbit post-quantum update.

comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.title: Software's share of constellation capacity gains
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.description: AI-produced mathematics and software (certified optimization, coexistence scheduling, custom codes, design tools) account for at least 10% of a major constellation's gain in usable capacity per satellite between 2026 and 2031.
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.status_oct2026: Capacity gains for 2026-2031 are dominated by hardware (V3 satellites: a 10x per-satellite step) and regulation (EPFD reform; Ku co-frequency beams per location from 1 to 8) (33FG).
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.why: If hardware gives 10x and software 10-30% on top, software's share of the multiplied gain is small, but at mega-constellation scale it can be billions of dollars a year (judgment). Under S2 the software nodes land in 2028-29, so the effect is visible by 2030.
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.strongest_case_small: Attribution is nearly impossible from outside and operators will not disclose it; hardware and spectrum dominate.
comms-capacity-per-dollar-share.signpost: Operator statements attributing capacity gains to software or AI; capacity per satellite rising faster than hardware specifications imply.

comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.title: Machine-checked crypto becomes a procurement norm
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.description: Government space buyers (for example SDA, or ESA for IRIS²) require machine-checked implementation and protocol proofs for the security functions of new satellites.
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.status_oct2026: We found no such requirement. Aviation already gives credit for formal methods (DO-333) (general), but AI-produced proofs are not qualified tools today (tl-position-6).
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.why: Once proofs are cheap and have been shown in flight, buyers can demand them at little cost; this is the strategic payoff of the verification channel. The band is capped at Medium because it needs tool qualification and regulator acceptance.
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.strongest_case_small: Procurement rules change slowly and are written by people who distrust AI-generated evidence. Tool qualification may lag well past 2031.
comms-verified-crypto-procurement-norm.signpost: An SDA, ESA or NSA solicitation listing machine-checked proofs as a requirement or evaluation credit.

comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.title: International shift to provable spectrum sharing
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.description: The ITU follows the FCC in replacing fixed EPFD limits with performance-based sharing criteria and checkable compliance showings.
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.status_oct2026: The FCC moved domestically on Apr 30 2026 (33FG). ITU Radio Regulations Article 22 EPFD limits remain, and changing them needs a decision at a World Radiocommunication Conference: WRC-27 in late 2027, the next around 2031 (general).
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.why: Certified showings remove one technical objection to performance-based rules (that compliance cannot be checked). The decision itself is political and runs on a four-year conference cycle that needs consensus among administrations, many of them protective of GSO incumbents. No scenario moves the calendar.
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.strongest_case_small: GSO operators and many administrations oppose relaxing the limits, and the issue may not be on an agenda before the conference around 2031.
comms-performance-based-sharing-regime.signpost: The WRC-27 outcome on Article 22 and the agenda set for the following conference; ITU-R study groups adopting performance-based methods.

comms-crqc-before-2031.title: Code-breaking quantum computer before 2031
comms-crqc-before-2031.description: A quantum computer able to break RSA-2048 or 256-bit elliptic-curve keys exists before the end of 2031. It would expose legacy satellite links and any recorded traffic protected by them.
comms-crqc-before-2031.status_oct2026: Gidney (May 2025): RSA-2048 needs under a million noisy qubits running for under a week. Family 279 (exact quantum factoring over a fixed gate set, T1) makes Shor's algorithm succeed with probability one in theory but does not reduce qubit or error-correction budgets (tl-position-5). The largest systems remain far below that scale (general).
comms-crqc-before-2031.why: This is a hardware race. Under S3, AI that speeds up its own hardware and runs closed-loop experiments could also compress quantum-hardware design loops; that is the only route by which the world of this release raises the risk. Fabrication, yield and cryogenics still bind. It matters here because any satellite whose key exchange is RSA or ECC, and whose traffic was recorded, is exposed when this node fires, which is why the crypto-agility nodes matter now.
comms-crqc-before-2031.strongest_case_small: Scaling from today's hundreds to thousands of physical qubits to about a million error-corrected qubits in five years is far beyond historical trends, and most expert surveys put it later (general).
comms-crqc-before-2031.signpost: Logical-qubit demonstrations at scale with error rates below threshold; new resource estimates below 100,000 noisy qubits for RSA-2048.

frontier-applied-posing.title: Engineering math posed as precise problems
frontier-applied-posing.description: Engineers and AI agents translate engineering questions (a stability margin, an error bound, whether a sensor layout determines a material property) into precise mathematical statements with explicit assumptions, ideally Lean-stated, and pool them in open problem banks like the ~4,000 problems OpenAI posed for pure mathematics.
frontier-applied-posing.status_oct2026: No applied problem bank exists at that scale. The Oct 6 problem set was pure-math-skewed: 16 PDE and 12 dynamics families of 372; formalized 3 of 16 and 2 of 12. First applied formal benchmarks: CAM-Bench (May 2026, 1,000 Lean targets in optimization, numerical linear algebra, numerical analysis; many textbook concepts missing from Mathlib) and StochBench (Sep 2026, 450 stochastic-process problems; best agent 34.9%). Ilin (Mar 2026) formalized a Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium result in 10 days for ~$200 with agents and zero human-written code; the failures were 'hypothesis creep' and 'definition-alignment bugs', which are posing errors, not proving errors.
frontier-applied-posing.why: For most applied problems the hard step is the statement, not the proof: which norm, which regime, which idealization. The catalog shows capability on hard PDE (362 Vlasov-Maxwell, the forced Navier-Stokes blowup), so the scarcity of applied results reflects what was posed. Under S2 models pose candidate statements from engineering context and agents build missing library pieces (Urban 2026: 130k lines of topology in two weeks for ~$100), so a 1,000+ problem applied bank is plausible by 2027. Human review of definitions remains essential (Ilin). This node gates frontier-xc-certified and frontier-math-unbinds and, outside this domain, every P2 verification chain.
frontier-applied-posing.strongest_case_small: Much of applied mathematics' value lies in modeling judgment that does not reduce to theorem statements; engineers do not think in theorems; export control (ITAR/EAR) and proprietary concerns will keep the most valuable space problems out of open banks, so posing stays artisanal inside each program.
frontier-applied-posing.signpost: NASA, ESA, DARPA or AIAA publishes a formally stated applied open-problem bank (500+ problems), or a lab releases 50+ PDE/numerics/UQ/control families in one release.

frontier-euler-blowup-r3.title: Euler blowup in open space, proven
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.description: A rigorous, likely computer-assisted, proof that the 3D incompressible Euler equations on R^3 with no boundary form a finite-time singularity from smooth, finite-energy data. It is the inviscid, unforced stepping stone to the Navier-Stokes question.
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.status_oct2026: Proven with a boundary by Chen-Hou (computer-assisted, 2022-23); Chen-Hou posted clarification notes in Jul and Aug 2026 answering a 2025 critique, so such proofs take years to settle. Low-regularity C^{1,alpha} blowup without boundary is known (Elgindi 2021, general; Chen May 2026). Smooth data on R^3: numerical evidence only. DeepMind's 'Discovery of unstable singularities' (Sep 2025) reached near double-precision profiles for the boundary case. Ganeshram-Duruisseaux-Anandkumar (Sep 2026) report a candidate self-similar R^3 profile and a stability framework; the finite set of explicit estimates is still missing. Forced Euler blowup was announced machine-checked by Alpoge-Buckmaster (Sep 2026). Not in the openai/math catalog.
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.why: All ingredients exist: an AI-found candidate profile, a stability framework, and computer-assisted estimate machinery. What remains is a large finite set of verified inequalities, which agentic proof plus interval arithmetic does well. Difficulty is at the level that fell on Oct 6 (judgment: 0 doublings beyond). Acceptance is the slow part: the bar is a Lean or independently re-run proof, given the Chen-Hou history. It unlocks frontier-ns-unforced and the MHD blowup question, since ideal MHD with zero field is Euler.
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.strongest_case_small: No engineering effect. Euler is inviscid, and any singularity would sit far below the molecular mean free path in a real fluid. Its value is as a credibility signal and a stepping stone.
frontier-euler-blowup-r3.signpost: A Lean- or interval-verified proof of smooth R^3 Euler blowup, with an independent re-run (Hexagon, Comparator or a second group).

frontier-ns-unforced.title: Navier-Stokes Millennium problem settled
frontier-ns-unforced.description: Resolution of the actual Clay statements (A)/(B) for the unforced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations: global smoothness, or finite-time blowup from smooth data on R^3 or the torus.
frontier-ns-unforced.status_oct2026: Open. OpenAI's Sep 8, 2026 claim covers only the forced statements (C)/(D) (Lean, T3). A self-published replay (Sep 17, 2026) reports the Lean certificate builds with no sorry; this is not a Comparator run with a statement audit, so the tier is unchanged. Lei-Ren (Sep 28) wrote an expository reconstruction of the profile construction and call it 'a major advance'. Petrillo-Glimm (Sep 20) proposed the 'positive defect problem' as the target for a programmatic unforced search. Family 376 (T1) embeds universal computation in forced flows, Tao's proposed route to blowup.
frontier-ns-unforced.why: One rung beyond what fell. Removing the forcing means the singularity must sustain itself against viscosity, likely via an unstable self-similar profile stabilized by a computer-assisted argument, or a Tao-style computing flow. Judgment: 1-2 difficulty doublings past the Oct 2026 level. Under S2 (a doubling every 6-9 months) the gap closes around 2029, and under S3 around 2028. Either answer acts only through P5. Years match the propulsion domain's prop-ns-clay-unforced.
frontier-ns-unforced.strongest_case_small: Zero engineering effect. CFD codes regularize, any blowup would sit below molecular scales, and a regularity proof confirms what every code assumes. The public reception ('AI solved fluid dynamics') may exceed the technical effect; the paper should address this head-on.
frontier-ns-unforced.signpost: A lab claims unforced blowup or regularity with a Lean proof and the Clay Institute responds; or no credible claim by end-2029, which favors S1.

frontier-turbulence-rigorous.title: Turbulence laws proven
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.description: Theorems that 3D Navier-Stokes with natural forcing (smooth, generic or white-in-time) dissipates energy at a rate independent of viscosity (the 'zeroth law') and obeys Kolmogorov-type inertial-range scaling, in a well-posed statistical framework.
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.status_oct2026: Onsager's conjecture is proven for Euler (Isett 2018; intermittent version Novack-Vicol 2023). Anomalous dissipation for forced Navier-Stokes is known only for constructed forcings (Brue-De Lellis 2023, general), now shown stable under geometric perturbation (C. Li, May 2026). Anomalous diffusion of passive scalars is proven (Armstrong-Vicol 2025), and the Kolmogorov 4/5 law holds conditionally for stochastic forcing (Bedrossian et al. 2019, general). The zeroth law for generic forcing and any intermittency correction remain open. No catalog family.
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.why: This is the theory engineering actually wants, because closures need statistics, not trajectories. It is harder than NS regularity in one respect: the right statements must be invented, so posing is part of the problem (judgment: 2-4 doublings plus posing). Chain: zeroth law and scaling, then a rigorous LES convergence theory (prop-les-convergence-theory), then closures with error bounds for canonical flows, then (data-gated) engineering closures (prop-closure-theory, hyper-sbli-heating-closure).
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.strongest_case_small: Kolmogorov scaling has been built into turbulence models since 1941, so a proof changes no RANS or LES practice. The costly engineering errors come from wall-bounded separation, transition, compressibility and chemistry, where DNS and experiment data bind, not theorems.
frontier-turbulence-rigorous.signpost: A proof of the zeroth law for Navier-Stokes on the torus with a fixed smooth or white-in-time forcing; or a lab release with a turbulence-theory family.

frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.title: Boltzmann and Landau equations proven well-behaved
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.description: Global existence, uniqueness and smoothness for the space-inhomogeneous Boltzmann and Landau equations with physical interactions (including Coulomb and very soft potentials), far from equilibrium. These are the kinetic equations behind rarefied reentry, DSMC and collisional plasmas.
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.status_oct2026: The space-homogeneous cases are done: Landau with Coulomb potential does not blow up (Guillen-Silvestre, Acta Math. 2025), and homogeneous Boltzmann with very soft potentials follows from monotone Fisher information (Imbert-Silvestre-Villani 2024). Inhomogeneous: regularity is known conditional on hydrodynamic bounds (Imbert-Silvestre program; Fernandez-Real-Ros-Oton-Weidner 2025), and a new continuation criterion rules out Euler-type blowup lifting into kinetics (Golding-Henderson-Silvestre, May 2026). The catalog claims 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation, T1) and 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian gases over its lifespan, with fluctuations, T1); 362 (relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, T3) shows problems of this kind now fall.
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.premise_tier: n/a (analog evidence: 362 at T3; 363/364 at T1, conditional)
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.why: Comparable in difficulty to 362, which was claimed in the Sep-Oct run, and the human program is close: conditional regularity reduces it to hydrodynamic bounds, and there is a new continuation criterion. Under S2 a lab that poses it settles it within a release cycle. Effect: P5 confidence for DSMC and kinetic codes, plus quantitative moment and decay bounds that feed solver error control (hyper-kinetic-solver-certification, plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics).
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.strongest_case_small: DSMC and kinetic codes have matched wind-tunnel and flight data for decades. Any inhomogeneous blowup would occur far from reentry conditions. The binding errors in rarefied aerothermodynamics are gas-surface interaction and chemistry data.
frontier-kinetic-global-regularity.signpost: A proof (human or AI) of global regularity for the inhomogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, or a lab kinetic-theory family covering it.

frontier-nonuniqueness-map.title: Where fluid and kinetic models are not unique
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.description: A systematic set of nonuniqueness and ill-posedness results, with matching uniqueness criteria, for the Euler, Navier-Stokes, Boltzmann and MHD models engineers simulate. It marks which regimes need an extra selection principle (entropy condition, vanishing-viscosity limit, finer physics).
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.status_oct2026: Convex integration gives nonuniqueness of weak Euler and NS solutions (general), including for compressible Euler with Riemann data (Chiodaroli-De Lellis-Kreml 2015, general), and sharp forced nonuniqueness for SQG (ARMA, Oct 2026). Ill-posedness in supercritical Sobolev spaces (Duke, Aug 2026). Catalog: 363 Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation (T1); 376 universal computation in forced NS (T1); the Sep 8 forced NS blowup (T3).
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.why: Negative results act fastest (analyst position d). A nonuniqueness theorem for a regime tells V&V teams that solver-to-solver disagreement there may come from the equation rather than the code, and tells modelers where to add a selection principle. Convex-integration constructions are long, technical and constructive, which suits agents. Feeds frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd and hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.strongest_case_small: The constructions use wild, low-regularity data (velocity below Holder 1/3) with no physical counterpart, and numerical dissipation already acts as a selection principle. Practitioners have lived with Scheffer-Shnirelman nonuniqueness since the 1990s without changing practice.
frontier-nonuniqueness-map.signpost: A nonuniqueness result for compressible NS or Boltzmann with physically reasonable data (bounded entropy, shock-tube-like), cited by a CFD V&V or DSMC group.

frontier-landau-damping-general.title: Landau damping proven for realistic plasmas
frontier-landau-damping-general.description: Nonlinear Landau damping (collisionless relaxation of plasma waves) proven beyond the idealized setting: Sobolev data, whole space, magnetized plasmas, weak collisions and full electromagnetic (Vlasov-Maxwell) fields, with explicit rates.
frontier-landau-damping-general.status_oct2026: Mouhot-Villani (2011, torus, Gevrey) is now Lean-formalized (Bedrossian, Sep 2026). Unconfined 3D near Poisson equilibrium (Nguyen-Wei-Zhang 2024-25); unconfined 2D (Ionescu-Nguyen, Sep 2026); screened two-species with large data (Mar 2026); weak-collision Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck (Luo 2024); Sobolev echo counterexamples (Bedrossian 2016, general). Magnetized and full Vlasov-Maxwell long-time behavior are open. Catalog 362 (T3) supplies global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, a prerequisite for long-time questions.
frontier-landau-damping-general.why: An active human program is closing in, and the difficulty is catalog-level. Formalization has started (Bedrossian), so kinetic theory is now formalizable despite the 3-of-16 PDE formalization rate. Downstream, quantitative damping rates and echo thresholds justify the linear dispersion relations used in electric-propulsion and space-weather wave models and inform kinetic closures (plasma-kinetic-closures). Overlaps the plasma domain's plasma-landau-longtime.
frontier-landau-damping-general.strongest_case_small: Plasma physics has used Landau damping since 1946 and confirmed it experimentally. Proofs give rates in small-perturbation regimes where linear theory already works, and Hall-thruster anomalous transport is turbulence, not damping.
frontier-landau-damping-general.signpost: A proof of nonlinear Landau damping for a magnetized Vlasov-Poisson or Vlasov-Maxwell system in Sobolev regularity.

frontier-mhd-wellposedness.title: Which plasma fluid models are well-posed
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.description: A map of well-posedness, singularity formation and ill-posedness for ideal, resistive, Hall and electron MHD in 3D, the models used for space weather, magnetic nozzles and fusion-propulsion concepts. A stretch goal is rigorous bounds on magnetic reconnection rates.
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.status_oct2026: Local well-posedness is classical. 3D global regularity is open and inherits Euler's difficulty: ideal MHD with zero field is Euler, so a smooth R^3 Euler blowup gives ideal MHD blowup directly. Hall-MHD is ill-posed near some steady states (Jeong-Oh 2022, general); reduced electron-MHD models form singularities (Dai 2025); ideal MHD below the classical threshold (Giardi, Sep 2026). Fast reconnection lacks rigorous theory. No catalog family.
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.why: Ill-posedness matters in practice: codes that include Hall terms need regularization, and a full map tells space-weather and nozzle modelers which models give results that converge under refinement (P3). Blowup results follow from Euler techniques, while reconnection-rate bounds are harder (judgment: 1-2 doublings). Weak feed to plasma-eruption-onset-theory and plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.strongest_case_small: Space-weather forecast skill is limited by solar boundary data (magnetograms) and coronal physics, not well-posedness. Operational solar-wind codes carry known numerical diffusion that already regularizes.
frontier-mhd-wellposedness.signpost: A proof of finite-time blowup or of ill-posedness for 3D Hall-MHD or ideal MHD from smooth data, or a rigorous resistive reconnection-rate bound.

frontier-nbody-arnold-diffusion.title: Long-term orbital stability with real constants
frontier-nbody-arnold-diffusion.description: Quantitative KAM, Nekhoroshev and Arnold-diffusion theorems for realistic n-body parameters: rigorous lower bounds on stability times and upper bounds on diffusion rates for the solar system, resonant asteroid and cislunar orbits, and long-lived constellation dynamics.
frontier-nbody-arnold-diffusion.status_oct2026: Arnold diffusion is proven in the planetary spatial 4-body problem (Clarke-Fejoz-Guardia, Publ. IHES 2024), and a degenerate mechanism in the restricted 3-body problem (Guardia-Paradela-Seara, Ann. ENS, Dec 2025). KAM for planetary systems is known only for tiny masses (general). Solar-system instability is known numerically (Laskar: ~1% chance of Mercury destabilizing in 5 Gyr, general). The catalog touches only model maps: 146 Sinai positive entropy of the standard map (T1), 347 strong Arnold fixed-point counterexamples (T3), 343 sharp symplectic ball packing (T1). It has no n-body results.
frontier-nbody-arnold-diffusion.premise_tier: T1/T3 (model maps only; n-body target unproven)
frontier-nbody-arnold-diffusion.why: KAM and Nekhoroshev constants are notoriously tiny. Theorems with realistic constants need high-order normal forms with interval arithmetic, exactly the long, careful work agents scale (judgment: 1-2 doublings plus heavy computation). Finite-horizon (years to decades) transport bounds for cislunar orbits are easier and expert-scarce; they belong to astro-nbody-transport-proofs and astro-stability-atlas, which this node strengthens.
frontier-nbody-arnold-diffusion.strongest_case_small: Missions use numerical propagation with margins and station-keeping, so billion-year stability theorems change nothing operational. The effect lands in astronomy and planetary science, not in flown systems.
frontier-nbody-arnold-diffusion.signpost: A computer-assisted proof of explicit stability-time or diffusion-rate bounds for a realistic Sun-Jupiter-Saturn or Earth-Moon resonance configuration.

frontier-chaos-linear-response.title: Derivatives of chaotic averages
frontier-chaos-linear-response.description: Theorems that long-time averages of chaotic systems (turbulent flows, plasma turbulence, the thermosphere) depend differentiably on design parameters, with computable bounds and convergent algorithms. This is the mathematics that would let adjoint and gradient optimization work on unsteady turbulent systems.
frontier-chaos-linear-response.status_oct2026: Linear response is proven for uniformly hyperbolic systems (Ruelle, general) but fails or is unproven for most realistic, non-hyperbolic dynamics. Shadowing-based sensitivity methods work heuristically at high cost (general). Rigorous enclosures of Lyapunov exponents exist for stochastic flows (2024). Catalog: 146 Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard map (T1), a famous non-hyperbolic chaos problem, suggests the capability has reached this terrain.
frontier-chaos-linear-response.why: Adjoint design is routine for steady flows but breaks for unsteady chaotic flows, because pathwise sensitivities grow like exp(lambda*t). Combustors, nozzles and thrusters are therefore designed by sampling, at roughly one simulation per parameter direction. A theorem saying when averaged sensitivities exist, with an algorithm, would turn chaotic-flow design into gradient optimization with thousands of parameters (frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design). A negative answer would also help (P3), since it ends a research line. This is an under-appreciated node: less famous than Navier-Stokes, far more consequential for design.
frontier-chaos-linear-response.strongest_case_small: Surrogate and Bayesian optimization with a few hundred simulations already handles modest parameter counts. Realistic flows may lack linear response in the needed regimes, and most design value comes from validated physics models, not gradients.
frontier-chaos-linear-response.signpost: A proof of linear response with a convergent sensitivity algorithm for a non-uniformly hyperbolic flow class (a Lorenz-type flow or a Galerkin-truncated Navier-Stokes system).

frontier-approx-ceilings.title: Proven limits for scheduling and network planning
frontier-approx-ceilings.description: Hardness-of-approximation ceilings for the combinatorial problems behind constellation tasking, ground-station siting, routing and network partitioning become verified theorems rather than beliefs, so planning tools and vendor claims are judged against known limits.
frontier-approx-ceilings.status_oct2026: Catalog: 102 Unique Games Conjecture (T3), which makes Goemans-Williamson Max-Cut (0.878) and 2-approximate vertex cover optimal; 125 metric k-median threshold 1+2/e, about 1.736 (T3); 117 uniform sparsest cut hardness (T3); 104 quasipolynomial mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games (T3); 124 polynomial-time scheduling on three identical machines (T1); 110 optimal randomized k-server (T1); 111 matroid prophet inequalities (T1). No outside Comparator run reported as of Oct 7, 2026; repo has a single initial commit.
frontier-approx-ceilings.why: Ceilings take effect within months (P3), once they are independently checked. Most were already believed, so the change is from belief to theorem: research spending moves from better general approximation algorithms to instance structure, exact MIP on small instances and learned heuristics. Volumes are large (Starlink performed 144,000+ collision-avoidance maneuvers in six months, per 33FG), but these are operational problems where structure dominates. This node bounds frontier-scalable-global-certificates.
frontier-approx-ceilings.strongest_case_small: Worst-case hardness says little about structured operational instances, and satellite scheduling already solves well in practice (branch-and-cut-and-price, EJOR 2025). These ceilings were assumed for 20 years.
frontier-approx-ceilings.signpost: An independent Comparator run plus statement audit on families 102, 125 and 117 (Hexagon or Buzzard's group).

frontier-nn-verification-complexity.title: How hard neural networks are to verify
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.description: A complete complexity map for verifying the properties of neural networks used in perception and control (robustness, reachability, Lipschitz bounds), including which architectures or training regimes make verification tractable.
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.status_oct2026: ReLU network verification is NP-complete (Katz et al. 2017, general). Sep 2025: deciding positivity of an l-layer ReLU network is W[l-1]-hard in input dimension; approximating the maximum or the Lipschitz constant is NP-hard; naive n^((l-1)d) enumeration is essentially optimal under ETH (Froese et al.). Tractable classes are partly characterized. Catalog: 102 UGC (T3) supplies hardness machinery; nothing is NN-specific.
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.why: Ceilings tell assurance architects that exact verification of large perception networks will not scale (exponential in input dimension under ETH). That pushes flight designs toward runtime assurance (simplex wrappers; verif-runtime-assurance) and verifiable-by-construction controllers. Positive results on tractable classes feed verif-nn-verification-scale. Complexity theory is the area where AI math is already strongest (40 TCS families, 20 with Lean).
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.strongest_case_small: Practitioners already know NN verification is hard and already use runtime monitors. The real blocker is specification: there is no formal statement of what 'detect the docking port' means.
frontier-nn-verification-complexity.signpost: A tractability theorem for a practically used architecture class (for example Lipschitz-constrained CNNs at flight scale), or fixed-depth hardness of approximate robustness certification.

frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.title: Capacity limits of laser and quantum links settled
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.description: Proofs of the ultimate data rates of the optical and quantum channels used for deep-space laser links and satellite QKD (bosonic thermal-noise channels, amplitude damping), turning conditional capacity formulas into theorems.
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.status_oct2026: Catalog: 273 entropy photon-number inequality (T1), which makes capacity formulas for bosonic thermal and broadcast channels unconditional; 276 classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping (T3); 272 entanglement without secret key (T1); 266 exactly three MUBs in dimension six (T1). Quantum capacities with superadditivity remain open (general).
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.why: Link budgets for optical deep-space and inter-satellite links quote capacity bounds. These become unconditional (P5 confidence), and QKD security proofs gain exact limits. Bands are one step down from the P5 default because the key premise (273) is T1. Under S2, verification bandwidth rises and 273 likely reaches T4 by 2027.
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.strongest_case_small: Engineers already used the conjectured formulas, and real links run far below capacity because of pointing, atmosphere, detector efficiency and coding. Effect on hardware: nil.
frontier-optical-quantum-capacity.signpost: Independent verification of 273 (Lean or expert reconstruction), and citation in CCSDS optical-link standards rationale.

frontier-p-vs-np.title: P vs NP resolved
frontier-p-vs-np.description: Resolution of P vs NP, or of the barrier problems around it (superpolynomial lower bounds for general Boolean circuits).
frontier-p-vs-np.status_oct2026: Open. The relativization, natural-proofs and algebrization barriers explain why known techniques fail (general). No catalog family.
frontier-p-vs-np.why: Harder than anything that fell. The barriers mean a proof needs genuinely new techniques, not more effort (judgment: many doublings beyond Oct 2026, possibly not bridgeable by scaling). Downstream it is nil either way: P != NP is already assumed by all cryptography and planning, and a practical P = NP algorithm is considered extremely unlikely.
frontier-p-vs-np.strongest_case_small: Even a proof of P != NP changes no engineering practice. It is included to show the ceiling of the exponential premise.
frontier-p-vs-np.signpost: Superpolynomial lower bounds for general Boolean circuits, or a method that provably evades the natural-proofs barrier.

frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.title: AI finds a crack in post-quantum crypto
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.description: An AI-produced cryptanalytic result that materially lowers the security of a standardized post-quantum scheme (ML-KEM, ML-DSA) or of the structured lattice problems underneath (Module-LWE), forcing parameter or algorithm changes.
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.status_oct2026: NIST standardized FIPS 203/204/205 in Aug 2024 (general); a 2024 claimed quantum lattice algorithm was withdrawn after a bug was found (general). Aug 2026: an autonomous agent workflow broke eight published academic constructions at their stated parameters (Ring-LWR commitment, middle-product encryption, a lattice e-voting protocol, and others), none of them standardized (Olejnik-Naskrecki). Catalog: 279 exact quantum factoring over a fixed gate set (theory only) and 138 Subset Sum in 2^0.49n (T1) do not touch deployed cryptography.
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.why: Module-LWE has survived about 20 years of study, but the capability is strongest at constructive, adversarial search, as the Aug 2026 breaks of academic schemes show (analyst position f). The space angle: satellites fly cryptography in hardware for 5-15 years, so even a parameter-level weakening mid-life forces rekeying or algorithm changes that many buses cannot make. Crypto agility is the hedge regardless of the probability.
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.strongest_case_small: AI breaks so far hit lightly vetted academic schemes. Standardized parameters carry tens of bits of margin, and hybrid classical-plus-PQC deployment means a partial break is not exploitable.
frontier-lattice-crypto-watch.signpost: Any AI-produced improvement to lattice-sieving or reduction asymptotics, or a concrete attack on a standardized or round-4 NIST scheme.

frontier-hjb-guarantees.title: Optimal control with proven guarantees
frontier-hjb-guarantees.description: Existence, regularity and dimension-robust approximation theorems for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman and reachability equations with state constraints, plus certified a posteriori error bounds for neural and tensor solvers, so guidance and collision-avoidance policies come with proofs.
frontier-hjb-guarantees.status_oct2026: Viscosity-solution theory is mature (general). State-constrained and hybrid HJB regularity is partial. Grid solvers scale exponentially: 100 points per axis in 6 dimensions is 10^12 nodes. Neural and tensor solvers mostly lack guarantees, though verifiable error bounds for PINN Lyapunov/HJB solutions appeared (Liu, Mar 2026), along with policy iteration under control constraints (Kundu-Kunisch, Sep 2026). Catalog: 104 quasipolynomial stochastic/parity games (T3) is the discrete analogue; 139 log-concave sampling (T3).
frontier-hjb-guarantees.why: GNC teams mostly need bespoke guarantees, such as a reachable-set bound for one vehicle or a stability certificate for one controller. These are expert-scarce rather than open and easier than catalog problems. With research-grade applied math public (S2: 2027) they become on-demand, and they can be checked formally once infra-mathlib-applied matures. Downstream: astro-scp-guarantees, verif-closed-loop-guarantees, hyper-certified-edl-guidance, astro-autonomous-ca-at-scale.
frontier-hjb-guarantees.strongest_case_small: Flight GNC already uses convex formulations (lossless convexification) that carry guarantees; the residual risk is model mismatch, not math. For general HJB classes the curse of dimensionality is a lower bound, so guarantees will cover structured cases only.
frontier-hjb-guarantees.signpost: A certified a posteriori error bound for a neural HJB solver in 6+ state dimensions, used in a published collision-avoidance or EDL guidance study.

frontier-scalable-global-certificates.title: Certified global optima for nonconvex design
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.description: Moment-SOS, branch-and-bound and MIP methods that certify a trajectory, layout or design is globally optimal, or within a proven gap, at engineering scale, using sparsity, symmetry and convergence-rate theory.
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.status_oct2026: Lasserre hierarchies converge, with finite convergence generically (general). Rate theory is advancing (Schlosser et al. 2025; Tran-Toh 2026; Henrion-Safey El Din, Sep 2026), and sparse tightness is characterized (Nie-Qu-Tang 2025). Scale is the limit: a degree-4 moment relaxation in n = 100 variables has a moment matrix of side C(102,2) = 5,151. Catalog: 102 UGC (T3) implies SDP-based ratios are worst-case optimal for many problems.
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.why: Certificates for specific instances are not ruled out by worst-case hardness. Exploiting problem structure (sparsity, symmetry, term sparsity) is expert-scarce, technique-heavy work that compounds under S2. Downstream: astro-global-optimality-certificates, verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates, and design-space closure for prop-ai-engine-design-loop. The value is assurance and an end to search; performance gains are typically a few percent of delta-v or mass in complex designs (general).
frontier-scalable-global-certificates.strongest_case_small: Engineers rarely need global optimality, only feasible-and-good. Local optimizers with multistart already find near-optimal designs, so certification buys assurance, not performance.
