frontier-scalable-global-certificates.signpost: A certified global optimum (proven gap under 1%) for a published multi-gravity-assist or constellation-design benchmark with 100+ decision variables.

frontier-certified-pde-error.title: Guaranteed error bars for smooth-regime simulations
frontier-certified-pde-error.description: A posteriori estimators and computer-assisted methods that give guaranteed, not asymptotic, error bounds for nonlinear PDE solutions in smooth regimes: heat conduction, structures, laminar and steady flows, electrostatics. This is the bulk of spacecraft analysis outside turbulence.
frontier-certified-pde-error.status_oct2026: Guaranteed a posteriori bounds are mature for linear elliptic problems (general). Validated integrators exist for semilinear parabolic PDEs (van den Berg-Breden-Sheombarsing 2024; simplified Jan 2026), and computer-assisted PDE proofs are routine for special problems (Ayala-Lessard 2026). NASA-STD-7009B (Mar 2024) requires credibility assessment but accepts estimated numerical error. No catalog family.
frontier-certified-pde-error.why: The methods exist in pieces. Applying them per problem (deriving the estimator and the constants for a given nonlinear operator) is expert-scarce, and AI does it on demand once applied math is public. Guaranteed bounds can replace three-level grid-convergence studies, which cost roughly 3-10x a single solve (general). Downstream: hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics, plasma-verified-kinetic-numerics, prop-cfd-auto-vv, materials-multiscale-certified, and frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.
frontier-certified-pde-error.strongest_case_small: Discretization error is rarely the dominant error in space analysis; model-form and input uncertainty dominate. Guaranteed bounds are often 10-100x loose, too loose to drive decisions.
frontier-certified-pde-error.signpost: A NASA or commercial thermal-structural code ships guaranteed a posteriori bounds for a nonlinear analysis, or NASA-STD-7009 guidance credits them.

frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.title: Error bars for turbulent and shocked flows
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.description: Rigorous statistical error bounds for simulations of chaotic, turbulent and shock-laden flows (combustors, plumes, reentry wakes), bounding errors in averaged quantities rather than in individual trajectories.
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.status_oct2026: No such theory exists. Pathwise error grows exponentially in chaotic flows, and nonuniqueness results (convex integration; 363 and 376, T1) show the limit equations may not select a unique answer without extra principles. Practice relies on grid studies and validation data; turbulence, transition and separation are the leading CFD gap (CFD Vision 2030, general).
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.why: This is the hardest applied node, and possibly impossible in pointwise form. What is achievable: bounds on statistics under ergodicity assumptions, with the selection principle stated explicitly and model-form error estimated from data. It chains four upstream nodes, two of them genuinely open, so even S3 stays Low. If it lands, it would make CFD credibility in prop-closure-theory, hyper-sbli-heating-closure and prop-cfd-auto-vv a computed quantity rather than expert judgment.
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.strongest_case_small: Even if achieved, closure (model-form) error dominates and is set by data, so the bound would be correct but large. Engineers would still calibrate against tests.
frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd.signpost: A rigorous convergence-of-statistics theorem for LES of forced turbulence on the torus, with explicit rates.

frontier-stiff-certified.title: Stiff chemistry solvers with certified error
frontier-stiff-certified.description: Error theory and verified implementations for stiff ODE/DAE integration of large reaction networks (combustion, ablation, plasma chemistry, batteries), including error bounds for reduced mechanisms that hold for non-dissipative chemistry.
frontier-stiff-certified.status_oct2026: Classical stiff theory (A- and B-stability, B-convergence) assumes one-sided Lipschitz or dissipative structure that combustion chemistry lacks (general). Order reduction is understood for linear problems (2025). Verified ODE integration exists in Isabelle (IsaVODEs 2024; 'Numerical Methods in Isabelle', Jan 2026), not yet at reaction-network scale. Catalog: 149 permanence of weakly reversible reaction networks (T1) gives structural boundedness for an important class of chemistry models.
frontier-stiff-certified.why: Mostly expert-scarce: AI can derive mechanism-specific error bounds and produce reduced mechanisms with a proven bound on ignition delay or species error. Reducing a ~50-species mechanism to ~15 typically cuts chemistry cost several-fold in reacting CFD (general). Downstream: prop-stiff-chemistry, hyper-gas-surface-chemistry, materials-battery-life-qual.
frontier-stiff-certified.strongest_case_small: Rate-constant uncertainty, often a factor of 2-10, dwarfs integration error, and CVODE-class solvers with tolerance control are already adequate. Certification addresses the smaller error.
frontier-stiff-certified.signpost: A certified reduced mechanism, with a proven bound on ignition delay, adopted in a rocket-engine CFD code.

frontier-rare-event-certified.title: Certified rare-event probabilities
frontier-rare-event-certified.description: Methods with provable, non-asymptotic error bounds for very small failure probabilities in high-dimensional, non-Gaussian models: 1e-4 collision probabilities, 1e-6 structural failure, margins. Covers importance sampling with certified variance, large-deviation bounds and certified surrogate-based UQ.
frontier-rare-event-certified.status_oct2026: Practice uses multilevel Monte Carlo, subset simulation and importance sampling with asymptotic or sample-based guarantees (general). Conjunction assessment at scale relies on Gaussian approximations (Starlink: 144,000+ maneuvers in six months, per 33FG), and space-weather drag uncertainty feeds directly into Pc (Parker et al. 2024). Catalog: 139 subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling (T3) and 140 memory-sample lower bounds for regression (T3) give ceilings. 360 Villani convexity/regular OT (T3) and 374 sharp 1/3 stability of OT maps (T1) bound transport-map filters (weak link).
frontier-rare-event-certified.why: Certified estimators are mostly expert-scarce, so on-demand AI unlocks them fast. Data binds the answer, though: no estimator beats the information in the data. Demonstrating 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence with zero failures takes ln(0.1)/ln(0.99) = 230 tests unless a validated physics model carries the extrapolation. Structural example: raising a monocoque shell buckling knockdown factor from 0.65 to 0.8 through certified imperfection statistics cuts buckling-critical wall thickness by sqrt(0.65/0.8) = 0.90, about 10% of that mass. Downstream: astro-nongaussian-uq-certified, hyper-certified-margin-uq, materials-allowables-stats-framework, prop-life-twin.
frontier-rare-event-certified.strongest_case_small: Engineering decisions use conservative margins anyway, and a certified estimator of a mis-specified model gives a precise wrong answer. Model-form error is not a mathematical object.
frontier-rare-event-certified.signpost: A conjunction-assessment provider publishes certified, non-asymptotic Pc bounds for non-Gaussian cases at catalog scale, or NASA-STD-7009 guidance cites certified rare-event estimators.

frontier-transport-certified.title: Radiation transport with error bounds
frontier-transport-certified.description: Deterministic and Monte Carlo radiation-transport methods (crew and electronics shielding, radiative heating during entry, neutronics for nuclear propulsion) with proven convergence and error bounds in the full 6+1-dimensional phase space, including asymptotic-preserving and low-rank solvers.
frontier-transport-certified.status_oct2026: Space-radiation codes predicted Artemis I absorbed dose blind, from Earth to Mars, accurately across ISS, Orion, BioSentinel and Mars-surface measurements (Slaba et al. 2025). Dominant remaining uncertainties are nuclear cross sections and biological response, not transport mathematics (general). Low-rank and asymptotic-preserving schemes lack general error guarantees (general). No catalog family.
frontier-transport-certified.why: The mathematical gap is real but expert-scarce rather than deep, so it falls once applied math is on demand. The effect is lower V&V cost and certified low-rank solvers fast enough for design loops, not better dose accuracy. Downstream: hyper-radiation-kinetics (radiative heating), prop-ntp-fuel-model (neutronics), materials-see-system-models (single-event effects).
frontier-transport-certified.strongest_case_small: Dose prediction is already validated to engineering accuracy; nuclear data and radiobiology dominate the error budget.
frontier-transport-certified.signpost: A certified low-rank transport solver used in a design analysis (an NTP core or crew-shielding trade).

frontier-inverse-stability.title: How much sensor data is enough
frontier-inverse-stability.description: Quantitative stability estimates, not just uniqueness, for the inverse problems behind structural health monitoring, heat-shield inspection, gravimetry and tomography: how measurement noise and sensor placement bound the damage or material properties that can be recovered.
frontier-inverse-stability.status_oct2026: Catalog: 372 global uniqueness for smooth isotropic Lame moduli from boundary data (T1); 365 joint metric-plus-connection recovery from one boundary patch, with conductivity nonuniqueness (T3); 366 planar Mumford-Shah crack regularity (T1); 368 3D Ball-Evans approximation (T1); 369 hot spots conjecture for planar simply connected domains (T1). Uniqueness typically comes with only logarithmic stability for Calderon-type problems (general), which is why practice relies on regularized inversion calibrated by test.
frontier-inverse-stability.why: Uniqueness says the data suffice in principle; stability constants for a given sensor layout say how many sensors and what noise level are needed. That is bespoke, expert-scarce work AI does on demand. Bands are one step down because most premises are T1. Downstream: hyper-tps-inverse-nde, materials-am-digital-twin-qual.
frontier-inverse-stability.strongest_case_small: Logarithmic stability means practical recovery depends on priors and regularization, not the theorem. NDE practice is calibrated by coupons and rarely changes sensor counts because of theory.
frontier-inverse-stability.signpost: A sensor-placement design derived from a stability estimate, used in a flight structural-health-monitoring system or a TPS inspection protocol.

frontier-xc-certified.title: Density functionals with proven error bounds
frontier-xc-certified.description: Exchange-correlation functionals, learned or constructed, with provable or rigorously certified error bounds on defined chemical classes relevant to space (propellants, ablators, high-temperature alloys, electrolytes), within the limits set by hardness results.
frontier-xc-certified.status_oct2026: The exact functional exists, but computing it is QMA-hard (Schuch-Verstraete 2009, general). The catalog tightens the limits: 275 QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy (T1) and 278 failure of Kohn-Sham ensemble representability (T1); also 263 ionization conjectures (T3). Learned functionals now beat hybrids at semi-local cost: Skala reaches 2.8 kcal/mol on GMTKN55 (Luise et al., Jun 2025) and was implemented in CP2K in Aug-Sep 2026. None carries an error certificate.
frontier-xc-certified.why: The hardness results (P3, acting now) say no universal efficient functional exists, so the path is class-restricted functionals certified against high-accuracy wavefunction references. Defining the class is a posing problem; generating CCSD(T)/QMC reference data is a compute-and-data problem. Downstream: materials-learned-functionals, hyper-gas-surface-chemistry, materials-energetics-design. Overlaps materials-dft-limits, which owns the hardness side.
frontier-xc-certified.strongest_case_small: Learned functionals already improve accuracy empirically, and materials programs validate by experiment anyway, so a certificate adds little. Reference-data cost binds, not mathematics.
frontier-xc-certified.signpost: A functional published with a proven or statistically certified error bound on a defined chemical class and adopted by a propulsion or materials group.

frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.title: Gradient design of turbulent and chaotic systems
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.description: Design tools that compute reliable sensitivities of time-averaged quantities in unsteady turbulent or plasma flows (combustor stability margins, nozzle heat loads, thruster erosion), enabling gradient optimization over thousands of parameters instead of sampling.
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.status_oct2026: Steady adjoint design is routine in aerospace (general). For chaotic unsteady flows conventional adjoints diverge, and shadowing methods are costly and heuristic (general).
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.premise_tier: n/a (rests on an unproven theory node)
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.why: If frontier-chaos-linear-response lands (S2: 2029), turning it into a tool is method design plus validation of designed hardware against tests, which is the binding physical gate. S3's autonomous labs compress validation, hence Medium. Downstream: prop-ai-engine-design-loop, prop-stability-design-tool, plasma-ep-predictive-design. The gain is design-space exploration at about the cost of two simulations per gradient instead of one per parameter.
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.strongest_case_small: Surrogate and Bayesian optimization already handle tens of parameters well; most design value comes from validated physics models; and a theory result may come back negative.
frontier-chaotic-adjoint-design.signpost: A published gradient-based optimization of an LES combustor or Hall thruster with 1,000+ design parameters, validated by test.

frontier-math-unbinds.title: Math expertise stops limiting space programs
frontier-math-unbinds.description: The scarce resource in space-program analysis is no longer people who can do research-grade applied math. Stability proofs, error bounds, optimality certificates and well-posedness checks are requested from AI like compute, and schedules are set by tests, data and certification instead.
frontier-math-unbinds.status_oct2026: Such work is expert-scarce today. Public models handle much routine analysis; research-grade capability is internal and unreleased.
frontier-math-unbinds.why: Under S2 the cognitive clock runs years ahead of the physical one. Engineering math needs, mostly easier than the catalog, are met by about 2028-29, and the binding constraints become tests, data and qualification (analyst position g). Rough scale: if analysis and V&V take ~20-30% of development engineering hours (general) and AI halves the mathematical share, program-level savings are ~5-15%, unless test campaigns also shrink, and they compress far less. This is the domain's main point for readers: the exponential mostly accelerates what was never the long pole.
frontier-math-unbinds.strongest_case_small: Organizations change slowly. Liability and certification require human sign-off, and much 'math' work is modeling judgment and data interpretation that stays with people.
frontier-math-unbinds.signpost: A prime contractor or NASA center reports replacing a specialist analysis function (for example GNC stability analysis) with AI-produced, human-reviewed proofs on a flight program.

hyper-flight-data-pipeline.title: High-cadence instrumented reentry flights
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.description: A steady stream of instrumented hypersonic and orbital-reentry flights (Varda W-series, Talon-A, MACH-TB, Starship, Inversion Arc), whose surface heating, pressure and in-depth TPS temperatures reach model builders. Defined as achieved at 12 or more instrumented reentries per year with reconstructed data usable for calibration.
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.status_oct2026: Varda W-5 reentered on 29 Jan 2026 under the AFRL Prometheus program with an in-house C-PICA heat shield. W-6 (launched 30 Mar 2026) carried a Sandia nose tile with embedded sensors for comparison against model predictions. Varda says it expects a monthly cadence. MACH-TB targets up to 50 tests a year, and Talon-A has flown more than 10 hypersonic flights. DoD describes test capacity as a national bottleneck across ~70 hypersonic programs.
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.why: Every AI-built aerothermal or material model in this tree has to be calibrated against flight data, because ground facilities cannot reproduce the combined flight environment. Flight count grows roughly linearly, from a few to tens per year, set by rideshare cadence and capital rather than by cognition. That makes this node the slope limiter for every data-bound node downstream, in all three scenarios.
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.strongest_case_small: Much of the best data is classified (defense hypersonics) or proprietary (SpaceX) and never reaches civil model builders. Cadence claims for commercial capsules have slipped before.
hyper-flight-data-pipeline.signpost: Varda, Inversion or AFRL publish reconstructed flight heating data; MACH-TB passes 20 flights in FY2027.

hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.title: Boltzmann foundations checked and scoped
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.description: Outside experts check and scope family 363 (Boltzmann solutions that conserve mass, momentum and energy exactly yet are non-unique) and family 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian hard-sphere gases, including fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan). The scoping should state whether the non-unique solutions satisfy the entropy inequality and whether they can occur at flight conditions.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.status_oct2026: Both families are manuscript-only (T1): no Lean proof in the repo and no outside review as of 2026-10-07. The analyst knowledge base rates the implications for rarefied modeling as Low.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.why: If 363 holds, the kinetic equation alone does not fix the physical solution in some regime, so DSMC and deterministic Boltzmann solvers need an explicit selection principle there (entropy, molecular chaos). If 364 holds, the particle-noise statistics of DSMC have a rigorous basis rather than being numerical artifacts. Both change confidence in the models, not the heating numbers. Band: P3 defaults to High, down one for the T1 premise in S1. In S2 and S3, cheap verification makes an expert check within 1-2 years likely.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.strongest_case_small: Nonuniqueness constructions are usually low-regularity solutions that violate the H-theorem or need contrived data. DSMC has matched flight and tunnel data for decades, and no reentry heating number will change.
hyper-boltzmann-foundations-check.signpost: Kinetic-theory specialists publicly endorse or refute 363 within 12 months, especially on whether the counterexamples are entropy-admissible.

hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.title: On-demand transition stability analysis for any vehicle
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.description: AI agents set up and run linear and nonlinear stability analyses (PSE, plane-marching PSE, resolvent/input-output, BiGlobal) on full 3D vehicle geometries with thermochemistry. They return N-factor maps and sensitivities to roughness and wall temperature in days rather than expert-months.
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.status_oct2026: The methods exist but only a few groups can apply them. BOLT-1B was analyzed by specialist teams using stochastically forced DNS and plane-marching PSE. The AIAA collection on transition prediction for complex geometry appeared in Mar 2026. LLM agents already automate routine CFD: OpenFOAMGPT 2.0 reports more than 450 end-to-end runs, but none for hypersonic stability.
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.why: Today a 3D stability analysis of a new vehicle takes a specialist team weeks to months (general), so most design iterations fall back on correlations (Re_theta/M_e). Once the expert labor is near-free (S2 from ~2027-28), each design iteration can carry a physics-based transition estimate, which is 10-50x more stability analyses for the same budget (judgment). P1 defaults to High. S1 is Medium because applied-math capability arrives later and diffuses slowly.
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.strongest_case_small: Stability theory gives N-factors, not a transition location. The critical N-factor and receptivity still have to be calibrated against flight, so the bottleneck moves to data rather than disappearing. Defense users may not run ITAR-controlled geometry through external AI services.
hyper-stability-analysis-on-demand.signpost: A published 3D hypersonic stability analysis set up end-to-end by an AI agent and validated against BOLT-1B or HIFiRE-5 data.

hyper-optimal-test-design.title: Information-optimal ground and flight test design
hyper-optimal-test-design.description: Bayesian optimal experimental design and sequential model calibration choose arc-jet conditions, shock-tube shots and flight sensor placements. Each test is aimed at the uncertainties that drive TPS thickness: material conductivity, radiative excitation rates and the transition N-factor.
hyper-optimal-test-design.status_oct2026: The methods are known but rarely applied at program scale. The Ames Arc Jet Complex is NASA's only reentry TPS ground facility, and its throughput is limited: in 2026 the 30 kW mARC II needed a cooling-sleeve fix just to extend run times. The Artemis I char-loss investigation took 121 tests across 8 campaigns.
hyper-optimal-test-design.why: When facility hours are the binding constraint, the lever is information gained per run. Well-designed sequential calibration campaigns often cut the runs needed for parameter estimation by 2-5x (general). Applied to the arc-jet and EAST queues, this multiplies the one physical gate in the domain that money cannot expand quickly. It also makes the tier-3 physics nodes reachable sooner.
hyper-optimal-test-design.strongest_case_small: Qualification requirements (envelope coverage) often fix test matrices, not information value, and facility availability sets the schedule. The real gain may be 20-30%, not 2-5x.
hyper-optimal-test-design.signpost: NASA Ames, ESA or a commercial plasma-tunnel operator advertises adaptive, model-driven test campaigns.

hyper-certified-margin-uq.title: Probabilistic margins with model-form error bounds
hyper-certified-margin-uq.description: Stacked deterministic multipliers are replaced by a joint probabilistic budget that carries material, aerothermal and model-form uncertainty through to a reliability statement on bondline temperature. Where data are sparse, the budget has rigorous bounds.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.status_oct2026: NASA's SRL TPS design (IPPW 2026) uses stacked factors: convective 1.22 forebody and 2.0 aftbody, radiative 1.5 and 1.47, recession +20%, bondline margin. Material properties dominate the thickness. The same study's alternative margining gives ~75% of baseline thickness at 99% confidence on bondline temperature.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.why: Stacking factors compounds conservatism, and NASA's own SRL numbers imply roughly a quarter of the thickness is margin on margin. Joint UQ is solved in principle but expert-scarce. Model-form error for extrapolating from ground to flight is genuinely open, and an AI doing research-grade applied math can attack it on demand. This is the shortest path from AI mathematics to mass on a flown vehicle.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.strongest_case_small: The mathematics was never the barrier; risk posture is. Probabilistic TPS methods have existed for about 20 years (general), and Artemis I's char loss pushes NASA toward more margin, not less.
hyper-certified-margin-uq.signpost: A NASA or ESA EDL margin-policy revision, or a mission PDR, that cites reliability-based TPS sizing.

hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.title: Certified error bounds for hypersonic CFD kernels
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.description: Proven a-posteriori error bounds and formally verified kernels (positivity-preserving shock capturing, stiff finite-rate chemistry integrators, radiation-transport quadrature). A predicted stagnation heat flux then carries a certified numerical-error bar, kept separate from physics-model error.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.status_oct2026: The release does not touch this: stiff numerics and radiation transport are absent, and only 3 of 16 PDE families are formalized. Practitioners study grid convergence informally, and it enters radiative-heating uncertainty budgets as a 'structural' term.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.why: Separating numerical error from model error stops grid effects from being double-counted inside physics margins. In S2, Mathlib coverage of PDE and numerics (~2028) plus a verified-numerics toolchain (~2029) make kernel-level proofs routine. Proofs about the full solution remain out of reach.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.strongest_case_small: Numerical error is rarely the dominant uncertainty; transition, radiation and material properties are. Multi-D compressible Euler weak solutions are known to be non-unique, so global certified bounds need assumptions engineers cannot check.
hyper-verified-aerothermal-numerics.signpost: A Lean- or Coq-verified flux or chemistry integrator adopted in a NASA, DLR or commercial production aerothermal code.

hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.title: Error-controlled kinetic solvers for the rarefied-to-continuum gap
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.description: Hybrids of DSMC, Fokker-Planck and discrete-velocity methods, with proven consistency with the Boltzmann equation and quantified statistical error, used for high-altitude aerocapture passes, early-entry heating and plume backflow.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.status_oct2026: DSMC (SPARTA and other codes) is standard practice, and a Fokker-Planck module in SPARTA matches DSMC at lower cost. No production solver carries certified error bounds. Families 363 and 364 are manuscript-only (T1).
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven; 363/364 at T1 are supporting only)
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.why: Transitional-regime heating (Knudsen number ~0.01-1) matters most for aerocapture, which spends a long time high in the atmosphere, and for upper-atmosphere entry. Today it is DSMC with expert-tuned collision models. The band rests on the capability channel. If it rested only on the T1 catalog premises, it would drop a band.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.strongest_case_small: Rarefied contributions to total heat load are small for most capsules, because peak heating occurs in the continuum (general). Certified bounds also do nothing about collision cross-section uncertainty.
hyper-kinetic-solver-certification.signpost: A kinetic code release with published, proven error estimates, or AI-derived collision models validated against shock-tube data.

hyper-tps-inverse-nde.title: Inverse-problem theory and algorithms for heat-shield inspection
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.description: Uniqueness and stability theory, plus algorithms, for recovering hidden TPS defects (bondline disbonds, subsurface cracks, density variation) from surface thermography, ultrasound and strain data. This includes which defects a given sensing mode provably cannot see.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.status_oct2026: Family 372 (global uniqueness for smooth isotropic elasticity from boundary data) is T1. Family 365 (joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch, plus conductivity nonuniqueness) is T3, Lean-formalized and unchecked. Family 366 (planar Mumford-Shah crack regularity) is T1. Practice relies on visual, tap and thermographic inspection with empirical thresholds. Starship's heat shield has about 18,000 tiles; Musk has described the job as inspecting tens of thousands of tiles.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.premise_tier: T1-T3 (supportive; the capability channel drives the band)
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.why: Rapid reuse needs inspect-by-exception: cheap sensors that show which tiles need attention. Uniqueness results say when boundary data determines interior properties. The conductivity nonuniqueness in 365 says thermal boundary data alone can miss some interior variations, which is a fast-acting P3 design rule: pair thermography with a second modality. AI also makes the bespoke inversion work, such as probability-of-detection modeling for a specific tile stack, cheap.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.strongest_case_small: These theorems concern smooth, isotropic media, while tiles are porous, anisotropic and full of sharp interfaces. Industrial NDE runs on empirical probability-of-detection curves, and SpaceX will use cameras plus machine learning regardless.
hyper-tps-inverse-nde.signpost: A reusable-vehicle operator or NASA publishes a model-based TPS inspection scheme with probability-of-detection derived from inverse theory.

hyper-transition-prediction-theory.title: Predictive hypersonic transition (receptivity, roughness, ablation)
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.description: A validated model that predicts transition onset on 3D vehicles from the freestream disturbance environment, surface roughness and ablation blowing, to within ~+/-20% in transition Reynolds number, without per-vehicle tuning.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.status_oct2026: Genuinely open. A coordinated international effort was published as an AIAA virtual collection in Mar 2026. BOLT-1B showed that flight transition differs from conventional-tunnel transition (Jan 2026), and its forebody took ~14 months and 100+ staff to build.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.why: Turbulent heating is roughly 3-5x laminar (general), so without trusted transition prediction, slender and lifting vehicles carry TPS sized for turbulent flow over much of their acreage. Predictive transition could save tens of percent of acreage TPS mass on such vehicles (judgment). Under S2, AI can produce the theory by 2029-30. Validation needs flight transition datasets, of which there are only a handful (BOLT, HIFiRE), and the flight disturbance environment is poorly characterized. The physical clock keeps S2 at Low.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.strongest_case_small: Blunt capsules and Starship's belly transition early anyway, and designs already assume turbulent heating. The payoff falls mainly on hypersonic gliders and weapons, not most space vehicles.
hyper-transition-prediction-theory.signpost: A blind prediction in which an AI-assisted model lands transition onset on a new flight test within 20%.

hyper-sbli-heating-closure.title: Turbulence closures for shock interactions and cold-wall heating
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.description: AI-derived RANS and wall-model closures (non-Boussinesq, variable turbulent Prandtl number, roughness and blowing) that predict separation extent and peak heating in shock-boundary-layer interactions (flaps, control surfaces, tile steps and gaps) to within ~+/-15-20% of DNS and experiment.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.status_oct2026: Standard RANS fails on hypersonic SBLI. The 2025 review by Raje, Parish, Hickey, Cinnella and Duraisamy lists SBLI heat transfer, compressibility, turbulence-chemistry interaction and ablation roughness and blowing as open research needs. The release contains no turbulence-closure results.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.why: Flap, hinge-line and gap heating set the local TPS on Starship-class flaps and control surfaces, which today are designed with LES or DNS spot checks plus factors. Deriving closures is a theory problem that AI can attack (constraint-respecting symbolic models trained on DNS) once enough DNS data exists. DNS is compute-bound, and AI-era compute growth helps. In S2 the cognitive part lands by ~2029, and data and validation take about another year.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.strongest_case_small: Machine-learned RANS closures have repeatedly failed to generalize outside their training data (general). Wall-modeled LES on GPUs may bypass RANS closures by 2030 and make the question moot.
hyper-sbli-heating-closure.signpost: A closure published with demonstrated out-of-distribution accuracy on unseen SBLI geometries in a blind comparison.

hyper-radiation-kinetics.title: Closing the radiative-heating gap (Mars, Venus, 12+ km/s return)
hyper-radiation-kinetics.description: State-resolved excitation and dissociation kinetics (the CO 4th positive system in CO2 atmospheres; N and O VUV emission for Earth return), built from ab initio rates plus shock-tube data, that cut radiative-heating uncertainty from 30-100% to ~15-25%.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.status_oct2026: For SRL's 8 km/s Mars entry, baseline simulations under-predicted VUV by up to 2x against EAST, and three UQ methods gave 30-100% uncertainty (Hansson, 24 Sep 2026). The forebody radiative heating factor is 1.5. Family 275 (QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energies, T1) acts as a ceiling on first-principles shortcuts.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven; 275 at T1 is a ceiling only)
hyper-radiation-kinetics.why: Radiative uncertainty sets the 1.5x factor on Mars forebody radiative heating. For Earth return at 12 km/s or more, radiation dominates and the uncertainty decides material choice (HEEET-class versus PICA). Halving the uncertainty could bring the factor toward ~1.2-1.25 and cut the radiative design heat load by ~15-20% (judgment). AI can generate rate sets and reduced kinetics, but the missing physics at SRL (heavy-particle excitation) was found by measurement, and EAST shot rate binds.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.strongest_case_small: The gap is experimental, not theoretical, and 275 says no general exact shortcut exists for the many-electron energies behind those rates. The best AI theory still needs shock-tube shots that take months to schedule.
hyper-radiation-kinetics.signpost: A paper at a radiation workshop (RHTGSM or IPPW) in which AI-generated rate sets match EAST VUV spectra within 20% without tuning.

hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.title: First-principles gas-surface chemistry for heat-shield materials
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.description: Finite-rate oxidation, nitridation and catalytic-recombination models for carbon, SiC and silica-based (tile coating) surfaces, derived from quantum chemistry plus molecular-beam data, to replace tuned recession and catalycity parameters.
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.status_oct2026: Finite-rate models exist, for example vitreous-carbon oxidation mechanisms extended to FiberForm (the PICA precursor), but they rely on fitted mechanisms. Family 278 (failure of Kohn-Sham ensemble representability, T1) marks cases where DFT can be formally underdetermined. Family 275 (T1) is a complexity ceiling.
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.premise_tier: n/a (capability-driven; 278/275 at T1 are ceilings only)
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.why: On reusable, non-ablating tiles, surface catalycity can shift heating by tens of percent up to ~2x between the non-catalytic and fully catalytic limits (general), so designers assume the worst case. Recession-rate uncertainty sets the 20% recession margin on ablators. AI-built mechanisms validated by autonomous molecular-beam and plasma-tunnel experiments (S2 from ~2029) could tighten both.
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.strongest_case_small: Real surfaces evolve through contamination, oxide growth and microstructure change, so first-principles rates are only one input. Arc-jet calibration remains mandatory, and arc jets are scarce.
hyper-gas-surface-chemistry.signpost: Autonomous plasma-tunnel or molecular-beam experiments publish AI-designed reaction mechanisms that predict catalytic heating within 20% on a new material.

hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.title: Predictive ablator response (pyrolysis, permeability, spallation)
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.description: Multiscale material response that goes from pore scale to volume average, with mathematically justified homogenization, calibrated permeability and pyrolysis kinetics, and criteria for spallation and char failure. It should be able to predict an Avcoat-type char loss before flight.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.status_oct2026: PATO recession predictions match plasma-tunnel data to about +/-20% (ESA conference, 2026). The Artemis I char-loss root cause (Avcoat lacking permeability, letting gas pressure build in the char) was found only after flight, through 121 tests. Artemis II splashed down on 10 Apr 2026 after a modified, non-skip entry, with reduced char loss on the same heat-shield design.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.why: Material-property uncertainty dominates TPS thickness (SRL: conductivity 2-sigma ~32%). A failure mode the models missed cost Artemis a trajectory change and an investigation of more than a year. An AI that formulates and checks thermomechanical failure criteria from micro-CT microstructure addresses the cognitive part. Validation needs arc-jet time, which in S2 is stretched by optimal test design.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.strongest_case_small: Batch-to-batch permeability in Avcoat is a manufacturing process-control problem, and better models do not make material uniform.
hyper-ablator-multiscale-response.signpost: A pre-test prediction of a char or spallation anomaly that arc-jet or flight data later confirms.

hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.title: Damage-accumulation model for reusable ceramic tiles
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.description: A predictive model of tile cracking, edge chipping, bond fatigue and hot-gas ingress through gaps over repeated entries, tied to inspection data, so that operators can inspect by exception and set life limits per tile zone.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.status_oct2026: Starship V3 Flight 13 (24-25 Jul 2026) deliberately stressed the heat shield: minimal tile loss, but cracked tiles and streaks at tile boundaries that suggest hot-gas penetration. Load-sensing tiles were flown and reflown tiles were tested. Musk said on 4 Aug 2026 that he would call the heat shield problem solved. Dan Rasky (co-inventor of PICA) called the current TPS a dead end for rapid reuse (29 Jul 2026). Flight 14 reached orbit on 28 Sep 2026 and splashed down; no ship has been caught or reflown.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.why: Shuttle-era tile programs needed extensive inspection between flights (general). Rapid reuse at Starship scale needs model-based triage that narrows inspection to flagged zones, plausibly a few percent of tiles per flight (judgment). Fatigue and fracture modeling plus Bayesian updating from load-sensing tiles is expert-scarce applied math that AI makes cheap. The data clock is the number of reflights.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.strongest_case_small: SpaceX would build this anyway with in-house ML on inspection imagery, and AI mathematics adds at most a few months. The hard problem may be material (ceramic tile fatigue under thermal cycling), and no model removes that.
hyper-tile-damage-accumulation.signpost: SpaceX states a ship reflight with heat-shield turnaround under 2 weeks, or publishes tile life-limit data.

hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.title: AI-run aerothermal design loop (shape + trajectory + TPS)
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.description: Multi-fidelity co-optimization of vehicle shape, entry trajectory and TPS layout, using AI-built surrogates (neural fields, reduced-order models) with validated or certified error bars. It cuts an entry-vehicle design cycle from months to days.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.status_oct2026: Surrogates exist in research: physics-enhanced 3D neural fields for Orion (arXiv 2603.28791, Mar 2026), and LLM CFD agents (OpenFOAMGPT 2.0, CFDAgent) that automate setup. None is used in production for certified EDL design.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.why: Entry design iterates between aerodynamics, trajectory and TPS, and each loop needs nonequilibrium CFD at 10-100 trajectory points (general). Agents plus surrogates could compress a cycle 10-30x (judgment). That opens shapes that were too costly to explore, such as lifting bodies and biconic Mars landers, and lowers the analysis-cost barrier for small companies (see the aerocapture demo).
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.strongest_case_small: Design-cycle time is rarely on a program's critical path; test and fabrication are. Neural surrogates struggle with shocks and extrapolation, and high-consequence final designs will still need full CFD plus test.
hyper-aerothermal-design-loop.signpost: A NASA or commercial entry-vehicle design review that cites trade studies driven by AI surrogates.

hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.title: Probabilistic heat-shield sizing adopted in practice
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.description: A NASA program, an ESA mission or a commercial capsule maker formally sizes heat-shield thickness to a reliability target using joint probabilistic margins rather than stacked factors.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.status_oct2026: Shown only as an alternative-margining study for SRL (~75% of baseline thickness at 99% confidence on bondline temperature; IPPW 2026). The SRL baseline still stacks factors. Varda makes its C-PICA heat shields in-house and flies roughly quarterly, aiming for monthly.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.why: Applying SRL's ~25% thickness reduction where forebody TPS is ~5-15% of entry mass (general) frees roughly 1-4% of entry mass for payload or margin elsewhere. On a 20 t-payload human-class Mars lander with a ~16 m heat shield, that is plausibly 0.5-1 t (judgment). Commercial capsule makers are not bound by NASA margin policy, so the band is not capped. A NASA crewed adopter would be capped at Medium.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.strongest_case_small: For small capsules TPS mass is small in absolute terms and reliability matters more. Post-Artemis I, NASA flagship and crewed programs will resist thinner margins.
hyper-probabilistic-tps-sizing.signpost: A NASA EDL margin-policy update, or Varda or Inversion disclosing reliability-based TPS sizing or reduced TPS mass.

hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.title: Validated supersonic-retropropulsion aero-propulsive models
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.description: Predictive models of plume-shock interaction, aerodynamic forces and moments, and heating during supersonic retropropulsion (SRP) for 20-100 t Mars landers, reduced to control-oriented models with quantified uncertainty and accepted by a lander program.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.status_oct2026: NASA's EDL Architecture Study found that all its 20 t human-scale concepts need SRP. Large DES and CFD runs on leadership supercomputers are the main tool (general). Falcon 9 and Starship Earth-reentry burns are the only full-scale data, and they are proprietary.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.why: Uncertainty in aero-propulsive interaction feeds GNC control margins and the propellant budget, and SRP propellant is a large share of landed mass (general). On-demand applied math turns expensive unsteady CFD campaigns into reduced-order models with uncertainty bounds. Validation needs flight data that only SpaceX holds at scale.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will validate empirically through Earth flights and accept risk on early Mars attempts. NASA's human Mars EDL has no decision driver before 2031.
hyper-srp-aeropropulsive-models.signpost: Published SRP models validated against Starship or Falcon flight data, or a NASA Mars architecture selecting a lander concept.

hyper-certified-edl-guidance.title: Formally verified entry, aerocapture and powered-descent guidance
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.description: Entry, aerocapture and powered-descent guidance (numerical predictor-corrector, convex powered-descent guidance) delivered with machine-checked proofs of convergence, constraint satisfaction and floating-point error bounds for the flight implementation, and accepted as verification evidence.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.status_oct2026: Convex powered-descent guidance has pen-and-paper proofs (general). Flight code is verified by test and Monte Carlo. The release shows agentic Lean at scale for mathematics, not for flight code, and no tool is qualified.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.why: Aerocapture allows a single pass, so a guidance failure means losing the mission. Proofs of robust convergence under atmospheric-density dispersions reduce Monte Carlo burden and perceived risk, and certification regimes already give credit for formal methods. Capped at Medium in S2 and S3 because acceptance is required.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.strongest_case_small: Guidance mishaps have historically come from requirements, sensor and integration errors, not from algorithm convergence, and a proof of the wrong specification is worthless.
hyper-certified-edl-guidance.signpost: A NASA or commercial EDL flight-software release with formal proof artifacts accepted as verification evidence.

hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.title: Coupled plasma-sheath and RF-link prediction tools
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.description: Coupled tools for nonequilibrium flowfield, electron density and full-wave electromagnetics that predict and minimize RF blackout through antenna placement, aft-side relay to constellations, and magnetic or electrostatic windows.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.status_oct2026: Starship relays through Starlink during reentry. Magnetic-window theory is at the screening-model stage (Lieu, arXiv 2608.10018, Aug 2026). The reentry sheath is collisional and weakly ionized, so family 362 (collisionless relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell, T3) does not bear on it.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.why: This is a coupled-physics analysis that is solved in principle but expert-scarce, so AI makes it routine for every vehicle. Better electron-density prediction also benefits from the ionization kinetics in the radiation node.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.strongest_case_small: Relaying through the wake to Starlink already largely solves the operational problem. Magnetic windows need heavy, high-field magnets, so the practical impact is small.
hyper-blackout-prediction-tools.signpost: A flight demonstration of active blackout mitigation, which would be a surprise before 2030.

hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.title: Rapidly reusable orbital heat shield (ship scale)
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.description: One Starship-class orbital vehicle reflies at least 5 times, with heat-shield turnaround under ~2 weeks and tile replacement limited to a small fraction per flight.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.status_oct2026: First orbital flight on 28 Sep 2026 (Flight 14, two orbits, early deorbit, splashdown). No ship has been caught or reflown. The tile stress test on Flight 13 showed cracking and gap streaks, and SpaceX publicly calls the heat-shield problem solved.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.why: Ship catch, then reflight, then 5 reflights is a hardware-iteration sequence paced by flight count. Booster reuse took roughly 1-2 years from first catch to routine reflight (general). AI damage models and inspection theory remove some inspection labor and shorten learning by perhaps 6-12 months in S2 and S3 (judgment). They do not change the ceramic material or the flight clock, so the band does not move across scenarios.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.strongest_case_small: SpaceX gets there through empirical hardware iteration, with or without AI mathematics. If the tile concept is a dead end for rapid reuse (Rasky), the fix is a new TPS architecture, a fabrication and qualification problem measured in years.
hyper-rapid-reuse-heatshield.signpost: First ship catch and reflight (2027?), with published turnaround time and tile replacement counts.

hyper-thinner-tps-flown.title: Flown heat shield sized with reduced, model-based margins
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.description: A flown reentry capsule or planetary probe whose TPS was sized by probabilistic, model-based margins and is at least ~15% thinner than stacked-factor practice, with flight data confirming the bondline predictions.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.status_oct2026: Commercial capsules fly every few months (Varda W-5 in Jan 2026, W-6 in 2026, with a Sandia instrumented nose tile). NASA's SRL study shows ~25% thinning is possible at 99% confidence.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.why: This is the shortest chain in the domain from AI mathematics to flown hardware: AI-run UQ, then probabilistic sizing, then a commercial capsule iterating on a monthly-to-quarterly cadence with instrumented heat shields. It frees ~1-4% of entry mass (general) and turns each flight into a calibration point. P7 defaults to Speculative; the band is raised because commercial capsules iterate in months and need no certification body to accept margins.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.strongest_case_small: Capsule makers may prefer to spend the margin on reliability and reuse rather than mass, so the change may be invisible from outside. Payload mass is rarely the binding constraint on small capsules.
hyper-thinner-tps-flown.signpost: A capsule operator reports flight-measured bondline temperatures matching pre-flight probabilistic predictions on a thinned heat shield.

hyper-aerocapture-demo.title: First aerocapture flight demonstration
hyper-aerocapture-demo.description: A vehicle uses a single atmospheric pass to capture into orbit (an Earth demonstration), validating the guidance, aerothermal and model-correlation performance that a planetary flagship would need before relying on aerocapture.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.status_oct2026: Aerocapture has never flown. On 11 Sep 2026 Inversion received a $350k NASA purchase order to study an Arc-based Earth aerocapture demo, running through 30 Jun 2027 with NASA Ames support. Uranus studies find MSL-heritage aeroshells adequate but require a risk-reduction flight demo first.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.why: In S2, AI collapses analysis cost (guidance design, dispersion analysis, aerothermal and rarefied analysis), so a small commercial vehicle could attempt the demo for tens of millions of dollars instead of as a NASA-class program. Funding and a ride bind. The earliest credible flight follows a 2027 study plus about 2 years of build.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.strongest_case_small: Analysis cost was never the barrier; NASA funding is, and the planetary budget is under pressure. The study is only $350k.
hyper-aerocapture-demo.signpost: NASA awards a flight contract for an aerocapture demo after the study ends in June 2027.

hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.title: Ground-validated design basis for 12-14 km/s Earth return
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.description: A validated aerothermal environment (radiative plus convective) and TPS response model (HEEET-class 3D woven material) for crewed Mars-return or fast sample-return entries, with radiative uncertainty of 25% or less, accepted by a mission project.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.status_oct2026: Earth entry at 12 km/s implies more than 3,000 W/cm2 and ~250 kPa (ESA). HEEET is designed for 1,500-8,000 W/cm2. Radiation becomes first-order above ~12 km/s. No funded mission needs this before 2031 (general).
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.why: Specific kinetic energy is ~72 MJ/kg at 12 km/s against ~30 MJ/kg from LEO, and radiation dominates. Radiative uncertainty sets material choice and thickness. AI-built kinetics could halve it, but without a mission to pull the work, nobody spends the shock-tube and arc-jet time.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.strongest_case_small: No funded mission needs it before 2031. Ground facilities cannot replicate the combined environment, and flight tests at these speeds are extremely rare.
hyper-12kms-entry-design-basis.signpost: NASA or ESA selects a mission with Earth entry at 12 km/s or more and a radiative heating factor below 1.3.

hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.title: Next deployable heat-shield flight (inflatable or mechanical, 10 m class or larger)
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.description: An orbital-entry flight of an inflatable (HIAD) or mechanically deployable (ADEPT) aeroshell of 10 m class or larger, the scale path toward the 16-18 m aeroshells studied for heavy Mars landers.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.status_oct2026: LOFTID (6 m) flew in Nov 2022. No funded follow-on was found as of Oct 2026. NASA's EDL Architecture Study considered HIAD and ADEPT for 20 t Mars payloads.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.why: Coupled fluid-structure-thermal behavior of flexible TPS (nonlinear membrane mechanics, flutter, fabric permeability) suits AI applied math well. Whether it flies depends on a budget line and a launch opportunity.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.strongest_case_small: Starship's rigid-body approach to heavy Mars EDL may make deployables irrelevant for cargo, and no budget line exists.
hyper-heavy-deployable-decelerator.signpost: NASA or ULA announces a LOFTID follow-on flight.

hyper-mars-heavy-landing.title: First landing of 20 t or more on Mars
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.description: A Starship-class or other vehicle lands 20 t or more intact on Mars, demonstrating heavy Mars EDL: entry at ~6-7.5 km/s, aerobraking, then retropropulsive descent.
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.status_oct2026: On 8 Feb 2026 Musk said SpaceX had shifted focus to a city on the Moon, with Mars to follow in roughly 5-7 years. The S-1 (20 May 2026) gives no Mars date. Starship reached orbit on 28 Sep 2026 and has not yet attempted propellant transfer. The late-2026 window is effectively not being used for a landing attempt (general inference).
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.why: The binding clock is the 26-month synodic window. Before end-2031 there are about two launch opportunities, around late 2028/early 2029 and around early 2031 (general), and propellant transfer, cryogenic storage and SpaceX's Moon priority come first. AI mathematics improves SRP and aerothermal models, plus margins (0.5-1 t on a 20 t-class lander, judgment), which raises the odds of a first attempt succeeding but cannot add windows. S3 is Medium only because S3 assumes AI accelerates engineering across the whole program, not just EDL.
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.strongest_case_small: AI mathematics has a near-nil effect on whether or when this happens. SpaceX's strategic choice and orbital refilling decide.
hyper-mars-heavy-landing.signpost: A SpaceX commitment to the late-2028 window, or the first ship-to-ship propellant transfer (2027?).

hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.title: Point-to-point rocket cargo, repeated demonstration flights
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.description: At least 3 suborbital point-to-point flights deliver 30 t or more of cargo to remote landing sites, with the vehicle recovered, per the Space Force Point-to-Point Delivery (P2PD) concept.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.status_oct2026: The 2022 DoD contract with SpaceX envisaged landing ~30 t of cargo in a 2026 test. The Johnston Atoll environmental assessment was suspended in July 2025. No demonstration as of Oct 2026.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.why: Point-to-point needs a rapidly reusable ship that can land on land, range and overflight approvals, sonic-boom and environmental clearance, and host-nation landing rights. Of these, only the aerothermal design is cognitive, and it is already adequate. AI mathematics has essentially no effect on the regulatory and range gates.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.strongest_case_small: The effect is nil. The program's fate turns on DoD priorities and SpaceX's manifest.
hyper-p2p-cargo-demo.signpost: A new environmental assessment or range agreement for P2PD landing sites.

hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.title: Routine, cheap reentry: 50+ commercial returns a year
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.description: Commercial capsule returns (in-space manufacturing, defense hypersonic testbeds, cargo) exceed ~50 a year worldwide, and TPS is no longer a pacing or major cost item.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.status_oct2026: Varda flew two reentries by mid-2026 (W-5 in Jan, then W-6) and targets monthly. Inversion, The Exploration Company and others are developing capsules (general). Landing sites are limited, for example Koonibba in South Australia.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.why: AI mathematics contributes at the margin: cheaper qualification by analysis for each new capsule variant, thinner and partly reusable TPS (+1-4% of entry mass), and faster design iterations. In S2 the AI-built aerothermal stack lets a 20-person company carry the analysis load of a NASA center. Demand for returned products, rideshare cadence and landing-site licensing are the real drivers.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.strongest_case_small: Demand is unproven, TPS is already a small share of cost, and launch rideshare cadence and reentry licensing bind first.
hyper-reentry-cadence-economy.signpost: A count of commercial reentries in 2028 above 20, with more than one operator.

hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.title: Aerocapture baselined for an outer-planet flagship
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.description: NASA or ESA baselines aerocapture for a Uranus, Neptune or Titan orbiter, cutting cruise time by years and shifting propellant mass to science.
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.status_oct2026: The Uranus Orbiter and Probe baseline uses propulsive orbit insertion with a 13-15 year cruise. Aerocapture studies show faster Uranus orbiters are feasible but require a flight demo.
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.why: Aerocapture can cut cruise to Uranus by several years and save insertion propellant (Uranus aerocapture literature). AI-cheapened analysis, plus guidance that can be verified, lowers perceived risk. Still, a successful demo and a flagship budget decision must both land before 2031.
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.strongest_case_small: Pressure on NASA's planetary budget makes any new flagship baseline decision unlikely before 2031, whatever the technology.
hyper-outer-planet-aerocapture-baseline.signpost: A Uranus flagship study update that carries aerocapture as baseline rather than as an option.

materials-dft-limits.title: Proven limits of density functional theory
materials-dft-limits.description: Theorems marking where Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT), and any efficient universal method for electronic energies, must fail: some ensemble densities have no Kohn-Sham representation (278), the ground-state energy of continuum Coulomb systems is QMA-hard (275), and an atom can bind only a bounded number of extra electrons (263).
materials-dft-limits.status_oct2026: Claimed in openai/math (Oct 6, 2026). 278 and 275 are manuscript-only (T1); 263 has an agent-written Lean proof in the repo, unchecked by outsiders (T3). No named outside expert endorsement or Comparator run found as of Oct 7, 2026.
materials-dft-limits.why: DFT is the workhorse for screening alloys, ceramics, semiconductors, battery electrolytes and propellant chemistry. If 278 holds, some ensemble densities (fractional occupations, open-shell and excited-state ensembles: the regime of transition-metal oxides, defect levels and radiation-damage centres) cannot be reproduced by any Kohn-Sham reference even with the exact functional. If 275 holds, no efficient algorithm computes ground-state energies of all molecules and solids (classically, and on quantum computers unless BQP = QMA). Ceiling results act within months (P3): they tell method developers to stop seeking one universal functional and to invest in domain-specific, data-driven corrections and targeted high-level methods. Band: P3 defaults to High; one band down in S1 because 278 and 275 are T1; S2/S3 assume formalization of continuum quantum mechanics catches up by ~2028 so the premises reach T3-T4.
materials-dft-limits.strongest_case_small: Practitioners already treat DFT as an uncontrolled approximation, and QMA-hardness of the universal functional on lattice models has been known since 2009 (general). Worst-case hardness says nothing about the structured instances space engineers compute. No code, workflow or flown material changes because of these theorems.
materials-dft-limits.signpost: A named electronic-structure theorist endorses or refutes 278/275 (moving them to T2), or an outside Comparator run of 263, by mid-2027; 278 cited in a functional-development paper as the reason for a design choice.

materials-mlip-certified-uq.title: Atomistic AI models with trustworthy error bars
materials-mlip-certified-uq.description: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) that report calibrated, property-level uncertainty (melting point, diffusion barrier, elastic constants) with coverage guarantees and out-of-distribution flags, so atomistic predictions can feed design decisions without case-by-case DFT checks.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.status_oct2026: Universal MLIPs are fast but uncertified. Meta's UMA family (trained on ~500M structures; UMA-M F1 = 0.930 on Matbench Discovery) runs 1,000 atoms at ~16 steps/s on one GPU and fits >100,000 atoms in 80 GB. Ensemble and conformal uncertainty methods exist, but without guarantees for properties derived from long molecular-dynamics runs. No catalog family addresses this.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.why: MLIPs are roughly 10^4-10^5 times cheaper than DFT for the same atoms (general), enabling nanosecond simulations of 10^5-atom cells, the scale where creep-relevant diffusion, grain-boundary oxidation and radiation-damage cascades happen. What blocks engineering use is trust: errors in unfamiliar configurations propagate unpredictably into derived properties. Bounding that propagation (perturbation bounds for stochastic dynamics, conformal coverage under distribution shift) is bespoke applied math that S2's research-grade capability attacks directly; the binding gate then becomes high-level reference data to test coverage. Unlocks high-throughput alloy, ceramic and electrolyte screening with error bars.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.strongest_case_small: Certification is only relative to the reference method, which inherits DFT's own errors (see 278); and the properties engineers qualify (creep, fatigue, toughness) are governed by microstructure at micron-to-millimetre scales that atomistics never reaches.
materials-mlip-certified-uq.signpost: A major MLIP release (UMA, MACE or Orb successors) ships property-level uncertainty with published coverage tests on held-out chemistries by end-2027, and NASA or AFRL ICME workflows adopt it.

materials-multiscale-certified.title: Certified bridges from microstructure to part properties
materials-multiscale-certified.description: Quantitative homogenization and coarse-graining theorems with computable error bounds for nonlinear, inelastic, random microstructures (printed metals, ceramic-matrix composites), so effective properties and their scatter follow from microstructure statistics with certified error.
materials-multiscale-certified.status_oct2026: Quantitative stochastic homogenization exists for linear elliptic problems; plasticity, damage and fatigue in random microstructures remain open (general). No catalog family addresses it, and the release's PDE formalization is thin (3 of 16 PDE families have Lean).
materials-multiscale-certified.why: This is a genuinely open research problem, not an expert-scarcity problem: today engineers bridge scales with calibrated empirical models and test scatter. Under S2, AI does research-grade PDE analysis by 2027-28, making a usable certified bound for one engineering class (for example elasto-viscoplastic polycrystals with porosity) plausible by 2029. Payoff: predicted scatter of fatigue and creep properties from microstructure, the missing link that would let allowables lean on models instead of hundreds of coupons.
materials-multiscale-certified.strongest_case_small: Rigorous bounds for nonlinear problems tend to be loose; engineers already get usable answers from calibrated crystal-plasticity finite elements; and fatigue is governed by rare worst defects (extreme-value statistics), not homogenized averages.
materials-multiscale-certified.signpost: A peer-reviewed or Comparator-checked quantitative homogenization result for a nonlinear inelastic random medium with explicit constants by 2028; Mathlib gains Sobolev-space and homogenization infrastructure.

materials-allowables-stats-framework.title: Design allowables from far fewer test coupons
materials-allowables-stats-framework.description: Statistical methods with proven coverage (hierarchical Bayesian, ICME-informed, transfer learning across machines and lots) that yield A- and B-basis design allowables from far fewer physical tests, accepted in MMPDS Volume II, CMH-17 and NASA-STD-6030 practice.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.status_oct2026: MMPDS created Volume II for process-sensitive materials such as additively manufactured (AM) metals; Senvol's machine-learning approach was shown equivalent to the conventional approach in America Makes work; America Makes still funds conventional allowables (GOTHAAM, $5.5M, 2026 call, AM 7075-class aluminium across three machine classes). NASA is characterizing ~50 AM materials across 8,000+ samples. NASA-STD-6030 (2021) ties allowables to statistical process control of each qualified process.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.why: Directly computed MMPDS-style A/B values traditionally need about 100 observations from at least 10 heats or lots, and a nonparametric A-basis needs 299 (general). For AM, 'a new process means a new material' (NASA AMRL framework, Apr 2026), so each machine and parameter set restarts the clock. Methods that pool information across machines and lots with provable tolerance-bound coverage could cut coupons 40-60% (assumption) and, more importantly, lots and calendar time. The math is solved in principle but expert-scarce, exactly what on-demand AI supplies; handbook-committee acceptance binds, so the band is capped at Medium. 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, Lean, T3) is theory for the posterior sampling these methods use; constants unknown, effect marginal.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.strongest_case_small: Statistics were never the hard part: regulators want physical lot-to-lot variability that only production time generates; handbook committees revise on multi-year cycles; and any coverage proof rests on assumptions (exchangeability across machines) that reviewers will dispute.
materials-allowables-stats-framework.signpost: An MMPDS or CMH-17 coordination group approves a model-informed or Bayesian allowables method, or a NASA-STD-6030 revision references model-based allowables, by 2028.

materials-autonomous-characterization.title: Reliable automated structure identification
materials-autonomous-characterization.description: Robust, uncertainty-aware solution of the characterization inverse problem (automated Rietveld refinement, disorder-aware phase identification, fusion of X-ray, neutron and electron-microscopy data) so autonomous labs' claims of new materials survive expert scrutiny.
materials-autonomous-characterization.status_oct2026: The A-Lab's 43 claimed novel compounds were disputed by Palgrave and Schoop (PRX Energy, 2024), who judged automated Rietveld analysis unreliable and concluded no new materials had been shown; Margraf estimated 80-84% of GNoME's predicted stable compounds would likely be disordered in practice.
materials-autonomous-characterization.why: Autonomous-lab throughput (DeepMind's UK lab plans hundreds of materials per day) is worthless if phase identification is wrong. Structure refinement is a non-convex inverse problem with identifiability limits; AI applied math can supply identifiability analysis, Bayesian refinement with calibrated posteriors and explicit disorder models. This unlocks credible closed-loop discovery, which the space chains (PV absorbers, coatings, electrolytes) need first.
materials-autonomous-characterization.strongest_case_small: Some ambiguities are physical (powder X-ray diffraction cannot distinguish certain orderings), so resolving them needs neutron, synchrotron or electron-microscope time, a facility gate that math cannot remove.
materials-autonomous-characterization.signpost: A blind round-robin in which automated characterization matches expert refinement on at least 90% of samples, or an autonomous-lab discovery paper that passes a published expert audit, by 2027.

materials-learned-functionals.title: Chemical accuracy at DFT cost
materials-learned-functionals.description: Machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals and atomistic models trained on wavefunction-level data that reach about 1 kcal/mol accuracy at semi-local DFT cost, extended from main-group molecules to transition metals, oxides and solids.
materials-learned-functionals.status_oct2026: Microsoft's Skala (preprint Jun 2025) reaches 2.8 kcal/mol on the GMTKN55 benchmark and chemical accuracy on small-molecule atomization energies at semi-local cost; transition metals and solids are not yet covered. 278 (T1) marks a class of ensemble densities that no Kohn-Sham scheme can represent.
materials-learned-functionals.why: Cutting energy errors from ~3-5 kcal/mol (hybrid functionals, general) to ~1 kcal/mol changes the reliability of rankings for propellant decomposition pathways, oxide-scale formation on ceramics and superalloys, defect levels in radiation-damaged semiconductors and electrolyte stability windows. Reference data bind: coupled-cluster and quantum Monte Carlo labels are compute-expensive, so S2 brings the node forward mainly through AI-derived exact constraints and active learning that cut data needs. 278 tells developers where Kohn-Sham-based learning must fail (strong static correlation), steering effort to embedding methods there.
materials-learned-functionals.strongest_case_small: Most space-materials properties are limited by temperature, kinetics and microstructure, not by 1-3 kcal/mol of electronic energy; and 278/275 imply strongly correlated systems stay out of reach.
materials-learned-functionals.signpost: A learned functional with documented error of 1 kcal/mol or less on transition-metal and solid-state benchmarks, released openly, by 2028.

materials-quantum-chem-advantage.title: Quantum computers beat classical chemistry
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.description: A fault-tolerant quantum computation delivers a chemically accurate result for an industrially relevant molecule or material that the best classical methods (DMRG, AFQMC, coupled cluster, neural wavefunctions) cannot match.
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.status_oct2026: Quantinuum Helios (2025): 98 physical qubits, demonstrations of up to 50 logical qubits, about 10 logical spin orbitals usable for chemistry. A Quantinuum-SoftBank white paper (Jul 2026) places chemically accurate simulation with >100 spin orbitals in its 2030s 'Lumos' generation; FeMoco needs 152. FeMoco estimates: ~2,142 logical qubits, ~4M physical qubits, ~4 days (2021), with 2025 algorithmic gains of 4-278x. 275 (T1) implies no universal quantum speedup; 265 (T1, 2D gapped area law) strengthens classical tensor-network methods for gapped 2D systems.
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.why: AI math acts on the algorithm side: resource estimates fell 4-278x in 2025 alone, and S2/S3 assume a further 10-100x (assumption), which would let ~2029 'Apollo'-class machines (~100 spin orbitals) attempt beyond-classical active spaces. Qubit fabrication binds. For space the payoff is indirect: catalysts for propellant decomposition and in-situ resource processing, and correlated-electron materials, not alloys or PV.
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.strongest_case_small: Classical methods, now AI-accelerated, keep moving the goalposts. 275 and 265 cut both ways: there is no universal quantum advantage, and classical tensor networks provably work for gapped 2D systems. Most space-materials problems are not strongly correlated.
materials-quantum-chem-advantage.signpost: A peer-reviewed beyond-classical chemistry result with error bars on logical qubits by 2029; published FeMoco-class resource estimates below 10^5 physical qubits.

materials-am-defect-physics.title: Predictive physics of 3D-printed metal parts
materials-am-defect-physics.description: Validated process-structure-property models for laser powder-bed fusion and directed-energy deposition that predict porosity, microstructure, residual stress and fatigue scatter from process parameters and in-situ sensor signals, with quantified uncertainty.
materials-am-defect-physics.status_oct2026: Active research, not yet qualification-grade: ASME's 2026 special issue on AM qualification calls for physics-informed machine learning, digital twins and uncertainty quantification; NASA's AMRL framework (Apr 2026) stresses that a new process means a new material; Washington State University used AI to find laser settings that make NASA's GRCop-42 printable on standard commercial machines.
materials-am-defect-physics.why: Fatigue life of printed parts is set by the largest lack-of-fusion pores and surface defects, giving one to two orders of magnitude of scatter in cycles to failure (general). A model mapping melt-pool signals to a defect population and then to a life distribution turns AM qualification from 'test every lot' into 'monitor and predict'. The cognitive pieces (multiscale melt-pool models, extreme-value statistics, inverse calibration) compress under S2; the binding gate is paired data (sensor logs, CT scans, fatigue results), generated at autonomous-lab speed from ~2028.
materials-am-defect-physics.strongest_case_small: Melt-pool physics is stochastic (spatter, powder variability, machine drift), so models stay statistical and machine-specific and physical testing remains the evidence regulators accept.
materials-am-defect-physics.signpost: A blind prediction challenge (for example NIST AM-Bench) in which models predict fatigue-life distributions of unseen builds within a factor of two, by 2028.

materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.title: Long-life predictions from short tests
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.description: Mechanism-based models with validated uncertainty that predict 10,000-hour creep rupture, oxidation and thermomechanical fatigue of high-temperature alloys and coatings from roughly 1,000-hour tests.
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.status_oct2026: Extrapolation relies on empirical parametric methods (for example Larson-Miller) and long tests. NASA's GRX-810, built for temperatures above 2,000 F (~1,100 C), claims more than 1,000 times the creep life of conventional superalloys, a claim that itself needed long tests. No catalog family addresses this.
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.why: A 10,000-hour creep test takes about 14 months of real time; it is the physical clock on any new hot-section alloy. Models linking atomistic diffusion (from MLIPs with error bars) to dislocation climb, precipitate coarsening and oxide growth could justify qualification decisions at ~1,000 hours with confirmatory long tests running in parallel, saving roughly a year per alloy (assumption).
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.strongest_case_small: New mechanisms (brittle-phase formation, oxide spallation, coarsening) appear only at long times, so practice rarely accepts extrapolation beyond about three times the test duration (general); engine primes and regulators will keep the long tests.
materials-creep-oxidation-life-models.signpost: A published blind prediction of 10,000-hour rupture life from 1,000-hour or shorter data, within a factor of two, for a new alloy by 2029.

materials-see-system-models.title: Predicting radiation errors in commercial AI chips
materials-see-system-models.description: Hierarchical stochastic models that turn limited proton and heavy-ion beam data into mission-level rates of silent data corruption and functional interrupts for complex commercial processors, GPUs/TPUs and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) running real AI workloads.
materials-see-system-models.status_oct2026: Google tested Trillium TPUs in a 67 MeV proton beam (Nov 2025): HBM irregularities appeared only after 2 krad(Si) versus a 750 rad(Si) shielded five-year dose, with no hard failures up to 15 krad(Si). Starcloud flew an Nvidia H100 in Nov 2025; Nvidia announced the Space-1 Vera Rubin module (GTC, Mar 2026; up to 25x H100 AI compute; 2027). ESA's CORHA-2 project (2024-27) is adding machine learning to radiation hardness assurance.
materials-see-system-models.why: With billions of transistors, device-by-device rate prediction is impossible; operators need workload-level error rates to size mitigation. Knowing the true silent-corruption rate lets an orbital-compute operator replace triple modular redundancy (~3x compute and power) with algorithm-based fault tolerance and checkpointing (~5-20% overhead, general): roughly 2.5x more useful compute per watt in a power-limited satellite. The math (composition of Poisson fault processes, fault propagation through architectures, Bayesian fusion of beam and flight data) is bespoke and suited to AI; scarce beam time and on-orbit statistics bind.
materials-see-system-models.strongest_case_small: Commercial operators may simply fly, measure and iterate, since on-orbit statistics beat models; and the dose margins Google measured suggest radiation is not binding in benign dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbits anyway.
materials-see-system-models.signpost: Published on-orbit error statistics from the Google/Planet prototypes (launch by early 2027) or Space-1 users, compared with pre-flight model predictions.

materials-perovskite-degradation-models.title: Knowing how long perovskite cells last in orbit
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.description: Mechanistic, predictive models of perovskite and perovskite-tandem degradation (ion migration, phase segregation, proton and electron damage, ultraviolet, thermal cycling, self-healing) that map accelerated ground tests to on-orbit lifetime.
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.status_oct2026: A perovskite/silicon tandem reached a certified 27.49% AM0 efficiency on 12.56 cm2, kept 93% after 1e12 protons/cm2 (150 keV) and ~80% after 1e14 electrons/cm2 (1 MeV), and flew stably on a 29.7 km balloon (reported Aug 2026). Potsdam/HZB tandems have been in orbit since Jul 2024; RIT is testing cells on a CubeSat; Hanwha Qcells is supplying tandems for a NASA-backed lunar demo. Mechanisms are known qualitatively, not predictively.
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.why: Perovskites tolerate particle radiation well, but their failure modes are coupled ion-electron-thermal processes with unknown acceleration factors, so no one can yet say what a three-year ground test means for a seven-year mission. AI applied math (coupled drift-diffusion-reaction models, Bayesian model identification) plus autonomous-lab degradation data can make acceleration factors quantitative. On-orbit exposure data to validate the mapping bind.
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.strongest_case_small: Buyers accept flight heritage, not models, and encapsulation and interconnect failures (packaging engineering) often dominate absorber chemistry.
materials-perovskite-degradation-models.signpost: At least one year of published on-orbit current-voltage data from the Potsdam or Chinese tandems with under 10% relative loss, plus a model that predicted it, by 2027-28.
