The JANUS predictive engineering model with one pressure-parameterized transport model predicts SPT-140 thrust within 7% and discharge current within 15% (8% and 17% when extrapolated to orbit) (Whittaker et al., AIAA 2026). Thomson scattering finds electron temperatures ~2x higher than probes.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.why: The candidate mechanisms (electron-cyclotron drift, gradient-drift and ionization instabilities, near-wall conductivity) are known; what is missing is affordable whole-device kinetic simulation plus theory that reduces it to a closure. S2 delivers both cognitively by ~2029; the binding gate is a validation campaign across several thrusters with non-invasive electron diagnostics at low background pressure, which takes about a year.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.strongest_case_small: Sixty years of failure suggests transport is multi-mechanism, geometry-specific and coupled to the test facility; even a good closure may only reach ~5% accuracy, a modest gain over today's calibrated 7-15%. Thrust is already predicted well by calibration, and programs qualify by test regardless.
plasma-hall-anomalous-closure.signpost: A closure that predicts discharge current within 5% across at least three different thrusters (e.g. H9, SPT-140, AEPS) without refitting, published by IEPC 2029.

plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.title: Magnetic nozzle detachment settled
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.description: Accepted kinetic theory and validated simulation of how plasma detaches from a magnetic nozzle and how electrons cool during the expansion: the thrust-producing stage of VASIMR, helicon thrusters and most fusion-drive concepts.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.status_oct2026: Kinetic electron cooling governs energy balance, ion acceleration and detachment (Kim et al., PSST 2023); fully kinetic PIC studies attribute electron detachment to inertia and gyroviscous effects. Ground chambers distort far-plume detachment measurements (general).
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.why: Once kinetic solvers and closures are cheap (S2 2028-29), the theory is a tractable reduction problem; the gate is validation, because detachment happens far downstream where vacuum chambers have walls and background gas. An in-space measurement would settle it.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.strongest_case_small: Detachment may be handled empirically well enough for current thrusters; the binding constraints for VASIMR-class and fusion drives are power supply mass and thermal rejection, not nozzle physics.
plasma-magnetic-nozzle-theory.signpost: Far-field plume measurements in orbit from a magnetic-nozzle thruster (Pulsar Fusion's Sunbird exhaust test is targeted for orbit in 2027) that match a pre-registered kinetic prediction.

plasma-eruption-onset-theory.title: Predicting when the Sun erupts
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.description: Physics-based, probabilistic prediction of flare and CME onset (torus and kink instability thresholds, reconnection onset) from observed active-region magnetic fields, 1-3 days ahead and clearly better than climatology.
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.status_oct2026: Operational flare forecasts are mostly statistical; Surya (Aug 2025) improves short-horizon (up to 2 h) flare forecasting by ~16%. The coronal magnetic field is not routinely measured; reconstructing it from photospheric magnetograms (force-free extrapolation) is an ill-posed inverse problem (general).
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.why: Two things are cognitive and compress under S2: theory of instability onset in realistic 3D fields, and regularized inverse methods for the coronal field with uncertainty. Fifteen years of SDO data plus DKIST and Solar Orbiter give enough to test against. The data gate binds on how much skill is achievable, not on whether progress happens.
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.strongest_case_small: Eruptions may be triggered by small-scale flux emergence below observational resolution, which would cap predictability no matter how good the theory is.
plasma-eruption-onset-theory.signpost: A physics-informed eruption forecast posting a Brier skill score above 0.3 for M-class-plus flares at 24 h on an independent community benchmark by 2028.

plasma-thermo-density-uq.title: Upper-atmosphere density with honest error bars
plasma-thermo-density-uq.description: Thermospheric density nowcasts and 1-3 day forecasts with calibrated uncertainty, cutting quiet-time error from ~20-40% toward ~10-15% and tracking 2-6x storm enhancements, by assimilating drag observed on thousands of constellation satellites.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.status_oct2026: Density is the dominant error in low-orbit prediction; storms raise it 2-5x within hours and empirical models disagree by 20-40% even in quiet times (CPAESS 2026 abstract). Gannon storm, May 2024: density up to ~6x baseline within 12 h, decay of tracked objects 38 -> 180 m/day, thousands of satellites maneuvered, Ap forecasts underpredicted by 100-300 at 1-3 day lead (Parker and Linares 2024). Feb 2022: a G2 storm raised drag up to 50% at ~210 km and 38 of 49 new Starlink satellites reentered.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.why: The sensors already exist: thousands of GNSS-tracked constellation satellites are drag probes. Using them requires joint estimation of density and each satellite's unknown, attitude-dependent ballistic coefficient, an identifiability and estimation-theory problem that is solved in principle but expert-scarce, exactly what S2's on-demand applied math supplies by 2028. The gate is data access: operator ephemerides are proprietary.
plasma-thermo-density-uq.strongest_case_small: At storm time most error comes from the driver forecast (Kp/Ap and the CME's magnetic field), not from the density model, so nowcast gains matter less to operators than 24-72 h forecasts, which stay data-limited (see plasma-bz-forecast).
plasma-thermo-density-uq.signpost: NOAA, Space Force or the Commerce space-traffic system adopts an assimilative density product built on commercial constellation ephemerides, with published calibrated uncertainty, by 2029.

plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.title: D-He3 fusion demonstrated at useful rates
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.description: Experimental demonstration of significant deuterium-helium-3 fusion power, the fuel most fusion-propulsion concepts assume because only ~5% of its energy comes out as neutrons versus ~80% for D-T (general), at the several-times-higher temperatures it requires.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.status_oct2026: Helion's Polaris reported the first private D-T fusion and 150 million deg C plasma (Feb 2026) and says it is working toward D-He3 temperatures; Helion's 50 MW Microsoft target is 2028. No D-He3 burn at meaningful power anywhere. A 1 GW(fusion) D-He3 engine would burn ~50 kg of He-3 per year of operation, versus terrestrial supply of order kilograms per year (arithmetic from 18.3 MeV per reaction; supply figure general).
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.why: This is a physical-clock node: it needs hotter, better-confined plasma and He-3 fuel. AI theory helps optimize pulsed FRC operation and diagnostics interpretation, but it does not heat plasma; under S3 autonomous experimental campaigns could compress the experimental program by a year or so.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.strongest_case_small: The AI-math effect here is close to nil; it is included to show where the chain to fusion propulsion is actually gated.
plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.signpost: Helion or TAE publishes measured D-He3 fusion rates (14.7 MeV proton spectra, neutron fraction) in a peer-reviewed venue.

plasma-ep-predictive-design.title: Design-before-build electric thrusters
plasma-ep-predictive-design.description: Engineering codes that predict a new Hall or gridded-ion thruster's thrust, efficiency, oscillations and plume within a few percent before hardware exists, and extrapolate ground tests to space with quantified uncertainty.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.status_oct2026: Calibrated engineering models predict thrust within 7% and discharge current within 15% (8%/17% ground-to-orbit) for the SPT-140 flown on Psyche (Whittaker et al., AIAA 2026); higher-fidelity Hall2De must be recalibrated per operating condition. NASA states its VF-5 facility reproduces known ground-to-flight differences for AEPS (Williams et al., Space Propulsion 2026).
plasma-ep-predictive-design.why: Two routes, either sufficient: affordable whole-device kinetic simulation used directly, or a validated closure (plasma-hall-anomalous-closure) inside cheap fluid codes. A new Hall thruster typically takes several build-test iterations at roughly a year each (general); a predictive code could cut iterations from ~3-4 to ~1-2. Validation needs test data across designs, which binds the year.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.strongest_case_small: Industry already builds thrusters successfully by build-test-iterate, and small-satellite thrusters iterate cheaply. The value concentrates in high-power devices where testing is hard, a small part of the market.
plasma-ep-predictive-design.signpost: A thruster designed with a predictive tool meets performance within 5% on its first hot fire, documented at IEPC or AIAA by 2030.

plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.title: Thruster lifetime qualified partly by simulation
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.description: Erosion and wear models (low-energy sputter yields, pole-cover and cathode-keeper erosion, near-wall plasma) validated well enough that NASA, ESA or a prime accepts model-based extrapolation for part of a life requirement, shortening multi-year wear tests.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.status_oct2026: AEPS (12 kW, Gateway PPE): three flight thrusters delivered 2025, environmental qualification complete, long-duration life demonstration in preparation, contract closeout mid-to-late 2027; throughput requirement 1,770 kg xenon plus 50% margin (Williams et al., Space Propulsion 2026). Pole erosion is now the life limiter in magnetically shielded thrusters and erosion models have underpredicted measured rates (U. Washington thesis 2025).
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.why: A 23,000-hour wear test is 2.6 years of continuous firing; running ~10,000 hours and extrapolating with an accepted model would save ~1.5 years and tens of millions in facility time (general). That requires both a predictive near-wall plasma model and acceptance by a qualification authority, so the band is capped at Medium and the chain lands late even in S2.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.strongest_case_small: Agencies are conservative and the decisive inputs are materials data (sputter yields at tens of eV), not plasma mathematics; the worst life limiters (e.g. pole erosion) were discovered in test, not predicted. AEPS lessons learned center on risk management, contract oversight and requirements, not physics.
plasma-ep-life-by-analysis.signpost: NASA or ESA formally credits a model-based life extrapolation in a qualification review (e.g. at an AEPS qualification acceptance review) by 2029.

plasma-stellarator-design-loop.title: AI-closed-loop fusion-machine design
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.description: Integrated optimization of stellarator (and other) magnetic configurations against turbulence, fast-ion losses, coil buildability and manufacturing tolerances in weeks, producing designs whose confinement is predicted with error bars.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.status_oct2026: Surrogates in the optimization loop already enable objectives such as full radial heat-flux profiles (arXiv 2609.28730); open optimizers exist (general). Proxima Fusion raised EUR 130M (Jun 2025): Stellarator Model Coil 2027, Alpha demonstration 2031. Type One Energy plans Infinity Two (350 MWe) for the mid-2030s. Family 146 (Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard map, T1, conditional) concerns the textbook model of magnetic-island overlap and field-line chaos: confidence in theory only.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.why: S2's multiphysics design optimization (2028-29) plus trusted surrogates closes the loop. The tool can exist on this schedule, but what it designs still has to be built: coil fabrication tolerances of millimetres over metre-scale coils are the binding gate for whether designs perform as optimized.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.strongest_case_small: Stellarator design is already highly optimized; the binding constraint for fusion is building and operating devices, so better paper designs add no fusion power before 2031.
plasma-stellarator-design-loop.signpost: A stellarator company commits an end-to-end AI-optimized coil set to manufacturing and publishes the predicted-vs-measured field errors.

plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.title: A credible paper design of a fusion rocket
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.description: An integrated design of a fusion propulsion system (e.g. Direct Fusion Drive: small field-reversed configuration plus magnetic nozzle, D-He3) whose sub-models are validated, showing specific power >= 1 kW/kg and multi-year life and closing gaps that today's concept studies wave away.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.status_oct2026: Direct Fusion Drive is a concept modeled by Princeton Satellite Systems and tested at small scale at PPPL; PSS and Pulsar Fusion apply ML to the PFRC experiment. Pulsar's Sunbird exhaust achieved first plasma with krypton in March 2026 with no fusion; an orbital exhaust test is targeted for 2027.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.why: Paper closure is cognitive and compresses under S2/S3, but every sub-model (confinement scaling of small FRCs, D-He3 burn, detachment, radiation and thermal loads) needs data from regimes no device has reached, so the design stays conditional on plasma-dhe3-burn-physics.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.strongest_case_small: Many paper designs already exist; a better one does not change investment or timelines unless experiments back its sub-models.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-design-closure.signpost: NASA, DARPA or ESA funds a fusion-propulsion design whose confinement and nozzle sub-models are validated against PFRC-2 or Polaris-class data.

plasma-fusion-net-gain.title: First magnetic-fusion net energy gain
plasma-fusion-net-gain.description: A magnetic-confinement device reaches scientific gain Q > 1, or Helion delivers net electricity, establishing the energy source that fusion propulsion would ultimately need.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.status_oct2026: CFS SPARC: first plasma targeted 2026 now looking like 2027, Q > 1 targeted soon after; second half of the vacuum vessel arrived May 2026. Helion Polaris: first private D-T fusion, 150 million deg C (Feb 2026); Microsoft PPA target 2028. TAE is merging with Trump Media (announced Dec 2025, close expected mid-2026), with its Copernicus device aiming at net energy before 2030.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.why: Physical-clock anchor: magnets, vacuum vessel, assembly, commissioning and tritium operations set the date. AI contributes through plasma control and faster commissioning (S3), not through mathematics.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.strongest_case_small: The AI-math contribution is close to nil; this node is in the tree to show the gate on fusion propulsion is hardware.
plasma-fusion-net-gain.signpost: SPARC first plasma date and the start of its D-T campaign; Helion's first electricity from Orion.

plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.title: AI-designed thruster flies and performs as predicted
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.description: First in-space operation of an electric thruster whose magnetic circuit, channel and cathode were designed mainly by an AI physics-based optimization loop, with on-orbit performance inside the pre-flight predicted band.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.status_oct2026: No such thruster exists. Small-satellite Hall and ion thrusters go from design to flight in roughly 18-36 months (general); Starlink flies thousands of Hall thrusters (krypton, then argon) designed by conventional iteration (general).
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.why: Cognitive clock: the predictive design tool lands 2030 in S2 and 2029 in S3. Physical clock: build, acceptance test and a rideshare slot add 18-24 months, so first flight is 2032 in S2 and 2031 in S3.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.strongest_case_small: The gain may be a few points of efficiency or a lighter magnetic circuit; the EP market is driven by cost, propellant (xenon/krypton/argon) supply, power-processing-unit mass and production rate, not design optimality.
plasma-ai-designed-thruster-flight.signpost: A startup or prime announces a thruster 'designed in simulation, first-article meets spec' and manifests it for flight.

plasma-high-power-ep-life.title: 100 kW-class thruster runs for thousands of hours
plasma-high-power-ep-life.description: A >= 100 kW electric thruster (nested Hall, lithium MPD or VASIMR-type) demonstrates >= 5,000 hours of ground operation with validated wear projections toward the ~23,000 hours a crewed Mars nuclear-electric mission needs.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.status_oct2026: NASA/JPL's lithium MPD thruster reached 120 kW (Feb 24, 2026); next phases target 500 kW-1 MW per thruster; a crewed mission needs 2-4 MW total and >23,000 h of thruster operation (NASA). VASIMR VX-200SS ran 88 h at 80 kW (Jul 2021), with no newer public endurance result found.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.why: 5,000 h is seven months of continuous firing, which cannot start until a flight-like 100 kW unit and a facility able to hold low background pressure at that power exist (~2028-29 at best). Wall-clock test time does not compress with cognition.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.strongest_case_small: The AI-math effect is close to nil on this node; model-based life credit (plasma-ep-life-by-analysis) is the only lever and it needs the test data first.
plasma-high-power-ep-life.signpost: NASA announces a >1,000 h test of a >=100 kW thruster by 2028.

plasma-abep-demo.title: Air-breathing electric propulsion flight test
plasma-abep-demo.description: A very-low-orbit satellite that scoops residual atmosphere and uses it as electric-propulsion propellant to cancel drag, demonstrated in orbit.
plasma-abep-demo.status_oct2026: Laboratory demonstrations only (general). Intake design is a rarefied-gas (Boltzmann/DSMC) problem; families 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation) and 364 (Boltzmann from Newtonian gases) are T1 and bear on confidence in the kinetic equations used, conditional, not on intake designs. Albedo's Clarity-1 (launched Mar 14, 2025) flew at 350-380 km on xenon ion propulsion for nine months with a drag coefficient 12% better than design (Albedo, Jan 2026).
plasma-abep-demo.why: AI design optimization of intakes and discharge chambers is cognitive and fast under S2, but a flight demo needs funding, an atomic-oxygen-tolerant discharge and a ride, which binds.
plasma-abep-demo.strongest_case_small: Atomic-oxygen erosion of discharge parts, low intake efficiency and power-per-drag are physics and materials limits; conventional EP at 275-380 km already works, as Clarity-1 showed, which weakens the business case.
plasma-abep-demo.signpost: An ABEP in-orbit demo is manifested with a launch date before 2030.

plasma-active-shielding.title: Magnetic radiation shield for crews
plasma-active-shielding.description: A superconducting-magnet active shield demonstrated in space that meaningfully reduces crew dose from solar particle events and galactic cosmic rays at acceptable mass.
plasma-active-shielding.status_oct2026: EU SR2S reached TRL 3 overall (some components TRL 4). NASA NIAC Phase I studied CREW HaT, an open Halbach-torus HTS configuration (NTRS 20250002403, 2025).
plasma-active-shielding.why: AI design optimization can trim coil mass and stress, but deflecting GeV-scale cosmic rays requires a large field-times-length product over a crew-sized volume (general), which sets a mass floor; space qualification of large HTS coils and cryogenics is a multi-year hardware program.
plasma-active-shielding.strongest_case_small: Physics-bound: the Stormer deflection physics is already understood, so better math does not change the mass floor.
plasma-active-shielding.signpost: A funded in-space demonstration of a large HTS magnet (any purpose) flying by 2029.

plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.title: Fusion-powered thrust in space
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.description: Any spacecraft producing measurable thrust from fusion reactions in orbit.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.status_oct2026: No fusion device has net gain at propulsion scale. Pulsar Fusion's Sunbird exhaust test (no fusion; krypton) is targeted for orbit in 2027; Princeton Satellite Systems has spoken of a fusion-propelled mission 'as early as 2028', which no evidence supports.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.why: Requires net-gain fusion in a compact, flight-mass device, a suitable fuel, and a launch-approved system. Even S3's near-free cognition leaves every one of these gated by experiments, fabrication and regulation.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.strongest_case_small: Not applicable: this node records a nil effect inside the horizon.
plasma-fusion-propulsion-flight.signpost: A fusion-propulsion company shows measured fusion products from a flight-configured device on the ground.

plasma-cme-arrival-skill.title: CME arrival forecasts within about 8 hours
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.description: Operational CME arrival-time forecasts with mean absolute error <= 8 h (from 13.2 h) and calibrated probability windows.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.status_oct2026: CCMC Arrival Time Scoreboard, 11 years: bias -2.5 h, mean absolute error 13.2 h, standard deviation 17.4 h, only slight improvement; errors dominated by CME reconstruction and background solar wind (Kay et al., Space Weather 2024). ESA's Vigil at L5 (carrying NOAA's CCOR coronagraph) is planned to launch in 2031.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.why: AI-built ensembles plus better background-solar-wind modeling (coronal field extrapolation, an ill-posed inverse problem where mathematics genuinely helps) could cut MAE by ~30-40% before side-view data exist; the full gain needs Vigil, which operates only after 2031. Operational transition (research-to-operations) adds 1-2 years.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.strongest_case_small: Eleven years of model development barely moved the error; the limit is the inputs, and AI cannot observe a CME from the side.
plasma-cme-arrival-skill.signpost: Rolling 12-month MAE of the best CCMC scoreboard models falls below 10 h during 2027-28.

plasma-bz-forecast.title: Knowing a CME's magnetic punch a day ahead
plasma-bz-forecast.description: Forecasting the southward magnetic field (Bz) of an incoming CME 12-24+ hours before arrival: the main driver of geomagnetic storm severity and of the storm-time density errors that hit satellites.
plasma-bz-forecast.status_oct2026: Magnetic structure is recognized as the main bottleneck; operationally Bz is known only as the CME passes L1, roughly 30-60 minutes before impact (SOLAR-1 operational 2026; timing general). Short-term in-situ methods still need a human in the loop (arXiv 2602.06926, Feb 2026).
plasma-bz-forecast.why: Requires either routine coronal magnetic-field measurement or in-situ monitors well upstream of L1, neither of which will exist by 2031. AI theory can extract partial skill from source-region magnetograms (flux-rope chirality and orientation rules), which is why S2/S3 are Low rather than Speculative.
plasma-bz-forecast.strongest_case_small: This is an observation limit, not a mathematics limit.
plasma-bz-forecast.signpost: Funding of a sub-L1 or off-Sun-Earth-line in-situ monitor, or a source-region method with Bz-sign skill above 70% on 50+ events.

plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.title: Storm-proof low-orbit operations
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.description: Constellation operators and space-traffic services run conjunction screening and station-keeping on probabilistic density forecasts with realistic covariance, so storms no longer cause mass loss of tracking custody, unplanned reentries or blind maneuvering.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.status_oct2026: During the May 2024 storm thousands of satellites maneuvered and conjunction assessment was poorly predictable even a day ahead (Parker and Linares 2024); KANOPUS-V 3 lost ~917 m of semi-major axis within days (CPAESS 2026 abstract). SpaceX's response to the Feb 2022 loss was operational (higher insertion orbits) (general).
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.why: Once density products carry calibrated uncertainty (2029 in S2), propagating it into covariance and screening is mature astrodynamics; the gate is adoption by operators and the government catalog, which typically takes 1-2 years.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.strongest_case_small: The largest operators already manage storms with margin and autonomy; the benefit concentrates in smaller operators and the public catalog. Losses like Feb 2022 were an operations choice and were fixed operationally.
plasma-storm-robust-leo-ops.signpost: At the next G4+ storm, count objects losing custody and emergency maneuvers versus May 2024.

plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.title: Radiation-belt and charging forecasts a week ahead
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.description: Probabilistic, physics-consistent forecasts of MeV electron flux and surface/internal charging hazard 1-7 days ahead, used in satellite operations and to size shielding and charging margins.
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.status_oct2026: Random-forest models (VAMPIRE/COVEN, Jun 2026) forecast ~2 MeV flux alert crossings up to a week ahead; SPARTAI gives multi-day MeV forecasts (Oct 2025); transformer and LSTM pipelines forecast 1 MeV flux 6 h ahead (arXiv 2605.15752). Charging codes (SPIS, NASCAP-2K) are mature; PAGER internal-charging models were validated against GEO anomalies (IEEE TPS 2026).
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.why: ML forecasts exist; AI applied math adds coupling to physics-based diffusion models and calibrated uncertainty so operators can act on probabilities (e.g. defer an orbit-raise or EP firing through a charging peak).
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.strongest_case_small: Already ML-driven, so the math increment is modest; designers will keep worst-case design environments (e.g. AE9/AP9) regardless of forecasts, so design margins do not shrink.
plasma-radbelt-charging-forecast.signpost: SWPC or ESA adopts a multi-day MeV electron probability product and an operator or insurer cites it in procedures.

plasma-vleo-at-scale.title: Commercial constellations below 300 km
plasma-vleo-at-scale.description: At least 100 commercial satellites operating sustainably below 300 km altitude, with propellant and drag margins sized from validated density statistics.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.status_oct2026: Albedo's Clarity-1 operated at 350-380 km for nine months (Mar-Dec 2025) and projects five-year life at 275 km averaged over solar cycles; it lost contact due to a radio memory fault, not drag (Albedo, Jan 2026). Solar Cycle 25 peaked Oct 2024; the declining phase runs to ~2030, lowering mean density but still producing large storms.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.why: Drag make-up propellant scales with the density margin designers carry: cutting a ~2x margin to ~1.3x through validated statistics trims the propellant reserve by about a third (illustrative arithmetic), which helps VLEO business cases. But constellations need capital, launches and production first.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.strongest_case_small: Capital, demand for very-high-resolution imagery, EP throughput and atomic-oxygen-tolerant hardware bind this, not density mathematics.
plasma-vleo-at-scale.signpost: A sub-300 km operator raises >= $100M and orders >= 50 satellites by 2028.

plasma-nep-mars-cargo.title: Megawatt electric cargo ships to Mars
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.description: An operational nuclear-electric (or megawatt solar-electric) cargo vehicle with MW-class electric propulsion flying to Mars.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.status_oct2026: NASA estimates 2-4 MW and >23,000 h thruster life for crewed nuclear-electric missions; earlier NASA Glenn COMPASS work sized a 1.9 MWe system for a 2-year crewed round trip and ~200 t cargo stages. Highest demonstrated single-thruster power: 120 kW lithium MPD (Feb 2026).
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.why: Needs a flight reactor or MW-class arrays, launch approval for a space reactor, and life-tested MW thrusters; each is a multi-year hardware and regulatory program.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.strongest_case_small: Not applicable: this node records a nil effect inside the horizon.
plasma-nep-mars-cargo.signpost: A funded flight-reactor program with a launch date, or a >= 500 kW thruster test campaign announced.

plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.title: Faster, cheaper electric-propulsion development
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.description: Development-to-qualification time for new EP thrusters falls ~30-50% and build-test iterations roughly halve because physics-based models replace parts of empirical iteration and wear testing.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.status_oct2026: AEPS: contract awarded 2016 (general), qualification still in progress with closeout expected mid-to-late 2027, about 11 years (Williams et al., Space Propulsion 2026).
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.why: Combines predictive design (fewer iterations) with model-based life credit (shorter wear tests). Both arrive 2030-31 even in S2 and the outcome needs one full development cycle to show, so it is visible only at the edge of the horizon in S3.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.strongest_case_small: Program management, supply chain and funding dominate EP schedules; AEPS's own lessons learned are about risk management, contract oversight and requirement definition, not physics.
plasma-outcome-ep-cycle-time.signpost: A new EP product announced with qualification completed in under three years, citing model-based life credit.

prop-ns-forced-verified.title: Forced Navier–Stokes blowup independently checked
prop-ns-forced-verified.description: Outside experts run Comparator on the Lean proof and audit the statement of OpenAI's Sep 8, 2026 claim that the forced 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations can blow up from smooth, finite-energy data, along with the concurrent Buckmaster–Alpöge Euler, Boussinesq and porous-medium blowup proofs. This moves the claim from T3 to T4.
prop-ns-forced-verified.status_oct2026: Claimed Sep 8, 2026 with a 166-page manuscript and Lean repository (~17 h formalization; ~88 h of ~10,000 agents). Buckmaster and Alpöge posted Lean-verified Euler/Boussinesq/IPM blowup preprints on Sep 7, followed by a public credit dispute. No independent review found as of Oct 7, 2026: T3. Duraiswami (arXiv 2609.17642, Sep 15, 2026) found nothing to suggest the mechanism is reachable in a flow one computes or builds. Related family 376 (universal computation in forced NS) is T1.
prop-ns-forced-verified.why: The Lean code is public and the dispute guarantees scrutiny, so a Comparator run plus a statement audit is likely within about 12 months in every scenario. The engineering consequence is a confidence change only (position d): the forced equations alone can fail to determine the flow, which CFD practice already assumes by adding numerical or model dissipation. No solver, closure or engine design changes.
prop-ns-forced-verified.strongest_case_small: The forcing is engineered to drive the singularity, and real propellants would cavitate or form shocks long before it occurs (Duraiswami 2026). Rocket CFD resolves or models scales where the continuum assumption itself fails. The propulsion impact is essentially nil. The node is on the tree to mark a dead end readers would otherwise take for a breakthrough.
prop-ns-forced-verified.signpost: First published Comparator report and statement audit for the NS Lean repository (via Hexagon or the IAS advisory group), expected within 6-12 months. A gap would drop the claim to T1.

prop-ns-clay-unforced.title: Unforced Navier–Stokes (Clay problem) settled
prop-ns-clay-unforced.description: AI resolves the actual Clay Millennium statement for the unforced 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations: global smoothness or blowup on R^3 or the torus.
prop-ns-clay-unforced.status_oct2026: Open. Forced blowup is claimed (T3), as is Euler blowup (Buckmaster–Alpöge, Lean). Family 376 (T1) shows that forced flows can embed universal computation, the route Tao proposed toward blowup constructions.
prop-ns-clay-unforced.why: Under S2, solvable depth doubles every 6-9 months, and the two hardest precursor steps (Euler blowup, forced NS blowup) fell in 2026, so removing the forcing by about 2029 is plausible. Either answer acts through P5 only. A blowup would occur at scales below the molecular mean free path in any real gas or liquid; a regularity proof would confirm what every code already assumes.
prop-ns-clay-unforced.strongest_case_small: No propulsion code, closure or test plan depends on the answer: a $1M prize result with roughly zero engineering effect. Its effect on public perception ('AI solved fluid dynamics') may exceed its technical effect, a communications risk the paper should address directly.
prop-ns-clay-unforced.signpost: A lab announces unforced NS blowup or regularity with a Lean proof, and the Clay Institute responds.

prop-les-convergence-theory.title: Convergence theory for turbulent simulations
prop-les-convergence-theory.description: A proven framework (for example statistical or measure-valued solutions) that states which LES/DNS statistics converge under mesh refinement, with computable error bounds, so that 'grid-converged LES' has a defined meaning.
prop-les-convergence-theory.status_oct2026: Open. LES has no classical grid-convergence theory; practitioners use heuristics such as resolving ~80% of turbulent kinetic energy (general). The Euler and forced-NS blowup claims (T3) reinforce that pointwise convergence can fail, so convergence has to be statistical.
prop-les-convergence-theory.why: This feeds prop-cfd-auto-vv: the credibility statement for an injector LES could carry a numerical error bar instead of an expert's judgment. If the bounds are computable, they would also show analysts when they are over-resolving, plausibly saving 2-4x compute on design LES (judgment, general).
prop-les-convergence-theory.strongest_case_small: The theory may give only asymptotic rates with no usable constants. Validation against experiment would still dominate credibility, and model-form (closure) error usually exceeds numerical error.
prop-les-convergence-theory.signpost: An AI-assisted proof of convergence rates for statistics of 3D LES with explicit constants, cited in an AIAA CFD workshop guideline.

prop-certified-stability-rom.title: Certified combustion-stability models
prop-certified-stability-rom.description: Low-order acoustic-network or Galerkin models of chamber thermoacoustics, delivered with rigorous linear and nonlinear stability margins: Lyapunov or sum-of-squares certificates and bounds on Hopf bifurcation and triggering amplitude under an uncertain flame-response band.
prop-certified-stability-rom.status_oct2026: Solved in principle but expert-scarce. DLR/TU Delft network models predict acoustic frequencies within <5% on two research combustors (de Jong Cantarino et al., IJSCD 2026). Growth rates and triggering thresholds still hinge on flame response, and reliable, efficient instability prediction remains rare (JAXA 2025). Family 143 [L] (uniform limit-cycle bounds, Hilbert's 16th) is T3 but theory only: it bounds how many oscillation states can coexist in planar polynomial amplitude models, with no practical constant.
prop-certified-stability-rom.why: Stability analysis of a given model is bespoke but routine mathematics, exactly the kind that becomes on-demand under position (a). With public research-grade models in 2027 (S2), a team can get certified margins for every injector variant in days instead of a specialist's months. The value is capped by the flame-response input (prop-flame-response).
prop-certified-stability-rom.strongest_case_small: Certifying the stability of a model with the wrong flame response gives false comfort: a proof of the wrong property. Bomb tests stay mandatory. The F-1 lesson is that triggered (nonlinear) instability is what destroys engines, and its inputs are physical.
prop-certified-stability-rom.signpost: A published AI-produced stability analysis that predicts unstable modes and triggering thresholds on a rig (DLR BKD/BKH, Purdue CVRC) before the test.

prop-stiff-chemistry.title: Fast chemistry with certified error
prop-stiff-chemistry.description: Reduced kinetic mechanisms and structure-preserving stiff integrators with provable error bounds on ignition delay, heat release and key species, so that detailed LOX/CH4 and LOX/H2 chemistry fits inside engine LES at a fraction of today's cost.
prop-stiff-chemistry.status_oct2026: Chemistry integration dominates reacting-flow cost: 48,000 core-hours for 2 ms of one spray LES with 54 species (UConn 2023). Mechanism reduction (DRG, QSS) is heuristic and checked by sampling. Family 149 (permanence for weakly reversible reaction networks, T1) gives a qualitative persistence guarantee for isothermal mass-action systems only. Conditional, theory only.
prop-stiff-chemistry.premise_tier: n/a (capability); 149 is T1, conditional and marginal
prop-stiff-chemistry.why: A 3-10x cut in reacting-LES cost (estimate, general) means 3-10x more design points per week and makes flame-response prediction affordable. Error certificates let teams trust reduced mechanisms outside their training conditions.
prop-stiff-chemistry.strongest_case_small: GPU chemistry and ML surrogates already deliver much of the speedup without proofs, and practitioners may not value certificates. Family 149 assumes isothermal, closed mass-action networks, while combustion is non-isothermal and open.
prop-stiff-chemistry.signpost: A reduced-mechanism generator with certified error bounds released in Cantera, Pele or a commercial CFD code.

prop-cfd-auto-vv.title: Automated CFD verification and credibility
prop-cfd-auto-vv.description: AI agents run code verification (manufactured solutions), solution verification (adjoint or a-posteriori error estimates), uncertainty quantification and NASA-STD-7009-style credibility assessment on every propulsion simulation at near-zero marginal cost.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.status_oct2026: Solved in principle, but rarely done in full on engine-design CFD because it is labor-intensive (general). CFD Vision 2030 progress reviews flag separated-flow prediction and UQ as persistent gaps (Aerospace America, Dec 2022).
prop-cfd-auto-vv.why: Every CFD result becomes a number with an error bar that separates numerical error from model-form error. That ends two expensive failure modes: hardware built on an unconverged simulation, and tests run to settle a question the simulation had already answered. It is also a prerequisite for any regulator credit for simulation.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.strongest_case_small: Validation data, not verification labor, limit V&V. Error bars on RANS are dominated by closure error, which verification cannot remove.
prop-cfd-auto-vv.signpost: An AI-generated credibility assessment accepted in a NASA or prime-contractor design review, or AI-automated solution verification in AIAA CFD Prediction Workshop entries.

prop-mass-gauging.title: Low-gravity propellant gauging limits
prop-mass-gauging.description: Proofs of which tank-fill states can be identified in microgravity from boundary sensors (capacitance, radio-frequency or impedance-type tomography), plus gauging algorithms with guaranteed error bounds.
prop-mass-gauging.status_oct2026: Gauging is a focus area of NASA's CFM portfolio, alongside boil-off and transfer. Family 365 [L] (joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch, with conductivity nonuniqueness) is T3 and acts as a ceiling: some interior configurations cannot be told apart from boundary data alone without priors or extra sensing.
prop-mass-gauging.why: Gauging uncertainty turns into reserve propellant: on a depot holding over 1,000 t, each 1% of gauging error is ~10 t of margin (illustrative, general). The ceiling side (P3) tells designers to stop pursuing tomography-only gauging and to fuse sensors with thermodynamic models.
prop-mass-gauging.strongest_case_small: Operators can gauge after a settling burn with conventional sensors and accept the margin. The nonuniqueness in family 365 concerns specific (often anisotropic) settings that may not match real tanks.
prop-mass-gauging.signpost: Flight gauging accuracy reported from LOXSAT or the Starship transfer demo (target <=1%).

prop-closure-theory.title: Turbulence and combustion closures with guarantees
prop-closure-theory.description: AI-built RANS, LES subgrid and flamelet closures that are realizable, frame-invariant and consistent in known limits, carry generalization bounds, and are validated across separated, swirling and reacting benchmark classes without per-case tuning.
prop-closure-theory.status_oct2026: Open; this is the field's central modeling problem. RANS cannot reliably predict separated flows (CFD Vision 2030). ML closures often fail to generalize beyond their training data (JFM 2025; arXiv 2604.25824, Apr 2026). A propulsion example: k-omega SST under-predicts LH2 tank self-pressurization by 15-16% and vapor temperature by up to 40%, versus 3% for laminar and 7% for IDDES (Kartuzova et al., SciTech 2025).
prop-closure-theory.why: Closure error is the dominant model-form error in propulsion CFD: wall heat flux for cooling, mixing, nozzle separation. Under S2 the cognitive part (deriving constrained closures, proving consistency) is fast. What binds is high-fidelity data at engine conditions. DNS at engine Reynolds numbers is infeasible even at exascale (Pele's largest run: 60 billion cells), and high-pressure reacting validation experiments take years.
prop-closure-theory.strongest_case_small: Turbulence closure has resisted 60 years of work and may be fundamentally underdetermined, because averaging loses information. A provably consistent closure need not beat a tuned one on a specific engine. LES and hybrid methods are already replacing RANS in design-critical areas.
prop-closure-theory.signpost: An AI-derived closure tops the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource separated-flow cases and a blind AIAA workshop case without retuning.

prop-flame-response.title: Predictive flame response at engine pressures
prop-flame-response.description: First-principles prediction of injector flame transfer functions and transcritical real-fluid mixing for LOX/CH4 and LOX/H2 at 100-350 bar. This is the missing input that decides whether a chamber mode grows.
prop-flame-response.status_oct2026: Measured on subscale rigs or extracted from costly LES; wall-modeled LES at engine conditions is described as prohibitively expensive (JAXA 2025). Raptor 3 has demonstrated 350 bar chamber pressure (newspaceeconomy, Apr 16, 2026), deep in the supercritical regime where injection models lack validation (general).
prop-flame-response.why: With flame response predicted, certified reduced models (prop-certified-stability-rom) predict growth rates, not just frequencies. Validation can start against decades of archived rig data, but it then needs about a year of blind rig tests. That experimental year binds in S2 and S3 alike.
prop-flame-response.strongest_case_small: Flame response depends on manufacturing detail (injector tolerances, additive-manufacturing roughness) and on transient states that models won't capture. Rigs remain necessary for every new injector family.
prop-flame-response.signpost: Blind prediction of an unstable mode's frequency and amplitude to within ~10% on a JANNAF, ESA or DLR combustor before the test.

prop-rde-mode-theory.title: Predictive theory of detonation-engine wave modes
prop-rde-mode-theory.description: A validated model of how many detonation waves an RDRE runs, when it switches modes, and how injectors couple to the waves, as functions of flow rate, mixture and back-pressure, so that engines can be designed to hold one stable mode.
prop-rde-mode-theory.status_oct2026: Open research: wave-mode bifurcation (APS DFD 2025), dynamic injector-response models (Mar 2025), and model equations that capture qualitative mode-locking (arXiv 2003.06655). Hardware is ahead of theory: NASA InRoDES fired a 10,000 lbf-class LOX/LCH4 thrust chamber for >340 s (Sep and Dec 2025).
prop-rde-mode-theory.why: RDRE gains of up to ~10% in thrust and specific impulse, or a 5x lower injection feed pressure (NASA NTRS 2024), appear only with stable, predictable modes. This is nonlinear-dynamics mathematics that S2 makes cheap, and the validating hot-fire campaigns take days to weeks.
prop-rde-mode-theory.strongest_case_small: RDRE development is advancing empirically (340-s firings, Venus flight). Theory may mostly explain what tests already found; the real gates are thermal management of a compact chamber and nozzle integration.
prop-rde-mode-theory.signpost: A published model that predicts mode transitions on a new RDRE geometry blind, confirmed by NASA or AFRL tests.

prop-cfm-models.title: Validated microgravity cryogenic fluid models
prop-cfm-models.description: Predictive models of self-pressurization, slosh, line chilldown and tank-to-tank transfer in low gravity, validated on flight data with quantified uncertainty (tank pressure within ~5%, boil-off within ~10%).
prop-cfm-models.status_oct2026: In 1 g, CFD reaches 3% (laminar) to 7% (IDDES) on tank pressure, but results hinge on the turbulence model and a tuned evaporation accommodation coefficient (Kartuzova et al., SciTech 2025). Microgravity data are scarce (ZBOT on ISS). NASA's CFM portfolio lists maturing predictive models through flight-prediction comparisons as an objective. LOXSAT (Eta Space/Rocket Lab, a 9-month LOX demo) was set for no earlier than Jul 17, 2026; the sources found do not confirm whether it has flown.
prop-cfm-models.why: Boil-off and transfer losses drive the tanker count (SpaceX '10-ish' vs NASA 'high teens'). In an illustrative depot model (tables), boil-off of 0.05-0.3%/day costs ~1 extra tanker at one tanker per 6 days, and 0.3-0.5%/day costs 3-5 extra at one per 12 days. Validated models let operators set margins from prediction instead of conservatism. In S2 the analysis is near-instant once flight data exist, but the data arrive on the launch clock (2027 onward).
prop-cfm-models.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will learn empirically from its own flights and keep the data, and margins will follow measured performance whether or not a public model exists.
prop-cfm-models.signpost: Publication of transferred mass, boil-off and chilldown losses from the first Starship ship-to-ship transfer, or NASA model-vs-flight comparisons from LOXSAT.

prop-psi-models.title: Predictive plume–surface interaction for landers
prop-psi-models.description: Validated models of how lander engine plumes erode regolith (rarefied-to-continuum gas flow, granular ejecta, cratering), used to set landing-site and engine-placement requirements.
prop-psi-models.status_oct2026: NASA reports that poorly constrained flight data inhibit accurate PSI prediction. Langley's vacuum-sphere PSI tests run through spring 2026, and MSFC PSI tools support HLS (NTRS 2023). Families 363 (Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation) and 364 (Boltzmann derived from Newtonian gases, incl. fluctuations) are T1 and touch the kinetic theory beneath DSMC. Conditional; P5 confidence only.
prop-psi-models.why: Multi-meganewton Raptor-class landing plumes on unprepared regolith are a mission risk for Starship HLS, and predictive PSI decides whether landing pads or high-mounted thrusters are needed. Family 364 would firm up the Boltzmann foundations for DSMC in the rarefied plume; family 363 flags where kinetic solutions need a selection principle.
prop-psi-models.strongest_case_small: DSMC already works for the gas phase. The gaps are granular physics and lunar flight data, which no theorem supplies, and operators can engineer around PSI with pads, throttling or thruster placement.
prop-psi-models.signpost: Pre-landing PSI predictions matched by post-landing imagery from CLPS or Artemis landers.

prop-ntp-fuel-model.title: Nuclear thermal fuel behavior model
prop-ntp-fuel-model.description: A validated multiphysics model of carbide or CERMET fuel corrosion, cracking and fission-product release in 2,500-3,000 K hydrogen under irradiation and thermal cycling. These are the physics that set NTP temperature, Isp and life.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.status_oct2026: GA-EMS fuel survived six thermal cycles to 2,600 K in flowing hydrogen at MSFC (Jan 2025). Core materials that endure 2,500-3,000 K hydrogen at >3 MPa remain the critical obstacle (general literature). Neutron transport (Monte Carlo) is mature (general). Families 278 (Kohn–Sham ensemble representability fails) and 275 (QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy) are T1: ceilings on DFT-based materials modeling. Conditional, P3.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.why: Fuel life and temperature set NTP's ~900 s Isp, against ~450 s for LOX/LH2 (general). A predictive model narrows the irradiation test matrix. But irradiation in test reactors (months to years to accumulate fluence) binds: autonomous labs speed up non-nuclear hot-hydrogen tests, not neutron dose.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.strongest_case_small: Fuel qualification is inherently empirical and regulators will require data. Families 278 and 275 confirm DFT limits that practitioners already work around.
prop-ntp-fuel-model.signpost: Release of a combined hot-hydrogen plus irradiation dataset (INL/MSFC) with blind model predictions.

prop-stability-design-tool.title: Design out combustion instability before hot fire
prop-stability-design-tool.description: An integrated workflow (predicted flame response, a certified reduced-order stability model and uncertainty quantification) that ranks injector and chamber designs by stability margin before hardware is built, used on a real engine program.
prop-stability-design-tool.status_oct2026: Instability is still found and fixed on the test stand. For the F-1, 'Project Go' ran 2,000 tests on 210 injector designs over two years before bomb tests showed damping within 45 ms (enginehistory.org; NASA History, Jul 12, 2019). Modern programs iterate faster with cheap additive injectors, but the loop remains test-driven.
prop-stability-design-tool.why: If even a third of instability redesign loops are avoided, a new engine saves months to a year and tens of hardware sets (judgment, general). The math (stability certificates) is fast under S2; flame-response validation and qualification testing are not.
prop-stability-design-tool.strongest_case_small: For well-funded teams, SpaceX-style rapid iteration with cheap 3D-printed injectors already makes testing cheaper than prediction (600+ Raptors built by Apr 2026). Bomb tests and stability rating stay mandatory, so the tests saved are development tests, not qualification tests.
prop-stability-design-tool.signpost: An engine program reports first-article stability qualification with no injector redesign and credits predictive tools.

prop-ai-engine-design-loop.title: AI-generated engines at scale
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.description: Computational engineering models generate complete additively-manufactured engines (geometry, regenerative cooling, injectors) in weeks. The node counts as achieved when a >=200 kN AI-generated engine completes a full-duration hot fire.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.status_oct2026: LEAP 71's Noyron generated a 5 kN LOX/kerosene aerospike that worked on its first firing (Dec 18, 2024). The 200 kN LOX/CH4 XRA-2E5 was printed as one Inconel part in 289 h (Mar 2026), with a hot fire planned before 2027. The Exploration Company licensed Noyron (Mar 24, 2026). Venus Aerospace credits 'AI-enabled design software' for its RDRE (Mercury Fund, Jul 21, 2026).
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.why: Design labor collapses toward zero, so the loop period is set by print time (~2 weeks for a large part) and test-stand availability. Once cap-design-optimization arrives, AI math adds guarantees such as proven cooling-channel thermal margins, but the loop already exists without it.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.strongest_case_small: Design labor was never the long pole for large engines; reliability growth and qualification are. Noyron-style tools encode engineering rules rather than frontier mathematics, so the openai/math release adds little here.
prop-ai-engine-design-loop.signpost: A full-duration XRA-2E5 hot fire, and the first orbital flight on an AI-generated main engine.

prop-turbopump-tool.title: Predictive turbopump cavitation and stability
prop-turbopump-tool.description: Models that predict rotating cavitation, cavitation surge and rotordynamic instability for new inducer and pump designs before water-flow and hot-fire tests.
prop-turbopump-tool.status_oct2026: CFD predictions of cavitation instabilities depend strongly on the chosen cavitation and turbulence models, and 3D linear perturbation theories with dynamic transfer matrices are advancing (Pisa thesis, Jun 2025). Several Raptor 3 engines shut down <20 s into boostback on a mid-2026 flight; commentary pointed to combustion, turbopump or sensor-redline margins, with no official cause (Nerra Network, Jun 18, 2026).
prop-turbopump-tool.why: Turbopump instabilities are a leading cause of engine failures (general). Stability analysis of transfer-matrix models is applied math that S2 makes cheap, but predicting the cavitation-compliance and mass-flow-gain inputs needs closures and rig data.
prop-turbopump-tool.strongest_case_small: Water-flow rig tests are cheap compared with hot fire, and design rules are mature, so prediction may save little.
prop-turbopump-tool.signpost: A blind prediction of rotating-cavitation onset for a new inducer, confirmed in a rig test.

prop-life-twin.title: Probabilistic engine life prediction for reuse
prop-life-twin.description: Physics-based life models for thermomechanical fatigue, low-cycle fatigue and creep in chambers, turbines and additively-manufactured parts, with uncertainty quantification, updated after each flight from sensors and inspection.
prop-life-twin.status_oct2026: Life estimation is hampered by heat-flux uncertainty, the choice of plasticity model and a lack of specimen characterization (Lisbon thesis 2024; Polito 2025). The methods are Morrow, Norton and Miner, validated on SSME-era data. Families 372 (global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity) and 366 (planar Mumford–Shah crack regularity) are T1 links to inspection inverse problems. Conditional, P5.
prop-life-twin.why: Reuse economics turn on refurbishment intervals. Probabilistic life models with UQ are expert-scarce applied math, the category S2 makes cheap. Operators already hold fleet data from hundreds of reflown engines, so data binds less here than elsewhere.
prop-life-twin.strongest_case_small: Operators extend life through fleet-leader experience anyway, so any gain is internal and hard to observe. Heat-flux uncertainty (a closure problem) limits physics-based accuracy.
prop-life-twin.signpost: An operator or NASA discloses model-based (not fleet-leader-only) engine life limits, or NASA accepts probabilistic life analysis for crewed reuse.

prop-start-transient.title: Predictive engine start and relight transients
prop-start-transient.description: Validated system-level models of line chilldown, ignition, turbopump spin-up and combustion onset for in-flight relights after a coast, used to design start sequences with quantified margin.
prop-start-transient.status_oct2026: A live 2026 problem: on Flight 13 (Jul 25, 2026) only 10 of 13 booster engines relit for landing, and about five were running at splashdown (Spaceflight Now). Start transients are stiff differential-algebraic systems with uncertain two-phase chilldown physics (general).
prop-start-transient.why: Relight reliability gates booster catch, ship landing and, most critically, HLS lunar descent after days to weeks in orbit. Modeling stiff transients with certified numerics is applied math, and every flight supplies validation data.
prop-start-transient.strongest_case_small: SpaceX will probably fix relight empirically within a few flights, and models will follow the data rather than lead it.
prop-start-transient.signpost: Several consecutive Starship flights with full booster and ship relight success, especially after long coasts.

prop-verified-engine-software.title: Formally verified engine control software
prop-verified-engine-software.description: Machine-checked proofs that engine-controller and health-management logic (start sequencing, redlines, abort logic, numerical filters) meets its specification, produced by AI agents at low cost and accepted in certification.
prop-verified-engine-software.status_oct2026: Certification standards already give credit for formal methods (DO-178C/DO-333), but AI agents and Lean are not qualified tools. The agentic formalization capability exists: openai/math formalized the main results of 162 papers in weeks. The 2026 Raptor 3 boostback shutdowns, with sensor trip as one hypothesis, show why redline logic matters.
prop-verified-engine-software.why: Engine controllers are safety-critical, and false or missed shutdowns from redline logic recur as a failure mode (general). AI proofs cut verification cost and make full formal coverage practical. The band is capped at Medium because it needs certification acceptance.
prop-verified-engine-software.strongest_case_small: Most engine failures are physical rather than software. Commercial launch licensing does not require formal verification, and writing correct specifications remains the bottleneck.
prop-verified-engine-software.signpost: The first NASA crewed-program or FAA certification credit for AI-generated formal proofs of propulsion controller software.

prop-ship-transfer-demo.title: Ship-to-ship cryogenic transfer demonstrated
prop-ship-transfer-demo.description: Two Starships dock in low Earth orbit and transfer tens to 100+ tonnes of LOX and liquid methane, with measured boil-off, chilldown loss and transfer efficiency.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.status_oct2026: Starship reached orbit for the first time on Flight 14 (Sep 28, 2026) and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites (Mach33, Sep 30, 2026). Ship-to-ship transfer has not flown yet and could come as soon as Flight 15 in late 2026 (Space.com). Internal tank-to-tank transfer was done on Mar 14, 2024. NASA OIG (Mar 2026) calls cryogenic transfer 'one of the most significant technical challenges'.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.why: Flights and vehicle readiness set the timing, and AI mathematics moves this node by roughly zero. It is on the tree because its data unlock prop-cfm-models and, downstream, the refueling economy.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.strongest_case_small: Not applicable: this node exists to show the physical clock. The AI-math effect on its date is nil.
prop-ship-transfer-demo.signpost: Announcement and flight of the propellant-transfer mission, with the transferred mass disclosed.

prop-rde-flight-demo.title: Detonation engine flies in space
prop-rde-flight-demo.description: A rotating detonation rocket engine of about 1,000 lbf or more operates as primary propulsion in a space or lander flight demonstration, beyond suborbital hops.
prop-rde-flight-demo.status_oct2026: Venus Aerospace flew a 2,000 lbf RDRE to 4,400 ft (May 2025). Juno Propulsion won a NASA TechLeap prize for a NASA-funded flight test later in 2026 (small thruster). NASA's InRoDES is a 10,000 lbf-class pump-fed LOX/LCH4 engine with >340 s chamber firings in 2025; a vacuum test comes next, then transfer to industry.
prop-rde-flight-demo.why: Hardware is limited by testing and funding. Cheaper analysis under S2 (mode theory, thermal design) trims iterations but cannot shorten vacuum testing, flight integration or the wait for a funded flight slot. Autonomous test campaigns under S3 pull the date about a year earlier.
prop-rde-flight-demo.strongest_case_small: A small in-space RDRE firing (Juno) may come in 2026-27 regardless of AI math. The >=1,000 lbf demo depends on a customer and money, not mathematics.
prop-rde-flight-demo.signpost: A Juno Propulsion in-space RDRE firing, NASA InRoDES vacuum-test results, or a lander provider baselining an RDRE.

prop-ntp-ground-test.title: Nuclear thermal engine ground hot fire
prop-ntp-ground-test.description: A fission-heated hydrogen engine (5-12.5 klbf subscale) fired on the ground with full exhaust capture: the first U.S. NTP reactor test since NERVA (1972).
prop-ntp-ground-test.status_oct2026: DRACO was cancelled in the FY2026 budget request (May 2025) because falling launch costs eroded its ROI (DARPA's McHenry, Breaking Defense, Jun 27, 2025). Congress directed >=$110M for NTP in FY2026, and Administrator Isaacman committed to execute it (Sen. Britt, Apr 29, 2026). The White House Space Nuclear Initiative (Apr 14, 2026) prioritizes NEP (SR-1 Freedom, 20 kWe, Mars launch at end-2028) and lunar surface power, with 'common NEP/NTP components'. A high-pressure exhaust capture system for 5-12.5 klbf tests exists as a design (NASA, 2023).
prop-ntp-ground-test.why: As of Oct 2026 there is no funded NTP engine program of record. A reactor ground test needs a program start, a fueled reactor, an exhaust-capture facility and nuclear safety approval, which on historical precedent takes 5+ years from start (general). AI compresses design and safety-analysis documentation (S2/S3) but not facility construction, fuel fabrication or approvals.
prop-ntp-ground-test.strongest_case_small: Policy and money decide this node, and the policy pivot to NEP was driven by cost and launch prices, not mathematics.
prop-ntp-ground-test.signpost: FY2027 or FY2028 budgets fund an NTP ground-test facility and reactor, or DOE and NASA announce an NTP program of record.

prop-hls-refuel-campaign.title: Full lunar-lander refueling campaign
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.description: Roughly 10-20 tanker flights fill a depot in LEO, which transfers a full load to Starship HLS for a lunar landing (uncrewed demo or crewed).
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.status_oct2026: NASA OIG (Mar 2026): more than 10 tankers are needed, the landing is planned for 2028, and NASA tracks a 'top risk' that cryogenic technologies won't be mature. ASAP (Sep 2025) warned HLS could be 'years late'. Estimates run from SpaceX's '10-ish' to NASA's 'high teens'. NASA plans an interim Artemis test flight in LEO in 2027 before landing attempts (Spaceflight Now, Jul 2026).
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.why: Launch cadence binds. At one tanker every ~6 days a campaign takes about 2 months, and every slip in cadence multiplies boil-off losses (tables). Validated boil-off and transfer models (prop-cfm-models) and reliable relights (prop-start-transient) save ~1-4 tankers per mission and some schedule margin: months, not years. S3's broad AI acceleration of hardware iteration is what lifts the band to High.
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.strongest_case_small: AI mathematics is not on the critical path. Vehicle reliability, launch cadence, docking and pad turnaround are.
prop-hls-refuel-campaign.signpost: The first depot-filling campaign with >=5 tankers flown, and NASA confirming a landing date after the 2027 LEO test.

prop-rde-operational.title: Detonation engines in operational service
prop-rde-operational.description: RDREs used as production propulsion on a commercial lander, upper stage or in-space vehicle, with predictable, qualified behavior.
prop-rde-operational.status_oct2026: There is no operational RDRE anywhere; only demonstrations exist (see prop-rde-flight-demo).
prop-rde-operational.why: Operational use requires a qualified engine whose mode behavior is predictable across throttle and mixture ranges, and that predictability is what mode theory buys. Qualifying a new combustion mode for operational use has historically taken several years after the first flight demo (general).
prop-rde-operational.strongest_case_small: Even with perfect theory, a ~10% Isp gain may not justify the qualification cost for most missions. Defense missiles and hypersonics, not space, may be the first operational users.
prop-rde-operational.signpost: A lander or upper-stage provider contracting an RDRE as baseline propulsion.

prop-reuse-extended.title: Model-based engine reuse life
prop-reuse-extended.description: Reusable engines whose overhaul and inspection intervals are set by validated probabilistic life models, extending the flights between overhauls (for example 2x) without added risk.
prop-reuse-extended.status_oct2026: Reuse life today is extended mainly by fleet-leader experience (general). Raptor 3 had accumulated >40,000 s of runtime by Apr 2026 (newspaceeconomy).
prop-reuse-extended.why: Cheaper refurbishment and faster turnaround feed directly into launch cost, and a doubled overhaul interval is plausible once life models are calibrated on fleet data. The accumulation of fleet data, flight by flight, sets the pace.
prop-reuse-extended.strongest_case_small: The gains are internal and hard to observe, and operators may extend life empirically just as fast.
prop-reuse-extended.signpost: Operator statements tying engine overhaul intervals to analytic life models, or NASA reuse certification for crewed flights citing probabilistic life analysis.

prop-ntp-crewed-mars.title: Nuclear thermal stage for crewed Mars
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.description: A flight-qualified NTP stage (~900 s Isp) available for crewed Mars transits, cutting trip time by up to ~25% (per DOE) and reducing crew radiation dose.
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.status_oct2026: There is no funded NTP flight program (DRACO was cancelled in 2025), and NEP was chosen for SR-1 Freedom (2028).
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.why: This requires a ground test, a flight demo and crew-rating, each a multi-year effort, and none has started. Math is not on the critical path.
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.strongest_case_small: The node is on the tree to mark a ceiling: AI math cannot fund a reactor or license a test.
prop-ntp-crewed-mars.signpost: An NTP flight-demo program of record with a launch date.

prop-engine-dev-compression.title: Engine development time and cost cut
prop-engine-dev-compression.description: New liquid engines reach qualification with materially fewer hot-fire tests and redesign loops (for example >=30% fewer than comparable heritage programs), with the saving attributed to predictive tools.
prop-engine-dev-compression.status_oct2026: Development remains test-driven. SpaceX has built 600+ Raptors through large-scale test-fail-fix iteration (newspaceeconomy, Apr 2026).
prop-engine-dev-compression.why: Design and analysis compress (P1), but reliability demonstration is statistical. Showing 0.99 reliability at 90% confidence with zero failures takes ~230 tests (n = ln 0.1 / ln 0.99) unless customers accept model-based Bayesian credit. Models cut redesign loops, not demonstration tests. Engine programs also run 3-7 years, so few programs started with S2 capability will qualify by 2031.
prop-engine-dev-compression.strongest_case_small: The cheapest route to reliability is already high-rate testing of cheap hardware, so prediction competes with a very fast empirical loop.
prop-engine-dev-compression.signpost: A program publicly attributing a reduced hot-fire count to predictive tools, or a customer (NASA, USSF) accepting model-based reliability credit.

prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.title: Routine orbital refueling economy
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.description: Depots and tankers operate routinely, with dozens of cryogenic transfers per year supporting lunar landers, Mars ships and high-energy missions, and boil-off and transfer losses are predicted rather than padded.
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.status_oct2026: Not yet demonstrated. Eta Space targets a commercial LOX depot (Cryo-Dock) by 2030 (satnews, May 2026).
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.why: The economics depend on tankers per delivered tonne. Validated boil-off, transfer and gauging models are worth ~1-4 tankers per HLS-class mission (illustrative tables), or 10-30% of campaign launches. The rest comes down to cadence and vehicle reuse.
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.strongest_case_small: Launch cadence and vehicle cost dominate, so model-driven savings are second-order.
prop-cislunar-propellant-economy.signpost: More than 20 ship-to-ship transfers in a calendar year, or a third-party depot (for example Cryo-Dock) receiving propellant.

science-gr-foundations.title: Black-hole foundations settled and checked
science-gr-foundations.description: Independent experts confirm the 2026 wave of mathematical general relativity: nonlinear stability of Kerr black holes across the full subextremal range (human preprints, Jun and Sep 2026), the AI-claimed strong cosmic censorship near Kerr (family 264) and the AI-claimed spacetime Penrose inequalities (family 260). Together they make 'perturbed black holes settle down to Kerr, and their mass bounds their horizon area' a theorem rather than an assumption.
science-gr-foundations.status_oct2026: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range claimed by Hintz (arXiv 2606.28253, Jun 2026) and Szeftel (arXiv 2609.40068, Sep 2026), human work, not yet refereed. Family 264 (strong cosmic censorship near two-ended Kerr data): T1, manuscript only. Family 260 (spacetime Penrose inequalities): T1 for the main inequalities; only a supporting construction (Cha-Khuri-Sakovich end replacement, Comparator target CKSBondiPenrose) has an agent-written Lean proof, unchecked, and the repo's lean/docs/260.md states the paper's general inequality 'remains unformalized'. Neither family appears in formalization.yaml as a formalized main result.
science-gr-foundations.premise_tier: T1 (families 260 main results and 264); human Kerr-stability preprints unrefereed
science-gr-foundations.why: Ringdown spectroscopy (LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA now, LISA after 2035) and EHT/BHEX photon-ring tests all assume a perturbed black hole relaxes to Kerr. Kerr stability proves it from outside; strong cosmic censorship near Kerr (264) says the interior generically cannot be continued past the Cauchy horizon with square-integrable connection; Penrose inequalities (260) bound mass below by horizon area for moving, charged and rotating data. Review bandwidth is the gate: a few dozen people can referee these, and 722 manuscripts arrived at once (tr-position-5). Formal checking is further off because Lean lacks Lorentzian geometry, so S1 is Medium; S2/S3 add AI-assisted refereeing and formalization.
science-gr-foundations.strongest_case_small: No working astrophysicist doubted the Kerr final state. Waveform models, ringdown tests and EHT analyses already assume it, so nothing in any instrument or mission changes; this removes a theoretical doubt only (tl-position-2).
science-gr-foundations.signpost: A named GR expert publicly endorses or finds a gap in families 260 or 264 by end-2027; Hintz or Szeftel accepted by a journal; first Lean library for Lorentzian causal structure.

science-energy-condition-nogo.title: Warp drives: sharp no-go theorems
science-energy-condition-nogo.description: Theorems stating, for every metric in a broad class, how much negative energy a 'warp' or 'propellantless' spacetime needs, or how much positive mass a positive-energy version must carry. Superluminal bubbles must violate the null energy condition; positive-energy subluminal shells must carry planetary-scale mass; the sharp constants are now being computed.
science-energy-condition-nogo.status_oct2026: Human literature, mostly T5: generic warp drives violate the null energy condition (arXiv 2105.03079, 2021); a subluminal warp satisfies all energy conditions only by adding a matter shell with positive ADM mass (arXiv 2405.02709, 2024); Lentz's positive-energy claim refuted (arXiv 2511.18251, Nov 2025); new no-go theorems and classification (arXiv 2602.16495, Feb 2026); exact minimum Eulerian negative energy for Natario drives, E_min ~ v^2 R^4/(4 Delta^3) (arXiv 2609.36211, Sep 28 2026). The spacetime positive mass theorem (zero ADM mass with dominant energy forces flat spacetime) is established. Family 260 (T1) extends Penrose mass-area bounds to data with arbitrary momentum, a marginal addition.
science-energy-condition-nogo.premise_tier: T5 for the null-energy and positive-mass results; T1 for the family 260 extension (not load-bearing)
science-energy-condition-nogo.why: Ceilings act within months (fc-position-1). The numbers are brutal: (1) by the Natario result, halving the bubble wall thickness multiplies the negative energy needed 8x and doubling the bubble radius multiplies it 16x; for R/Delta = 100 the sharp bound is 2,500x the older v^2R^2/Delta estimate. (2) A positive-energy configuration that contains a trapped surface of enclosing radius 10 m must have ADM mass >= r/2 in geometric units, about 6.7e27 kg or 3.5 Jupiter masses (family 260 for moving data, conditional on T1). (3) Any 'zero-mass' warp metric that is not flat must violate the dominant energy condition (positive mass rigidity). An exponentially improving model can extend these to every published warp class with sharp constants, which is cognitive work only.
science-energy-condition-nogo.strongest_case_small: The answer was already 'no' before AI: the null-energy result dates from 2021 and positive mass from 1979-81. Family 260 applies only to energy-respecting data with trapped surfaces, which typical subluminal warp shells lack, so the catalog adds almost nothing to propulsion. Nothing that could fly is removed.
science-energy-condition-nogo.signpost: An AI-produced general theorem covering all published warp classes (Alcubierre, Natario, Lentz, Bobrick-Martire, Fell-Heisenberg, Fuchs et al.) with interval-certified or formal checks; or a credible counterexample class that survives audit.

science-qei-curved.title: Hard limits on negative energy from quantum fields
science-qei-curved.description: Quantum energy inequalities cap how much negative energy any quantum field can hold and for how long. They are proven for free fields in flat space and some curved backgrounds; general curved spacetimes and interacting fields remain open. Settling them would close the 'quantum loophole' (Casimir-type sources) that warp and wormhole proposals rely on.
science-qei-curved.status_oct2026: (general) Ford-Roman and Fewster quantum inequalities established for free fields; averaged null energy condition proven for flat-space QFT (2016-17); interacting and generic curved cases open. Not in the catalog.
science-qei-curved.why: Exotic-propulsion proposals concede classical matter cannot supply negative energy and point to quantum effects. A general quantum inequality would bound the product of negative-energy magnitude and duration for any physical source, completing the ceiling started by the classical theorems. Under S2 research-grade mathematical physics is routine by 2028-29, so partial-to-general results by 2029 are plausible.
science-qei-curved.strongest_case_small: Interacting four-dimensional quantum field theories are not rigorously constructed, so the fully general theorem may not even be statable; and the classical no-go results already exclude every macroscopic proposal at absurd energy scales.
science-qei-curved.signpost: A proven quantum energy inequality for a nontrivial interacting model or for general globally hyperbolic backgrounds, with AI credited.

science-beyond-gr-wellposed.title: Beyond-Einstein gravity made simulable
science-beyond-gr-wellposed.description: Proving which modified-gravity theories have a well-posed initial-value problem, so black-hole mergers can be simulated and turned into templates, or proving they do not. Without it, gravitational-wave tests of general relativity rely on parametrized, theory-agnostic deviations.
science-beyond-gr-wellposed.status_oct2026: Well-posedness shown for Horndeski and Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet at weak coupling in modified harmonic gauge (Kovacs-Reall 2020, general); puncture-gauge formulation for four-derivative scalar-tensor theories (Phys. Rev. D, Oct 2023); first fully nonlinear Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet scattering simulations (arXiv 2605.04224, May 2026). Dynamical Chern-Simons and strong coupling open, usually handled by order-reduction schemes without proofs. No catalog family.
science-beyond-gr-wellposed.why: A well-posedness proof lets numerical-relativity groups produce merger waveforms in a specific alternative theory, so LISA (2035+) and ground detectors can test that theory directly. A negative result is just as useful (tl-position-2): it marks theories that can only be treated as effective field theories, telling analysts which tests are meaningful. Pure PDE analysis, exactly the S2 2027-28 capability.
science-beyond-gr-wellposed.strongest_case_small: Most strong-field tests already use parametrized deviations, general relativity has passed every test so far, and LISA does not fly until 2035, so the payoff is mostly bounds on theories rather than a discovery.
science-beyond-gr-wellposed.signpost: Proof or disproof of strong hyperbolicity for dynamical Chern-Simons beyond weak coupling; NR codes adopting proven formulations.

science-second-order-self-force.title: LISA's hardest waveforms: second-order self-force around spinning black holes
science-second-order-self-force.description: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (a stellar-mass black hole spiraling ~1e5 orbits into a massive one) can only be decoded if the phase is modeled to better than about a radian over the whole signal. That requires second-order gravitational self-force for generic (eccentric, inclined) orbits around spinning Kerr black holes.
science-second-order-self-force.status_oct2026: Second-order calculations exist only for quasicircular orbits around non-spinning (Schwarzschild) black holes (arXiv 2112.12265; effective-source paper arXiv 2508.00087, 2025); a June 2026 paper states 'these calculations have only been attempted for the simplest case of circular orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime' and demonstrates a numerical-relativity route in Kerr for a scalar charge (arXiv 2606.04998); Lorenz-gauge elliptic methods in progress (arXiv 2608.07934, Aug 2026). Adiabatic-order Kerr waveforms for equatorial orbits exist in the FastEMRIWaveforms framework (Phys. Rev. D, Apr 2025); interpolation errors in such fast models are themselves a bias source (PRD, Mar 2026).
science-second-order-self-force.why: The phase expands as phi = phi_0/epsilon + phi_1 + O(epsilon) with mass ratio epsilon ~1e-5 to 1e-6; adiabatic waveforms carry only phi_0, and the O(1) post-adiabatic term phi_1 needs second-order self-force (general). The formalism exists; what is missing is expert labor: renormalized second-order sources, gauge transformations, mode coupling and eccentric/inclined Kerr orbits, by a field of a few dozen specialists. This is the 'solved in principle, expert-scarce' class where on-demand AI applied math (P1) acts first. Under S2 it lands ~2029, four to six years ahead of a pre-AI path that aimed only to finish before the 2035 launch.
science-second-order-self-force.strongest_case_small: LISA's science date is fixed by its 2035 launch, so finishing early buys risk reduction, not earlier science; and offline-online surrogates still need validation against independent codes.
science-second-order-self-force.signpost: First second-order self-force results for eccentric orbits or a Kerr background by 2028, with AI credited in methods or authorship.
