science-nr-precision.title: Merger simulations precise enough for LISA's loudest signals
science-nr-precision.description: LISA will see massive black-hole mergers at signal-to-noise ratios in the hundreds to thousands, where waveform error dominates the error budget. Simulations need mismatches near 1e-6 (indistinguishability scales as ~1/(2 SNR^2), general) at mass ratios above 10 and spins near 0.9, versus ~1e-4 typical today.
science-nr-precision.status_oct2026: SXS third catalog (CQG, Aug 2025): 3,756 configurations, precessing up to mass ratio 8 and spins <= 0.8. Typical resolution mismatch ~1e-4, but ~1e-1 for the longest (~180-orbit) runs (arXiv 2502.14025). Bias studies show neglected harmonics and eccentricity bias LISA parameters (arXiv 2502.12237, 2602.09088, 2601.07739). GPU code generation for NR emerging (arXiv 2501.14030).
science-nr-precision.why: A 100x accuracy gain at extreme parameters requires better formulations, a-posteriori error estimators, high-order discontinuous-Galerkin codes and GPU ports (cognitive, compresses under S2), then very large supercomputer allocations (capital, does not compress). That is why S3 is no better than Medium: compute time binds even when cognition is free.
science-nr-precision.strongest_case_small: Accuracy can also be bought by hybridizing NR with self-force and effective-one-body models, which the field already does; AI mostly speeds code work, and the 2035 launch sets the deadline.
science-nr-precision.signpost: A public catalog with precessing runs at mass ratio >= 16 and mismatch <= 1e-5; NR codes shipping certified error estimates.

science-lisa-readiness.title: LISA analysis stack passes its accuracy tests
science-lisa-readiness.description: End-to-end validation in LISA mock-data challenges: waveform models (post-adiabatic self-force inspirals, NR-calibrated mergers) plus the 'global fit' that separates tens of thousands of overlapping signals, shown to recover injected parameters without bias at realistic signal strengths. The ground-test analog for a science instrument.
science-lisa-readiness.status_oct2026: LISA adopted by ESA in Jan 2024 (general); construction began Jun 17 2025; launch planned 2035 (ESA). Global-fit and source-separation methods under active development (e.g., arXiv 2606.01236, May 2026).
science-lisa-readiness.why: Readiness requires both waveform families plus validation within the consortium's data-challenge cadence and acceptance process (adoption gate). Under S2 the theory inputs land 2029-30, so readiness is credible by 2030; under S1 the self-force input is not done by 2031.
science-lisa-readiness.strongest_case_small: Being ready in 2030 rather than 2033 changes nothing observable before the 2035 launch; the gain is lower schedule risk for the science ground segment.
science-lisa-readiness.signpost: LISA data-challenge results with post-adiabatic EMRI injections recovered without bias.

science-lisa-precision-science.title: LISA does precision strong-gravity science from day one
science-lisa-precision-science.description: When LISA flies, its first-year data yield unbiased black-hole masses and spins, extreme-mass-ratio tests of the Kerr metric and bounds on beyond-Einstein theories, because the theory work was finished years before launch instead of during operations.
science-lisa-precision-science.why: Shown to make the physical clock visible: AI mathematics can move LISA's theory readiness forward by four to six years under S2, but the science cannot begin before the spacecraft fly in 2035.
science-lisa-precision-science.signpost: ESA LISA milestones (critical design review, launch date) hold or slip; no AI scenario moves them.

science-retrieval-identifiability.title: Exoplanet atmosphere readings with honest error bars
science-retrieval-identifiability.description: Theorems and certified tools stating which molecules, abundances and temperature structures a given spectrum can and cannot determine (identifiability), plus retrieval methods robust to wrong one-dimensional model assumptions. Turns today's 'parallel interpretations' into quantified, comparable claims.
science-retrieval-identifiability.status_oct2026: JWST shows 'established inverse methods ... can lead to disparate interpretations even with JWST's quality of data' (Seager et al., PNAS, Sep 2025). The K2-18 b DMS signal remains disputed (homogeneous MIRI survey, ApJL Sep 2026; 661-molecule agnostic search, ApJL May 2026; Hycean vs mini-Neptune debate, arXiv 2605.17803). No general identifiability theory for retrieval forward models (general).
science-retrieval-identifiability.why: Identifiability maps tell observers which wavelength range, resolution and SNR make a molecule recoverable; robust inference stops 1D-model misspecification from producing false detections. That shortens claim-and-rebuttal cycles from months to weeks and feeds HWO's wavelength and resolution requirements. Pure applied mathematics and statistics; the gate is community adoption.
science-retrieval-identifiability.strongest_case_small: Degeneracies are physics, not math: if the spectrum lacks the information, no theorem creates it. JWST's noise floor, stellar contamination and opacity errors are the real limits.
science-retrieval-identifiability.signpost: A community retrieval comparison (K2-18 b, TRAPPIST-1 planets) reporting AI-derived identifiability maps; journals asking for identifiability statements.

science-opacity-line-lists.title: Molecular fingerprints good enough for biosignature claims
science-opacity-line-lists.description: Accurate line lists, pressure broadening and collision-induced absorption for biosignature and false-positive molecules (DMS, DMDS, CH3Cl, N2O, PH3, O2-O2 and others) over the needed temperatures, computed by AI-driven quantum chemistry and validated in the laboratory.
science-opacity-line-lists.status_oct2026: Opacity data of uneven quality underlie broad molecule searches (661 species tested for K2-18 b, ApJL May 2026); incomplete opacities are a known retrieval systematic (general). Catalog 275 (QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy, T1) and 278 (failure of Kohn-Sham ensemble representability, T1) are worst-case ceilings on general electronic-structure methods, not obstacles for small molecules.
science-opacity-line-lists.premise_tier: n/a (catalog families enter only as ceilings, conditional on T1)
science-opacity-line-lists.why: Ab initio line-list production is labor-heavy and expert-scarce; AI theory compresses it, and autonomous spectroscopy labs (S2/S3) validate faster. Lab validation stays the slowest link, so even S3 is only Medium. The hardness results (275, 278) say no general algorithm exists, which reinforces the need for lab checks rather than blocking progress.
science-opacity-line-lists.strongest_case_small: Line-list production is already a mature pipeline (ExoMol, HITRAN); lab spectroscopy capacity, not theory, limits validation.
science-opacity-line-lists.signpost: Database releases with AI-computed line lists validated against lab spectra for 50+ new species.

science-biosignature-false-positive-theo.title: Knowing when 'signs of life' are not life
science-biosignature-false-positive-theo.description: Predictive photochemistry, geochemistry and 3D climate models that list the non-biological routes to O2, O3, CH4 with CO2, DMS and other biosignatures for a given star and planet, with probabilities attached. This is the theory HWO needs to turn a detection into a claim.
science-biosignature-false-positive-theo.status_oct2026: JWST results push the field to 'parallel interpretations' that may not be resolved until the next generation of observatories (PNAS, Sep 2025); 1D retrievals are 'highly averaged' representations of 3D processes (same).
science-biosignature-false-positive-theo.why: Under S2 AI builds physics theory by 2028-29 and autonomous labs supply rate constants, so a quantified false-positive map is credible by 2030. Mission-design effect: it decides whether HWO needs ultraviolet (O3), near-infrared to ~1.8 microns (CH4, CO2) or both, which drives coronagraph and detector choices.
science-biosignature-false-positive-theo.strongest_case_small: Planetary context (interior, history, surface) is underdetermined by remote data; even perfect theory yields a probability, not a verdict.
science-biosignature-false-positive-theo.signpost: HWO science-requirements documents cite AI-generated false-positive maps; autonomous photochemistry labs publishing rate constants at scale.

science-coronagraph-limits.title: Proven limits for starlight suppression
science-coronagraph-limits.description: Sharp, provable bounds on how much planet light any coronagraph can deliver at a given inner working angle, bandwidth and 1e-10 contrast for HWO's candidate apertures (on-axis segmented versus off-axis), plus designs that approach them. Shows which architectures cannot meet the 25-exo-Earth goal before money is spent.
science-coronagraph-limits.status_oct2026: HWO needs raw contrast ~1e-10 and 1-sigma photometric precision ~3e-12 (arXiv 2510.02547, Oct 2025); vortex and forked-grating designs under study (JATIS, Sep 2026); coronagraph design is already posed as optimization with electric-field conjugation (JATIS 2022); an analytic error budget from optical disturbances to flux-ratio noise appeared Sep 2026 (arXiv 2609.32023). Ideal-coronagraph limits exist only for idealized apertures (general).
science-coronagraph-limits.why: Coronagraph design reduces to optimization over linear optical operators, where convex duality yields provable upper bounds (a ceiling, P3) and the primal solution yields designs (P4, if manufacturable). Architecture down-select for HWO happens over roughly 2027-30, so a ceiling that arrives in 2027-28 can prune options while it still matters.
science-coronagraph-limits.strongest_case_small: Achieved contrast is set by mask fabrication tolerances, polarization aberrations, detector noise and stability, not by the optimality of the design; Roman's coronagraph experience shows hardware dominates.
science-coronagraph-limits.signpost: HWO architecture trade documents citing provable throughput bounds; testbed results at 1e-10 broadband with AI-designed masks.

science-wfsc-certified.title: Picometer-stable telescopes with guaranteed control
science-wfsc-certified.description: Wavefront sensing-and-control loops with proven convergence and robustness bounds against thermal and vibration disturbances, co-designed with the error budget, keeping contrast drift below ~1e-11 over hours-long exposures.
science-wfsc-certified.status_oct2026: HWO EAC1 modeling shows significant thermal and vibrational disturbances (JATIS 12(4) 041012, May 2026); segment-level sensing and control studies (JATIS 041024, Jul 2026). Roman launched Aug 30 2026 and took its first coronagraph observation Sep 30 2026 (NASA), the first space demonstration of active wavefront control for high contrast.
science-wfsc-certified.why: Control and estimation with guarantees is applied math (S2 2027-28); proving it works needs vacuum-testbed campaigns and comparison with Roman's in-flight data, which take years and do not compress much (experiment gate).
science-wfsc-certified.strongest_case_small: Control theory is not the bottleneck: metrology, deformable mirrors, detectors and thermal engineering are, and testbed time is scarce.
science-wfsc-certified.signpost: Roman Coronagraph in-flight contrast vs pre-launch models (2026-27); a vacuum-testbed demonstration of HWO-level stability with AI-derived controllers.

science-hwo-design-closure.title: HWO's design closed by AI-integrated modeling
science-hwo-design-closure.description: End-to-end integrated models (structure, thermal, optics, coronagraph, retrieval, survey yield) run and optimized by AI and used to freeze HWO's aperture, coronagraph type, wavelength range and stability requirements with quantified science yield.
science-hwo-design-closure.status_oct2026: HWO is in pre-formulation using Exploratory Analytic Cases (NASA); exposure-time and yield tools exist (pyEDITH, arXiv 2608.28477; EXOSIMS dynamic scheduling, JATIS May 2026); launch in the 2040s (Astro2020, general). NASA FY2026 budget $24.4B; FY2027 request $18.8B (Planetary Society).
science-hwo-design-closure.why: Under S2, multiphysics design optimization arrives 2028-29 and can close HWO's requirement tree faster with fewer contractor study cycles. Agency decision points follow budgets, so capital binds; a FY2027 request 23% below FY2026 is a direct threat.
science-hwo-design-closure.strongest_case_small: Design closure on paper does not make HWO cheaper to build or launch sooner than the 2040s; agency milestones follow budgets and politics.
science-hwo-design-closure.signpost: HWO architecture down-select date and whether it cites AI-run integrated modeling; FY2027 appropriation for HWO.

science-vlbi-identifiability.title: What space interferometry can prove about black holes
science-vlbi-identifiability.description: Identifiability and stability theorems for sparse-aperture imaging: which Earth-space baselines (lengths, orientations, frequencies) uniquely determine a black hole's photon-ring diameter and shape, and hence its spin and the Kerr hypothesis, despite unknown plasma emission and station gain errors.
science-vlbi-identifiability.status_oct2026: Reconstructing images from sparse, corrupted Fourier samples is 'a challenging inverse problem' (ApJ, Jan 2026); BHEX targets the photon ring with the first submillimeter Earth-space VLBI (SPIE, Aug 2026). No catalog family applies: the catalog's inverse-problem results (365, 372) concern elliptic boundary data, not Fourier sampling.
science-vlbi-identifiability.why: Orbit and baseline choices for a space-VLBI mission are fixed at proposal time; a theorem stating which baseline sets make ring parameters identifiable (and which cannot, a ceiling) can steer a 2026-27 proposal and ngEHT design. Instrument design via inverse-problem theory, acting in 1-2 years.
science-vlbi-identifiability.strongest_case_small: Mission design already uses simulation-based trade studies; theorems mostly confirm what simulations show, and angular resolution is set by baseline length over wavelength regardless.
science-vlbi-identifiability.signpost: BHEX or ngEHT design documents citing proven identifiability conditions for baseline selection.

science-bhex-flight.title: First submillimeter space-VLBI mission flies
science-bhex-flight.description: A BHEX-class satellite links with ground telescopes to measure a black hole's photon ring, producing the sharpest images in astronomy.
science-bhex-flight.status_oct2026: BHEX team plans a 2026 NASA Small Explorer proposal and a 2031 launch (blackholeexplorer.org); 4 K cryocooling and antenna designs under development (Cryogenics 2026; SPIE 2024).
science-bhex-flight.why: Identical across scenarios on purpose: flight needs competitive selection (roughly one-in-several odds, general), a 4-5 year build and a launch slot. AI mathematics improves the proposal, not the selection odds or the build time. Roughly 30% selection times 40% on-time gives about 10-15%, Low.
science-bhex-flight.strongest_case_small: It is already Low; AI changes nothing measurable here.
science-bhex-flight.signpost: NASA Small Explorer selection announcement including or excluding BHEX; NASA astrophysics budget for Explorers.

science-cosmo-certified-inference.title: Cosmology inference that knows its own errors
science-cosmo-certified-inference.description: Simulation-based inference, emulators and covariance estimates with proven calibration and error bounds, so Stage-IV surveys (DESI, Euclid, Rubin, Roman) can separate new physics from analysis artefacts with far fewer expensive simulations.
science-cosmo-certified-inference.status_oct2026: Field-level weak-lensing inference with only 60 N-body simulations (Jun 2026); benchmarks of exact, emulated and simulation-based inference (ApJ, Jun 2026); 3x2pt simulation-based pipelines (arXiv 2609.24946, Sep 2026). Catalog 374 (sharp 1/3 stability of optimal-transport maps, T1) bears on error propagation in optimal-transport reconstruction of cosmic initial conditions; catalog 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, T3) assumes well-conditioned log-concave targets that real posteriors are not. Both theory-only.
science-cosmo-certified-inference.premise_tier: n/a (catalog links conditional, T1/T3, not load-bearing)
science-cosmo-certified-inference.why: Coverage guarantees and certified emulator errors let collaborations trust neural inference and cut simulation budgets; the gate is collaborations' slow, blinded validation procedures (adoption).
science-cosmo-certified-inference.strongest_case_small: The dominant survey systematics are astrophysical (baryonic feedback, photometric redshifts, intrinsic alignments, shear calibration), not inference mathematics; and collaborations validate pipelines slowly by design.
science-cosmo-certified-inference.signpost: Euclid or Rubin key-project analyses adopting simulation-based inference with formal coverage guarantees.

science-dark-energy-verdict.title: Is dark energy changing? A decisive answer
science-dark-energy-verdict.description: Confirmation or refutation, at about 5 sigma, of DESI's hint that dark energy evolves, by combining DESI final data with Euclid, Rubin, Roman and CMB data.
science-dark-energy-verdict.status_oct2026: DESI DR2 BAO (PRD, 2025) is consistent with DR1; preference for dynamical dark energy does not diminish from DR1 to DR2 (Nature Astronomy, Sep 2025), though some non-parametric reconstructions find reduced support (MNRAS, Dec 2025). Roman launched Aug 30 2026.
science-dark-energy-verdict.why: Photon-limited: the answer arrives with survey data releases. AI shortens the analysis lag by perhaps a year and lowers the chance a systematic is mistaken for physics; it does not change the answer or bring the data forward.
science-dark-energy-verdict.strongest_case_small: This is the clearest case where AI mathematics barely matters: same band in all scenarios.
science-dark-energy-verdict.signpost: Combined DESI final and Euclid DR1 analyses (2027-28).

science-helio-tomography.title: 3D Sun-to-Earth reconstructions with guarantees
science-helio-tomography.description: Uniqueness and stability theory, plus certified algorithms, for reconstructing the 3D corona and solar wind (density and magnetic structure) from a few viewpoints and polarized light, a problem now solved with ad hoc regularization.
science-helio-tomography.status_oct2026: PUNCH (NASA Small Explorer, launched 2025) uses polarization to place structures in 3D (Solar Physics, 2026); discrete polarimetric tomography of CMEs tested on synthetic multi-spacecraft images (Mar 2026); coronal magnetic-field extrapolation from surface data remains ill-posed (general).
science-helio-tomography.why: Limited-angle tomography has a mature mathematical theory to extend; AI applies it to polarized Thomson scattering and multi-viewpoint geometry, telling forecasters which features are determined by the data and which are prior. Feeds the plasma team's space-weather data-assimilation chain.
science-helio-tomography.strongest_case_small: With one to three viewpoints the problem is genuinely underdetermined; theory can only say what more data would be needed.
science-helio-tomography.signpost: Space-weather centers adopting tomographic CME products with stated uncertainty.

science-helio-constellation-design.title: Observing constellations designed by inverse-problem theory
science-helio-constellation-design.description: Choosing how many spacecraft, where (L1, L4/L5, polar, inner heliosphere) and what they measure, by proving which configurations make the 3D reconstruction unique and stable, instead of choosing by heritage and intuition.
science-helio-constellation-design.status_oct2026: Current missions (ESA Vigil at L5, ~2031, general) were designed with conventional trades; no mission concept yet justified by reconstruction-uniqueness analysis (general).
science-helio-constellation-design.why: Instrument and constellation design via inverse-problem theory: once uniqueness conditions are known, design optimization can trade spacecraft count against reconstruction error. Adoption happens in concept studies; flight is after 2031.
science-helio-constellation-design.strongest_case_small: Launch slots, rideshare availability and budgets decide constellations; Vigil is already designed.
science-helio-constellation-design.signpost: A heliophysics mission concept study (multi-point L4/L5/polar) citing reconstruction-uniqueness analysis.

science-coronal-heating-theory.title: Why the corona is hot: settled
science-coronal-heating-theory.description: A predictive, data-validated theory of coronal heating and solar-wind acceleration (waves and turbulence versus small-scale reconnection and switchbacks), built by AI from Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter and PUNCH data.
science-coronal-heating-theory.status_oct2026: Open for about 80 years (general); Parker Solar Probe has made perihelia near 9.9 solar radii since Dec 2024 (general); large data volumes are under-analyzed (general).
science-coronal-heating-theory.why: One of the few open physics problems where the data largely exist and theory-building is the bottleneck, so S2/S3 physics-theory capability could matter. If settled, it decides what the next heliophysics missions measure (high-cadence spectroscopy versus in-situ kinetic plasma).
science-coronal-heating-theory.strongest_case_small: Several mechanisms probably operate; 'settled' may mean an energy budget, not one answer; consensus forms slowly and decisive tests may need new in-situ data.
science-coronal-heating-theory.signpost: An AI-built heating model makes a quantitative prediction confirmed at a later Parker Solar Probe or Solar Orbiter encounter.

science-quantum-sensor-design.title: Quantum sensors designed against full error budgets
science-quantum-sensor-design.description: AI-derived systematic-error models (relativistic time transfer, magnetic and gravity-gradient effects, wavefront aberrations) and provably robust quantum-control sequences for space clocks and atom interferometers.
science-quantum-sensor-design.status_oct2026: ESA's ACES clock ensemble on the ISS since 2025 (ACES payload paper, 2025; relativistic geodesy study using ACES links, arXiv 2609.21786, Sep 2026); differential atom-interferometer magnetometry in NASA's Cold Atom Lab (Nature Communications, Jul 2026); a quantum gravity gradiometer pathfinder is funded (EPJ Quantum Technology, Mar 2025).
science-quantum-sensor-design.why: Error budgets and robust control are bespoke applied math done by small teams; on-demand AI makes them cheap and complete (P1). Validation needs ground and ISS experiments.
science-quantum-sensor-design.strongest_case_small: Performance is limited by lasers, vacuum, vibration and atom-source hardware in orbit; error budgets are already well understood by the expert teams.
science-quantum-sensor-design.signpost: A flight-instrument design review citing AI-derived systematic-error models; ACES or Cold Atom Lab results matching AI-predicted systematics.

science-quantum-sensor-flight.title: AI-co-designed quantum sensor flies
science-quantum-sensor-flight.description: A space atom-interferometer gravity gradiometer or next-generation clock whose design and control were materially derived with AI demonstrates its predicted sensitivity in orbit.
science-quantum-sensor-flight.status_oct2026: Pathfinder funded; no AI-co-designed quantum sensor known to be in flight development (general).
science-quantum-sensor-flight.why: Flight hardware cycles run 4-7 years; a design frozen in 2027-28 flies 2031 at best. Qualification and launch bind in every scenario.
science-quantum-sensor-flight.strongest_case_small: Even S3's faster cognition does not shorten vacuum, vibration and radiation qualification.
science-quantum-sensor-flight.signpost: Quantum gravity gradiometer pathfinder launch date and design methods.

science-archival-discovery-engine.title: AI mines the space-science archive at scale
science-archival-discovery-engine.description: AI systems that pose and answer research questions against archival mission data (JWST, Hubble, Gaia, TESS, Fermi, Parker Solar Probe, SDO), building models, running analyses and drafting results, with humans choosing problems and auditing.
science-archival-discovery-engine.status_oct2026: GPT-5 case studies documented new research steps in physics and astronomy (arXiv 2511.16072, Nov 2025); physicists call for AI verification frameworks before discovery claims (VERaiPHY review, arXiv 2607.10039, Jul 2026).
science-archival-discovery-engine.why: The capability channel (tl-position-4) with no physical gate: the data are already paid for and public. Most analysis-limited questions in archives are easier than the catalog's problems.
science-archival-discovery-engine.strongest_case_small: Human verification and refereeing bandwidth (tr-position-5) caps how many results become knowledge, and archival low-hanging fruit is finite.
science-archival-discovery-engine.signpost: First AI-led discovery in a mission archive confirmed by a follow-up observation; archive-use statistics.

science-claims-audit.title: Extraordinary claims audited in weeks
science-claims-audit.description: Independent AI re-analyses and certified checks of extraordinary claims (biosignatures, dark-energy anomalies, new-physics hints, exotic-propulsion metrics) published within weeks, with interval-certified or Lean-checked components where possible.
science-claims-audit.status_oct2026: Observer-robust energy-condition tests for warp metrics with interval-arithmetic certificates exist (Warpax, arXiv 2602.18023, Feb 2026); the Lentz positive-energy warp claim (2020) was refuted only in Nov 2025 (arXiv 2511.18251); K2-18 b claims were contested over many months (general).
science-claims-audit.why: Ceilings and counterexamples act fastest (tl-position-3); a five-year refutation lag shrinks to weeks once outside teams can pose the question. Formal (Lean) checking of GR claims waits on Lorentzian geometry in Mathlib (infra-mathlib-applied).
science-claims-audit.strongest_case_small: Contested claims are usually limited by data quality, not analysis speed; faster audits do not settle data-starved questions.
science-claims-audit.signpost: A journal or agency formally requiring AI-run independent re-analysis for extraordinary claims.

science-lightsail-stability.title: Lightsails proven to ride the beam
science-lightsail-stability.description: Sail shapes and metasurface designs with proven passive stability under laser propulsion (no tumbling or sliding off the beam) plus thermal and structural margins: the math-and-design half of beamed interstellar-precursor propulsion, the physics-allowed alternative to warp concepts.
science-lightsail-stability.status_oct2026: Beam-riding stability shown in models and early laboratory force measurements (general); no path yet to the ~100 GW-class phased laser arrays a fast interstellar probe needs (general).
science-lightsail-stability.why: Contrast case: here AI mathematics enables (stability proofs, optimized designs) rather than only bounding. The design is cognitive and lands early; everything after it is capital and hardware.
science-lightsail-stability.strongest_case_small: The binding constraints are the laser array (capital, power, phasing) and sail materials, not stability theory.
science-lightsail-stability.signpost: Laboratory demonstration of self-stabilizing laser propulsion of a sail-like membrane.

science-lightsail-demo.title: Laser-propelled sail demonstrated
science-lightsail-demo.description: Ground or orbital demonstration of stable laser-driven propulsion of a gram-scale or smaller sail.
science-lightsail-demo.why: Funding and laser hardware bind; only S3's broader economic effects make an early demonstration plausible.
science-lightsail-demo.strongest_case_small: No sponsor, no demo, whatever the mathematics.
science-lightsail-demo.signpost: A funded program for a high-power laser propulsion demonstration.

science-propulsion-funding-redirect.title: No-go theorems redirect breakthrough-propulsion money
science-propulsion-funding-redirect.description: Sharp, audited no-go results move the small pool of breakthrough-propulsion funding and attention away from warp and reactionless concepts toward physics-allowed frontiers (fusion, beamed sails).
science-propulsion-funding-redirect.status_oct2026: NASA's Breakthrough Propulsion Physics Project (1996-2002) reported six of 14 tasks reaching null conclusions (NTRS 20060000022) and about a third of 16 tasks not viable (NTRS 20040070788); warp research continues to be published (e.g., atmospheric-signature study of zero-ADM-mass warp bubbles, arXiv 2608.10800, Aug 2026).
science-propulsion-funding-redirect.premise_tier: T5 for the core no-go theorems
science-propulsion-funding-redirect.why: Ceilings change what people stop doing (fc-position-1 exception). Program managers and investors can cite an audited theorem instead of a debate. Medium in every scenario because the gate is human belief, not mathematics.
science-propulsion-funding-redirect.strongest_case_small: The dollars at stake are tiny (single-digit millions per year, general) and the most committed proponents rarely respond to theorems; the ceilings were mostly known by 2021.
science-propulsion-funding-redirect.signpost: Funding calls (NIAC, private institutes) explicitly excluding concepts that require energy-condition violation.

science-return-per-dollar.title: More science per mission dollar
science-return-per-dollar.description: With analysis, theory and modeling nearly free, the science extracted from each flown observatory rises sharply; photons, downlink and mission count become the bottleneck of space science.
science-return-per-dollar.status_oct2026: Archives of JWST, Hubble, Gaia, TESS and heliophysics missions are public and under-analyzed (general); budget pressure is rising (NASA FY2027 request $18.8B vs $24.4B FY2026).
science-return-per-dollar.why: The main 2031 outcome in this domain. The cognitive clock compresses analysis of data already paid for; nothing physical gates it until the archives are exhausted, after which new photons bind.
science-return-per-dollar.strongest_case_small: Paper counts are not discoveries; referee bandwidth limits absorption; budget cuts may remove missions faster than AI raises yield per mission.
science-return-per-dollar.signpost: Discoveries from archival data per year; agency reports on archive science yield.

science-portfolio-shift.title: Space science shifts money from analysis to photons
science-portfolio-shift.description: Agencies and decadal surveys rebalance toward more data-collecting missions (small satellites, rideshares, probes) and laboratory data, because AI makes analysis and theory cheap.
science-portfolio-shift.status_oct2026: Priorities set by decadal surveys (Astro2020; the next astrophysics survey is expected around 2030-31, general).
science-portfolio-shift.why: If cognition is near-free, the marginal dollar buys more science as data than as analysis. Agencies act through budget cycles and decadal surveys, so the effect appears at the next survey at the earliest.
science-portfolio-shift.strongest_case_small: Budgets are set by politics, and flagship commitments (HWO, the LISA contribution) lock in spending for a decade.
science-portfolio-shift.signpost: Terms of reference for the next astrophysics decadal survey addressing AI analysis capacity.

struct-test-data-commons.title: AI-ready structural and thermal test data
struct-test-data-commons.description: Machine-readable databases of the physical evidence this domain runs on: shell-buckling tests with measured imperfections, fatigue and crack-growth spectra, thermal-vacuum correlation sets, microgravity two-phase flow data and deployment telemetry, opened to AI models inside agencies and large firms.
struct-test-data-commons.status_oct2026: Fragmented. NASA Shell Buckling Knockdown Factor (SBKF) test reports sit in NTRS as PDFs; Wagner and Huehne released Monte Carlo knockdown databases and code on Zenodo (Jul 2026); ISS flow boiling and condensation datasets were published 2024-2025; most company data are proprietary or export-controlled (general).
struct-test-data-commons.why: Analyst position (g): this domain is limited by modeling fidelity, data and verification cost, not conjectures. Every physics node below (damage, two-phase flow, deployment, mid-frequency vibration) is data-gated: an AI that can build theory still needs validated tests with known uncertainties. Organizing existing evidence is cheap compared with new tests (a single 8-ft shell test or thermal-vacuum campaign takes months); under S2 the incentive to make data AI-readable is strong, so large organizations do it internally by 2028.
struct-test-data-commons.strongest_case_small: Export control, proprietary interest and poor metadata in legacy tests (unmeasured imperfections, uncertain boundary conditions) mean much historical data cannot validate anything; new tests are still needed.
struct-test-data-commons.signpost: NASA or ESA releases a structured, AI-queryable buckling, fatigue or thermal test database, or a major launch company says it validates models on its full flight-test archive, by 2028.

struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.title: Firmer math under elasticity, crack and inspection models
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.description: Independent confirmation of the release's elasticity and fracture results: smooth isotropic Lame moduli are uniquely determined by boundary measurements (372); metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch, with conductivity nonuniqueness (365); regularity of planar Mumford-Shah crack sets (366); the 3D Ball-Evans approximation problem (368).
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.status_oct2026: 372, 366 and 368 are T1 (manuscript only). 365 is T3 (agent-written Lean proof in the repo, unchecked by outsiders). No outside Comparator report as of 2026-10-07. PDE formalization is weak in the release (3 of 16 PDE families).
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.why: These four families are the release's only direct contact with structural mechanics. 372 tells inspection engineers that full boundary data determine elastic stiffness in principle; it says nothing about how stably, and Calderon-type problems are typically only logarithmically stable (general), so it raises confidence without changing tools. 366 underpins the Griffith/Francfort-Marigo variational fracture energies behind phase-field fracture codes: minimizing crack sets are well-behaved in 2D. 368 is a technical tool for nonlinear-elasticity existence and approximation theory (invertible deformations), relevant to large-deformation finite elements. The conductivity-nonuniqueness half of 365 is a negative result: some conductivities cannot be recovered from one boundary patch, a potential ceiling for electrical-resistance damage sensing in carbon-fiber structures (conditional on the T3 premise and on the counterexample class being physically relevant). Under S2, AI-assisted formalization of PDE catches up (2028), so confirmation by 2031 is likely.
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.strongest_case_small: Engineers already run elastography, guided-wave inversion and phase-field fracture codes without these theorems; uniqueness in principle is not stability; the counterexamples may live in coefficient classes (rough, anisotropic, non-generic) that real laminates never present.
struct-elasticity-fracture-foundations.signpost: An independent Comparator run on 365, or inverse-problems specialists endorsing 372 in a refereed venue, by end-2027; any SHM paper using 365's nonuniqueness construction to bound resistance-based damage sensing.

struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.title: Hot spots conjecture (planar case) confirmed
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.description: Family 369 claims that on any simply connected planar domain, the slowest-decaying non-constant temperature mode of an insulated (Neumann) plate takes its maximum and minimum on the boundary, settling Rauch's 1974 conjecture for that class.
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.status_oct2026: T1 (manuscript only). Human literature in 2025-2026 proves only special classes (lip-type and symmetric domains in higher dimensions, TAMS-B Apr 2026; convex hyperbolic domains with small eigenvalues; trapezoids and kites). A certified-numerics project (cert-machine, Zenodo, Oct 5 2026, not refereed) certified a non-symmetric convex trapezoid case.
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.why: A dead-end leaf for engineering, included to show the mapping honestly. Real radiators and panels are 3D, multi-material, with radiative (not insulated) boundaries, and thermal engineers compute their modes numerically for every geometry. The theorem confirms an intuition (slowest insulated thermal mode peaks at edges) and could inform sensor-placement heuristics for thin insulated plates; it changes no design. Effect on space thermal engineering: nil to negligible.
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.strongest_case_small: This node is itself the strongest case: radiative boundary conditions, 3D geometry and numerical design make the planar Neumann theorem irrelevant to hardware.
struct-hot-spots-thermal-modes.signpost: Expert acceptance (refereed version or endorsement by spectral-geometry specialists) by 2027. No engineering signpost is expected.

struct-worst-imperfection-theory.title: Worst-case imperfection theory for thin shells
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.description: Rigorous answers to the open question of which manufacturing imperfections (shape, amplitude, number, location) most reduce the buckling load of thin cylinders and cones, with provable lower bounds on the knockdown factor given a factory's measured imperfection statistics.
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.status_oct2026: Genuinely open. Ubamanyu, Blond, Hutchinson and Reis (arXiv, Jul 2026) show the localized dimple, nearly worst-case for spheres, is not worst-case for cylinders, and find a statistical size effect; Wagner et al. (Proc. R. Soc. A, 2025) propose a regime-aware mechanistic design curve; the 1960s SP-8007 lower bounds remain the reference.
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.why: This is a nonconvex variational and stochastic problem in nonlinear shell theory (Koiter asymptotics, energy barriers, extreme-value statistics of defect populations): bespoke research-grade applied math of the kind S2 makes routine by 2028. A provable lower bound tied to measured imperfection spectra is what lets designers replace empirical lower-bound curves with tighter, defensible knockdowns (see struct-shell-knockdown-rules).
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.strongest_case_small: Humans are converging anyway (mechanistic design curve, probabilistic knockdowns, SBKF); boundary conditions and load imperfections, not geometric theory, drive much of the test scatter; any bound is only as good as one factory's imperfection data.
struct-worst-imperfection-theory.signpost: A paper (AI-assisted or not) proving worst-case imperfection families, or computing certified lower bounds, for axially compressed cylinders by 2028.

struct-certified-uq-margins.title: Structural margins with certified uncertainty bounds
struct-certified-uq-margins.description: Reliability-based structural margins with rigorous rare-event probability estimates and quantified model-form error, as a defensible alternative to stacked deterministic factors (ultimate factors of ~1.25-1.4, model-uncertainty factors, test factors).
struct-certified-uq-margins.status_oct2026: Practice is deterministic factors of safety (NASA-STD-5001 family, general) plus model-credibility assessment (NASA-STD-7009); probabilistic design used selectively. The release contains nothing on uncertainty quantification. 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, Lean, T3) is theory for the posterior sampling such methods use.
struct-certified-uq-margins.premise_tier: n/a (139 is T3 but peripheral; constants unknown, so P4 effect marginal)
struct-certified-uq-margins.why: Reliability methods, multifidelity Monte Carlo and Bayesian calibration are largely solved in principle but expensive and expert-scarce per program; model-form error and high-dimensional rare events remain open. On-demand AI applied math makes doing this properly on every program affordable. Replacing a stacked factor of ~1.4 with a reliability-equivalent margin is typically worth several percent to ~10% of primary-structure mass (general).
struct-certified-uq-margins.strongest_case_small: Factors of safety cover unknown unknowns (workmanship, unmodeled load paths) that no UQ captures; crewed-system safety organizations will keep deterministic factors; the method is not the bottleneck, test data are.
struct-certified-uq-margins.signpost: NASA or ESA publishes a probabilistic structural design standard or handbook revision allowing reduced factors with quantified reliability, or a launch provider reports using certified UQ margins, by 2029.

struct-midfreq-vibroacoustics.title: Closing the mid-frequency vibration gap
struct-midfreq-vibroacoustics.description: Error-controlled prediction of launch vibroacoustic response in the mid-frequency band (roughly a few hundred Hz to ~1-2 kHz), where finite-element models are too costly and statistical energy analysis is invalid, via hybrid FE-SEA and reduced-order models with a posteriori error bounds.
struct-midfreq-vibroacoustics.status_oct2026: A long-standing open problem (general); practice envelopes predictions with margins and relies on acoustic and random-vibration tests. NASA NESC's Norton-Thevenin Receptance Coupling (2023-2024) cuts the cost of coupled loads analysis but does not address mid-frequency fidelity.
struct-midfreq-vibroacoustics.why: Mid-frequency is hard because modal and statistical descriptions both break down. AI can design and prove error estimators for hybrid methods quickly under S2, but validation needs reverberant-chamber and flight data with quantified uncertainty. If solved, component random-vibration levels could be set from prediction with smaller margins, feeding struct-launch-env-margins.
struct-midfreq-vibroacoustics.strongest_case_small: Qualification by test remains mandatory; uncertainty in the forcing (liftoff acoustics, transonic buffet) dominates structural model error, so even perfect structural models leave most of the margin in place.
struct-midfreq-vibroacoustics.signpost: A hybrid FE-SEA method with proven error bounds, validated against chamber data, ships in a commercial vibroacoustics code by 2029.

struct-shm-inverse-limits.title: Damage detection with proven detection limits
struct-shm-inverse-limits.description: Problem-specific stability estimates, optimal sensor placement and model-assisted probability of detection (MAPoD) for guided-wave, strain and electrical-resistance damage sensing, telling engineers what damage size a given sensor layout can and cannot see.
struct-shm-inverse-limits.status_oct2026: MAPoD for guided-wave SHM on composite cryogenic tanks for reusable launchers is active research (ONERA, Jul 2026); SHM is not yet qualified as an inspection replacement on launch vehicles (general). The release supplies uniqueness (372, T1) and nonuniqueness (365, T3) theory and crack regularity (366, T1), not stability constants.
struct-shm-inverse-limits.premise_tier: T3 for the ceiling (365); T1 for 372 and 366 (those contributions conditional)
struct-shm-inverse-limits.why: The question that earns inspection credit is not whether damage is identifiable in principle (372: yes, for smooth isotropic moduli with full boundary data) but how small a delamination N sensors detect at 90/95 confidence. That is quantitative stability plus statistics: solved in principle, expert-scarce, ideal for on-demand AI. Negative results act fastest (P3): 365's conductivity nonuniqueness and typical logarithmic stability mark where resistance-based sensing skins cannot localize damage, steering programs to guided waves or denser arrays. The node's main pathway is capability; the catalog adds confidence and one ceiling.
struct-shm-inverse-limits.strongest_case_small: Real SHM is limited by sensor aging, bonding and temperature/cryogenic compensation, not inverse-problem theory; regulators and operators accept POD from physical specimen tests, not proofs.
struct-shm-inverse-limits.signpost: A launch operator or NASA program reports SHM-based POD curves accepted in place of a scheduled NDE inspection; SHM papers citing 365 or 372 by 2028.

struct-verified-fe-solvers.title: Finite-element solvers with machine-checked error bounds
struct-verified-fe-solvers.description: Structural and thermal finite-element solvers (linear statics, modal, steady conduction-radiation) whose discretization and floating-point errors carry proved bounds (guaranteed a posteriori estimators plus verified arithmetic), so an analysis result ships with a certificate.
struct-verified-fe-solvers.status_oct2026: Guaranteed error estimators exist for model problems (general); verified floating-point toolchains are emerging at flight-software scale (verification domain); nothing at production FE scale; Mathlib coverage of PDE and numerics is thin.
struct-verified-fe-solvers.why: Certification by analysis rests today on solver verification by benchmark plus test correlation. Proof-carrying error bounds remove the code- and solution-verification layer of NASA-STD-7009-style credibility, freeing scarce reviewers for model-form questions. Analyst position (b): formal verification is the bridge to safety-critical use, here applied to numerics rather than flight code.
struct-verified-fe-solvers.strongest_case_small: Discretization error is rarely the dominant uncertainty in structures (joints, boundary conditions, damping and loads are); a certificate on the wrong model is worthless (the specification problem).
struct-verified-fe-solvers.signpost: An open or commercial FE code ships certified error bounds for linear statics or modal analysis with a formal proof artifact by 2029.

struct-damage-tolerance-physics.title: Predictive damage and fatigue models for reusable structures
struct-damage-tolerance-physics.description: Validated physics-based models of crack growth and composite damage progression under the low-cycle, high-amplitude, cryogenic and thermal-cycling spectra of reusable stages and tanks, replacing conservative empirical scatter factors and knockdowns.
struct-damage-tolerance-physics.status_oct2026: No consensus predictive theory for composite failure (general); NASA NESC documented limits of linear elastic fracture mechanics for small cracks in COPV liners (2020); reusable vehicles rely on inspection, fleet-leader experience and conservative life factors (general).
struct-damage-tolerance-physics.why: Damage physics is multiscale and data-hungry. AI theory-building (S2, 2029) can propose closures quickly, but each must survive coupon-to-subcomponent test campaigns (months per load spectrum; cryogenic fatigue rigs are scarce). Autonomous labs (S3) compress coupon testing by about a year, not subcomponent and full-scale tests.
struct-damage-tolerance-physics.strongest_case_small: Operators already reach reuse by test-fix-fly and inspection, so better theory changes margins not feasibility; composite damage modeling has absorbed decades of expert effort without converging because material variability, not cognition, is the limit. Overlaps the materials domain.
struct-damage-tolerance-physics.signpost: A damage model predicts a blind fatigue or residual-strength test series within stated bounds (a successor to the blind-prediction exercise format) by 2029.

struct-two-phase-microgravity-models.title: Predictive two-phase cooling physics in microgravity
struct-two-phase-microgravity-models.description: Validated mechanistic models of flow boiling, condensation, critical heat flux and flow-regime transitions in microgravity pumped loops and heat pipes, at the heat fluxes 100-250 kW compute satellites need.
struct-two-phase-microgravity-models.status_oct2026: Correlation-based. ISS flow boiling and condensation results published 2024-2025 (Int. J. Heat Mass Transfer); microgravity onset-of-boiling studies 2026. Two-phase pumped loops and oscillating heat pipes have flown, but not at AI1's heat flux, quantity or cost (33FG, Jun 2026).
struct-two-phase-microgravity-models.why: Two-phase transport cuts heat-transport mass (33FG model: ~2.0 kg/kW for Starlink-like transport to ~0.8 kg/kW loop-based) and lets radiators run nearer chip temperature, which matters through T^4. Designers carry margins for microgravity uncertainty. Flight data bind: an ISS campaign yields hundreds of test points, while compute-satellite fleets will stream telemetry from ~2027-28, which S2 AI can turn into models; whoever owns the fleet owns the model.
struct-two-phase-microgravity-models.strongest_case_small: Engineers design around uncertainty with margin and favorable-orientation ground tests; the margin penalty may be only ~10-20% of heat-transport mass; SpaceX will iterate hardware faster than theory matures.
struct-two-phase-microgravity-models.signpost: Operator telemetry from AI1 or Starcloud-class two-phase loops published or used in an open model; a microgravity critical-heat-flux model validated within about 15% by 2029.

struct-deployment-mechanics.title: Predictive simulation of large deployable structures
struct-deployment-mechanics.description: Validated models of deployment for 50 m to km structures: frictional contact and latching, stored-strain composite booms, tape-spring snap-through, membrane wrinkling and thermally induced vibration, where today's simulations lean on ground tests that gravity corrupts at scale.
struct-deployment-mechanics.status_oct2026: ACS3 (launched Apr 2024) deployed an ~80 m2 sail on 7 m composite booms; NASA says current booms support sails up to 500 m2 and follow-on booms up to 2,000 m2. Hinge misalignment in over-constrained deployable panels for space solar power is still being quantified (JSME, 2026). Rigid-body Coulomb friction has known existence and uniqueness pathologies (Painleve paradox, general).
struct-deployment-mechanics.why: At 100 m and beyond, gravity-offload rigs stop being representative, so qualification must be by analysis plus subscale and flight data, which requires models with understood error. AI supplies the math (nonsmooth dynamics, similitude scaling laws, tension-field wrinkling theory) quickly under S2, but validation needs flight deployments, of which there are few per year.
struct-deployment-mechanics.strongest_case_small: Most deployment failures are workmanship and mechanism problems (snags, stiction, harness routing) that no model predicts; programs mitigate with simplicity and redundancy, not prediction.
struct-deployment-mechanics.signpost: A 500 m2-plus deployable flies with pre-flight predicted deployment shape and loads matched within stated bounds; NASA flies its follow-on boom technology.

struct-agentic-analysis-workflows.title: AI agents run and check structural and thermal analysis
struct-agentic-analysis-workflows.description: AI agents set up, run, check and document finite-element stress, loads, buckling and thermal analyses end to end (meshing, boundary conditions, margins of safety, thermal-model correlation to thermal-vacuum data, coupled-loads cycles), with an engineer signing off.
struct-agentic-analysis-workflows.status_oct2026: Research prototypes in 2026: LLM agents driving commercial FE codes through MCP (arXiv Sep 2026), multi-agent end-to-end FEA for solid mechanics (arXiv May 2026), PDE-Agents (arXiv Jun 2026). No public flight-program use (general).
struct-agentic-analysis-workflows.why: Analyst position (a): most engineering math is bespoke and easier than the catalog. The bulk of structures and thermal effort is setup, checking and correlation by scarce senior analysts: solved in principle, expert-scarce. Under S2 an analysis cycle costs several times less; a thermal-model correlation that takes weeks after a test could take days (assumption).
struct-agentic-analysis-workflows.strongest_case_small: Analysis labor is a minority of program cost; export-control and data-access rules slow adoption at primes; accountability keeps human sign-off time roughly constant.
struct-agentic-analysis-workflows.signpost: A NASA center, prime or new-space firm says AI agents produce flight-program stress or thermal analysis reports with human sign-off, by 2027-28.

struct-shell-knockdown-rules.title: Lighter buckling design rules for tanks and interstages
struct-shell-knockdown-rules.description: Analysis-based, mechanistic or probabilistic knockdown factors replace the 1960s lower-bound curves for cylinders and cones (and the universal 0.65 for composites) in agency and industry design practice.
struct-shell-knockdown-rules.status_oct2026: NASA SBKF developed and test-validated analysis-based knockdown approaches on 8-ft metallic and composite cylinders (2010s-2022); a NASA review warns the universal 0.65 composite factor can be unconservative; Wagner et al. (2025) report weight savings above 14% and up to 31% in optimized configurations with a mechanistic design curve. Standards adoption is incomplete.
struct-shell-knockdown-rules.why: For an unstiffened isotropic cylinder in axial compression the classical buckling load scales with wall thickness squared, so required thickness scales as KDF^-1/2: moving the knockdown from 0.65 to 0.80 cuts buckling-critical wall mass ~10%, to 0.90 ~15%; stiffened, sandwich and optimized shells see 14-31% (Wagner et al.). The math arrives in 2028 under S2; standards revision (SP-8007, ECSS buckling handbook) and validation tests on representative shells bind, so the band is capped at Medium.
struct-shell-knockdown-rules.strongest_case_small: Buckling-critical structures (interstages, intertanks, unpressurized barrels, adapters) are a minority of dry mass; new-space firms test to failure and do not follow SP-8007 strictly; a kilogram saved on a booster buys only ~0.1-0.2 kg of payload (general).
struct-shell-knockdown-rules.signpost: A NASA SP-8007 or ECSS buckling-handbook revision adopting regime-aware or probabilistic knockdowns, or a launch-vehicle program citing them, by 2029.

struct-launch-env-margins.title: Tighter launch vibration and acoustic environments
struct-launch-env-margins.description: Component and spacecraft random-vibration, acoustic and shock test levels derived from error-bounded predictions calibrated on flight data, instead of enveloped data plus fixed margins, reducing overdesign and test failures.
struct-launch-env-margins.status_oct2026: Environments are enveloped flight data plus fixed qualification margins (for example qualification at acceptance +3 dB, general); NESC's NTRC methods cut coupled-loads cost (2023-2024); each coupled-loads cycle with a launch provider takes weeks (general).
struct-launch-env-margins.why: Random vibration sizes brackets, secondary structure and electronics boxes; a 3 dB margin doubles the test PSD (about 1.4x g-rms). With high-cadence vehicles generating flight data and AI building calibrated predictive models, environments can be stated as exceedance probabilities. Launch-provider user guides and agency test standards gate adoption, so Medium is the cap.
struct-launch-env-margins.strongest_case_small: Launch providers have little incentive to tighten published environments; forcing uncertainty dominates; savings fall on small parts and test-failure rates rather than vehicle mass.
struct-launch-env-margins.signpost: A launch provider publishes environments derived from flight-calibrated predictive models with stated exceedance probability.

struct-radiator-optimization.title: AI-optimized radiators and heat transport
struct-radiator-optimization.description: Coupled conduction-radiation-two-phase design optimization (panel topology, heat-pipe and loop layout, view factors to Earth and arrays, micrometeoroid segmentation, deployment structure) that reaches ~2.5 kg/m2 panels and ~3 kg/kW thermal-subsystem mass at ~370 K chip temperature.
struct-radiator-optimization.status_oct2026: 33FG model: Starlink V3-like thermal ~19.4 kg/kW at 310 K; StarThink V2 ~3.0-3.4 kg/kW at 370 K with 2.5 kg/m2 two-sided panels; proven radiators run 2.5-5 kg/m2, and values below ~5 rest on two-phase hardware not yet flown at this scale. AI1 spec (Jun 2026): 110 m2 deployable liquid radiator at ~1,400 W/m2.
struct-radiator-optimization.why: The design space is large but well-posed (T^4 nonlinearity, view-factor coupling, MMOD puncture probability): expert-scarce, ideal for on-demand AI. Assume a 10-25% thermal-mass cut at fixed technology (assumption). At 1,400 W/m2, a GW of waste heat needs ~0.71 km2 of panel, so each 1 kg/m2 of areal density is ~714 t (~7 Starship flights at 100 t) per GW; the AI design gain is ~350-900 t per GW against ~10,000-14,000 t of total satellite mass per GW, i.e. ~2.5-6% of launched mass.
struct-radiator-optimization.strongest_case_small: Radiator physics is simple and SpaceX and Starcloud already optimize it with conventional tools; manufacturing cost per m2 at Starlink volume and chip-temperature limits matter more than design insight (33FG: thermal is not a physics blocker).
struct-radiator-optimization.signpost: A flown compute satellite discloses radiator areal density below 3 kg/m2; AI1 telemetry shows ~1,400 W/m2 sustained.

struct-cert-by-analysis.title: Qualification by analysis replaces some structural tests
struct-cert-by-analysis.description: Agencies and operators accept validated, uncertainty-quantified analysis with certified numerics in place of some static, modal and environmental tests (for example protoflight instead of dedicated qualification units, fewer static test articles for derivative structures).
struct-cert-by-analysis.status_oct2026: NASA-STD-7009 provides a credibility framework; tests remain mandatory for primary-structure qualification in NASA and ESA practice (general).
struct-cert-by-analysis.why: A dedicated qualification article for primary structure costs tens of millions of dollars and a year or more (general); each avoided test is a schedule step. Certified UQ plus certified numerics plus AI-run correlation make a credible case for derivatives first. Needs agency acceptance, so capped at Medium.
struct-cert-by-analysis.strongest_case_small: Test failures routinely expose what analysis missed (joints, workmanship); no agency will drop tests on first-of-kind primary structure; savings concentrate on derivatives.
struct-cert-by-analysis.signpost: A NASA or ESA program formally grants credit to model-based qualification in place of a planned structural test, by 2029-30.

struct-fsp-next-gen-design.title: Second-generation fission power designs
struct-fsp-next-gen-design.description: AI multiphysics optimization of reactor, shield, Brayton converter, radiator and lander integration for follow-on fission systems (lower kg/kWe at 100 kWe-plus, Mars or nuclear-electric variants) after the first unit's design is frozen.
struct-fsp-next-gen-design.status_oct2026: NASA directive (Jul 31 2025): at least 100 kWe, closed Brayton cycle, heavy lander with up to 15 t available, launch-ready by Q1 FY2030, awards to two providers within six months of the RFP; reactor under ~6 t (New Space Economy, Apr 2026); final RFP expected early 2026. NASA spent over $200M since 2000 on 1-200 kWe concepts without flight readiness (directive).
struct-fsp-next-gen-design.why: A timing trap: first-of-a-kind systems with near-term launch dates freeze their designs (PDR ~2027) before AI multiphysics design capability matures (S2 ~2029), so AI-math gains land in second units. Shield design rests on radiation transport, which the release does not touch; AI applied math helps there only under S2.
struct-fsp-next-gen-design.strongest_case_small: Space nuclear power is bounded by fuel supply, launch approval, nuclear ground testing and budgets, not design insight; a second-generation program may not be funded before the first unit operates.
struct-fsp-next-gen-design.signpost: NASA awards FSP contracts and announces a follow-on (Mars-class or 200 kWe-plus) design study, ideally naming AI-assisted multidisciplinary optimization.

struct-flown-lighter-structure.title: First flight structure sized with AI-certified margins
struct-flown-lighter-structure.description: A launch-vehicle barrel, interstage or large spacecraft primary structure flies after being sized with analysis-based knockdowns and certified uncertainty margins instead of legacy lower bounds, at 10-30% lower mass for its buckling-critical parts.
struct-flown-lighter-structure.status_oct2026: No such flight attributed to AI-derived design rules. Agency programs still reference SP-8007-type knockdowns; new-space firms rely on test-to-failure (general).
struct-flown-lighter-structure.why: Chain: worst-case imperfection theory (2028) -> design rules (2029) -> build and validation test of a flight article (~1 year) -> flight 2030 in S2. S3 gives no gain because the build-and-test cycle binds. Vehicle-level payoff is modest: ~1-3% payload on an upper-stage-limited vehicle (analyst estimate).
struct-flown-lighter-structure.strongest_case_small: Attribution is nearly impossible because companies already push margins via test; vehicle-level mass savings of 1-3% are within normal design-iteration noise.
struct-flown-lighter-structure.signpost: A launch or spacecraft program publicly states that a flown structure was sized with probabilistic or mechanistic knockdowns (by 2030).

struct-shm-inspection-credit.title: Sensor-based inspection credit for reusable stages
struct-shm-inspection-credit.description: Built-in structural health monitoring with quantified probability of detection replaces scheduled teardown or scanning inspection for defined zones of reusable stages or tanks between flights.
struct-shm-inspection-credit.status_oct2026: Demonstrated on specimens and subscale composite cryotanks (ONERA, 2026); an SHM payload for in-flight re-certification was prepared for ISS exposure (SPIE, Apr 2026); no launch vehicle uses SHM as formal inspection credit (general).
struct-shm-inspection-credit.why: Inspection is a large part of reuse cost: non-destructive testing of large structures is slow and access-limited (ONERA, 2026). Proven detection limits plus certified margins let operators set inspection intervals from data. Sensor qualification under thermal-cryogenic aging binds, which no amount of cognition compresses.
struct-shm-inspection-credit.strongest_case_small: Commercial operators set their own regimes and may find visual and borescope inspection plus fleet leaders cheap enough; sensor reliability, not math, limits SHM.
struct-shm-inspection-credit.signpost: An operator or NASA program announces SHM-based inspection credit for a reusable stage or tank by 2029.

struct-highflux-radiator-flight.title: 100-kW-class deployable radiators fly on compute satellites
struct-highflux-radiator-flight.description: First flights of deployable liquid or two-phase radiators rejecting 100-250 kW per spacecraft (SpaceX Starmind AI1: 110 m2 at ~1,400 W/m2; Starcloud-class follow-ons), on the physical clock and largely independent of AI mathematics.
struct-highflux-radiator-flight.status_oct2026: AI1 spec published Jun 2026 (150 kW peak, 120 kW average, 110 m2 radiator, 70 kW/t target, 70 m wingspan); Musk (Oct 1 2026): over 250 kW of solar per Starmind spacecraft, rack near 250 kW average; Starcloud-1 ran an H100 in orbit from Nov 2025; Starship reached orbit on Sep 28 2026 deploying 26 Starlink V3. First AI1 launch date not published (assumption: 2027).
struct-highflux-radiator-flight.why: Anchor node for the orbital-compute chain: the hardware arrives regardless, sized with conventional tools. 33FG's reconstruction puts AI1's thermal system at ~532 kg (25% of 2.1 t) and notes that below ~5 kg/m2 it relies on two-phase hardware SpaceX does not yet build in-house. AI-math effects enter on the second iteration.
struct-highflux-radiator-flight.strongest_case_small: This node is the counterfactual baseline: everything here happens without any AI mathematics.
struct-highflux-radiator-flight.signpost: AI1 launch and published thermal telemetry (sustained ~1,400 W/m2; chip temperature near 85-95 C).

struct-radiator-lightweight-production.title: Sub-2.5 kg/m2 radiators in serial production
struct-radiator-lightweight-production.description: Two-phase or oscillating-heat-pipe deployable radiators at or below 2.5 kg/m2 planform, running at ~370 K chip temperature, built at Starlink-like volume (thousands of m2 per month).
struct-radiator-lightweight-production.status_oct2026: Lab and prototype panels reach ~1.9-3.9 kg/m2 (33FG survey of NASA and industry prototypes); commercial deployables ~3.5-4.9 kg/m2 (Redwire Q-Rad per 33FG); none in mass production at this areal density (general).
struct-radiator-lightweight-production.why: Going from 4 to 2.5 kg/m2 at ~1,400 W/m2 saves ~1,070 t of radiator per GW (~11 Starship flights at 100 t). AI design (2028 in S2) shortens iteration; the manufacturing ramp and qualification bind, so S2 and S3 tie at 2029. In S3, AI-run factories make reaching it by 2031 High.
struct-radiator-lightweight-production.strongest_case_small: The gain rides on manufacturing learning curves and supplier insourcing, where AI mathematics plays a small role; 70 kW/t may already be economic without it.
struct-radiator-lightweight-production.signpost: SpaceX insources two-phase radiator production (33FG expects within a few years of first purchase) and discloses areal density for a Starmind version.

struct-fsp-radiator-qual.title: Lightweight 600 K radiators qualified for fission power
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.description: Titanium-water or cesium-titanium heat-pipe radiator panels near 3 kg/m2 rejecting the ~230-300 kW of waste heat from a 100 kWe Brayton system, qualified for launch vibration, freeze-thaw and ~10 years of lunar micrometeoroid exposure.
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.status_oct2026: A Cs-Ti heat-pipe panel design reaches 2.98 kg/m2 and rejects >56 kWth at 600 K with launch stresses under 10% of yield (JBIS, Jul 2025); ACT's SBIR Phase III work on Ti-H2O/graphite-fiber radiators added freeze-thaw tests and a 10-year lunar MMOD analysis (ICES, Jul 2026); titanium wick treatments studied (AIAA SciTech, Jan 2026).
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.why: At ~25-30% Brayton efficiency, 100 kWe means rejecting ~230-300 kWt; at an average radiating temperature near 450 K and ~3 kW/m2 net on the lunar surface (general), that is ~100 m2 and ~300 kg of panel at 3 kg/m2. The technology is on track without AI mathematics; qualification testing and program funding set the date.
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.strongest_case_small: The radiator is not the long pole of fission surface power; fuel, licensing and the lander are.
struct-fsp-radiator-qual.signpost: FSP provider PDR with radiator qualification test results, 2027-2028.

struct-large-sail-flight.title: A 1,000 m2-class solar sail flies
struct-large-sail-flight.description: A solar sail of at least ~1,000 m2 (NASA's follow-on boom class targets up to 2,000 m2) flies, qualified substantially by validated deployment simulation plus subscale tests.
struct-large-sail-flight.status_oct2026: ACS3 flew ~80 m2 (2024); NASA states current composite booms support up to 500 m2 and follow-on booms up to 2,000 m2; no funded 1,000 m2-class flight mission identified (general).
struct-large-sail-flight.why: Better deployment models reduce the risk of scaling 10-25x in area, but the binding gate is a funded mission; sails compete for small science budgets. The math moves the risk, not the money.
struct-large-sail-flight.strongest_case_small: Sail scale-up is gated by funding and membrane durability, not modeling; meanwhile 70 m-class compute-satellite arrays (AI1's 70 m wingspan) are flying anyway on the commercial track.
struct-large-sail-flight.signpost: NASA or another agency funds a 1,000 m2-plus sail mission by 2028.

struct-reusable-life-management.title: Model-and-sensor life management of fully reusable heavy stages
struct-reusable-life-management.description: Fully reusable heavy launchers (Starship-class and peers) manage structural life with validated damage models and built-in sensors, sustaining fast turnaround without routine teardown inspection and with life limits set by analysis rather than fleet-leader experience alone.
struct-reusable-life-management.status_oct2026: Starship reached orbit on Sep 28 2026 with both stages expended at sea (33FG); booster and ship reuse at scale not yet operational; Falcon-class booster reuse relies on inspection and fleet-leader experience (general).
struct-reusable-life-management.why: Needs both inspection credit (2029 in S2) and validated damage physics (2030), then flight hours to build confidence. Fleet experience accumulates only with flights, which no cognition compresses; S3's autonomous labs pull the damage models a year earlier.
struct-reusable-life-management.strongest_case_small: SpaceX may reach airline-like turnaround empirically, making the AI-math contribution unmeasurable; operators may never publish how they set life limits.
struct-reusable-life-management.signpost: A Starship booster or ship flies 10-plus times with publicly described sensor-based inspection between flights.

struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.title: 100 kW-per-tonne compute satellites in serial production
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.description: Compute satellites at ~100 kW/t (versus AI1's ~70 kW/t design point and a Starlink V3-like ~11 kW/t) built at hundreds to thousands per year.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.status_oct2026: AI1 ~70-71 kW/t on peak power (33FG reconstruction, Jun 2026); 33FG's StarThink V2 reference reaches ~102 kW/t with 2.5 kg/m2 radiators and improved solar; 33FG identifies solar areal density (ROSA-class 1.8-2 kg/m2) as the primary constraint.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.why: Requires lighter radiators (2029) plus lighter solar arrays and denser compute; the AI-math contribution is design optimization of the thermal and structural share (~35% of a 100 kW/t satellite's mass is thermal per 33FG V2). Manufacturing ramp binds, so S3 does not beat S2.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.strongest_case_small: Solar areal density and chip power density move kW/t more than thermal design; 70 kW/t may be good enough economically, removing the push to 100.
struct-100kw-per-tonne-fleet.signpost: SpaceX discloses a Starmind version at or above 100 kW/t.

struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.title: A 100 kWe fission reactor operating on the Moon
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.description: A fission surface power system delivering at least 100 kWe operates on the lunar surface (one-year demonstration followed by nine operational years in NASA's plan).
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.status_oct2026: Directive targets launch readiness by Q1 FY2030 on a heavy lander; NASA-DOE MOU renewed (Jan 2026); December 2025 executive order calls for a lunar surface reactor ready for launch by 2030; three Phase 1 industry teams (Westinghouse, Lockheed Martin with BWXT and Creare, IX). Award status in Oct 2026 not confirmed in this research.
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.why: Scenario-invariant on purpose: the binding gates are a heavy cargo lander able to land ~15 t (itself behind schedule), nuclear launch approval, fuel supply and nuclear ground testing. Launch-ready late CY2029 implies landing 2030-31 at best. AI mathematics does not move licensing or lander schedules, and the first unit's design freezes before AI design tools mature.
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.strongest_case_small: This node is the clearest nil chain in the domain.
struct-fsp-lunar-100kwe.signpost: Two-provider FSP award, a ground test of the flight-design reactor, and a heavy-lander cargo landing demonstration.

struct-km-monolith.title: Kilometre-scale monolithic structure in orbit
struct-km-monolith.description: A single connected structure at least 1 km across (solar-radiator plane for GW compute, space solar power array or large antenna) deployed or assembled in orbit.
struct-km-monolith.status_oct2026: Starcloud's white paper (Sep 2024) sketches a 5 GW station with a ~4 km x 4 km array assembled modularly; Google Suncatcher (Nov 2025) instead flies 81 satellites within a 1 km radius at 100-200 m spacing; SpaceX said on Oct 6 2026 that Starmind needs ~10-satellite tight-formation clusters at ~10 Tbps; Chinese space-solar-power truss-assembly robotics is active (2026); Caltech's MAPLE beamed power in orbit (2023) with 50 m unit tiles planned.
struct-km-monolith.why: Formation flying is replacing structure: guidance, navigation and optical links give km-scale clusters without km-scale structures, so the business case for a monolith weakens even as modeling improves. Deployment physics (2030 in S2) and certification by analysis (2030) arrive too late to fly a funded km-scale structure by 2031.
struct-km-monolith.strongest_case_small: Even with perfect models, nobody is paying for a monolith when formation flying works; the most likely km-scale builder (Chinese space solar power) runs on its own schedule.
struct-km-monolith.signpost: A funded km-scale assembly demonstration (for example a Chinese space-solar-power milestone), or an orbital-compute operator abandoning formation flying for a monolith.

struct-design-cycle-compression.title: Structures and thermal design cycles 3-10x faster
struct-design-cycle-compression.description: Time from a requirement change to signed-off stress, loads and thermal analysis compresses severalfold across the industry, cutting non-recurring engineering and allowing more design iterations per program.
struct-design-cycle-compression.status_oct2026: Agentic FEA is at research-prototype stage (2026); coupled-loads and thermal correlation cycles still take weeks (general).
struct-design-cycle-compression.why: The earliest and most certain effect in this domain. If structures and thermal analysis is ~10-20% of spacecraft non-recurring engineering (general) and agents cut its labor 50-80% (assumption), NRE falls ~5-15%; the larger benefit is more iterations per month, which compounds into lighter, better-margined designs.
struct-design-cycle-compression.strongest_case_small: Program schedules are bound by hardware procurement and physical tests (thermal vacuum, vibration), not analysis; faster analysis can simply wait longer for the test chamber.
struct-design-cycle-compression.signpost: Primes or new-space firms report analysis cycle-time reductions, or stress-analyst hiring shifts toward review roles, by 2028.

struct-structural-mass-step.title: 5-15% lighter structures on new vehicles and spacecraft
struct-structural-mass-step.description: Vehicles and spacecraft designed from ~2028 show 5-15% lower structural mass for equivalent loads, from combined knockdown, uncertainty-margin, launch-environment and optimization gains.
struct-structural-mass-step.status_oct2026: No measurable trend attributable to AI mathematics (general).
struct-structural-mass-step.why: Needs new designs started after the methods exist (2028-29) to finish qualification and fly; most fleets flying in 2031 were designed earlier. Vehicle-level effect is small: structure saved on an upper stage converts ~1:1 to payload, on a booster ~0.1-0.2:1 (general), so a 10% structural cut is a few percent of payload at most.
struct-structural-mass-step.strongest_case_small: Launch economics are set by propulsion, reuse and cost, not structural mass (Starship deliberately uses heavier, cheaper stainless steel); measured mass fractions will not separate AI effects from normal improvement.
struct-structural-mass-step.signpost: New vehicle or spacecraft reveals citing AI-derived design rules with disclosed dry-mass fractions.

struct-gw-orbital-compute.title: 1 GW of compute operating in orbit
struct-gw-orbital-compute.description: Cumulative at least 1 GW of compute power in orbit (about 4,000 satellites at ~250 kW, or ~10,000-14,000 t at 70-100 kW/t), rejecting ~1 GW of waste heat through ~0.7 km2 of radiator panel.
struct-gw-orbital-compute.status_oct2026: SpaceX filed for up to 1 million orbital data-center satellites (Jan 2026) and is partnering with Nvidia on Starmind AI1 (Aug 2026); Starcloud raised $170M (Mar 2026); Google Suncatcher plans two prototypes with Planet by early 2027; Starship reached orbit Sep 28 2026. Orbital compute in Oct 2026 is at kilowatt scale (general).
struct-gw-orbital-compute.why: 1 GW at 70-100 kW/t is ~100-140 Starship flights at 100 t. The AI-math share is second-order: lighter radiators and better thermal design save ~350-1,000 t per GW (~3-11 flights), a few percent. Scenario differences mostly reflect compute demand and capital (S2/S3 make orbital compute more urgent), not mathematics. Launch cadence, chip supply and capital bind.
struct-gw-orbital-compute.strongest_case_small: Thermal physics (T^4, junction-temperature limits) is unchanged, and the timing is set by Starship cadence and financing; AI mathematics could vanish from the chain without moving this node by more than months.
struct-gw-orbital-compute.signpost: Starmind production rate and dedicated Starship flights per year; SpaceX reporting deployed orbital compute in hundreds of MW by 2029.

verif-code-proof-agents.title: Agents that prove real flight code
verif-code-proof-agents.description: AI agents write contracts, loop invariants and proofs for production embedded code (C, Ada/SPARK, Rust) and discharge them in an existing checker (Frama-C, GNATprove, Verus, or Lean via extraction), at a marginal cost of compute hours instead of proof-engineer years.
verif-code-proof-agents.status_oct2026: Partly exists. Off-the-shelf LLMs produced verified code for 82% of Dafny, 44% of Verus and 27% of Lean specifications in the vericoding benchmark (Sep 2025). The best agent fully solved 27 of 43 repository-scale instances in Vero (Aug 2026). OpenAI's pipeline formalized the main results of 162 papers in under four weeks (openai/math, Oct 6 2026; agent-written, review status unchecked, so T3 as evidence of the pipeline). No catalog family applies; the evidence is the pipeline itself.
verif-code-proof-agents.why: Formal methods in aerospace have been limited by proof labor, not tools: seL4 took about 25 person-years and roughly 27 lines of Isabelle per verified line of C. Proof writing is exactly what agents now do. The remaining gate is mature formal semantics for the target language: strong for SPARK and Frama-C C, weaker for C++ and for Rust in Lean. Under S2, with agent task horizons doubling every 6-9 months, repository-scale success moves from about 63% (Aug 2026) to routine during 2027. Under S1 public models get there by about 2028. 'Achieved' here means verifying a 10-50 KLOC real embedded codebase to functional-contract level with under 10% human proof effort.
verif-code-proof-agents.strongest_case_small: Benchmarks use clean specs and small repositories. Flight code is legacy C and C++ with hardware registers, interrupts, concurrency and undocumented assumptions, where proofs stall on modeling the environment rather than on proof search. A proof of an unreviewed spec adds little assurance.
