verif-code-proof-agents.signpost: A tool vendor or agency (AdaCore, AbsInt, TrustInSoft, Galois, NASA, ESA) reports AI-generated SPARK or Frama-C proofs over more than 10 KLOC of real embedded code with human effort a small fraction of the seL4 ratio; Vero-class repository benchmarks pass 90%.

verif-skolem-positivity.title: Settle the Skolem and Positivity problems
verif-skolem-positivity.description: Decide whether a linear recurrence ever hits zero (Skolem) or always stays positive (Positivity), both open in general. They are the exact mathematical core of asking whether a discrete-time linear loop, such as a sampled control law or estimator update, ever crosses a threshold.
verif-skolem-positivity.status_oct2026: Open. Decidability is known only at low order, and some results are conditional on number-theoretic conjectures (general). Not in the openai/math catalog. The release's logic and number-theory output suggests problems of this kind are now within reach of frontier systems.
verif-skolem-positivity.why: Either a decision procedure or an undecidability proof would fix the ceiling for exact, unbounded verification of linear loops with rational coefficients, and would feed invariant generators and termination provers. It sits at the intersection of logic and number theory, where the Sep-Oct 2026 releases show the most progress. Bands reflect the chance an AI system settles it by 2031, not that it changes flight practice.
verif-skolem-positivity.strongest_case_small: Flight verification never needs exact unbounded decidability. Engineers prove sufficient conditions (Lyapunov functions, linear matrix inequalities, bounded horizons, interval margins) that are already decidable or cheap, and flown code runs in floating point, not exact rationals. Expect a P3 ceiling result with near-nil effect on tools.
verif-skolem-positivity.signpost: A lab, Hexagon or arXiv claim settling Skolem or Positivity at order 5 and above with a Lean statement; verification-tool papers citing it within a year.

verif-game-solving-synthesis.title: Faster worst-case game solving for synthesis
verif-game-solving-synthesis.description: Family 104 claims quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games. These games are the back end of reactive synthesis (building mode logic from temporal-logic specs) and of probabilistic model checking (fault management under random failures).
verif-game-solving-synthesis.status_oct2026: Family 104 has a Lean main result in the repo, unchecked by outsiders (T3). Parity games already had quasipolynomial algorithms from 2017 (general); the stochastic and mean-payoff cases are the new part. Practical solvers (strategy iteration, value iteration) already handle engineering-sized instances.
verif-game-solving-synthesis.why: Once independently checked (T4), the result resets the worst-case complexity map for synthesis and probabilistic verification and removes a long-standing theoretical doubt; tool builders will cite it as a ceiling. The node is the result being established and known. Its effect on flight-verification practice is near nil (P4 effect: Low).
verif-game-solving-synthesis.strongest_case_small: Worst-case bounds do not govern practice. Real synthesis and model-checking problems are limited by state-space size and specification quality, and existing solvers rarely meet worst cases. No change to flight verification workflows is expected.
verif-game-solving-synthesis.signpost: An independent Comparator run on family 104 via Hexagon; any implementation that beats strategy iteration on standard probabilistic model-checking benchmarks.

verif-spec-engineering.title: AI-drafted formal specifications
verif-spec-engineering.description: AI turns natural-language requirements, interface control documents and concepts of operations into formal, machine-checkable specifications (contracts, temporal logic, unit-typed interfaces). It checks them for consistency and realizability and flags hidden environmental assumptions for human sign-off.
verif-spec-engineering.status_oct2026: NASA's FRET turns structured English into temporal logic and, through Ogma and Copilot, into runtime monitors that flew in NASA's ICAROUS autonomy framework. Research pipelines (Forge, Jun 2026) close the loop from LLM-written code to Dafny, CSP and Isabelle checks. Spec writing remains scarce senior-engineer work, and no space program publicly uses AI-drafted formal specs for flight-critical functions.
verif-spec-engineering.why: Once proofs are cheap, specs become the bottleneck: a proof of the wrong property is worthless (analyst position h). In all 9 software-related losses in our failure table, the missing piece was an assumption, interface spec or process step, not proof capacity. AI cuts spec drafting and consistency checking several-fold (general). Each spec still needs a qualified engineer to accept that it says what the mission needs, so human review bandwidth binds. 'Achieved' means use on a flight program for a safety-critical function.
verif-spec-engineering.strongest_case_small: AI drafts may encode the same wrong assumptions the team already holds and give them false authority by making them formal. For domain experts who are not fluent in temporal logic, reviewing a formal spec is not much faster than writing one.
verif-spec-engineering.signpost: NASA, ESA or a lander company publishes a case study of LLM-drafted FRET or contract specs accepted at a flight review; a certification-authority position paper on AI-authored low-level requirements.

verif-verified-gnc-numerics.title: Proven floating-point GNC code
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.description: Machine-checked bounds on round-off, overflow and conversion errors for guidance, navigation, control and estimation code, generated per module by agents. The tools are Astree, PRECiSA with Frama-C, or Lean FloatLib-class libraries. The result is that a proof about real-number math also holds for the code that flies.
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.status_oct2026: Solved in principle and expert-scarce. Astree proved absence of runtime errors in 132 KLOC of A340 primary flight-control code in 1 h 20 min (2003). NASA verified the floating-point C of the DAIDALUS detect-and-avoid well-clear module with PVS, PRECiSA and Frama-C, including round-off bounds and overflow freedom (2023). In Lean, FloatLib (Sep 2026) unifies IEEE binary and decimal formats, posits and P3109 with proofs; FloatSpec is a port of Flocq in progress.
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.why: Ariane 501 was lost to an unprotected 64-bit float to 16-bit integer conversion. Runtime-error analysis of that class is automatic today, and per-module round-off proofs in the DAIDALUS style become a compute job once agents write the annotations. The coverage gate is verified libraries for linear algebra, quaternion kinematics and filters with floating-point semantics.
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.strongest_case_small: Runtime-error freedom is already cheap with Astree-class tools, and numerical round-off rarely kills missions. The Ariane case needed the right input ranges, which is an assumption problem, not a proof problem.
verif-verified-gnc-numerics.signpost: A Lean or Coq library with a verified floating-point Kalman filter or quaternion propagator; NASA or ESA GNC teams publishing agent-generated round-off proofs on flight code.

verif-closed-loop-guarantees.title: Machine-checked GNC stability and safety envelopes
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.description: Proofs that a guidance, control and estimation loop stays inside a safe envelope, including actuator saturation, sampling, delay, sensor gating and mode switches. The proofs use barrier certificates, Lyapunov functions, reachability or differential dynamic logic, and are produced on request rather than by rare specialists.
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.status_oct2026: Tools exist: differential dynamic logic (KeYmaera X), sum-of-squares barrier certificates, reachability analyzers. They have been applied to aircraft collision avoidance (general). Building certificates for saturated, sampled, mode-switching loops is expert-scarce, and nonlinear hybrid verification at full-vehicle scale is partly open. Family 143 (uniform limit-cycle bounds for planar polynomial vector fields, T3) is theory-only and does not reach this workflow.
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.why: This is the bespoke math, easier than the catalog's, that analyst position (a) says matters most: a stability or keep-out proof for one control law. Under S2, research-grade applied math is on tap by 2028. The gate then becomes Lean/Mathlib coverage of ODEs, hybrid systems and real analysis, or the use of existing provers such as KeYmaera X with agent-written proofs. 'Achieved' means a flown GNC loop whose key stability or safety property is machine-checked, including saturation and mode logic.
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.strongest_case_small: Most flown GNC is close to linear, with well-understood classical margins checked by Monte Carlo. Flight losses trace to sensor logic and assumptions more than to unstable control laws. Proofs over idealized dynamics may not survive unmodeled flexible modes, propellant slosh or plume effects.
verif-closed-loop-guarantees.signpost: An agent-produced, machine-checked barrier certificate for powered-descent or rendezvous guidance published with flight-like dynamics (saturation, delay, slosh).

verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.title: Certified onboard trajectory optimizers
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.description: Proofs that the onboard convex solvers used for powered-descent guidance and rendezvous model-predictive control converge within a fixed iteration and timing budget for every admissible state. They are paired with cheap runtime certificates (duality gaps) checked each control cycle.
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.status_oct2026: Onboard convex guidance (lossless convexification) has flight-test heritage on rocket test beds (general). Proofs that a specific solver implementation converges within a fixed iteration and timing budget are rare. Runtime duality-gap certificates are cheap but seldom used as safety evidence.
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.why: Crewed landing and propellant transfer increasingly rely on onboard optimization. Certifying it needs both math (convergence and feasibility for every admissible state) and timing evidence on the flight processor. The math compresses under S2; timing characterization on radiation-tolerant processors and HIL qualification bind.
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.strongest_case_small: Programs can avoid certifying the optimizer by wrapping it in runtime assurance with a simple backup guidance law, which is cheaper and already accepted practice.
verif-onboard-optimizer-certificates.signpost: A lander or HLS provider describing certified onboard optimization in an AIAA GNC paper or design review; verified convex-solver code with worst-case execution time bounds.

verif-nn-verification-scale.title: Verifying neural perception at flight scale
verif-nn-verification-scale.description: Proving robustness and correctness properties, over the operational domain, of neural networks used for terrain-relative navigation, hazard detection or pose estimation. This is genuinely open: exact verification is NP-hard, and 'correct perception' resists formal specification.
verif-nn-verification-scale.status_oct2026: VNN-COMP 2025 (8 teams, 16 regular and 9 extended benchmarks) shows steady progress on small and medium networks. Flight-scale vision networks and perception properties remain out of reach. SAE ARP6983 / EUROCAE ED-324 (targeted Jun 2026 and Q4 2026) and EASA NPA 2025-07 base machine-learning assurance on data and process, not proof. No catalog family addresses it.
verif-nn-verification-scale.why: Exact verification of ReLU networks is NP-hard (general), and the property itself ('detects every hazardous crater') is defined by data, not by math. New relaxations and verification-friendly architectures from on-demand research math could move the frontier, but the gap in specification remains even in S3, which is why the band stays Low.
verif-nn-verification-scale.strongest_case_small: Space programs do not need to verify the network. They wrap it in runtime assurance or use it only for advisory functions, so this open problem may simply be routed around.
verif-nn-verification-scale.signpost: VNN-COMP results on networks at terrain-relative-navigation scale; ED-324/ARP6983 or EASA guidance granting credit for formal robustness proofs of neural networks.

verif-environment-assumption-models.title: Validated sensor and terrain envelopes
verif-environment-assumption-models.description: Formally stated, test-validated envelopes for what sensors and environments can do during critical phases: laser rangefinder and altimeter dropouts and reflectivity, IMU saturation durations, terrain discontinuities, lighting. Proofs can assume them and simulators can sample them.
verif-environment-assumption-models.status_oct2026: Ad hoc. Recent lunar losses trace to sensor and environment surprises: Hakuto-R M1's 3 km crater rim (2023), Resilience's late rangefinder readings (2025), Athena's altimeter interference, low-sun lighting and crater appearance mismatch (Mar 2025), and earlier Schiaparelli's 1 s IMU saturation (2016). LRO maps and flight telemetry exist but are not packaged as formal assumptions.
verif-environment-assumption-models.why: Proofs and tests are conditional on environment assumptions. AI can quickly fuse orbital maps, test data and telemetry into formal envelopes, but the envelopes are only as good as sensor characterization tests and the few landings that produce truth data. S3's autonomous labs speed sensor testing on the ground, not the supply of lunar truth data, which is why even S3 stays Medium.
verif-environment-assumption-models.strongest_case_small: Each new site, sensor and lighting condition differs, so envelopes generalize poorly and teams will still discover new failure physics in flight.
verif-environment-assumption-models.signpost: A shared, formally stated lunar-descent sensor and terrain envelope dataset (for example from NASA CLPS or ESA) adopted by two or more lander teams.

verif-assumption-falsification.title: AI red-teaming of flight assumptions
verif-assumption-falsification.description: Agents search physics-based simulations and data for scenarios that break the assumptions under which flight software was proven or tested: terrain steps, saturation longer than designed, sensor delays, reboot timing, unit mismatches. Each finding becomes a test or a strengthened spec.
verif-assumption-falsification.status_oct2026: Monte Carlo dispersion campaigns and temporal-logic falsification tools exist (general). Hakuto-R M1's late landing-site change was not simulated against crater-rim terrain, and Schiaparelli's fault logic did not cover an IMU saturation lasting about 1 s.
verif-assumption-falsification.why: Counterexamples act fastest (analyst position c): a found scenario changes the design within weeks. Agents can rerun targeted searches over terrain, sensor timing and fault combinations every time the design or landing site changes, which is exactly where Hakuto-R M1, Schiaparelli and Ariane 501 escaped. The gate is the fidelity of simulators and sensor models.
verif-assumption-falsification.strongest_case_small: AI can only find failures the simulator can represent; Athena's and Resilience's sensor physics would not have appeared in typical simulations. Mature teams already run large dispersion campaigns.
verif-assumption-falsification.signpost: A lander team attributing a design change to AI-found falsifying scenarios; NASA CLPS asking for assumption-falsification reports at mission readiness reviews.

verif-fdir-model-checking.title: Exhaustive checks of fault logic and configuration
verif-fdir-model-checking.description: Agents build formal models of fault detection, isolation and recovery logic, mode machines, reboot and timing behavior, command sequences and parameter tables from code and interface documents. They then model-check them exhaustively, including emergency in-flight patches.
verif-fdir-model-checking.status_oct2026: Model checkers (SPIN, NuSMV, Kind 2) are mature; building faithful models is the cost. Failures in this class: Starliner OFT (mission timer 11 h off, service-module valve mapping error, 2019), Beresheet (IMU restart blocked the other IMU's data, causing a reboot loop and engine shutdown, 2019), Hitomi (wrongly updated thruster parameter, 2016), IM-1 (rangefinder safety switch left enabled; the in-flight patch missed a data-valid flag, 2024).
verif-fdir-model-checking.why: Four of the nine software-related losses in our failure table sit in this class. Agents can extract models from code and interface documents and check every fault combination and command sequence. They can also check emergency patches within hours; IM-1's patch was written and uploaded mid-mission. The binding input is accurate hardware behavior (bus blocking, timer sources), which needs characterization data.
verif-fdir-model-checking.strongest_case_small: Starliner's errors were also catchable by the end-to-end integrated test the program skipped. The root problem was process discipline, which cheap tools do not guarantee.
verif-fdir-model-checking.signpost: A CLPS or commercial-crew post-flight review crediting model checking with catching a fault-logic error before flight; NASA or ESA tools that automatically extract FDIR models from flight code.

verif-checker-not-generator.title: Certification credit through qualified proof checkers
verif-checker-not-generator.description: AI writes proofs and contracts; an already-qualified checker (SPARK GNATprove, Frama-C WP, Astree, or later a qualified Lean kernel) verifies them. Because the AI's output is checked, the AI itself needs no tool qualification, so DO-333 credit for replacing unit tests can flow to AI-generated proofs once humans approve the specs.
verif-checker-not-generator.status_oct2026: DO-333 lets formal analysis replace most executable-object-code verification except hardware/software integration tests. Airbus replaced unit tests with proofs on A380 software (Caveat, 2002), with industry-reported savings of 30-50%. Qualifying a small proof-certificate checker instead of a complex tool has been studied (University of Iowa). NASA accredits tools rather than qualifying them (NPR 7150.2, general). No public credit yet for AI-generated proof artifacts.
verif-checker-not-generator.why: Under DO-330, qualification is required for tools whose output is not otherwise verified. If AI writes proofs and a qualified checker verifies them, the AI plays the role of a human proof author and needs no qualification. The human obligations that remain are reviewing specs (low-level requirements) and justifying assumptions. That makes the regulatory gate a plan-acceptance step (software certification plan, stage-of-involvement audits) rather than a new standard. Capped at Medium because an authority must still agree.
verif-checker-not-generator.strongest_case_small: Authorities may treat AI-authored specs and annotations as development artifacts that need independence and review effort, eroding the savings. Lean-native pipelines, where AI labs are strongest, lack a qualified checker and must take the slower infra-tool-qualification path.
verif-checker-not-generator.signpost: An FAA or EASA certification review item, certification-authority position paper or EASA guidance on AI-assisted verification under DO-333; the first software certification plan that publicly lists AI-generated proof artifacts.

verif-runtime-assurance.title: Proven safety wrappers for unverifiable autonomy
verif-runtime-assurance.description: Instead of verifying a neural or learned controller, verify a small monitor, a recoverable-set (barrier) condition and a simple backup controller, and switch to the backup before safety is lost (the Simplex architecture). Agents make the proofs of the wrapper and the switching logic cheap.
verif-runtime-assurance.status_oct2026: ASTM F3269 and NASA guidance define runtime assurance. Monitors generated by FRET and Copilot flew in NASA's ICAROUS, and R2U2 targets rovers and small satellites. Spacecraft use is mostly research. The expensive parts are proving the recoverable set and the switching logic.
verif-runtime-assurance.why: Neural and learned components (hazard detection, terrain-relative navigation) cannot be verified directly (see verif-nn-verification-scale), so assurance moves to a small, provable monitor and a simple backup. Agents make the barrier-certificate and switching proofs cheap. The binding gate is showing, on hardware-in-the-loop rigs and in flight, that the backup really recovers.
verif-runtime-assurance.strongest_case_small: Conservative wrappers trigger too often and erode the performance that justified the learned component, and a proven wrapper built on a wrong recoverable-set model is still unsafe.
verif-runtime-assurance.signpost: A lunar lander or rendezvous mission flying a learned component inside a proven Simplex wrapper; runtime assurance referenced in ED-324/ARP6983 or NASA guidance as a certification path.

verif-verified-onboard-stack.title: Formally verified onboard software stack
verif-verified-onboard-stack.description: seL4-class verified separation kernels and hypervisors, telecommand parsers, and software-update authentication become cheap enough to fly on ordinary missions. Flight software and onboard AI payloads can then share one processor with proven isolation.
verif-verified-onboard-stack.status_oct2026: seL4: 8,700 lines of C, 200,000 lines of Isabelle proof, about 25 person-years (estimated under 10 if redone), with 160 bugs found (144 during C verification). ECSS-E-ST-40C Rev.1 and ECSS-Q-ST-80C Rev.2 (Apr 2025) added explicit security requirements. Verified kernels remain niche in space.
verif-verified-onboard-stack.why: At seL4's ratio, a verified 10 KLOC kernel or telecommand stack costs roughly $5M of proof labor. At agent cost it becomes a compute bill plus spec review, so verified separation kernels, command parsers and update authentication can become standard, letting onboard AI payloads share processors with flight software under proven isolation.
verif-verified-onboard-stack.strongest_case_small: Isolation proofs assume correct hardware. Multicore timing interference, radiation upsets and processor errata are measured, not proven, and those qualification campaigns stay physical.
verif-verified-onboard-stack.signpost: A constellation or lander operator announcing a verified kernel or hypervisor in flight; ESA or a defense constellation program requiring formally verified telecommand parsing.

verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.title: A lunar lander flies proof-checked descent software
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.description: A commercial lander flies terminal-descent GNC and fault management whose key properties are machine-checked: altitude plausibility, measurement-rejection gates, engine-cutoff and reboot logic. Its assumptions are red-teamed against terrain and sensor models.
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.status_oct2026: Commercial and agency landers 2016-2025: Schiaparelli (IMU-saturation logic), Beresheet (command-triggered reboot loop), Hakuto-R M1 (filter rejected valid altimetry after a crater rim), IM-1 (configuration and patch flag), Peregrine (helium valve), Resilience (rangefinder), Athena (altimeter, lighting, tipped over). No lander has publicly flown formally verified descent logic (general).
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.why: New-entrant landers face no certifying regulator for mission software and have repeatedly lost missions to logic errors (Beresheet, Hakuto-R M1), so the incentive is strong. Software freezes 12-18 months before flight, and commercial landers fly a few times a year. Even with S2 capability in 2027, the first flight with proof-checked descent logic lands around 2029; launch cadence, not cognition, binds.
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.strongest_case_small: Half of recent lander losses were hardware or sensor physics (Peregrine's valve, Resilience's rangefinder, Athena's altimeter and lighting), which proofs do not touch. Teams may also adopt quietly and never disclose.
verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight.signpost: A CLPS or private lander team publicly stating formal verification of descent GNC and fault management in a readiness review or press kit.

verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.title: Assured autonomous docking and propellant transfer
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.description: Rendezvous, proximity operations, docking and ship-to-ship propellant transfer flown with machine-checked passive safety (collision-free under failures) and abort logic, plus runtime assurance on the guidance.
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.status_oct2026: Starship reached orbit on Flight 14 (Sep 28 2026) and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Ship-to-ship propellant transfer has not yet been demonstrated; a demonstration is reported for Q4 2026. Artemis III was reprofiled to a crewed low-Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test with lander pathfinders in late 2027. The HLS program has reportedly planned around 15-17 Starship flights per landing.
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.why: Each lunar landing chains many autonomous rendezvous and transfers. Proven passive safety and abort logic lower the risk per operation and the test burden per software change. But confidence is gated by the number of flight demonstrations, not by proof capacity, and launch cadence does not compress with cognition.
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.strongest_case_small: SpaceX builds confidence through flight count; formal proofs may stay internal and invisible. Docking risk is dominated by hardware: mechanisms and cryogenic-transfer physics.
verif-rpo-assured-autonomy.signpost: Artemis III (late 2027) safety documentation citing formal verification of rendezvous abort logic; the first successful ship-to-ship propellant transfer.

verif-constellation-verified-updates.title: Proof-checked software updates across constellations
verif-constellation-verified-updates.description: Each over-the-air update to thousands of satellites is gated by automatic re-proof of key invariants: collision-avoidance decision logic, safe-mode entry, deorbit capability, command authentication. Proofs re-run in hours, enabling weekly verified releases.
verif-constellation-verified-updates.status_oct2026: Starlink satellites made 207,152 avoidance maneuvers from Dec 2025 to May 2026 (more than 355,000 a year), mostly decided onboard. Update practices are proprietary, and the FCC requires maneuver reports, not software assurance.
verif-constellation-verified-updates.why: At this volume of onboard decisions, a logic regression in collision-avoidance or safe-mode code is a fleet-wide risk. Once the specs exist, re-proving a fixed set of invariants on every update is a compute job, with no regulator in the loop. Under S2, operators get verified weekly releases by about 2028.
verif-constellation-verified-updates.strongest_case_small: Operators already manage risk with staged rollouts, telemetry and fast rollback, which may be cheaper than proofs for non-catastrophic functions, and they disclose little.
verif-constellation-verified-updates.signpost: An operator (SpaceX, Amazon Kuiper, defense constellation contractors) or an FCC filing referring to formally verified collision-avoidance or deorbit logic.

verif-hls-autonomy-certification.title: Crewed lunar-lander autonomy certified with proofs
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.description: NASA human-rating certification (NPR 8705.2C with NPR 7150.2 Class A software) for a crewed lander accepts machine-checked proofs as part of the evidence for landing guidance, abort and fault-management autonomy.
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.status_oct2026: The first crewed landing moved to Artemis IV in 2028 (one report says Sep 2028 for SpaceX). NPR 8705.2C requires single-failure tolerance to catastrophic events, crew override of automation, and autonomous capability for functions whose loss would be catastrophic. No human-rated system has used AI-written proofs as evidence.
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.why: The 2028 landing's software baseline will largely be set before public research-grade verification arrives, so AI proofs enter through block upgrades for 2029-31 landings. NASA's technical authority must accept the evidence, so the band is capped at Medium.
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.strongest_case_small: Human rating relies on testing, redundancy and crew override, and proofs add to that evidence rather than replace it. After Starliner, NASA's risk posture favors more testing, not less.
verif-hls-autonomy-certification.signpost: NASA HLS or commercial-crew certification documents referencing formal proofs; NASA standards or software-engineering handbook guidance on AI-generated verification evidence.

verif-afss-part450.title: Proof-backed flight termination under FAA Part 450
verif-afss-part450.description: Autonomous flight safety system logic and other Part 450 computing-system safety items are licensed with formal proofs as an accepted means of compliance alongside RCC-319 testing.
verif-afss-part450.status_oct2026: Section 450.141 requires operators to identify computing-system safety items, set safety requirements by criticality and use a development process suited to that criticality. AC 450.141-1A, which includes an RCC-319 appendix on mission data loads, is an accepted means of compliance. There is no explicit credit for formal proofs, but the performance-based rule allows alternative means.
verif-afss-part450.why: Flight-termination logic is small, critical and well specified, which makes it the ideal first proof target in launch. Part 450's performance-based structure lets an applicant propose proofs without a rule change, but the FAA must accept them, so the band is capped at Medium.
verif-afss-part450.strongest_case_small: License timelines are driven by environmental review, mishap investigations and public-safety analysis, not by software evidence (general). Flight-termination software is already heavily tested, so proofs will not speed licenses or raise launch cadence.
verif-afss-part450.signpost: An FAA advisory-circular revision or a license record citing formal verification of computing-system safety items; Range Commanders Council updates to RCC-319 recognizing formal analysis.

verif-assurance-cost-collapse.title: Verified code 30-100x cheaper; certified programs about 2.4x cheaper
verif-assurance-cost-collapse.description: The cost per functionally verified line falls from hundreds of dollars (seL4-class) to roughly $5-20 under S2. A full DAL-A-equivalent program's software cost falls about 2.4x because physical integration testing remains. Turnaround to re-verify a change drops from weeks to days.
verif-assurance-cost-collapse.status_oct2026: Baseline: DO-178C Level A runs about $100 per line (range $25-100), verification is up to 80% of cost, and productivity is under 10 lines per person-day. seL4-class full functional proof costs roughly $300-600 per line (general, derived from about 25 person-years for 8.7 KLOC).
verif-assurance-cost-collapse.why: Cost model (general, our assumptions). Starting shares of a Level-A budget and their S2 multipliers: requirements and design 20% x0.7, code 10% x0.3, unit verification 35% x0.1 (replaced by proof), software integration 15% x0.4, hardware/software integration and system test 20% x0.8. The total is 42.5% of baseline, about 2.4x cheaper. Under S1 the total is about 70-80% of baseline; under S3, with AI-run test rigs, about 30-35%. Full functional proofs fall from hundreds of dollars per line to about $5-20 because spec review dominates and compute costs cents per line. The larger effect is assurance level per dollar and change turnaround.
verif-assurance-cost-collapse.strongest_case_small: Software is a modest share of mission cost and schedule. HIL rigs, environmental testing and integration remain physical and set program pace.
verif-assurance-cost-collapse.signpost: Program cost reports or vendor case studies showing more than 50% reduction in verification hours on a safety-critical flight program.

verif-new-entrant-advantage.title: Assurance stops being a moat for primes
verif-new-entrant-advantage.description: Small teams (lander and constellation startups) reach assurance levels that once required large verification departments. Primes' advantage shifts from process capacity to certification relationships, while qualified-checker vendors and AI-model providers capture new value.
verif-new-entrant-advantage.status_oct2026: Primes hold certification know-how and large V&V departments. New entrants run small teams and account for most recent software-caused lander losses (Beresheet, Hakuto-R M1, IM-1 configuration).
verif-new-entrant-advantage.why: Uncrewed commercial missions have no certifying regulator for mission software, so new entrants can adopt as soon as the tools work, while primes on cost-plus contracts have weaker incentives to cut verification hours. Value concentrates where trust is scarce: in the small set of qualified checkers (AdaCore, AbsInt, TrustInSoft and similar) and in access to frontier models.
verif-new-entrant-advantage.strongest_case_small: Primes adopt the same tools quickly (Airbus led formal methods in avionics) and keep the regulator relationships. Value may accrue to AI labs and checker vendors rather than to either group of space companies.
verif-new-entrant-advantage.signpost: A new entrant winning a NASA, ESA or defense contract with formal assurance as a cited discriminator; a prime reorganizing its V&V department around spec engineering.

verif-mission-loss-rate.title: Fewer missions lost to software logic (hard to see by 2031)
verif-mission-loss-rate.description: The share of mission losses caused by software logic, configuration and fault-management errors falls measurably.
verif-mission-loss-rate.status_oct2026: Of the 12 notable losses and near-losses in our failure table (1996-2025), 9 were primarily or partly software, logic or configuration errors. Of the six commercial lunar missions in the table since 2019, three losses (Peregrine, Resilience, Athena) were primarily hardware or sensor physics.
verif-mission-loss-rate.why: Even if verified software works as intended, only a few dozen lander and RPO flights will occur by 2031, too few to separate a lower software-caused loss rate from noise. Hardware and sensor failures also keep the total loss rate high. The effect may be real but unmeasurable inside the horizon.
verif-mission-loss-rate.strongest_case_small: With cheap proofs, teams may ship more ambitious autonomy faster, keeping the loss rate flat while capability rises (risk homeostasis, general).
verif-mission-loss-rate.signpost: Root-cause reports of 2027-2030 lander or RPO failures: a shift from logic and configuration causes toward hardware and sensor causes would support the chain.
